authors.name: N. Guignot
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

authors.name: A. Maillard
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: New hierarchical matrices for fast kernel matrix-vector products with Applications to Gaussian processes and kernel ridge regression
papers.abstract: This article presents two new multilevel hierarchical matrices to perform fast kernel matrix-vector products in $d$ dimensions $(d>1)$, namely $\mathcal{H}_{hw}^{\prime}$, $\mathcal{H}_{hw}^{\prime \prime}$. We introduce a novel hybrid weak admissibility condition to construct these hierarchical matrices. More precisely, at coarser levels of the tree (i.e., larger blocks), we use a weak admissibility condition, wherein \textbf{far-field} and \textbf{vertex-sharing} clusters are considered admissible, while at the finer levels (i.e., smaller blocks), the \textbf{adjacent} clusters are treated as admissible. The admissible blocks at coarser levels of $\mathcal{H}_{hw}^{\prime}$ and $\mathcal{H}_{hw}^{\prime \prime}$ are represented using semi-nested and fully nested bases, respectively. In both hierarchical matrices, the finer levels at which adjacent clusters are treated as admissible are constructed in a non-nested fashion. Thus, they can be viewed as a hybrid of $\mathcal{H}$ and $\mathcal{H}^2$ matrices. We use adaptive cross approximation (ACA) and nested cross approximation (NCA) to construct non-nested and nested bases, respectively. The fast matrix-vector products are performed using the proposed hierarchical matrix formats. To evaluate the performance and usefulness of the proposed hierarchical matrices, we conduct some numerical experiments. The numerical results show that they outperform their uniform admissibility counterparts in terms of storage and matrix-vector product cost, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed hybrid formats. We also show that the proposed formats are competitive with the standard (or strong) admissibility-based $\mathcal{H}^2$-matrices. Furthermore, we showcase some interesting applications of the proposed hierarchical matrices.

papers.title: An Adian-Rabin theorem for quantum automorphism groups of graphs
papers.abstract: Given a graph $G$, does it have quantum symmetries, or in other words, is the algebra of the quantum automorphism group non-commutative? In the world of ordinary groups, determining whether a finitely presented group is commutative is undecidable. This is an immediate consequence of the Adian-Rabin theorem, which shows that many natural properties of finitely presented groups are undecidable. In this paper, we prove an Adian-Rabin theorem for quantum automorphism groups of graphs, showing that many natural properties of the quantum automorphism group of a graph (including having quantum symmetries) are undecidable. We also show that it's undecidable to determine if the discrete quantum automorphism group is non-trivial. Our methods are based on solution groups of linear system nonlocal games, and we also prove an Adian-Rabin theorem in this context.

papers.title: STORY2DIFF: A Dataset Linking Real-World User Stories to Code Changes
papers.abstract: Research on requirements-to-code tasks needs examples in which a genuine requirement is paired with the change that implemented it. Existing user-story collections, however, largely contain isolated or synthetic text. To address this limitation, we present STORY2DIFF, a dataset of 7,785 English user stories linked to merged pull requests from January 2017 to July 2026. The dataset is mined from a set of 982 public Java and Python repositories. Each record in the dataset combines the original issue, extracted Connextra elements, the associated pull request and commit metadata, a file-level diff capturing the code changes introduced by the associated pull request, and the affected files before and after the change. The tool we built to mine STORY2DIFF can be used to repeat the automatic extraction of the records, using different parameters (e.g., a different timeframe). The dataset can support a variety of tasks, including requirement discovery, traceability, change- impact estimation, and requirements-aware code generation. Dataset: https://github.com/riganelli/user-story-mining-pipeline/ releases/tag/V4.0.1. Video: https://youtu.be/qOhXUeyeiTQ.

papers.title: Continuous tuning of quantum critical behavior in hybrid Josephson junction arrays
papers.abstract: We report finite-temperature scaling of voltage-driven quantum phase transitions in hybrid Josephson junction arrays. A dual-gate geometry separately tunes interisland coupling and proximity-induced superconductivity, providing access to superconducting, insulating, and metallic transport regimes. The critical resistivity and scaling exponent evolve continuously with electrostatic tuning. Where the three regimes converge, the critical resistivity approaches $h/4e^2$, consistent with the self-dual limit, while the scaling exponent approaches the quantum-percolation estimate. Tuning toward stronger insulating behavior raises the critical resistivity and shifts the scaling exponent toward the classical-percolation value, while both parameters decrease toward the metallic regime. These results connect scaling regimes previously reported in different two-dimensional superconducting systems through continuous electrostatic control.

authors.name: L. L. Olsen
authors.institution: University of British Columbia, Okanagan Campus

authors.name: S. Sasmal
authors.institution: Council of Scientific and Industrial Research

authors.name: F. Krizek
authors.institution: Czech Academy of Sciences, Nuclear Physics Institute

papers.title: Pointed Hurwitz--Brill--Noether theory
papers.abstract: We study the geometry of Hurwitz--Brill--Noether spaces with vanishing conditions at a totally ramified point. Degeneration to a curve with an elliptic tail simplifies the combinatorics of Larson, Larson--Larson--Vogt, and Aggarwal, giving inductive proofs of Aggarwal's results in the one-point setting, and yields an efficient recursion for the algebraic Euler characteristics. Finally, when the expected dimension is negative, we give a numerical criterion ensuring the universal Hurwitz--Brill--Noether locus admits a component of expected relative dimension, generically finite over its image in the Hurwitz space, analogous to the existing results of Pflueger and Teixidor i Bigas for classical Brill--Noether loci.

papers.title: From a Lifshitz Transition to Spin-Density-Wave Order: Sr$_2$RuO$_4$ under Uniaxial Strain
papers.abstract: In recent years, the effects of uniaxial strain on Sr$_2$RuO$_4$ have been extensively investigated, revealing a pronounced enhancement of the superconducting critical temperature accompanied by experimental indications of an emergent magnetically ordered state. In this Letter, we study the impact of strain on the spectral and magnetic properties of this material within an advanced many-body theoretical framework. We find that strain induces an anisotropic Lifshitz transition, which enhances the electron scattering rate along the elongation axis while simultaneously promoting coherent Fermi-liquid behavior in the perpendicular direction, in close agreement with experimental observations. Taking into account this anisotropic behavior allows us to capture the magnetic instability leading to a finite-temperature ordered state at large strain values. Our analysis further reveals that the magnetic response is dominated by two competing wave vectors associated with distinct nesting vectors: one within the $\gamma$ sheet and the other between the $\alpha$ and $\beta$ sheets of the Fermi surface. Both wave vectors can stabilize magnetic order, with their competition depending sensitively on the coherence of the respective Fermi surface sheets.

authors.name: Evgeny A. Stepanov
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: A New Invariant for Doubly Periodic Solutions of the Sinh-Gordon Equation
papers.abstract: Spectral curves of constant mean curvature tori in Euclidean three-space are real hyperelliptic curves carrying two meromorphic differentials with integral periods. These transcendental period conditions are studied through Whitham deformations, which deform the curve while preserving the periods. We extend Whitham deformations to all real hyperelliptic curves of this type, by holding fixed the plane spanned by the periods, or this plane together with its complex structure. Under mild nondegeneracy conditions the resulting isoperiodic sets are manifolds of dimensions three and one, respectively. Along the one-dimensional isoperiodic sets, a generalization of the Willmore energy is a local parameter away from its critical points, to which the spectral curves of tori belong. Finally, using homology bases adapted to the branch points, we find discrete invariants of the isoperiodic sets of doubly periodic curves: a triple of integers and a refined conformal type.

papers.title: Efficient Learning of Mechanism Designs and Compositionality
papers.abstract: Learning mechanism behaviour requires a representation of how connected parts jointly constrain motion. We study whether exposing reusable constraint subassemblies improves prediction from limited data. Assur-KB represents planar mechanisms through irreducible modules, boundary interfaces, and solve dependencies while retaining source geometry. Our theoretical results characterize transfer through module interfaces and establish physical limits arising from missing interface information and accumulated sensitivity. To test the representation claim directly, the experimental design compares matched mechanism-curve pairs across training budgets within the same multilayer-perceptron family. This controlled comparison establishes the utility of the complete representation in the evaluated learning setting. Assur-derived features provide a geometric-mean $1.8\times$ advantage in sample efficiency over flattened adjacency and position inputs across budgets of 50-10,000 mechanisms. Separate experiments establish invariance under tested joint relabelings, higher valid-generation rates under dyadic composition, and a coarser structural index over 10.02 million mechanisms. In summary, the theory and experiments identify how physical constraint structure supports limited-data prediction and which interface conditions govern compositional reuse.

authors.name: Andre Freitas
authors.institution: Agencia Regional para o Desenvolvimento da Investigacao Tecnologia e Inovacao

papers.title: Towards Full-Text Scholarly Argument Mining using Entity-Anchored Claim Extraction
papers.abstract: Argument mining in full-text scholarly articles remains an important yet challenging task. This difficulty stems not only from the need to model long-distance dependencies but also from the substantial effort required to annotate sentence-level argumentative components throughout lengthy documents. To address these challenges, we introduce a novel approach that leverages scientific entity mentions (e.g., tasks, datasets, and models) to identify and structure claims in scholarly literature. We validate our approach through a case study involving 50 full-text research papers on sentiment analysis. We first establish a reliable human gold standard (Krippendorff's $\alpha = 0.80$), identifying 113 claim-bearing sentences and extracting 199 structured claim records from 300 candidate sentences. To address the annotation bottleneck, we employ a majority-voting ensemble of large language models (LLMs) to generate a silver-standard dataset comprising 1,487 claims. Encoders fine-tuned exclusively on the silver-standard dataset outperform those trained on a small human-annotated gold-standard dataset and demonstrate strong zero-shot transfer to NLP papers outside the training corpus.

papers.title: Temporal regularization of petal modes in SCAO systems: The Soft-Limiter approach
papers.abstract: Extremely large telescopes (ELTs) rely on segmented mirrors and thick support structures that fragment the pupil. In single-conjugate AO (SCAO), this produces differential pistons, or petal modes. The Pyramid Wavefront Sensor (PWFS), baseline for ANDES, MICADO, HARMONI, and GMT-NGSAO, has poor sensitivity to these modes in the visible under realistic residual turbulence. We aim to prevent the "Island Effect", where poorly observed differential pistons accumulate and degrade the PSF, without compromising continuous-mode correction. We propose the Minimum Mean Square Error (MMSE) Soft-Limiter, a deterministic, lightweight controller combining a subspace MMSE estimator derived from von K\'arm\'an priors with a continuous temporal regularization. It acts as a leaky integrator applied only to the relative petal degrees of freedom. End-to-end SPECULA simulations of ELT/ANDES show that, while a classical integrator loses lock and wanders across multiple fringes at seeing $\ge 1.0''$, the MMSE Soft-Limiter confines the differential piston within a single fringe over the $0.6-1.2''$ range. It bounds the petal excursion and its science-band impact under severe turbulence, while keeping optimal continuous-mode correction at good seeing, without the Strehl penalty of spatial mitigation such as Edge Actuator Coupling. We derive and verify the operating window for the leakage gain, $g \lesssim g_{\mathrm{eff}}/\pi$: below it, the fast loop retains genuine physical steps up to $\lambda_{WFS}/2$ with a small droop. This maintains a stable modulo-$\lambda_{WFS}$ wavefront on the fast sensor, letting a slower phasing sensor resolve integer ambiguities. As the window narrows with turbulence, its boundaries cross near $1.0''$ seeing; beyond this, retaining physical discontinuities becomes the sole responsibility of the phasing channel, a key design driver for segmented ELTs.

papers.title: Torsion Theories in a non-pointed Context II: iterated torsion theories
papers.abstract: Generalizing a known result in the context of homological categories, we show that, in a regular protomodular category $\mathcal{C}$ equipped with a posetal, monocoreflective subcategory whose coreflector inverts monomorphisms, every torsion theory, in a non-pointed sense, satisfying suitable properties gives rise to a torsion theory in the category $\operatorname{Arr}(\mathcal{C})$ of arrows in $\mathcal{C}$. Moreover, we show that the induced torsion theory in $\operatorname{Arr}(\mathcal{C})$ satisfies the same good properties of the original one in $\mathcal{C}$, allowing to iterate the process. Examples of this situation can be found in protomodular varieties of universal algebras with more than one constant or in duals of elementary toposes.

papers.title: Geometry of $m$-direct-sum morphisms
papers.abstract: Let $V$ be a complex vector space of dimension $mk$ ($m\ge2$). A morphism from a positive-dimensional projective variety $f\colon X\to\mathrm{Gr}(k,V)$ is $m$-direct-sum if $V=U_{x_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus U_{x_m}$ for every $m$ pairwise distinct points $x_1,\dots,x_m$ on $X$, where $U_x\subset V$ is the subspace represented by $f(x)$. We show that $X$ is necessarily a smooth rational curve. When the so-called drill $d(f)$ of $f$ is $1$ or when the rank $k$ is at most $2$, we give complete classifications of $f$ up to the automorphisms of $\mathrm{Gr}(k,V)$. As applications, we classify all so-called skew scrolls in $\mathbb{P}^3$, which completely answers a question of Day. Then we show that if $X\subset \mathbb{P}(V)$ is a smooth, projective, nondegenerate subvariety whose higher-order Terracini locus is empty, then $X$ is the rational normal curve, which strengthens the critical Terracini rigidity discovered by Ballico and Chiantini. By using the same machinery, we also prove a dual version of Terracini rigidity. Finally, we show that $m$-unisolvent systems form an abelian category of finite length and that $7$ is the least diagonal exponent of a simple rank-three $2$-unisolvent system.

papers.title: Class groups of polynomial Krull domains
papers.abstract: A polynomial Krull domain is a Krull domain contained between $\mathbb Z[X]$ and $\mathbb Q[X]$. The domains of this class are precisely the Noetherian integrally closed domains between these polynomial rings by a result of Heinzer, and they have been recently classified by Chang and the second author of this paper as rings of polynomials which are integer-valued over a finite set of ultrametric balls in $\mathbb C_p$, as $p$ ranges through the set of primes in $\mathbb Z$. We show here that every ideal class of a polynomial Krull domain contains a prime ideal. Furthermore, given such a Krull domain $R$, we prove that there exists a polynomial Krull domain $R'$ that is Dedekind, contains $R$ and has the same class group as $R$.

papers.title: A Multi-Layer Navigation System for Smart Wheelchairs with a Limited Input Interface
papers.abstract: Smart wheelchairs are robotic devices that gather information from the surroundings and allow people to safely drive through various environments. They usually rely on the interpretation of high-level user's intentions, typically decoded through human-robot interface (HRI) or brain-machine interface (BMI). However, navigating in an unknown environment and accurately understanding user commands remain significant challenges. Misinterpretation of commands or the environment can lead to user frustration, distrust of the system, or even unsafe situations. In this paper, we present a novel Multi-Layer Navigation System (MLNS) for a smart wheelchair that enables navigation in unknown environments while interpreting and safely contextualizing user's intentions even in the case of limited and faulty commands. The stack relies on a Virtual Sensors-Driven Potential Fields (ViSPF) method for obstacle detection that accounts for the wheelchair's actual size, a Model Predictive Control (MPC) module for trajectory generation, and an open-vocabulary computer vision algorithm for target identification. Finally, a system based on Priority Queue (PQ) was implemented for target selection. We validated our system on a real smart wheelchair with experiments involving 10 participants without disabilities, including scenarios with faulty input interfaces. The results demonstrate the robustness and effectiveness of our system in real-world environments, proving its potential for practical applications in assistive technologies.

papers.title: Mean-convex horizontal mean curvature flow in the Heisenberg group
papers.abstract: We study the arrival time equation of the mean-convex horizontal mean curvature flow in the Heisenberg group. We prove existence of viscosity solutions when the initial set is horizontally mean-convex and either non-characteristic, or axisymmetric and with horizontal mean curvature extending continuously across the characteristic set. A key ingredient is an approximation scheme by sets with prescribed Riemannian mean curvature, which preserves the mean-curvature bounds up to an arbitrarily small error. We further show that, when the evolving level sets form a generalized \(C^2\)-foliation, the horizontal mean curvature blows up around characteristic points. This provides an obstruction to self-similar evolution in the axisymmetric class considered above and, in particular, shows that the Pansu sphere cannot evolve self-similarly.

papers.title: Benchmarking Graph Neural Networks for AC Power Flow: The Role of Inductive Biases and Physical Constraints
papers.abstract:
Fast and accurate models for AC power flow (ACPF) are increasingly important as modern electrical grids require more frequent system analyses. Graph neural networks (GNNs) naturally exploit electrical grid topology, yet the effects of architectural design choices on predictive performance remain poorly understood given differences in graph representations and evaluation settings across studies.
  We present a unified benchmark of representative GNN architectures for ACPF prediction under a common experimental framework. All models use identical preprocessing and training procedures and comparable parameter budgets, isolating the impact of message-passing mechanisms and inductive biases. We also analyze errors by distance from the slack bus and systematically ablate key design components. We evaluate predictive accuracy and physical consistency on the IEEE 14-bus and IEEE 118-bus systems.
  Results indicate that anisotropic message-passing architectures offer the most favorable trade-off between predictive accuracy and physical consistency under the studied parameter and topology constraints. Explicit edge features encoding line impedances and global context aggregation are particularly important for representing electrical interactions and system-wide dependencies, especially for voltage-angle predictions on the topologically bottlenecked IEEE-118 grid. Under a budget with approximately fixed parameters, two or three message-passing layers generally provide the best balance between depth and representation width, while additional depth offers no consistent improvement. Ablations also show that standard residual and root connections are not necessarily beneficial in shallow models, and that aggregation operators involve trade-offs between statistical accuracy and physical consistency. These results provide practical guidelines for designing graph-based power system models.

papers.title: Sensing Fast and Distant Targets in Overspread Channels with Zak-OTFS and Modular Arithmetic
papers.abstract: Delay-Doppler (DD) modulations, such as Zak-transform-based orthogonal time frequency space (Zak-OTFS) modulation, represent the channel as a sparse set of delay and Doppler shifts, which makes them well suited for radar sensing. Sensing with a single DD frame, however, is unambiguous only when the channel spread factor, i.e., the product of the delay and Doppler spreads, is below one. Long-range mobility scenarios, including drones, airplanes, low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites, and underwater acoustic links, typically violate this crystallization condition, so that a single frame aliases the target delays, Doppler shifts, or both. Existing methods add a time-frequency pilot to a conventional DD frame and resolve the aliasing in only one dimension. We propose a frame design that combines multiple DD bases with different delay and Doppler periods, which together cover an overspread channel, on the same bandwidth and frame size. For two frames, we show that modular arithmetic on the wrapped peak positions uniquely recovers each target by pairing the peaks through their common projection and their gains, and we derive the condition under which this pairing is ambiguous. We implement the design with two superimposed Zak-OTFS frames and propose two receivers: dual-frame sensing (DS), which performs the joint detection directly, and DS with cross-pilot cancellation (DS-XC), which additionally cancels the cross-pilot interference, re-estimates the gains by joint least squares, and removes ghost targets. Both receivers keep a detection rate close to one as the spread factor grows, and DS-XC also achieves the lowest false-alarm rate and channel normalized mean squared error (NMSE). In a 100 km drone scenario, DS-XC detects 98% of the targets, compared with 81% for the best baseline, with a complexity that grows near-linearly with the time-bandwidth product for a fixed number of targets.

papers.title: A Dantzig-Wolfe reformulation of the EndoWake model for optimal wind farm layouts
papers.abstract: Wind Farm Layout Optimization places turbines to maximize the expected energy under a wind rose, each turbine lowering the wind downwind. In the EndoWake model the wind field is a variable, propagated by linear inequalities, and layouts are certified by branch-and-check. On a ladder of grids it certifies the $10\times10$ grid and leaves the larger grids open after one hour. We tighten the relaxation by a convexification computed rather than derived: every pattern of turbines inside a small tile of the grid is enumerated once with its power and enters the master as a column. The device is valid because the wind field is antitone, and exact, for the cubic power curve, with a Benders cut at integer layouts. Reduced-cost fixing and propagation between overlapping tiles shrink the master before the tree search, and the tree repeats the fixing at every improving incumbent. The incumbent comes from a tile heuristic or an LP dive. On the same computer as the branch-and-check, the $12\times12$ and $14\times14$ grids close in 48 and 395 seconds. The $16\times16$ grid is certified on five seeds from random starts, one job per seed, the heuristic on a GPU, in 1413 seconds under the uniform rose and 6484 seconds under a non-uniform one. Times are medians. A pre-specified test set of 36 unseen instances with forbidden cells confirms the advantage in the axial setting. Certified means closed at the solver's gap of $10^{-4}$: the optimum lies within it plus a residual of at most 0.00042%.

papers.title: Operator-Aware Posterior Sampling for Multivariate Weather Downscaling
papers.abstract: Statistical downscaling is the task of reconstructing high-resolution meteorological fields from coarse inputs. A principled approach formulates downscaling as a Bayesian inverse problem, using a diffusion prior over high-resolution fields and incorporating the coarse field only at inference through a likelihood. This decouples the prior from the coarse source, allowing one pretrained model to adapt to different sources. However, two challenges limit this flexibility: (1) when coarse and target fields come from different reanalysis systems, no fixed coarsening operator can capture their relationship; and (2) guidance gradients can differ by orders of magnitude across variables, making a single guidance strength ineffective. This paper addresses both challenges within the guidance loop, leaving the prior unchanged. We learn the forward operator from paired data and normalize the gradient per channel. We show that this normalization corresponds to steepest descent under a block-max norm, allowing a single guidance strength across variables. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/CarloSaccardi/operator-aware-weather-downscaling.

papers.title: Annotation-Free Representation Learning for Polyp Retrieval in Colonoscopy Videos
papers.abstract: Colonoscopy is inherently comparative: reliable visual assessment of polyps often depends on complementary views acquired under different viewpoints and imaging conditions. Retrieving such views requires polyp tracklet representations, which recent contrastive methods learn from temporal cues but still build from manually annotated bounding boxes. We propose an annotation-free framework that constructs tracklet views directly from raw colonoscopy videos, enabling temporal self-supervised learning on full-procedure videos, including frames without visible polyps. On REAL-Colon, our method achieves state-of-the-art results on tracklet retrieval and re-identification, outperforming both self-supervised and supervised baselines. We then introduce few-shot polyp retrieval, a task closer to clinical use, where a few observations of a target polyp are used to retrieve its remaining tracklets: with only two examples, our method surpasses most competing methods given ten. Finally, we show that a modest number of unlabeled procedures suffices for competitive performance, making on-site model development more practical. Code is available at https://github.com/lparolari/freerep.

authors.name: Carlo Biffi
authors.institution: Institute of Condensed Matter Chemistry and Technologies for Energy

papers.title: Interacting particles in random irregular media
papers.abstract: In this paper, we first develop novel tools of independent interest in the field of stochastic calculus related to SDEs with distributional drift, namely the formulation of a quasi-Stroock-Varadhan martingale problem in the sense that the test functions are of class $C^{1,2}$ instead of solutions of Kolmogorov type PDE. This has several applications, among which, the time restriction and the notion of conditional rough martingale problem and related solution.

papers.title: Analysis of Multi-Wavelength Data for 30 Galactic Emission-Line Stars with Dusty Envelopes
papers.abstract: We selected 30 stars with V-band brightnesses of 11-16 mag, visual color-indices B-V of approximately 1.3 mag or less, and large near-IR color-indices (J-H and H-K of approximately 0.7 mag or greater) to search for the presence of the B[e] phenomenon. Spectroscopic observations confirmed the presence of emission lines previously detected in 11 stars of the sample and revealed them in 4 other stars for the first time. Spectral energy distributions (SEDs) in the optical and IR spectral regions were analyzed and compared with theoretical SEDs. The fundamental parameters were estimated using the SED fits corrected for the interstellar and circumstellar (CS) extinction and Gaia DR3 distance measurements. Properties of 14 objects previously classified as pre-main-sequence stars were reevaluated. The B[e] phenomenon was found in 16 objects, most of which exhibit observed properties of FS CMa type objects, a still small group of Galactic stars or binary systems with predominantly hot CS dust. Properties of 2 objects (IRAS 06237+0020 and IRAS 19156-0935) are consistent with those of Proto-Planetary Nebulae at early phases of this evolutionary stage. The nature and evolutionary status of 11 sample objects remain uncertain and require further investigation.

papers.title: Cosmological lensing as a jump process
papers.abstract: We develop a jump-process formalism for the probability density function (PDF) of gravitational lensing fields. In the Born approximation, each lens adds a jump to the convergence $\kappa$ and the two components of the shear, making lensing a jump process in redshift. For independent lenses, the joint PDF of the lensing fields obeys a compensated Kolmogorov-Feller equation, which we solve in closed form in Fourier space and extend to clustered lenses using their two-point correlation function. A Fourier-Hankel inversion then yields the joint PDF of $\kappa$ and the shear magnitude $\gamma$, from which the magnification PDF follows, including its high-magnification tail, without sampling noise. We use these PDFs to train an updated version of the FLUMEN emulator, which makes likelihood-based inference from the full magnification distribution feasible across cosmologies. To motivate such analyses, we estimate that samples of $10^4$ Roman supernovae, $10^5$ Rubin supernovae, 300 Einstein Telescope standard sirens, and 12 LISA standard sirens could constrain the matter fluctuation amplitude $\sigma_8$ respectively to 4.8\%, 5.1\%, 8.5\%, and 19\%, with the other cosmological parameters fixed.

authors.name: Galymzhan Baltabay
authors.institution: National Institute of Chemical Physics and Biophysics

papers.title: The Athlete as a Scientist of One: Agentic Bayesian Experimental Design for Individualized Physiology from Consumer Wearables
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents for personal health read wearable data and recommend, but do not learn about the individual in a way that can be audited or falsified. We present EpiCoach, an agentic system that treats one athlete, a cross-country mountain biker, as the subject of accountable N-of-1 science. Claims about the athlete live in an evidence-gated hypothesis registry: each must issue a probabilistic prediction about a future session before it occurs, and its belief moves only through computed evidence from a logged statistical fit. Predictions come from a mechanistic digital twin inferred from heart rate, GPS and barometric altitude: a lagged heart-rate response model, a fitness-fatigue model with learned time constants, and a latent technical-descending skill state, measured on discovered trail segments. The agent prescribes the next training week as a constrained experiment maximizing information gain subject to load and safety constraints, around two instrument rides. We evaluate the system two ways over eighteen months of data. A rolling-origin replay benchmark shows the twin beats standard forecasters on heart rate but not segment time, and the agentic loop matches a static model. A live prospective phase runs the weekly cycle: in its first three weeks the ledger sealed 20 predictions, scored 14, the descent forecast calibrated after one correction, the climb forecast pessimistic as the athlete improved, and the safety officer vetoed the agent twice. Every correction is preserved in the registry, a template for auditable, falsifiable personalization in digital health. We release the registry, benchmark and protocol.

papers.title: What Is the Role for Humans in Creative Writing? Creativity and Diversity in Human-AI Collaboration
papers.abstract: As AI agents increasingly participate in creative teamwork, writing emerges from hybrid human-AI teams. Although AI can improve the creativity of individual outputs, these gains may come at the cost of homogenization. What is the best role for human intervention? We introduce a transmission-chain paradigm inspired by cognitive models of writing, with four stages: Plan, Write, Review, and Revise. Each stage receives the previous output and passes its own forward. Using data from 333 participants across 427 stories, we compared creativity, diversity, and enjoyment across human, AI, and hybrid chains. Consistent with prior work, all-AI chains produced more creative but less diverse stories than all-human chains. Introducing a single human into an otherwise all-AI chain increased diversity depending on role. Human planning provided the best balance: it preserved AI-level creativity, increased diversity that persisted through downstream AI stages, and maintained enjoyment. We discuss implications for designing human-in-the-loop creative pipelines.

authors.name: Chenyi Li
authors.institution: Hunan Institute of Science and Technology

authors.name: Katherine M Collins
authors.institution: Nathan Kline Institute for Psychiatric Research

authors.name: Nori Jacoby
authors.institution: Max Planck Institute for Empirical Aesthetics

papers.title: Fu-TCM: a multimodal large language model that learns traditional Chinese medicine diagnostic reasoning
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are advancing in multimodal understanding and reasoning, accelerating medical model development. Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) uses evidence from the four examinations to determine disease location and nature, differentiate syndromes and guide treatment. This diagnostic process constitutes a complete chain of reasoning. We present Fu-TCM, a multimodal TCM LLM trained on data retained after cleaning and filtering an initial collection of approximately 7.12 million examples derived from classical texts, textbooks, medical images, clinical cases and publicly available datasets. The model was further optimized using Bianzheng-Grounded Policy Optimization (BGPO), which explicitly targets syndrome differentiation through rewards for response format, intermediate TCM reasoning fields and final syndrome predictions. Fu-TCM-27B led all six benchmarks spanning TCM reasoning, text and vision, achieving a macro-average accuracy of 81.01% and surpassing the strongest reference model with complete results across all six benchmarks by 7.13 percentage points. Its largest margin was 11.90 points on Fu-bianzheng. Case-level analyses further showed a positive association between intermediate-field accuracy and final syndrome-selection accuracy in most evaluated models. These findings suggest that TCM syndrome differentiation may be computationally learnable and that structured reasoning supervision can improve performance across TCM tasks.

authors.name: Yaping You
authors.institution: China Academy of Chinese Medical Sciences

papers.title: Modified Scattering for Infinite-Rank Hartree--Fock Equations
papers.abstract: We study the long-time behavior of the Hartree--Fock equation with Coulomb interaction in dimensions $d\geq2$ for small initial density matrices of possibly infinite rank. We prove global well-posedness and modified scattering governed by a resonant Hartree-Fock equation. Our approach is based on the half-density formulation and a final-state construction for the resonant dynamics. We also characterize the stationary states of the resonant Hartree--Fock equation and prove that ordinary linear scattering fails when the initial density matrix has rank at least two. These results extend long-range modified scattering to genuinely operator-valued infinite-rank Hartree-Fock evolution. Despite cancellation between the direct and exchange terms, the long-range effect persists, with resonant dynamics evolving on the same logarithmic time scale as in the Hartree equation.

papers.title: Tight Asymptotic Bounds on the Size of Order Graphs
papers.abstract: Order graphs were introduced by Arroyuelo et al.\ (TODS 2024) as a generalization of the ring index, to support worst-case optimal joins on relations of arity $d$ while storing as few columns as possible: the index stores one column per edge, so its size is proportional to the number of edges of an order graph. It was known that the minimum number of edges lies between $\Omega(2^d\sqrt d)$ and $O(2^d d)$, and the lower bound had been claimed to be $42$ for $d=6$. We first exhibit an order graph with only $40$ edges for $d=6$, and show that the proof of that lower bound holds only for unions of cycles, whereas order graphs can be smaller than the smallest set of cycles. We give a corrected statement and proof that holds for every order graph: there must be at least $\max_m\binom dm\lceil m/2\rceil$ edges. This bound is $40$ for $d=6$, so our $40$-edge graph is optimal. We then settle the asymptotic question: the minimum size is $\Theta(2^d\sqrt d)$. This is obtained via an explicit construction, based on symmetric chain decompositions of the Boolean lattice, with at most $(d-1)\binom{d}{\lfloor d/2\rfloor}+2^d$ edges. The upper bound is within a factor $4+O(d^{-1/2})$ of the lower bound, and both numerically and asymptotically better than trie switching.

papers.title: It\^o versus Stratonovich for shot noise with state-dependent amplitude: why the answer is Marcus
papers.abstract: For Gaussian white noise the It\^o and Stratonovich prescriptions differ by $O(dt)$ per time step, which accumulates into the familiar spurious drift $\tfrac12 D\,II'$. We show that for renewal shot noise with state-dependent gain, $\dot x=-C(x)-I(x)\xi[t]$ with $\xi[t]$ a train of Dirac spikes of finite random amplitude, the two prescriptions differ by a finite amount at every event, and that where $I$ vanishes the difference can become qualitative. The Marcus kick, the jump-process counterpart of the Stratonovich prescription, is the flow map of $dx/ds=I(x)$: no kick can cross a zero $x^\ast$ of $I$, for any jump and waiting-time statistics. The It\^o kick is only the tangent map of that flow. For $I(x)=1+\beta x$ it crosses $x^\ast=-1/\beta$ if and only if $\xi\beta>1$ and collapses the whole line onto $x^\ast$ at $\xi\beta=1$; below threshold it is itself a Marcus kick with a remapped jump law. Bounded jump laws thus have a threshold, while unbounded ones leak across the barrier for \emph{any} parameters. The discrepancy cannot be absorbed into a renormalised drift beyond lowest order, and only the Marcus kick is generated by a single operator, which makes the master equation of Bianucci, Bologna and Mannella (2026) intrinsically Marcus. Numerically, the standard Heun kick is a second-order truncation of the Marcus map that preserves the barrier only because its order is even; it shortens every jump, biasing second moments in proportion to the squared jump amplitude and the jump kurtosis, and depleting the region near the barrier. We give the exact-flow integrator that replaces it.

authors.name: Marco Bianucci
authors.institution: Istituto di Scienze Marine del Consiglio Nazionale delle Ricerche

papers.title: Non-Zero Radius: The Missing Component of Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Inspired by the analogy between the all-or-none activation of biological neurons and the true-false of logic circuits, McCulloch and Pitts proposed a mathematical model of the biological neuron in 1943 with the aim of simulating logical reasoning. Although Norbert Wiener considered the model overly simplistic at the time, it later became a building block of modern neural networks, including large language models. Despite their remarkable empirical success, however, conventional neural networks remain largely black-box systems and struggle with reliable symbolic reasoning. Viewing vectors as spheres of zero radius, we relax the zero-radius constraint and represent concepts as spheres with non-zero radii. We argue that sphere-based representations can capture additional features of biological cognition, including representing spatial concepts as regions and reasoning through model construction and inspection. Building on sphere embeddings, we introduce Sphere Neural Networks (SphNNs), which use a transition map to achieve symbolic-level Aristotelian syllogistic reasoning without training data, thereby taking an initial step toward the original goal of McCulloch and Pitts. We suggest that the zero-radius constraint may reflect an aspect of the oversimplification identified by Wiener and may limit conventional neural networks' capacity for symbolic-level logical reasoning.

papers.title: Regularity theory for non-local almost minimal surfaces via Euler-Lagrange inequalities at small scales
papers.abstract:
We extend the notion of non-local almost minimal sets introduced in [Dipierro, Valdinoci, and Villa, J. Math. Pures Appl. (2026)] by admitting lower-order powers for the remainder term.
  We combine classical techniques and a new, weaker version of the Euler-Lagrange inequalities (at a microscopic scale) to obtain $\mathcal{C}^{1,\alpha}$-regularity for non-local almost minimal sets, up to Hausdorff dimension $n-3$.
  In turn, this formulation is well-suited for the non-local counterpart of the so-called Massari's problem for sets with prescribed mean curvature. In particular, such a generalization allows us to consider sets with $L^p$ non-local mean curvature (with $p\geq n/s$), which do not satisfy any curvature equation (neither in the classical nor in the viscosity sense).
  The results presented here lie beyond the reach of previously established methodologies. Indeed, the approach developed herein is based on a conceptual shift relative to the existing literature, which relied on a strong form of the Euler-Lagrange equation that is not available for general non-local almost minimal sets.

authors.name: Riccardo Villa
authors.institution: Istituto Zooprofilattico Sperimentale della Lombardia e dell'Emilia Romagna "Bruno Ubertini"

papers.title: NeurEO: dissecting Earth observation embeddings with computational neuroscience
papers.abstract: Earth embeddings are compressed representations of rich Earth observation data that enable downstream models to tackle a wide range of complex geospatial tasks. Yet, this increase in performance comes at the cost of decreased interpretability, as the semantic meaning of Earth embeddings is unknown. To address this challenge, we borrow methods from the field of computational neuroscience, which aim to interpret activity in (biological) neurons. Here, we adapt and apply these methods to assign meaning to AlphaEarth embeddings. We analyse embedding features both as stand-alone data, equivalent to spontaneous neural activity, and in relation to land cover and elevation correlates, equivalent to stimulus-response neural activity. We demonstrate correlational and multi-scale structure in the embedding features. Embedding features can display highly specific and directional tuning to land cover and elevation, such as a `North vs South woodland edge' response. When we remove the main trends of combined land cover responses (like water versus land tuning), we discover fine-grained representational details with increased effective dimensionality. Together, our analyses start to unravel what these Earth embeddings represent, which is critical for developing trustworthy downstream applications.

authors.name: Ioannis N Athanasiadis
authors.institution: Dalle Molle Institute for Artificial Intelligence Research

papers.title: MemSteer: Turning User Histories into Supervision for Agent Memory Optimization
papers.abstract: An effective agent memory system should adapt to a user's history and task requirements. Human-annotated supervision can guide this adaptation by providing feedback for evaluating and improving memory designs. Yet suitable labels are rarely available for new user histories, and manually constructing QA pairs and supporting evidence is costly. We introduce MemSteer, which turns unlabeled user histories into question-answer (QA) supervision with supporting evidence for memory-design optimization. MemSteer constructs an evidence-grounded answer plan that specifies how facts across related records jointly support a reference answer. The plan guides question generation, while source-grounded auditing and blind answer recovery check the resulting annotations. To study the utility of this supervision, we develop MemSteer-Opt, which combines QA-based design evaluation with evidence-guided failure diagnosis to revise memory store, retrieval, and context construction without updating model parameters. Experiments on ATM-Bench and RHELM show that this supervision is competitive with official-QA-guided optimization. Relative to Base-BM25, MemSteer-Opt improves ATM-Bench Question Score by 13.4 points and RHELM accuracy by 4.1 and 6.6 points without and with external data, respectively. The supervision also benefits two existing optimizers on ATM-Bench, while new-user experiments demonstrate continued design optimization using supervision generated from the target histories.

papers.title: Recurrent Bipartite Graph Neural Networks for QC-MDPC Error Decoding in McEliece Cryptosystems
papers.abstract: As the advent of large-scale quantum computing threatens classical encryption, Quasi-Cyclic Moderate Density Parity-Check (QC-MDPC) codes have emerged as a foundational element of Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC). However, decoding these relatively dense codes using classical Belief Propagation algorithms often leads to failures caused by short graph cycles that stall the decoder. In cryptographic applications, these failures are severe security vulnerabilities that leak secret key information. To address this, this paper proposes a Recurrent Bipartite Graph Neural Network (R-BGNN) as proof of concept. By integrating Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) into the message-passing framework and employing a multi-topology curriculum training strategy, the R-BGNN actively learns to break limit-cycle oscillations. Evaluated across 20 unseen matrix topologies, the proposed architecture significantly outperforms classical Bit-Flipping and Min-Sum baselines, reducing the Decoding Failure Rate (DFR) by 63.7\% at moderate noise levels ($t=10$) while converging in fewer iterations.

papers.title: The Utility of Physics-Informed Machine Learning in Solar Power Production Forecasting
papers.abstract: Physics-informed machine learning (PIML) and hybrid modeling have attracted significant attention as approaches for combining physical knowledge with the flexibility of deep learning. In this work, we investigate whether these approaches deliver their commonly claimed benefits for large-scale photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting. We develop two hybrid forecasting architectures that integrate the ADR physical PV efficiency model with the TSMixer neural forecasting architecture through feature augmentation and residual learning. The proposed models are evaluated on a dataset comprising over 3 million samples from 3,713 PV installations across 33 European countries. We assess convergence speed, forecasting accuracy, transferability across geographical regions, and data efficiency. Although the physics-informed models seem to exhibit slightly faster convergence during training, they do not achieve consistent improvements in test-set accuracy, generalization, or performance under limited training data compared to the purely data-driven baseline. These findings suggest that, for modern deep forecasting architectures trained on large datasets, explicitly incorporating the ADR physical model provides limited practical benefit for day-ahead PV forecasting.

papers.title: A physics-informed uncertainty-aware surrogate for $p$-$n$ junction diodes
papers.abstract: We develop an uncertainty-aware physics-informed surrogate for a one-dimensional $p$-$n$ junction diode, conditioned on device length, doping and bias. Using the internal state of the device as predicted by the surrogate we develop a test-suite of quantities of interest including the terminal current, depletion width, peak field and stored charge. The formalism and the quantities are can be extended to asymmetric junction and two-dimensional diodes as shown by means of benchmark analysis. For the one-dimensional symmetric junction surrogate, we obtain 0.11% median $L_1$ error on the electrostatic potential, and 1.5% and 0.61% on the electron and hole densities. Finally, we develop an uncertainty analysis which determines the validity of surrogate answer within the user-specified tolerance.

papers.title: NEOPIC: A Neural Operator Framework for Particle-based Kinetic Plasma Simulations
papers.abstract: We introduce NEOPIC, a framework for learning the field operator in particle-based methods applied to kinetic plasma simulations. Its key novelty is a neural operator that acts directly on the empirical measure of the particles, rather than on a grid, and is evaluated at the particle positions. No mesh or tree is needed and, unlike grid-based neural operators, no deposition onto a mesh takes place, so the particle noise that dominates the inputs of particle simulations is not aliased. Since it replaces only the field solve, it serves as a plug-and-play field solver for particle-based methods: it can be trained on data from particle-in-cell, particle-in-Fourier or tree codes, and combined with any time integrator, including implicit schemes. We prove that the discrete evaluation coincides with the continuous operator at any number of particles (representation equivalence) and derive an error analysis that separates sampling, learning and time-stepping errors: up to the learning error, NEOPIC has the error structure of standard Monte Carlo particle methods. We show that the particle noise in the training data acts as an implicit regularizer, which gives guidance on the number of training particles in relation to the particle numbers used at inference. A complexity analysis shows that NEOPIC is an $O(N_p)$ method whose constants are set by the architecture alone, independently of any mesh or tree. Numerical experiments on electrostatic benchmarks in two and three dimensions, including Landau damping, two-stream and bump-on-tail instabilities, a cyclotron mini-app and a Penning trap, confirm the theoretical findings. A single model trained on several mini-apps generated by different reference methods captures all of them and remains stable up to twice the training time window, which points towards foundation models for fields in particle-based methods.

papers.title: Extraordinary stiffening and reciprocal control in a DNA condensate/actin composite
papers.abstract: Soft composites, materials consisting of inclusions within a polymeric matrix, offer a broad design space with diverse mechanical properties. Composite stiffness is normally set by the volume fraction of filler, and classical theory predicts at most ~25% stiffening when inclusions occupy 10% of the volume. Here we introduce a composite of phase-separated DNA droplets that occupy <10% of an entangled actin network, yet stiffen it 25-fold, reversibly. Microscopy reveals that actin penetrates the DNA droplets, leading network elasticity to determine their size; thus the system exhibits reciprocal control between matrix and droplet properties. We attribute the extraordinary stiffening to entrainment of actin by the droplets, which enlarges the effective inclusions until their contact network dominates the mechanics. This shows that liquid-liquid phase separation can control not only local compositions, but also mechanics, achieving exceptional stiffening at modest filler fractions through local geometries that constrain the matrix beyond the inclusions themselves.

papers.title: Sign reversal of ST-FMR signals in CoFeB/Pt explained by contributions beyond spin-orbit torque
papers.abstract: Spin-orbit torques (SOT) provide an efficient route for electrical control of magnetization and is of central interest for low-power magnetic memory applications. Spin-torque ferromagnetic resonance (ST-FMR) is a widely used technique to quantify SOT efficiencies. However, the rectified voltage measured in ST-FMR can contain contributions that are not directly related to SOTs, which affects the accuracy of the extracted torque efficiencies. This may contribute to the large variation of reported SOT efficiencies in literature. In this study, we investigate the damping-like torque efficiencies in CoFeB/Pt heterostructures as a function of Pt thickness. Conventional ST-FMR analysis yields an apparent sign reversal of the extracted efficiency at a Pt thickness of approximately 10 nm. By combining complementary measurement geometries and analysis approaches, we separate the torque-induced signal from additional voltage contributions that share the same angular dependence. Our results show that non-torque voltage contributions can produce an apparent sign reversal in conventional ST-FMR analysis, highlighting the need to distinguish SOT-induced signals from parasitic contributions and we show how to reliably determine the SOT efficiencies.

papers.title: The $6\frac{1}{2}$-functor formalism of Cartier modules
papers.abstract:
Let $p$ be a prime. We construct a coherent formalism of geometric operations on Cartier modules with coefficients in ind-coherent sheaves on noetherian derived $\mathbb F_p$-schemes. For such a scheme $X$, we consider the stable presentable category $\mathrm{Cart}(X)$ of ind-coherent sheaves $M$ equipped with a structural morphism $F_{*,X}M \to M$, where $F_X$ denotes the Frobenius endomorphism.
  We construct pushforward functors for arbitrary morphisms and exceptional pullback functors for separated morphisms almost of finite type, together with coherent composition and base-change equivalences. We single out conditions under which these functors admit further adjoints.
  On derived schemes separated and almost of finite type over $\mathbb F_p$, we construct compatible closed symmetric monoidal structures given by shriek tensor products, and establish which functors are symmetric monoidal.
  The constructions arise from a general procedure for forming functor formalisms of Cartier objects, using their description as lax limits and the universal properties of span $2$-categories developed by Cnossen--Lenz--Linskens [arXiv:2505.19192].

papers.title: Ambisonics: Introducing an Accessible, Distributed Approach
papers.abstract: This paper presents an accessible, distributed approach to higher order ambisonics using a network of low-cost microcontroller-based devices. Leveraging recent advances in embedded computing, networked audio, and precise time synchronization, the system offers an alternative to conventional centralized architectures that typically require expensive multichannel interfaces and high-performance digital signal processing hardware. The proposed architecture combines an audio plugin for soundfield design with a modular network of ambisonics processing units, which, exploiting the parallelisable nature of ambisonics decoding, are each responsible for a subset of loudspeaker outputs. Synchronization is achieved through the IEEE 1588 Precision Time Protocol, complemented by adaptive clock correction to maintain sub-microsecond alignment between devices. A third-order ambisonics implementation demonstrates the viability of the approach, with potential scalability to higher orders and larger arrays. Overall, this work contributes to the development of frugal, distributed solutions for immersive audio, expanding access to ambisonics-based systems for a wide range of applications.

papers.title: Nijenhuis Lie $n$-algebras
papers.abstract:
We introduce a homotopical framework for Nijenhuis operators on semistrict Lie $n$-algebras ($n$-term $L_\infty$-algebras) for every $n \ge 1$ and, more generally, on arbitrary $L_\infty$-algebras. A Nijenhuis operator is defined as a family $N = (N_q)_{q \ge 1}$ of multilinear maps, with $N_1$ linear, realizing an $L_\infty$-morphism from an $N$-twisted copy of the structure to the original one. We prove that this condition is equivalent to the vanishing, at every arity $m$, of the $m$-th Nijenhuis torsion up to a correction term $\Lambda^N_m$ formed by higher-component substitutions, and we provide a closed combinatorial formula for $\Lambda^N_m$ as a sum over set partitions. Along the way, we show that the arity-$k$ Nijenhuis torsion factors canonically as a composite of $k$ commuting elementary slot deformations.
  The resulting objects form a category $\mathbf{NijLie}_n$; we establish that $\mathbf{NijLie}_m$ embeds as the full subcategory of $\mathbf{NijLie}_n$ on objects concentrated in the bottom
  $m$ degrees for all $m \le n$. These levels assemble into a tower whose first three stages are classical Nijenhuis Lie algebras, the Nijenhuis Lie $2$-algebras of Das, and the newly introduced Nijenhuis Lie $3$-algebras. We characterize the strict and skeletal objects at every level, introduce $n$-term representations up to homotopy of a Nijenhuis Lie algebra,
  and prove that the semidirect product construction establishes an equivalence between the category of such representations and split abelian $\mathbf{NijLie}_n$-extensions.
  Finally, two corrections to published level-three identities are documented, and all component identities up to arity five are verified via computer algebra.

papers.title: Tensor products of Leibniz bimodules and Grothendieck rings -- an addendum
papers.abstract: We continue our investigation of certain associativity properties (namely, alternativity, power-associativity, or being a Jordan ring) of the non-associative multiplication defined on the Grothendieck group of the category of finite-dimensional Leibniz bimodules which we started in \cite{FW}. Namely, we prove that for every finite-dimensional non-zero Leibniz algebra over an arbitrary field this Grothendieck ring is not power-associative. As a consequence, the Grothendieck ring is also neither alternative nor a Jordan ring. This corrects and generalizes some of our results in the last section of \cite{FW}.

papers.title: A New AFIB Detection Method with Deep Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Early detection of atrial fibrillation (AFIB), characterized by irregular heart rhythms, can potentially save thousands of lives annually [20]. Numerous studies have attempted to address this challenge using various algorithms and methodologies. This paper introduces a novel and robust method that enhances the precision of AFIB detection. Neural Networks (NN) are widely recognized for their ability to identify complex electrocardiogram (ECG) patterns, facilitating the accurate detection of irregular heart rhythms. This study explores multiple conventional machine learning algorithms alongside neural network approaches to develop a robust AFIB detection system. To evaluate the effective- ness and robustness of the proposed method, the MIT BIH arrhythmia database (MITDB) and the Long-term Atrial Fibrillation Database (LTAFDB), both available on the Physionet site. Our approach presents a novel feature engineering technique, employing specific features such as a time series of the differences in successive heart rates (dBPM) rather than traditional inter-beat intervals. The model analyzes inputs labeled into five distinct classes, using only clean intervals identified through a new labeling method for training while treating others as outliers. This strategy ensures a more accurate and reliable AFIB detection process. The best-performing model, a Deep Neural Network (DNN), achieved an F1 score of 95.18% for binary atrial fibrillation classification on a benchmark dataset distinct from the training set. Models trained using our approach have demonstrated superior performance than previously published models.

papers.title: Four-Coloring Planar Graphs in Linear Time
papers.abstract:
The famous Four Color Theorem (4CT) states that any planar graph can be colored with four colors, but how do we find a 4-coloring? In our previous paper [FOCS'26], we presented a simple combinatorial algorithm to 4-color planar graphs in $O(n\log n)$ time. We improve it here to $O(n)$ time, which is optimal. The algorithm from our previous paper is based on proving that every planar triangulation has a linear number of reducible configurations or obstructing cycles. The bottleneck for the algorithm is that we need $O(\log n)$ Kempe changes to extend a recursive 4-coloring to the reducible configurations. Each Kempe change can involve a constant fraction of the graph and takes linear time.
  Here we show that all $O(\log n)$ Kempe changes can be identified and implemented in $O(n)$ time. The idea is to spend $O(n)$ time to preprocess the graph so that we can identify and simulate each good Kempe change in $O(n/\log n)$ amortized time. Thus, we implement all $O(\log n)$ Kempe changes in $O(n)$ total time. Based on this, we implement the whole 4-coloring in linear time.
  We note that creating such a representation for fast identification and simulation of the right Kempe changes is a challenge of data structures, unlike the previous paper that builds on a new graph theoretic understanding of reducible configurations.

papers.title: On the maximum interval index of a graph
papers.abstract: For a connected graph P G on n vertices, the interval index is defined by Int(G) = {u,v} subset V(G) (|I(u, v)| - 1), where I(u, v) denotes the set of all vertices lying on a shortest u - v path. It was conjectured that, among all connected graphs on n vertices, the path Pn attains the maximum value of the interval index. In this paper we settle this conjecture, and we prove that the maximum is attained only for Pn, except for n = 4, when the cycle C4 attains the same value. We also prove that, for every n >= 31, the maximum interval index among graphs without pendant vertices equals (n^3 - n)/6 - 2(n - 4) and it is attained by a dumbbell graph, obtained by joining two 4-cycles by a path.

authors.name: Martin Knor
authors.institution: Slovak University of Technology in Bratislava

papers.title: Enhancing Atrial Fibrillation Detection Through Hyperparameter Optimization
papers.abstract: This study explores the role of hyperparameter optimization (HPO) in enhancing the detection of Atrial Fibrillation (AF) using both machine learning and deep learning models. We evaluated a range of standard classifiers - Decision Tree, Random Forest, and XGBoost classifiers, alongside deep learning architectures including Recurrent Neural Networks, Deep Neural Networks, and Siamese Neural Networks. To fine-tune these models, we applied four HPO methods: Genetic Algorithm, Hyperband, Optuna, and SMAC3. The experiments were conducted using inter-patient and intra- patient data splits to assess model generalization and robustness in the presence of class imbalance, which is reflective of real-world AF occurrence. Our results, based on PhysioNet electrocardiogram datasets, showed that the Hyperband-optimized XGBoost model outperformed all others, achieving a peak F1 score of 96.95%. These findings highlight the critical role of suitable HPO strategies in enhancing the accuracy and robustness of AF classification outcomes in clinical settings.

papers.title: Tuning La0.7Sr0.3MnO3 magnetic anisotropy via interfacial coupling in homometallic trilayers
papers.abstract: In this work we explore the complex magnetic behaviour of SrMnO3/La0.7Sr0.3MnO3/SrMnO3 trilayers combining magneto-optic Kerr effect (MOKE) and magneto-resistance measurements. The interplay of structural and orbital reconstruction and the competition of ferromagnetism/antiferromagnetism at the interfaces is responsible of a variety of complex magnetic properties, highlighting the use of heterostructures as an effective strategy to tune and control magnetic behaviour. We demonstrate the possibility to tune the magnetic properties of a ferromagnetic La0.7Sr0.3MnO3 (LSMO) layer, embedded in two homometallic antiferromagnetic layers (SrMnO3, SMO), by properly varying the role of interfaces using two different LSMO thickness values. Spin reorientation of the LSMO magnetic easy axis away from its room temperature orientation was observed below 125 K, due to the predominance of exchange interaction at the interface over the substrate-induced magnetic anisotropy, in agreement with established models for homometallic manganite heterostructures. The competition of super-exchange and exchange interactions at the interface results in a highly frustrated interfacial spin glass state, resulting in 20-fold enhancement of the coercive field and exchange bias. The modification of the magnetocrystalline anisotropy driven by the interfacial effects leads to a change in the anisotropic magneto-resistance response of the system, which dominates the low temperature behaviour.

papers.title: Time evolution in the multi-component dynamical Keldysh models
papers.abstract: We construct a time evolution operator for a dynamical quantum models with a multi-component random Gaussian field characterized by a long correlation time. We analyze three paradigmatic cases: non-Abelian $SU(2)$ symmetry class for the three-component Gaussian noise and Abelian symmetry classes $U(1)$ and $Z_2$ for the two- and one-component noises correspondingly. Starting with a limiting case of the infinite correlation time (Keldysh model) we shown that statistics of the two-component random field with a non-zero mean is described by the Rice distribution. We derived and solved the system of coupled linear differential equations for the exact diagonal and off-diagonal single-particle Green's functions. We showed how the finite time correlation in Keldysh models are accounted by a continuous fractions method.

authors.name: M. N. Kiselev
authors.institution: The Abdus Salam International Centre for Theoretical Physics (ICTP)

papers.title: Uniform estimates for complex Monge-Amp\`ere equations II: Hermitian manifolds
papers.abstract: We establish uniform estimates for degenerate complex Monge--Amp\`ere equations on compact Hermitian manifolds under weak Orlicz integrability assumptions on the densities. Our estimates apply uniformly to Hermitian metrics and to semipositive uniformly non-collapsing reference forms. For arbitrary big reference forms, we obtain uniform relative $L^\infty$-estimates with respect to the extremal function with minimal singularities, and establish continuity of the resulting solutions on the regular locus. As an application, we prove the existence of solutions with minimal singularities to degenerate complex Monge--Amp\`ere equations associated with big forms. The proofs combine local Orlicz estimates with pluripotential-theoretic envelope techniques and uniform control of the Monge--Amp\`ere masses, overcoming the lack of invariance of the total Monge--Amp\`ere mass in the Hermitian setting.

papers.title: Excitons in solid molecular hydrogen from quantum Monte Carlo
papers.abstract: We use quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) methods to investigate the lowest neutral excitation of solid molecular hydrogen in phase-I under increasing compression, with emphasis on structural and response properties. We employ QMC wave functions for the excited state that feature only a single orbital substitution, or a multideterminant expansion including every single particle-hole transition, and compare the results with the Bethe-Salpeter equation (BSE) and time-dependent density-functional theory (TDDFT). We examine a number of nuclear configurations representing thermal and quantum fluctuations. The effect of the multideterminant expansion is marginal on the QMC excitation energies but crucial on the exciton localization and related quantities, irrespective of full optimization and imaginary time projection. In the strong insulating regime at low density, multideterminant QMC results match and in some cases surpass the degree of localization afforded by BSE. A similar trend is observed for transition dipole moments and excitation-induced forces, with generally good agreement between QMC and BSE but marked discrepancies for nuclear configurations where localization differs significantly. TDDFT generally gives a more extended exciton with correspondingly weaker transition dipole moments. These differences decrease upon compression, as the system approaches a semiconducting regime where multiple particle-hole transitions are less important.

authors.name: Saverio Moroni
authors.institution: Scuola Internazionale Superiore di Studi Avanzati

papers.title: Machine learning-guided real-time AC optimal transmission switching
papers.abstract: The operation of power grids has substantial economic consequences, affecting generation costs and, ultimately, electricity prices. The Optimal Transmission Switching (OTS) problem seeks to reduce these costs by selectively switching off transmission lines. However, OTS gives rise to a challenging mixed-integer nonlinear optimization problem that is difficult to solve at operationally relevant timescales, particularly as rapidly changing loads create a need for real-time switching decisions. To address this challenge, we develop a machine learning-guided method that identifies high quality line switching decisions in real time. Specifically, we construct a grid-specific switching-value model that rapidly estimates the generation-cost reduction associated with opening transmission lines by fine-tuning a pretrained model for AC optimal power flow (AC-OPF). The switching-value model provides signals to guide promising switching decisions, and topologies proposed by the model are evaluated using exact AC-OPF solvers to verify feasibility and obtain the actual generation cost. We develop multiple strategies that use the ML surrogate to efficiently explore the combinatorial space of transmission topologies, including Fixed-Rank Search, Adaptive-Rank Search, and Swap-Enhanced Search. Across multiple benchmark networks, our proposed algorithms identify line switching decisions that significantly reduce generation cost within a 50s computational budget. In particular, under a realistic data center buildout scenario on the 2,000-bus synthetic Texas grid, our approach reduces generation costs by 31.97% and gross nodal load payments by 94.34%. More broadly, our results demonstrate that a fine-tuned surrogate can effectively guide search even without guaranteeing feasibility, enabling classical optimization methods to tackle large nonlinear combinatorial problems on operationally relevant timescales.

papers.title: A 3D measurement workflow for assessing replication quality and tool degradation in moulded microfluidic channels
papers.abstract: Mould-based replication, such as injection moulding with 3D-printed inserts, needs a check of how faithfully microchannels are transferred from master to polymer replica. It is usually limited to a width or depth ratio from one cross-section, which misses the sidewall shape and depends on where the section is taken. We present a workflow that assesses the whole channel from 3D scans of master and replica, without sectioning. The scans are registered on a common grid, and each height map is converted into a map of local slope. The correlation of the two slope maps over the channel interior, RQ$_d$, is reported with the channel dimensions and height- and slope-error maps. These outputs separate a change of shape from a change of size and locate it. A user can thereby compare mould materials, detect tool wear, and tell whether a deviation arose before or during moulding. On synthetic channels with known degradation, RQ$_d$ fell steadily as the sidewalls were rounded, whereas the height correlation levelled off. For injection moulding with stereolithography-printed inserts in three resins, RQ$_d$ ranged from 0.17 to 0.91 over fifteen insert-to-part pairs. The height correlation placed the ten well-formed channels within 0.03. Over a twenty-shot run, one insert's RQ$_d$ fell from 0.90 to 0.72 as its sidewalls wore, while its height correlation stayed above 0.93. We developed open-source software that implements the workflow. Because the workflow needs only registered 3D scans of a master and its replica, it can in principle be applied to other mould-based processes.

authors.name: Jerome Charmet
authors.institution: HES-SO University of Applied Sciences and Arts Western Switzerland

papers.title: Unlimited OCR Works 2
papers.abstract: Unlimited OCR ushers the era of long-horizon parsing, substantially mitigating the growth of working memory as document lengthens. However, as document length scales to hundreds of pages, the visual context grows substantially, sharply increasing the computational cost of each decoding step and limiting the scalability of ultra-long document parsing. Inspired by human book transcription via localized focus without re-scanning preceding pages, we introduce Unlimited OCR 2, a document parsing model that looks only at what it transcribes. Building on Unlimited OCR, we upgrade all the decoder attention modules to Sparse Reference Sliding Window Attention (SR-SWA), bounding active reference tokens to a fixed capacity and thus sustaining constant computational costs across arbitrarily long documents. By combining SR-SWA with Unlimited-Horizon Decoding Paradigm, Unlimited OCR 2 enables document parsing over virtually unlimited lengths without prohibitive memory overhead. At the hundred-page scale, Unlimited OCR 2 achieves 7.0$\times$ and 5.6$\times$ per-step speedups over Full Attention and R-SWA, respectively. Furthermore, it delivers state-of-the-art end-to-end performance on both MPDocBench and MarathonDocBench, our newly proposed benchmark targeting hundred-page document parsing. Ultimately, the capacity for uninterrupted, one-shot document parsing signifies a fundamental paradigm shift into the OCR 3.0 era.
