papers.title: Matrix orthogonal polynomials related to diffference operators for $L$-orthogonal polynomials
papers.abstract: The difference operator $J$ arising from the higher order occurrence for the $L$-orthogonal polynomials is studied using various families of matrix orthogonal polynomials. The matrix orthogonal polynomials determine the polar decomposition of $J$ and its adjoint $J^\ast$ considered as operators on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N})$. The special case of symmetric $J$ leads to the case where the matrix polynomials reduce to diagonal matrix polynomials. The example of the symmetric case with constant coefficients for $L=2$ is discussed in detail.

papers.title: Control of Seizure Dynamics in a Bistable System with Pulsatile Inputs
papers.abstract: Bistable neural population models describe transitions associated with epilepsy through the coexistence of a stable equilibrium representing normal neural activity and a stable limit cycle representing seizure-like oscillations. Perturbations that drive the system outside the equilibrium's basin of attraction can trigger transitions to seizure-like activity. Enlarging this basin enables the system to recover normal activity from a larger set of perturbed states, providing a model-based mechanism for reducing frequency of seizure initiation. Motivated by electrical brain stimulation, this paper investigates basin enlargement using pulsatile feedback control. Combining higher-order averaging with periodic near-identity transformations, we establish conditions under which nonzero-mean and zero-mean pulsatile feedback gains enlarge the basin of attraction and derive guidelines for pulse design. Numerical simulations validate the theoretical enlargement.

authors.name: Xianlong Zhao
authors.institution: Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs

papers.title: A fully convolutional neural network to classify UXOs using multicomponent electromagnetic induction data
papers.abstract: Unexploded ordnance (UXO) clearance relies on electromagnetic induction (EMI) methods to detect and classify buried and submerged metallic objects, but the standard classification workflow requires physics-based inversion and manual expert review. We present a fully convolutional neural network (CNN) that classifies UXO directly from multicomponent time-domain EMI data, bypassing the inversion step entirely. The CNN uses a segmentation-like architecture that preserves the spatial dimensions of the input and outputs a high-resolution classification map suitable for generating a diglist. Two CNNs are used in sequence: the first detects anomalies due to metallic objects and characterizes the spatially correlated noise present in the preprocessed field data; the second performs multi-class classification using synthetic training data augmented with that noise. A physics-based parameterization of the clutter class is used to train the network to discriminate clutter from UXO across a broad range of object types. We validate this approach on two field datasets acquired with the UltraTEMA-4 system at the Sequim Bay marine test site. On a calibration grid with 21 seeded objects, the CNN detects all UXOs and discriminates two out of four clutter objects. On an independent blind grid with 35 seeded objects (17 UXOs, 18 clutter), the CNN detects and classifies all UXOs and achieves a false-positive count comparable to that of the physics-based inversion approach. We see the two methods as complementary: once trained, the CNN classifies rapidly and with minimal supervision, making it well suited as a fast first-pass tool or as an independent check on physics-based results.

authors.name: Lin-Ping Song
authors.institution: First Affiliated Hospital of Chinese PLA General Hospital

papers.title: Skeleton Coding: Program Structure as a Specification for Agents
papers.abstract: Coding agents are typically provided end-to-end behavioral specifications that the code they produce should satisfy, such as tests and input--output examples. How many such specifications must a developer provide, and which ones, for the agent to produce the developer's intended program? We argue that this cannot be determined a priori, for it depends on the structure of the implementation, which is left to the agent to decide. An agent first commits to a structure---a decomposition into data types, modules, and functions---which fixes a class of candidate programs; behavioral specifications then select a program within that class. A set of tests that suffices for one structure may leave another badly underdetermined, requiring different edge cases or exponentially more examples. Since the structure is chosen by the agent, developers cannot ensure their specification is complete without reverse-engineering it from thousands of lines of generated code. To resolve this, we introduce Skeleton Coding, in which developers jointly specify the structure---in high-level, code-like format---alongside behavioral specifications. Theoretically, we model AI-assisted coding as a control problem, and show that skeletons can reduce exponentially the number of tests developers must supply to steer an agent toward an acceptable program. Empirically, across four models and three benchmarks, the best-performing skeleton specifications reduce mean test error by 48.4% relative to the best end-to-end behavioral specifications. Even when the agent can query a complete reference implementation, adding a skeleton reduces mean test error relatively by up to 27.0%. Skeletons also narrow the average gap between small and large models by about 52.4% while lowering implementation cost by 15--26x, and reduce code erosion by 24.7% on average.

papers.title: Drift-induced nonreciprocity in image-polariton-mediated dipole emission
papers.abstract: Electrical current bias offers a magnet-free route to nonreciprocal light propagation at the nanoscale. Here, we theoretically explore drift-induced nonreciprocity in graphene heterostructures containing hexagonal boron nitride (hBN), where graphene plasmons interact with hBN phonon polaritons in the infrared. Both the random-phase approximation and the Boltzmann transport equation are used to characterize the nonlocal optical response of drift-biased graphene. We compare graphene on hBN with an image-polaritonic structure comprising graphene, a thin hBN spacer, and a gold substrate. Carrier drift produces pronounced directional shifts of the polariton dispersion, while coupling to hBN phonon polaritons strongly modifies the nonreciprocal response. In the image-polaritonic structure, the graphene polaritons become up to twice as confined while retaining a comparable Fizeau shift. The nonreciprocal polariton dispersion produces directional near-field emission and nonreciprocal dipole-dipole interactions, the latter quantified through the cross density of optical states, reaching a left-right dissymmetry of up to ~40%. Our results identify image polaritons in drift-biased graphene as a compact, electrically tunable platform for directional coupling between quantum emitters at the nanoscale.

papers.title: Approximating the poles of a Painlev\'e V transcendent for the Fredholm determinant of the sine kernel
papers.abstract: The Fredholm determinant of the sine kernel has an expression as an integral containing a Painlev\'e transcendent $r$ satisfying Painlev\'e V, in the same way that the Fredholm determinant of the Airy kernel has an expression involving the Hastings-McLeod solution of Painlev\'e II. In this paper we use Pad\'e approximation to approximate the poles of this Painlev\'e transcendent $r$ in the complex plane. We use Pad\'e approximation near $0$, Hermite-Pad\'e approximation near $0$ and two-point Pad\'e approximation near $0$ and infinity.

papers.title: Neuromorphic design of a rhythmic network
papers.abstract: Central Pattern Generators (CPGs) have long inspired the design of rhythms that combine endogenous generation and exogenous interaction. In neurodynamics and engineering studies, CPGs have been primarily analysed and designed as networks of coupled oscillators. In contrast, the present article regards CPGs as networks that propagate events through excitable rather than oscillatory nodes. The proposed event-based perspective reduces the design of network-level rhythmic properties to the tuning of local nodal input-output characteristics. This reduction enables a distributed and robust design methodology: nodes can be tuned independently, they can be heterogeneous, and the global rhythm results from local event propagation rather than from a specific global tuning of the network parameters. The present article builds on previously introduced concepts that parallel existing characterizations of oscillators: the event describing function (eDF), which characterises the propagation delay of a node, and the event phase response curve (ePRC), which characterises the phase sensitivity of a node. Event-based CPGs made of excitable rather than oscillatory nodes emerge as a principled design framework for robust rhythm generation.

papers.title: Caerus: Prefetching by Thinking Globally and Acting Locally
papers.abstract:
Modern processors rely heavily on data prefetching to bridge the growing performance gap between computation and memory accesses. In offset prefetching, prefetches are issued at an address delta relative to the most recently observed access, selecting deltas that have exhibited high coverage in the recent access-stream history. The Best-Offset Prefetcher (BOP) exemplifies this approach by selecting a single uniformly-issued global offset that delivers timely prefetches. However, its lack of context-sensitive accuracy tracking results in significantly increased DRAM traffic and sometimes disappointing performance. Conversely, Berti, the state-of-the-art offset prefetcher, achieves impressive prefetching performance and accuracy. However, its Program-Counter (PC)-local approach to extracting offsets limits its ability to capture global memory patterns, meaning there are many scenarios where simpler global offset prefetchers, such as BOP, outperform it.
  Observing the limitations of contemporary offset prefetchers, we present Caerus: an offset prefetcher that employs PC-local filtering on multiple non-overlapping globally derived offsets. Caerus extracts multiple offsets from the global memory trace and maximizes their combined coverage by training each offset only on accesses not already covered by previously learned offsets. The accuracy of each extracted offset is tracked per-PC based on whether it can cover future accesses for any PC. This allows Caerus to address complex delta patterns while maintaining high accuracy. In SPECspeed 2017, Caerus gains a geomean speedup of 8.3%, outperforming Berti by 2.0% while achieving low hardware and DRAM-traffic overhead.

authors.name: Jacky Wong
authors.institution: Merck & Co., Inc., Rahway, NJ, USA (United States)

papers.title: DINOv2 for PET: A Pre-Training Domain Benchmark Across Classification, Segmentation, and Prognosis
papers.abstract: DINO (self-DIstillation with NO labels) has become a stan- dard for self-supervised pre-training, producing features that generalise across datasets and downstream tasks. In medical imaging it has been adopted mainly for radiology (X-ray, CT and MRI), where even natural- image DINO features transfer well. In the literature, these features have been reported to transfer worse to functional imaging such as PET. Yet PET-specific DINO models have barely been introduced, and even less validated across multiple tasks and datasets. We present PET-DINOv2-2D, the first DINOv2 model pre-trained on 2D PET, and benchmark it against open-source encoders: the origi- nal DINOv2 (pre-trained on the LVD-142M natural-image dataset) and OmniRad (pre-trained on CT, MRI and ultrasound). Using the same lightweight heads for every backbone, and despite far less pre-training data, PET-DINOv2-2D matches or outperforms both on three down- stream PET tasks: normal/abnormal classification, lesion segmentation and recurrence-free survival prognosis. Its advantage is largest when few labels are available, suggesting that PET pre-training gives more transferable, label-efficient features. Code is made available at https://github.com/nuclivision/pet-dinov2-2d/.

papers.title: Phenomenological implications of cosmic (super)strings with time-varying tension
papers.abstract: Cosmic strings and cosmic superstrings could have formed in the early universe. In a particular class of models, the tension associated with these defects is time dependent, either because the strings themselves are composed of evolving moduli fields, or because they are directly coupled to evolving scalar fields leading to an effective time dependence in the string tension. Here we take seriously the possibility of this time dependence and investigate the phenomenological consequences of such an evolution, comparing the results to the more traditional case of a fixed time independent tension. In particular, for five different time varying models, motivated by different possible forms of evolution of the string tension, we evaluate their Gravitational Wave (GW) contributions as well as their impact on the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB). Performing an MCMC analysis of the models we find there are indeed interesting spectral signatures in the GW emission at frequencies between the current PTA and interferometer data, but the signatures are not unique to these strings, making them hard to pin down using current data. However, we do find cosmic strings with evolving tension fit the GW data as well as other favoured models.

papers.title: BRACHIO: Broad Representations Across Centres for Head-and-neck Imaging Oncology (HECKTOR 2026)
papers.abstract: The HECKTOR 2026 challenge benchmarks machine learning for head and neck cancer, where teams delineate primary and nodal tumour volumes, perform TN staging, and predict recurrence-free survival (RFS). This report describes the submissions for the HECKTOR challenge of team nucli. As the three tasks span both dense and global information from multicentric PET/CT scans, we utilise self-supervised pre-trained encoders, training a 2D DINOv2 encoder (PET-DINOv2-MIPs) on HECKTOR 2026's PET scans. Our final test submission ensembles a DynUNet trained from scratch with a SwinUNETR whose Swin trunk was initialised from a SimMIM-pre-trained checkpoint for segmentation, reaching a mean Dice of 0.5409. For TN staging, GTVp/GTVn geometric features from the segmentation masks are fit to stage probabilities by logistic regression (LR) and fused with PET-DINOv2-MIPs deep features (PCA + LR) via a second-level LR, reaching balanced accuracies of 0.3962 (T-stage) and 0.6432 (N-stage). For the RFS prognosis task, we fine-tune the last two blocks of the PET-DINOv2-MIPs ViT-S encoder jointly with an MLP head under a CoxPH loss, concatenating clinical covariates with the imaging features, reaching a test Harrell's C-index of 0.6577 and a weighted challenge score of 0.5802. The prognosis result is comparable to the best entry of the previous edition and consistent with our internal cross-validation, while our segmentation result is well below it and limits the staging results that depend on it.

papers.title: Unweaving the mechanics of woven fabrics through automated model discovery
papers.abstract: Woven fabrics have multiple structural, aesthetic, and medical applications that require knowledge of their mechanical properties. While isolated fiber properties are easily determined, bulk properties of woven material, which can be coated or locally reinforced, require knowledge of yarn density, weave style, and other characteristics that are difficult to obtain experimentally. Additionally, fiber rearrangement, twist, yarn contact, and fiber-direction coupling result in non-linear mechanical responses. As a result, there is no universal material model for woven materials, and each fabric requires a specific model and parameter calibration. Recently, methods to simultaneously discover material models and their parameters from experimental or synthetic datasets have been proposed. Here, we use automated model discovery to simultaneously extract the material model and its parameters from biaxial test data of a TPU-coated woven nylon fabric. We show that Constitutive Artificial Neural Networks discover a sparse three-term hyperelastic material law with one isotropic and two anisotropic contributions, reproducing the measured biaxial response with a mean $R^2=0.97$. Across 20 initializations, predictive accuracy remains robust despite variations in the exact sparse representation, consistent with strong correlations between several candidate terms. LARS-LASSO independently recovers the same dominant constitutive contributions at approximately 100-fold lower computational cost. These results are directly applicable to numerical finite-element models of fabric-based structures, including soft robotic devices. More broadly, these results provide a foundation for further model discovery, improved constitutive modeling, and mechanistically informed optimization of woven fabric structures.

papers.title: Characterization of sets in metric spaces where the big Lipschitz derivative is infinite
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a metric space without isolated points. In this paper we prove that $E$ is a $G_\delta$-set in $X$ if and only if there exists a continuous function $f:X\to\mathbb{R}$ whose big Lipschitz derivative is infinite precisely on $E$. To this end, we introduce a new generalization of the classical Takagi function to the setting of metric spaces.

papers.title: Two-Stage Clipping: Linear-Time Approximate and Exact Mixed-Norm Projections for Transformers
papers.abstract:
Large Language Models (LLMs) based on Transformer architectures have achieved remarkable performance across artificial intelligence tasks, but their computational cost remains a major bottleneck. Structured sparsification provides a promising approach to reducing this cost. In particular, $\ell_{1,\infty}$ projections can induce column-wise sparsity in model matrices, but existing proximal methods (Prox) typically require $\mathcal{O}(nm\log(nm))$ operations for matrices in $\mathbb{R}^{n\times m}$, limiting their computational and energy efficiency.
  In this paper, we introduce Two-Stage Clipping (TSC), an efficient structured sparsification operator inspired by bilevel optimization. Rather than solving a bilevel optimization problem in the strict sense, TSC decomposes the computation into two successive stages. First, group-level quantities are projected to allocate the global sparsity budget and identify active groups. Second, the resulting values are used as group-wise clipping thresholds for the matrix coefficients. For square attention matrices ($n \times n$), the complexity of our TSC method is $O(n^2)$, which is linear in the number of matrix coefficients.
  We establish a theoretical bound on the discrepancy between TSC and the exact proximal projection and show on synthetic data that the additional Euclidean approximation cost remains small in practice. Extensive benchmarks demonstrate substantial runtime improvements over proximal baselines and validate the theoretical norm identities underlying the proposed construction.

papers.title: Stability Study of Photo-inscribed Bragg Gratings in Sapphire Fibers at Very High Temperature
papers.abstract: Fiber Bragg gratings inscribed by femtosecond laser in sapphire fibers were subjected to thermal cycling up to 1500$\degree$C. Adding a multimode silica fiber reduces modal interference, improves the quality of the Bragg spectrum and the measurement accuracy. The measurement uncertainty is about 1.9$\degree$C at 1500$\degree$C.

papers.title: The dark surface of (163693) Atira and implications for inner-Earth asteroid origins
papers.abstract: We compare the physical properties of inner-Earth asteroid (163693) Atira with the NEOMOD3 population model. Its radar-derived diameter of 4.9 km and absolute magnitude H$_V\simeq$16.4 imply a geometric albedo of p$_V\sim$0.02. Photometry with the Astrophysical Research Consortium 3.5-m telescope and ARCTIC yields g-r=0.49$\pm$0.03, r-i=0.20$\pm$0.02, i-z=0.02$\pm$0.03, a$^\ast$=$-0.05\pm0.03$, and a g-to-i spectral slope of 3.4$\pm$0.9$\%$/100 nm. The photometric reflectance favors a provisional X-type classification; combined with the low albedo, it supports a Tholen P-type interpretation. NEOMOD3 assigns an approximately 66$\%$ probability of delivery through inner Main Belt channels and 26$\%$ to central and outer Main Belt channels. Atira's NEOMOD3 albedo-category probabilities are $0.07\pm0.02$, $0.64\pm0.04$, and $0.29\pm0.04$ for p$_V<$0.1, 0.1$\leq$p$_V<$0.3, and p$_V\geq$0.3, respectively. Across 38 inner-Earth objects, including Atira and 'Ayl\'o'chaxnim, inner Main Belt delivery generally dominates, and intermediate albedo is favored for 33 objects. Atira therefore represents an uncommon low-albedo outcome, compatible with delivery of dark material from the inner Main Belt or more distant primitive populations. Further characterization of inner-Earth asteroids will test whether current population models reproduce their compositional diversity.

papers.title: Coexistence of Superconductivity and Chern insulators with |C| $\geq 1$ in twisted rhombohedral bilayer-trilayer graphene
papers.abstract: Rhombohedral multilayer graphene (RMG) has been demonstrated as a promising platform for investigating strongly correlated phases of matter. Here, we observe a coexistence of superconductivity and Chern insulators in a twisted rhombohedral bilayer-trilayer graphene moir\'e superlattice. Superconductivity, evidenced by a sharp transition with a critical temperature of ~180 mK, nonlinear I-V with a BKT temperature of 135 mK, and a signature of phase-sensitive interference patterns, emerges from a symmetry-breaking Fermi surface near v = -2 and D = 0, and it survives at a large in-plane magnetic field up to 2 T, strongly deviating from the Pauli limit. Moreover, we observe a strong modulation of the Ginzburg-Landau coherence length from 467 nm to 145 nm as the in-plane magnetic field increases from 0 to 2 T, whereas the critical current Ic barely changes. Unlike previous studies in RMG, we observe a competition between superconductivity and a correlated insulator at v = -2, monitored by displacement fields and twist angles. Note that we also observe integer Chern insulators with C = 1, 3, and -3 at v = 1/2, 1, and 3, respectively, for large D > 0 in the same superconducting device. The observations establish twisted rhombohedral graphene multilayers as a fascinating system to investigate unconventional superconductivity, high Chern number topology, and their interplay.

authors.name: Qiu Yang
authors.institution: Lanzhou University of Finance and Economics

papers.title: V-CAPE: Visual Consistency Assessment for Product Image Editing
papers.abstract: Recent advances in generative image editing enable complex transformations such as background replacement, object manipulation, and pose adjustment from natural language instructions. However, verifying that these transformations preserve visual consistency, defined as the preservation of an object's intrinsic visual attributes, including geometry, texture, color, and fine-grained details, remains a largely unsolved problem. This challenge is particularly pronounced at scale, where manual inspection is infeasible and automated quality assessment (AutoQA) could become essential. In this work, we introduce Visual Consistency Assessment for Product Image Editing (V-CAPE), a large-scale dataset for evaluating visual consistency in generative image editing. The dataset consists of 40K unique source-target product image pairs, each annotated with binary accept/reject labels and structured failure modes capturing fine-grained inconsistencies such as geometric distortions, pose errors, and identity mismatches. V-CAPE combines real-world edited images with a synthetic subset constructed from 3D assets, enabling both realistic evaluation and controlled analysis. Vision-language models (VLMs) across all evaluated size categories on AutoQA achieve accuracy below 65%, indicating that the dataset poses a substantial challenge regardless of model scale. Our results highlight fundamental limitations of current models in verifying visual consistency under transformation, positioning V-CAPE as a benchmark for advancing fine-grained image editing evaluation.

papers.title: Pooled Testing under Congestion: Operational Scaling Laws for Pool-Size Selection
papers.abstract:
Classical pooled-testing rules choose pool sizes to reduce the number of tests. In practice, however, samples arrive over time, pools take time to form, testing capacity is finite, and positive pools create bursts of follow-up work. These operational features can make the test-efficient pool size far from the delay-efficient one.
  We formulate pooled testing with stochastic arrivals and finite testing capacity as a queueing system, and derive exact performance representations and asymptotic scaling laws for fixed-batch Dorfman testing and a dynamic two-threshold policy. The analysis reveals three distinct design regimes. When test usage is the main concern, the classical Dorfman rule is recovered and the optimal pool size scales with the inverse square root of prevalence. When delay accumulated while the laboratory is busy testing another batch matters, positive pools create service-time variability that grows more rapidly with pool size than the mean retesting burden, and the optimal scale shifts to the inverse cube root of prevalence. When waiting to assemble a pool is itself costly, the optimal fixed pool size remains bounded even as prevalence becomes very small. Under severe capacity scarcity, congestion remains relevant at the classical Dorfman scale: the square-root law survives, but with a capacity-dependent constant.
  Dynamic pooling separates two operational decisions that fixed pool sizes conflate. A lower threshold determines when routine testing should begin, while an upper threshold limits pooling when backlog is high. The lower threshold follows the cube-root scale, whereas the upper threshold primarily acts as congestion control. The results show how prevalence, capacity, and delay jointly determine pooling decisions and explain why operationally optimal pools can be much smaller than those suggested by test-efficiency calculations alone.

papers.title: Prescribed mean curvature surfaces of Riemann minimal type
papers.abstract: We construct analogues of Riemann minimal examples among surfaces in the Euclidean 3-space whose mean curvature is given by a prescribed function on the unit sphere in terms of their Gauss map. Specifically, we obtain a 2-parameter family of complete, properly embedded surfaces foliated by circles and straight lines and invariant under a nontrivial translation.

papers.title: Slant: Shaping Traffic for Resource-Efficient Microservices
papers.abstract: Microservice architectures rely on load balancers to distribute requests across service replicas, yet existing designs largely optimize for balanced routing without considering how routing shapes autoscaling signals and resource efficiency. We present Slant, a resource-aware load balancing framework that intentionally creates safe traffic imbalance to improve resource utilization. Slant profiles service-specific critical points, computes conservative multi-dimensional capacity, derives imbalance-aware routing weights that maintain hot and cold pods, and falls back to safer behavior under anomalies. By exposing clearer utilization signals, Slant works with existing vertical pod autoscalers (VPAs) without modification. Experiments on three microservice benchmarks show that Slant reduces allocated CPU cores by up to 26\% while lowering P99 latency by up to 18\% compared to Round-Robin. Under dynamic workloads, Slant triggers VPA scale-up 45\% faster and completes scale-in 40\% faster. Under anomalies, it recovers 40\% faster from pod failures and limits latency amplification to 1.8$\times$ versus 2.6$\times$ during downstream slowdowns.

authors.name: Dongxiao Yu
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Training language models in simulation for psychiatric intake
papers.abstract: In psychiatric practice, the clinical intake interview remains a primary diagnostic instrument, requiring the clinician to establish rapport while disentangling complex, overlapping presentations. Here, we show that multi-turn reinforcement learning (RL) in simulation environments improves language model performance on structured text-based psychiatric intake, spanning history-taking, differential diagnosis, and initial management planning. In a randomized, double-blind crossover study ($N = 60$ matched scenario pairs, 120 encounters) comparing the RL-trained agent against its identically prompted base model, 32 board-certified psychiatrists role-played standardized patients while a separate panel of 15 independent, board-certified psychiatrists scored the de-identified transcripts. The trained agent outperformed the base model in 76.7% of matched scenario pairs ($p < 0.0001$), with gains on an adapted clinical-examination rubric ($d_z = 0.77$, $p < 0.0001$), patient-centered communication (82.0% vs. 65.2%, $p < 0.001$), and differential diagnosis appropriateness (68.3% vs. 33.3%, $p < 0.001$). Across 127 psychiatrist-validated simulated intake scenarios, the trained agent nearly doubled its base model's clinical rubric score (0.706 vs. 0.379; composite reward 0.564 vs. 0.294, $p < 0.0001$). To systematically probe conversational safety, we established two Delphi-consensus taxonomies, of clinical safety risks and relational competencies, from which 256 challenging adversarial presentations were derived; we find that training in simulation environments more than halved under-triage of acute safety risks (12.9% vs. 30.5%, $p < 0.0001$). Simulation environments thus provide a controlled testbed for training and stress-testing psychiatric conversational agents, with gains that transferred to psychiatrist-enacted encounters, though residual gaps require safeguards and clinician oversight.

authors.name: Desmond C. Ong
authors.institution: The University of Texas at Austin

authors.name: Eric Lin
authors.institution: National Institute of Standards and Technology

papers.title: Greenscapes: Optimized Vegetation Configurations in Cities
papers.abstract: Vegetation plays a central role in cities, serving functional roles such as balancing shade and sky exposure, shaping the microclimate, carbon sequestration, and providing acoustic screening. Furthermore, aesthetic choices in landscape styles (formal, modernist, picturesque) are important for citizens' well-being and should be considered in the design of urban landscapes. In this paper, we present a novel method for placing vegetation, ranging from shrubs to large trees, in 3D urban scenes. Our method uses individual lots as input and employs a conditioned Vision-Language Model (VLM) to generate a top-down rendering of vegetation, placing large trees, small trees, and shrubs on lawn areas. This rendering is then converted into a 3D scene by detecting individual plants and selecting appropriate 3D assets. To refine the proposed configurations, we define an optimization loop that keeps the VLM-generated positions fixed after a deterministic feasibility repair and uses CMA-ES to optimize per-instance scale transformations along with discrete vegetation asset substitutions. To define the objective function for the optimization, we evaluate the generated 3D scenes with efficient surrogate models of shade and path-based acoustic exposure. Furthermore, we render in-scene views at each optimization step to compute view-dependent perceptual descriptors, enabling the generation of both aesthetic and functional vegetation layouts for urban scenes.

authors.name: Dominik L. Michels
authors.institution: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology

papers.title: {DEMAND}: {A}n organic glass scintillator array for direct measurements of $(\alpha,n)$ and $(p,n)$ reactions in inverse kinematics
papers.abstract: We have developed an array of up to 20 organic glass scintillator detectors, each consisting of a $3~\mathrm{cm}\times3~\mathrm{cm}\times3~\mathrm{cm}$ scintillator cube coupled to a photomultiplier tube. Sensitive to neutrons from a few hundred keV to several tens of MeV, the array was designed for use with recoil separators in inverse-kinematics measurements of astrophysical $(\alpha,n)$ and $(p,n)$ reactions. It provides a prompt start signal for identifying recoil-neutron coincidences from the recoil time of flight. We characterize eight detectors used in an inverse-kinematics measurement of $^{22}\mathrm{Ne}(\alpha,n)^{25}\mathrm{Mg}$, using source and in-beam data. From the widths of $\gamma$-ray Compton-edge peaks at 311, 341, 477, and 1062 keVee, we find an energy resolution described by $\mathrm{FWHM}(E)/E=\sqrt{A^2/E+B^2/E^2+C^2}$, with $A=0.00(7)$, $B=0.0618(54)$, and $C=0.135(5)$. The time-difference spectrum of nearest-neighbor $\gamma$-$\gamma$ coincidences from a $^{22}\mathrm{Na}$ source (250--600 keVee) gives a FWHM coincidence timing resolution of $910(40)$ ps, corresponding to a single-detector resolution of $640(30)$ ps. Mixed neutron-$\gamma$ fields from the in-beam reaction and a $^{241}\mathrm{AmBe}$ source show pulse-shape discrimination with an $n$-$\gamma$ figure of merit $>1$ down to about 100 keVee. Below 100 keVee, the total neutron yield can still be extracted using two-Gaussian fits to energy-gated pulse-shape discrimination spectra. Monte Carlo simulations of the present $^{22}\mathrm{Ne}(\alpha,n)^{25}\mathrm{Mg}$ measurement give a neutron singles detection efficiency of $1.56(45)%$, with uncertainty dominated by systematic effects in the simulation inputs.

authors.name: D. T. Doherty
authors.institution: Commissariat à l'Énergie Atomique et aux Énergies Alternatives

authors.name: C. J. Paxman
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

authors.name: C. Ruiz
authors.institution: Biomedical Research Networking Center in Bioengineering, Biomaterials and Nanomedicine

authors.name: M. Williams
authors.institution: Commissariat à l'Énergie Atomique et aux Énergies Alternatives

papers.title: Understanding axial attention in TSFMs through single location regression
papers.abstract: Recent advances in Time Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) increasingly rely on axial attention mechanisms, but despite their empirical success, the theoretical properties of axial attention remain largely unexplored. To bridge this gap, we extend the Single Location Regression framework introduced in Marion et al. [2025] to 2D structured data, in order to study sparse information settings where a target depends on a small number of tokens. We formulate an analytically tractable axial attention-type predictor and rigorously analyze its statistical properties and training dynamics. We prove that under a specific asymptotic regime and with knowledge of the underlying oracle parameters, our predictor achieves Bayes optimality, whereas a class of semi-linear simplifications strictly fails to do so, underlining the role of the inner non-linearity. We prove that for a specific temperature scaling, Projected Gradient Descent converges globally to the optimal oracle parameters. Extensive numerical experiments validate our theoretical findings and highlight the critical role of inverse temperature scheduling in empirical convergence.

authors.name: Andrei-Tiberiu Pantea
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Thin ends and topological spanning trees
papers.abstract:
Halin conjectured in 1964 that every connected graph has an end-faithful spanning tree. He proved this for countable graphs, but in the early 1990s Seymour and Thomas and, independently, Thomassen found uncountable counterexamples. Both are infinitely connected and hence one-ended, and their unique end has uncountable degree (i.e.\ contains uncountably many pairwise disjoint rays).
  Several authors have since asked how much of the conjecture survives. Diestel asked in 1992 whether a graph has an end-faithful spanning tree as soon as all its one-ended connected subgraphs have one; by a theorem of Polat, this would give end-faithful spanning trees in all connected graphs whose ends have countable degree. Diestel and K\"uhn introduced topological spanning trees, a topological variant of end-faithful spanning trees that exists in every one-ended connected graph, and asked in 2004 whether every connected graph has one. And Carmesin asked in 2019 whether every graph has a spanning tree that is end-faithful at least for its thin ends, the ends of finite degree.
  We answer all three questions in the negative. We show that the uncountably chromatic graph from an earlier note of ours on a problem of Erd\H{o}s and Hajnal has only ends of countable degree, each dominated by only countably many vertices, yet it has neither an end-faithful nor a topological spanning tree. A refinement of this graph moreover has no spanning tree that contains a ray from every end of degree~1.

papers.title: Read, Allocate, Route: Role-Coupled Tokenization for Pixel-Space Generative Transformers
papers.abstract: Pixel-space generative Transformers typically use one token per image patch, so capturing finer detail requires more tokens and makes global attention increasingly expensive. We observe that finer detail does not necessarily require more global communication: low-frequency structure benefits from global exchange, while high-frequency detail can be modeled locally. Based on this insight, we introduce SpecSlot, a pixel-space rectified-flow Transformer that decouples output detail from the length of the global attention sequence. SpecSlot expands each spatial anchor into multiple slots, each assigned a disjoint band of DCT coefficients; this separates anchor density from spectral subdivision. Only the lowest-frequency slot from each anchor participates in global attention, while all slots interact locally. This allows the model to increase spectral detail without enlarging the global sequence. A spatial head further adds a local correction to the spectral prediction, while the generative state, target, and loss remain in pixel space. On ImageNet-256, SpecSlot achieves a comparable final FID to a FLOPs-matched JiT control while converging faster. On ImageNet-512, it improves FID by 2.84 over the control with 3.9% fewer FLOPs, and comes within only 0.69 FID of JiT-B/16 at 38.2% lower cost. On text-to-image generation, SpecSlot surpasses JiT-B/8 on DPG-Bench by 1.06 at 40.6% lower forward cost.

papers.title: Characterizing Reaction Types through Linear Free-Energy Relationships in Cavities
papers.abstract: Polaritonic chemistry holds the promise of controlling chemical reactivity through confined light-matter interactions, yet how reactions respond inside optical cavities remains debated. Here, we take a more zoomed-out view, inspired by electrostatic catalysis. We extend nonempirical linear free-energy relationships to cavity-modified reactions and show that their behavior falls into four distinct reaction types set by simple response-crossing rules. Reactions can follow conventional Bell-Evans-Polanyi (BEP) or counterintuitive Opposite-BEP behavior regardless of cavity tuning, or switch between the two as the cavity frequency is varied. We establish this picture analytically and demonstrate it in the Shin Metiu model and in four molecular reactions treated with ab initio electronic-structure methods. Even at this deliberately coarse-grained level, cavity-modified reactivity already shows qualitatively different and strongly counterintuitive behavior, including reactions that switch character with cavity frequency. Yet this complexity can still be reduced to a simple competition between permanent-dipole and polarizability responses. This reaction-type classification therefore provides a new route to organize and anticipate cavity-modified reactivity.

authors.name: Davis M. Welakuh
authors.institution: Max Planck Institute for the Structure and Dynamics of Matter

papers.title: Finite-State Uncertainty-Aware Widely-Linear Equalization for Aeronautical GMSK Links
papers.abstract: Aeronautical and unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) receivers must equalize doubly selective channels under synchronization uncertainty and limited onboard computation and memory. We propose a finite-state, uncertainty-aware widely-linear (WL) equalization algorithm for Gaussian minimum-shift keying (GMSK) links. The algorithm uses synchronization estimates and their reliability descriptors to select one of a small number of precomputed filters, avoiding repeated online coefficient synthesis. Using a finite-memory Laurent model, we design the stored affine WL filters from conditional physical-state moments. We derive an exact characterization of excess mean-square error (MSE) relative to adaptation to continuous side information, Lloyd-type conditions for finite-state design, local timing--frequency mismatch certificates, and an orthogonal decomposition of design and information losses. On a reference channel at $E_b/N_0=8$~dB under high synchronization-estimation uncertainty, a $16$-state bank reduces pseudo-symbol MSE by $51.9\%$ relative to point-estimate WL time-varying MMSE equalization and by $6.6\%$ relative to posterior-mean (PM) substitution. With identical partitioning, routing, and storage, conditional-moment filters reduce MSE by $10.1\%$ and full-waveform average bit error rate (ABER) by $15.6\%$ relative to representative-state filters. Across $18$ synthetic three-path channels with individually fitted banks, MSE and ABER decrease by $5.3\%$ and $12.9\%$, respectively, relative to PM substitution. The $16$-state receiver stores $2048$ real coefficients. Posterior integration, robustness sweeps, and software timing measurements quantify the tradeoff between equalization accuracy, online computational cost, and bank refresh.

papers.title: RoboSeed: Multidimensional Evaluation of Vision-Language-Action and World-Action Models: Capability, Resource Affordability, and Research Evidence
papers.abstract:
Choosing a robot action model requires evidence about task capability, adaptation cost, deployment requirements, and the reliability of reported conclusions. Success rates alone offer limited guidance to researchers with different computing budgets and goals. We propose RoboSeed, a multidimensional evaluation framework for vision-language-action (VLA) and world-action models (WAM), within a continuing program to train, evaluate, and openly release robot models with verifiable evidence for model selection.
  The framework defines five dimensions: capability, downstream training affordability, deployment affordability, locally verified research value, and reproduction evidence. It maps empirical measurements and audit criteria to 0-100 profiles using fixed normalization anchors, with balanced, training-constrained, and deployment-constrained preference settings. Interface and protocol checks establish when comparisons are appropriate. Missing measurements remain explicit, incomplete aggregate scores are withheld, and weighted input coverage identifies evidence gaps.
  We apply the framework to representative VLA and WAM models, drawing on local training, released-weight evaluation, task-level audits, and an evaluation-system study. The results reveal budget-dependent backbone choices, sensitivity to adaptation recipes, and differences between language and visual task interfaces. Reproducible scoring code and machine-readable evidence support extension to additional models. The study provides dimension-level assessments and priorities for further measurement, while incomplete serving traces and heterogeneous protocols preclude overall numerical rankings.

authors.name: Haolan Lei
authors.institution: Xi’an University of Posts and Telecommunications

authors.name: Chuang Yang
authors.institution: Jiangxi University of Water Resources and Electric Power

papers.title: Usable String Matching by Humans through Overlaid Presentation
papers.abstract:
We explore the ability of humans to compare strings, an error-prone activity which occurs in critical contexts (e.g., bank wire transfers), where it is not always possible to trust a machine to help.
  We hypothesize that understanding human cognitive and perceptual limitations can improve how people verify whether two character strings are identical. We vary the strings' relative positions and presentation formats to measure comparison speed and accuracy.
  We present results from two online experiments with 178 human subjects who compared pairs of strings to determine whether the two strings were identical. The strings varied by length (5 characters to small paragraphs), difference (matching versus making a random change or a hard-to-detect one), alignment (vertical versus horizontal), and presentation (Overlay versus Adjacent).
  Our experiments test whether, by encoding and memory tasks into perceptual tasks, overlay formats can offer advantages in speed and accuracy. Results show that overlay offers a substantially faster method, with improved accuracy for long strings. Nevertheless, mean error rates were at least 4 percent, indicating that even the improved approach may be insufficiently accurate for many verification tasks.

authors.name: Mehdi Bouhamidi
authors.institution: Laboratoire d'Automatique, de Mécanique et d'Informatique Industrielles et Humaines

papers.title: Engineering Canalized Near-Field Radiative Heat Transfer between Fixed Nanoparticles with Twisted $\alpha$-MoO$_3$ Trilayers
papers.abstract: Canalized phonon polaritons in twisted van der Waals crystals offer a route to control nanoscale thermal energy flow. Building on the established twisted $\alpha$-MoO$_3$ trilayer platform, we examine how internal twist angles modify near-field radiative heat transfer (NFRHT) between a prescribed nanoparticle pair while both the nanoparticle axis and the bottom-layer crystallographic orientation remain fixed. Under this constraint and at equal total $\alpha$-MoO$_3$ thickness, the optimized trilayer reaches 2.84 times the bilayer maximum radiative power, while its mean power over the sampled internal twist configurations is 1.51 times the bilayer value. The second internal twist coordinate also enlarges the set of configurations supporting strong transfer, with local angular tolerance when either internal angle is varied separately. Momentum-space Green-tensor diagnostics and real-space energy-density maps associate the enhancement with stronger receiver-directed scattering and improved channel alignment. Selected trilayer configurations retain enhanced coupling across the sampled family of nanoparticle resonances and at long distances. These results quantify the additional internal configurational freedom available for engineering radiative heat transfer under a fixed laboratory-frame geometry.

authors.name: Yang Hu
authors.institution: Alfred-Wegener-Institut Helmholtz-Zentrum für Polar- und Meeresforschung

papers.title: Optical Calibration of a Frequency-Domain-Multiplexed X-Ray TES Microcalorimeter Array via Photon-Number-Resolved Statistics
papers.abstract: Transition-edge sensor (TES) microcalorimeters for future X-ray space observatories require accurate low-energy calibration, a regime where conventional X-ray sources are limited by intrinsic linewidth, count rate, or experimental complexity. In this work, we investigate fibercoupled optical photons as a compact calibration tool for an Athena-like TES array. Optical pulses at 405 nm were generated with an acousto-optic modulator and delivered through an optical fiber onto a selected TES pixel inside a dilution refrigerator, via a dedicated cryogenic alignment interface. Externally triggered pulses were processed with an optimal-filter pipeline, including baseline subtraction, drift correction, and multi-Gaussian reconstruction of the pulse-height spectrum. The reconstructed spectra show resolved photon-number peaks consistent with the Poissonian statistics expected from an attenuated coherent source, reaching equivalent energies above 400 eV with a mean photon number exceeding 100 per pulse. The detector response was further tested for linearity by comparing the measured photon-number distributions against those predicted from the independently calibrated number of photons sent to the detector and a single, globally estimated detection efficiency, confirming Poissonian, linear behaviour across nearly two orders of magnitude in photon number. These results demonstrate that fiber-delivered optical photons can probe the few-eV to sub-keV response of Athena-like TES microcalorimeters, offering a practical and extensible framework for future low-energy calibration studies.

papers.title: Proof of the conjecture about inequality of $1/H$-variations of fractional Brownian motion along the equidistant and the Lebesgue partitions
papers.abstract: We give an analytic proof of the comparison conjectured by Das, \L{}ochowski, Matsuda and Perkowski for the fractional Brownian level-crossing constant: for standard fractional Brownian motion, $c_H>\mathbb{E}|Z|^{1/H}$ when $0<H<1/2$ and $c_H<\mathbb{E}|Z|^{1/H}$ when $1/2<H<1$, where $Z\sim N(0,1)$. At $H=1/2$, both constants equal one. The main tool is Gaussian comparison under ordering of increment variances. It applies because truncated variation is translation invariant and lattice-submodular, as follows from its minimum-total-variation characterization. A tangent variogram produces Brownian motion with an independent Gaussian drift on the upper side, and a periodic Brownian bridge on the lower side. The former has an explicit stationary reflection rate. For the latter we calculate an integrated cyclic crossing count by first-passage Laplace transforms. Elementary hyperbolic, theta-series, and Gamma inequalities then give strict comparisons on both full parameter ranges. No numerical integration, simulation, interval certificate, or quantitative local expansion at $H=1/2$ is used.

papers.title: On Terao's conjecture for at most nine planes
papers.abstract: In this note we show that Terao's freeness conjecture holds for arrangements of at most nine planes in the complex projective $3$-space. Moreover, we show that every essential and irreducible free arrangement of at most nine planes in $\mathbb{P}^{3}_{\mathbb{C}}$ is divisionally free, and we list all intersection lattices of such arrangements. Our approach is based on Ziegler's restriction theorem and a simple count involving the numbers of multiple lines. As a by-product, we show that Cynk--Szemberg octic arrangements are never free. Finally, motivated by a recent work of Dimca and Pokora, we present examples of weak Ziegler pairs of plane arrangements, including pairs of octic arrangements leading to rigid double octic Calabi--Yau threefolds.

authors.name: Bartosz Jarosławski
authors.institution: Uniwersytet Komisji Edukacji Narodowej w Krakowie

papers.title: Inner $\mathrm{C}^{\ast}$-Selfless Groups
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of inner $\mathrm{C}^{\ast}$-selfless groups and study their structural properties. We prove a Fourier coefficient extraction theorem for invariant subalgebras of crossed products by such groups under a compatibility assumption on the action. Consequently, every inner $\mathrm{C}^{\ast}$-selfless group has the relative $\mathrm{C}^{\ast}$-invariant subalgebra rigidity property, and every finite product of such groups has the $\mathrm{C}^{\ast}$-invariant subalgebra rigidity property. We also introduce another group-theoretic notion, which we call cyclic Powers property. This implies inner $\mathrm{C}^{\ast}$-selflessness, complete $\mathrm{C}^{\ast}$-selflessness, and the Powers property, among others. We establish it for groups admitting a topologically free extreme boundary action on a compact Hausdorff space with more than two points, and for Zariski-dense discrete subgroups of $\mathrm{PSL}(d,\mathbb K)$ containing a biproximal element, where $\mathbb K$ is a local field and $d\geq2$. In particular, we obtain the Powers property for $\mathrm{PSL}(d,\mathbb Z)$, $d\geq3$, answering a question posed more than twenty years ago by Bridson-de la Harpe. Finally, we show that every non-trivial mixed identity-free discrete group has the relative invariant subalgebra rigidity property for its group von Neumann algebra. This shows that the Baumslag-Solitar groups $\mathrm{BS}(m,n)$ with $|m|,|n|\geq2$ and $|m|\ne|n|$ have the relative ISR property, thereby answering a question of Dudko-Jiang.

papers.title: What Does an Ontology Catch? Curated, LLM-Generated and Data-Derived Ontologies as Checkers of LLM Agents over Knowledge Graphs
papers.abstract: LLM agents that answer questions over Web knowledge graphs are increasingly wrapped in checks derived from the graph's ontology, on the assumption that a formal schema makes a reliable judge. Yet a checker can be wrong as well: it can miss errors, and it can flag correct answers and push the agent into "fixing" them. Whether a curated ontology is worth its cost as such a judge, and how it compares with an ontology an LLM writes or a schema mined from the data, is unknown. We make the checker itself the object of study. Across curated, LLM-generated and data-derived ontologies, used as prompt context, as a checker, or both, and across open-weight and proprietary agents on public graphs and a private graph of nearly $10^{9}$ triples, we account for what ontology-derived checks catch and what they wrongly flag. We show how each source trades caught errors against false alarms, how a curated schema used as published can contradict its own data, which errors structural checks miss, and whether combining sources or giving the agent the checker's specific feedback pays off. On UniProt, the curated ontology flags more correct answers than either an ontology derived from the data or one an LLM derives from a summary of the data with masked identifiers. On real agent answers, its flags are only marginally more precise than random flags.

authors.name: Rund Tawfiq
authors.institution: Sano – Centre for Computational Personalised Medicine International Research Foundation

authors.name: Tomasz Kosciolek
authors.institution: Sano – Centre for Computational Personalised Medicine International Research Foundation

papers.title: Exh subspaces of bounded variation spaces generated by submeasures
papers.abstract: In the present paper we are building one more bridge between the theory of ideals on the set of natural numbers and the theory of spaces of functions of bounded variation. It is already known that $F_\sigma$ ideals (that is, ideals of the form $\text{Fin}(\phi)$, where $\phi$ is a lower semicontinuous submeasure on $\mathbb{N}$) lead to a nice generalization of different concepts from the theory of functions of bounded variation (Waterman variation and Chanturya classes). In this paper we show that analytic P-ideals (that is, ideals of the form $\text{Exh}(\phi)$, where $\phi$ is a lower semicontinuous submeasure on $\mathbb{N}$) lead to a generalization of spaces of functions continuous in $\Lambda$-variation. The properties of this generalization are investigated.

authors.name: Paweł Sawicki
authors.institution: Institute of Nuclear Physics, Polish Academy of Sciences

papers.title: Toward Complete Speaker Anonymization: a Streaming Cascaded System for Voice Privacy and PII Removal
papers.abstract: We present a cascade streaming voice privacy system, consisting of ASR, NLP, and TTS modules. By leveraging recent improvements in all three aspects of speech and language processing, we show that such a system is capable of achieving a result comparable to state-of-the-art offline voice privacy systems, while providing controllable capabilities of content protection beyond voice. With an estimated utterance-onset end-to-end latency of 717 ms, the presented system preserves speech content with 11% WER on Librispeech, while detecting PII with a 69% SLU F1 score and achieving up to 47.66% EER against a semi-informed attacker.

papers.title: A Hierarchy of Composition Procedures for Logic-Based Workflow Patterns
papers.abstract: Logic-based workflow patterns capture recurring behavioural structures together with reusable temporal specifications. Their composition raises distinct problems as workflow structures become richer, including instantiation, nesting, conditional execution, repeated occurrences, and traceability of generated formulae. This paper proposes a hierarchy of Pattern Composition ($\Pi C$) procedures, from $\Pi C_0$ to $\Pi C_4$, that organizes these requirements as progressively richer compositional capabilities. The hierarchy separates compositional complexity from the expressive power of the temporal-logic fragment, represented by $TL_j$, yielding a framework $\Pi C_i[TL_j]$ for developing logical workflow specifications. We develop activation-aware Pattern Composition ($\Pi C_2$), which distinguishes the structural presence of a nested pattern from its execution in a particular workflow context. We formalise its recursive procedure, analyse its properties, and define an evaluation protocol for conditional activation, conservativity under mandatory composition, and specification growth. The hierarchy also characterizes selective occurrence qualification for iterative patterns ($\Pi C_3$) and provenance for tracing generated formulae to their sources ($\Pi C_4$). Finally, we outline $\Pi C_{\mathrm{Assist}}$, an orthogonal mode in which AI proposes and refines pattern expressions subject to the hierarchy's compositional checks.

papers.title: Jailbreak Connectivity: Towards Diverse, Transferable, and Universal Multimodal Large Language Model Jailbreak
papers.abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) are vulnerable to visual jailbreak attacks that bypass safety safeguards. Existing methods typically optimize isolated adversarial examples, limiting attack diversity, transferability, and generalization. We propose Jailbreak Connectivity (JC), a framework based on the observation that effective adversarial inputs can be connected through low-loss regions in image space. JC optimizes continuous adversarial paths: path sampling yields diverse jailbreak images, lightweight surrogate classifiers guide cross-model transfer, and a distribution-level objective enables universal attacks across harmful queries. On MM-SafetyBench, JC achieves average attack success rates of 84.01%, 85.77%, and 97.95% on Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, InternVL3.5-8B, and Gemma-3-12B-IT, respectively, exceeding the strongest baselines by up to 68.36 percentage points. In black-box evaluations, JC improves attack success rates over FigStep by 24.69 and 27.34 percentage points on GPT-5.6 and Gemini 3.1 Pro, respectively. These findings reveal structured vulnerabilities in MLLM safety alignment and inform more comprehensive security evaluation.

papers.title: Sharp lifespan estimates for heat equations with H\"ormander operators
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the Cauchy problem $u_t-\mathcal L u=h(t)u^p$, $u(0)=\varepsilon u_0\ge0$, where $p>1$, $h\ge0$ is only locally integrable, and $\mathcal L=\sum_{j=1}^mX_j^2$ is a homogeneous H\"ormander sum of squares on $\mathbb R^n$ of homogeneous dimension $q$. Diffusion spreads the solution out and weakens the nonlinearity, while the reaction $h(t)u^p$ may force blow-up. We prove that the outcome is decided by the single quantity $\mathcal{H}_{p,h}(T)=\int_0^Th(t)(1+t)^{-\frac q2(p-1)}\,d t$, in which the reaction at time $t$ is weighted by the factor by which diffusion has weakened the solution: small data are global if $\mathcal{H}_{p,h}(\infty)<\infty$, while otherwise the lifespan $T_\varepsilon$ satisfies $c\,\varepsilon^{-(p-1)}\le\mathcal{H}_{p,h}(T_\varepsilon)\le C\,\varepsilon^{-(p-1)}$ for small $\varepsilon$. Our technique of proof is based on a backward-semigroup functional combined with a Gaussian-envelope energy and an ODE cap telescoped along interlaced geometric grids. The result contains the Euclidean, Heisenberg, Carnot and Grushin cases, yields explicit lifespan laws for power, logarithmic, exponential, periodic and intermittent coefficients, and exhibits effects with no autonomous counterpart, such as a lifespan with no power law in $\varepsilon$. We also prove regularity and a priori estimates for classical solutions and discuss what remains true for a general nonlinearity $f(u)$.

papers.title: Assessing Language Models for Scientific Applications: Inertial Confinement Fusion as a Use Case
papers.abstract: Advancing language models for specialized scientific applications requires evaluations of scientific fluency, physical reasoning, and quantitative analyses. Using inertial confinement fusion (ICF) as a test case, we have developed an expert-curated benchmark of 250 questions spanning qualitative reasoning, numerical calculation, symbolic derivation, and equation formulation. Responses have been evaluated using deterministic numerical and symbolic checks together with language-model judges. We compared a variety of out-of-the-box closed-source and open-source large language models with Prospero, a model specialized through combined domain-adaptive pretraining and supervised fine-tuning for ICF. We also conducted initial retrieval-assisted evaluations. Prospero improved its aggregate score by 10.7 percentage points over its base model, with gains across all question types. Frontier models achieved the highest aggregate scores, but critical physics errors persisted, particularly in numerical calculations. We note that domain-specific performance can improve through specialization, but benchmark gains alone do not establish scientific reliability. Retrieval improved performance for a smaller model but yielded no statistically significant improvement for a frontier model. Two scientific stress tests further illustrate useful capabilities and the need for expert assessment of physical assumptions and model validity. Based on these findings, we recommend evaluating existing domain capabilities and retrieval benefits before committing to substantial additional specialization.

papers.title: Electromagnetic emission at the Langmuir frequency from laser interaction with an unmagnetized plasma
papers.abstract: We present the first experimental observation of electromagnetic emission at the Langmuir frequency, $\omega_p$, resulting from laser-plasma interaction in an underdense and unmagnetised plasma. The emission is spatially resolved and analyzed in polarization. It originates from an electrostatic wave excited by the Raman instability. Despite its frequency being very close to the plasma's cutoff frequency, $\omega_{pe}$, this radiation can escape the plasma by following the decreasing slope of the plasma density profile. Radiation at $2\omega_p$, is also observed. This experimental platform offers a powerful tool to explore the processes of wave coupling at the origin of some radio solar bursts.

papers.title: On the existence of minimizers for the generalized liquid drop model
papers.abstract: We consider a broad class of generalized liquid drop models in which a perimeter term competes with repulsive nonlocal interactions with finite first moments. For all such kernels satisfying the natural physical assumption of reflection positivity we show existence of minimizers for all masses, in the (super-)critical regime. Moreover, in the subcritical regime we give the first quantitative estimate of the range of masses for which existence holds, which converges to the whole positive real line as one approaches the critical regime. This result builds on the nonlocal curvature approach introduced and developed in the periodic setting in \cite{dr24}.

papers.title: Kinematic methods of spiral nature identification: limitations and applicability
papers.abstract: The nature of spiral arms in galaxies remains debated, with several competing formation scenarios, including density waves, kinematic spirals, dynamic spirals, and recurrent modes, that are difficult to distinguish observationally. We tested two kinematic methods - the phase reversal method and the velocity harmonic dominance method - using toy models and mock data from TNG50 simulations. For bar resonances, the phase reversal method is strongly orientation-dependent and yields reliable corotation estimates only when the bar is aligned with the disc minor axis. For spiral arms, the phase reversal method does not always yield reliable results and should be used in tondem with another kinematic method. The velocity harmonic dominance method is more robust: it distinguishes between density wave, kinematic, and dynamic spiral patterns, although it still shows some sensitivity to orientation. Uncertainties in the rotation curve do not strongly affect its results. We also apply both methods to the observed grand-design spiral galaxy NGC3938 as an illustrative example; the results suggest the presence of multiple spiral modes, consistent with the recurrent modes scenario and this interpretation relies on different indirect evidence. Based on our findings, we propose a strategy for classifying spiral structure in observed galaxies that combines multiple independent tests. Applying this analysis to an extended sample will allow us to validate its predictive power and to investigate the diversity of spiral formation scenarios.

papers.title: Position- and Temperature-Dependent Responsivity in a KID-Based Phonon-Mediated Detector
papers.abstract: We report on the position- and temperature-dependent response of a kinetic inductance phonon-mediated (KIPM) detector. To study position-dependence, we used a controllable mirror attached to a micro-electromechanical system (MEMS) to steer optical light with a 100 $\mu$m spot size over the backside of the cryogenic detector. With both pulsed and continuous operation of the LED, we observe features of the detector housing and find that the signal is strongest when the LED is pointed directly at the KID. The "off-KID" response is measured to be 34% of the "on-KID" response and is largely independent of direction. We model phonon propagation and collection in the KIPM detector with G4CMP and assert that the isotropic angular dependence is unlikely to be due to discrete phonon absorption "sinks", such as the microwave feedline or the device mounting points, but can be explained instead by an isotropic energy loss in the crystal. We furthermore utilize the temperature flexibility of the MEMS and KIPM detector system to investigate temperature-dependent responsivity, both at the sensor level (i.e., frequency shifts in the KID) and at the detector level (i.e., position dependence). We fit the KID's response to a two-component heat capacity and present the model as an alternative way to understand the KID's response to absorbed energy. We show on- and off-KID data at a range of temperatures and show that the phonon dynamics are not temperature dependent. We comment on the resulting implication for KID dynamics and design improvements.

papers.title: Phase-Space Realization of Stochastic Multivalued Dynamics with Gyroscopic Subdifferential Coupling
papers.abstract: We introduce a new framework for stochastic variational inequalities with oblique reflections generated by non-symmetric matrix coefficients. The loss of symmetry fundamentally changes the structure of the reflected dynamics: besides the dissipative component, it produces a genuinely gyroscopic component describing rotational effects that are invisible to the associated energy forms. To capture this hidden component, we consider planar obstacle problems and we lift the dynamics to an extended phase-space system, where the dissipative and gyroscopic mechanisms are naturally separated. This leads to a new notion of solution, for which we establish existence and uniqueness. The resulting framework allows for genuinely rotated reflections, which can lead to angle-controlled rotations.

papers.title: The Power Watershed as a Differentiable Segmentation Layer
papers.abstract: Can a Watershed transform, the classical tool of morphological segmentation, be placed at the end of a deep network and trained through? The Power Watershed (PW) is the limit of the seeded Random Walker (RW) as p grows to infinity with edge weights raised to the power p. At every finite p the RW solves a sparse positive-definite linear system and is exactly differentiable with respect to the edge weights and the unaries through one adjoint solve; its multi-label form costs one right-hand side per label, and its limit is the PW. We study this family as the last layer of a segmentation network, the watershed layer (WS layer). A conditioning study measures how the solve, the gradient and the distance to the limit evolve with p, and the implicit gradient is checked against unrolling. On synthetic data with correct edge costs the WS layer transforms a soft prediction into an exact boundary. On nuclei segmentation (PanNuke), a binary WS layer is level with a thresholded U-Net. With the instances as labels, the WS layer turns the U-Net into an instance segmenter whose number of labels is set per image by the markers rather than by the output layout, and the network is trained through that partition: instance F1 score rises from 0.656 to 0.795 over a U-Net with connected components, level with the same network followed by a tuned marker watershed. At the training temperature the partition is a watershed of the learned costs, and the finite temperature lets the solve hedge, discounting weak markers and sharing contested pixels. The hedging puts the WS layer 0.015--0.020 F1 ahead of the baseline when trained on a tenth of the data, at the price of having to deploy the finite-p solve rather than its exact limit at inference. Code and the full experimental record are released.

papers.title: On the Generalization Gap of Streaming Federated Learning with Markovian Data
papers.abstract: Streaming federated learning (SFL) allows clients to train a shared model from continuously arriving data without retaining large local datasets. Such streams often exhibit temporal dependence, yet its effect on generalization remains poorly understood. In this paper we study the expected generalization gap of the aggregated model when client data follow Markov processes, using information-theoretic and rate-distortion techniques. Our framework accommodates heterogeneous Markovian dynamics across clients and distinguishes temporal dependence from information acquired during local learning. We establish bounds under cross-entropy loss, specializing them to Linear Next-Token Prediction (LNTP) and Self-Attention Next-Token Prediction (SANTP). These results quantify the effects of client count, communication rounds, sample size, data dimension, mixing time, and context length. In particular, they reveal a communication--generalization tradeoff: although frequent aggregation may help optimization, it can weaken generalization guarantees. They also suggest a potential advantage of distributed over centralized streaming learning under a fixed total data budget. Temporal dependence enters through the square root of the mixing time. By analyzing the history-state process, we obtain refined bounds with improved context-length dependence under suitable mixing conditions. Experiments on GPT-style language-model pretraining with TinyStories and real-world time-series forecasting illustrate how collaboration and communication frequency influence generalization under temporal dependence

papers.title: TableTune: Measured, Self-Correcting Draft-Length Tables for Dynamic Speculative Decoding
papers.abstract: Speculative decoding speeds up large language model (LLM) serving only while the GPU has spare compute, so the best draft length, the number of tokens a small drafter guesses per step, shrinks as the batch grows. vLLM lets operators set the draft length for each batch size with a hand-written table, but nothing measures or corrects that table. We present TableTune. Its tuner times the decoding step for every batch size and draft length on vLLM's own serving path and computes, in minutes, the table that maximizes throughput. Its controller, a vLLM plugin, tracks how many guesses are accepted in live traffic and rebuilds the table while serving. We measure TableTune only against other ways to speculate. On an H100, the tuned table delivers at least 94% of the throughput of the best fixed draft length at every load in four of five drafter settings (88% in the fifth) without the operator having to know which length that is. Against reimplementations of TurboSpec- and Nightjar-style control on the same engine, its worst-case loss is never higher than theirs, and with the EAGLE-3 drafter it is 3% against 9% and 12%. On a mixture-of-experts model, vLLM's documented table loses up to 18% and the tuned table at most 3%. Starting from mistuned tables, the controller raises throughput by up to 58% (up to 45% on vLLM's default runner), and after a workload switch with the DFlash drafter it recovers 96% of a stale table's loss. In llm-d's optimized-baseline deployment as shipped, two Qwen3-32B replicas on four GPUs, the tuned table is up to 32% faster than a fixed draft length of 3 and up to 25% faster than vLLM's documented table at high load, and the controller raises the documented table's throughput by up to 29%.

papers.title: Rethinking Neural Thickets Without Weight Perturbations
papers.abstract:
The Neural Thickets hypothesis posits that pretrained language models lie in dense neighborhoods of task-specific experts in weight space, which random Gaussian perturbations can uncover. We reproduce the reported gains, but show that they do not require this geometric explanation. Perturbing a single decoder block already recovers much of the improvement, while keeping the model entirely frozen and adding a random bias to its output logits matches or exceeds full-weight perturbations on most reasoning tasks. This suggests an alternative explanation based on output diversity, validation-based selection, and voting. We formalize this view as Perturb-Select-Vote (PSV), a general procedure that generates perturbed predictors, selects high-performing members on a small validation set, and aggregates their predictions.
  This interpretation connects Neural Thickets to established inference-time methods, including sampling, self-consistency, and verifier-guided selection. A first-order analysis further shows that small weight perturbations act primarily through their induced logit shifts. We extend this analysis to vision, where logit PSV substantially improves performance under domain shift, including on Earth observation, while full-weight perturbations provide little additional benefit. Together, these results suggest that the gains attributed to nearby weight-space experts can instead be obtained through output diversity, selection, and voting. Logit PSV realizes these benefits with a fully frozen model, providing a simple, training-free alternative to full-weight perturbation ensembles across language and vision.

papers.title: RoSAMDepth: Robust Self-supervised Depth Estimation Leveraging Segment Anything Model
papers.abstract: Robust depth estimation aims to maintain high-quality depths across diverse conditions. However, most existing methods estimate depth without taking into account the object-level information. As a result, the predicted depth may easily deviate within objects and become blurred under adverse conditions. To overcome this weakness, we propose RoSAMDepth, a novel framework that can assist robust self-supervised depth estimation in leveraging rich and diverse object-level priors from the Segment Anything Model (SAM). We focus on incorporating object-level information across three key aspects: a segment-guided representation contrasting method that injects object-level awareness into the feature representation space; an adaptive regional outlier masking strategy combined with a regional Gaussian likelihood loss that enforces regional depth smoothness; and an object-level reliability estimation strategy that mitigates the influence of unreliable supervision. Extensive experiments across multiple datasets and diverse weather conditions demonstrate that our method produces sharper, more accurate depth predictions, consistently outperforming state-of-the-art methods. Our code is available at https://github.com/xagao/RoSAMDepth.

papers.title: Video Generation Meets Agent Harness: Agentic Video Generation, Agentic World Modeling and Recursive Self-Improvement
papers.abstract: Video generation is shifting from end-to-end synthesis toward agentic generation, where planning, tool use, and feedback enable coherent, controllable multi-shot videos. In parallel, video world models provide action-conditioned observations and predicted futures, serving as interactive environments for agents. We study their intersection through the agent harness: an executable runtime that constructs context, exposes tools, maintains state, routes feedback, and manages budgets around video models. This report examines three directions. First, agentic video generation, where harnesses coordinate scripting, shot planning, asset management, production, and editing, alongside the evaluation challenges of these systems. Second, agentic world modeling, where harnesses mediate observation, control, execution, and state. We discuss hybrid designs in which game engines or agent-written programs maintain world state while video models render observations, and how agents and world models can mutually evaluate and improve one another. Third, recursive self-improvement (RSI) in video model development, distinguishing output revisions, updates to harness state, generator parameters, and evaluators, and changes to the improvement procedure itself. We identify how these improvements feed back into subsequent development. Across these directions, we analyze essential agent capabilities, including audiovisual perception, long-horizon planning, memory, code-based interaction, feedback-guided control, skill reuse, and multi-agent coordination. We conclude with challenges in autonomous video production, lifelong memory, programmable hybrid control, autonomous model development, provenance, cost accounting, and evaluation linking video quality and task performance to sustained improvements in models and harnesses.
