papers.title: Phase-resolved X-ray spectroscopy of the Vela pulsar with NICER observations
papers.abstract: PSR J0835-4510 (a.k.a. the Vela pulsar) is the best studied pulsar in the Southern hemisphere given its high radio brightness and large glitch activity. However, its X-ray brightness is comparatively lower, making the study of its X-ray profile difficult. We aim to investigate the X-ray emission of the Vela pulsar coming from the surface of the neutron star to infer the properties of its hotspots and assess whether they share a common spectral shape. We also aim to prove whether the 2021 glitch affected the hotspots. We used ephemeris obtained from high-cadence radio observations with the radio telescopes of the Argentine Institute of Radio Astronomy to combine all the NICER observations of the Vela pulsar after its 2019 glitch and before its 2024 glitch. We obtained a folded pulse profile for three different energy ranges and subsequently studied their phase-resolved energy spectra. We additionally analyzed a Chandra observation to quantify the pulsar's contribution to the total soft X-ray emission detected by NICER, which cannot spatially resolve the pulsar from the surrounding pulsar wind nebula (PWN). The pulsar contribution to the total observed emission represents less than 40-45% of the flux below 0.9 keV, dropping to 3-4% in the 0.9-2.0 keV range and further down to ~2% above 2 keV, where the PWN fully dominates. We find that the X-ray folded profile of the Vela pulsar was not measurably perturbed by the 2021 glitch. We studied separately seven regions of the pulse profile. We found that all of them are well modeled by one or two blackbodies. The temperatures of these hotspots are between $0.79(7) \times 10^{6}$ K $\leq T \leq 4.8^{+0.8}_{-0.6} \times 10^{6}$ K, while their sizes vary between $0.048^{+0.016}_{-0.009}$ km $\leq R \leq 3.9^{+0.9}_{-0.6}$ km, and their luminosities between $5\times10^{30}$ erg/s $\lesssim L < 1\times10^{32}$ erg/s.

papers.title: Communication-Efficient Clustered Federated Learning in Non-IID Wireless Networks
papers.abstract:
Current and emerging mobile networks face increasing privacy, scalability, and performance challenges as distributed learning becomes essential for advanced 6G services. These challenges are amplified by the presence of non-IID data, naturally arising in heterogeneous wireless environments, that degrade the performance of standard Federated Learning (FL) approaches. To address non-IID data across clients, we propose a Clustered Federated Learning (CFL) framework that assigns clients to specialized models during training. Data-domain clustering initializes model-based clustering, enabling identification and exploitation of client similarities without sharing raw data while reducing communication cost.
  Motivated by mmWave beam selection, we evaluate our methods on a wireless simulation dataset (DeepMIMO) and complement it with two non-IID benchmarks (FEMNIST, Rotated CIFAR-10) to isolate different non-IID characteristics. Our best configurations improve accuracy over IFCA by 4.8 pp on DeepMIMO and 10.6 pp on FEMNIST while reducing downlink data volume by 83.1 % on FEMNIST compared to IFCA.
  We demonstrate that different clustering strategies suit different non-IID characteristics. These results show that our CFL methods enable resource-efficient, and high-performance distributed learning in future 6G networks.

papers.title: Teaching a Tree to Recover: Online Distillation of an LLM Supervisor with Counterfactual Replay
papers.abstract: Autonomous mobile robots commonly pair a global planner with a local model predictive controller (MPC), but nonconvex obstacle avoidance and a limited horizon can make the robot freeze in complex layouts. Deciding whether to replan, wait, or call for help is a supervisory decision. Recent work queries a large language model (LLM) supervisor on every anomaly, which is slow and costly. We instead distill the LLM online into a decision tree. After each training episode, counterfactual replay labels recoveries as needed, unnecessary, or harmful. These labels retire unhelpful rules. In simulation, on 20 unseen layouts where the MPC alone freezes, the tree handles at least 18 correctly across all seeds, either by reaching the goal or by calling for help when no feasible path exists. The tree matches both an always-query LLM supervisor and expert-designed rules, while issuing no LLM queries at test time. Handwritten rules cannot anticipate the long tail of situations a physical robot will encounter. Online distillation is a promising remedy: the tree handles familiar cases, and the LLM is consulted only for new ones, whose validated recoveries become new rules. Language models can thus also serve as designers of supervisors rather than only as runtime supervisors.

papers.title: TACFormer: Transformer-Based Generative Model for Target-Conditioned De Novo PROTAC Design
papers.abstract: Targeted protein degradation (TPD) represents a fundamental shift in drug discovery, moving beyond traditional target inhibition toward the event-driven removal of disease-causing proteins. A prominent strategy for TPD is the use of proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs), heterobifunctional molecules that selectively route a protein of interest (POI) to the ubiquitin-proteasome system for degradation. While PROTAC design still relies heavily on trial-and-error synthesis and experimental testing, deep generative models offer a promising means to explore PROTAC chemical space in silico and generate novel molecules. However, many existing generative methods formulate PROTAC design primarily as a linker-generation problem, with POI-binding (warhead) and E3-ligase-binding components fixed in advance. This restricts exploration of the full PROTAC chemical space and often leaves the POI implicit through the predefined warhead, rather than using protein-level information as an explicit conditioning signal during generation. To address these limitations, we propose TACFormer: a transformer-based generative model for target-aware de novo PROTAC design. The model conditions a GPT-style molecular decoder on pretrained ESM-2 representations of POI sequences, allowing POI-level information to steer full-molecule generation. Our results show that TACFormer generates highly novel and chemically diverse PROTACs while showing consistent POI-dependent shifts in generated chemical space. In particular, molecules generated under specific target conditions preferentially populate chemical neighborhoods associated with POIs in the held-out dataset, while extrapolating to novel chemotypes. By natively integrating biological context into the generative process, TACFormer moves PROTAC design toward a more biology-informed exploration of degrader chemical space.

papers.title: Induced representations from the Heisenberg parabolic subgroup of $SL(n+2,\mathbb{R})$
papers.abstract: The group $G = SL(n+2,\R)$ has a parabolic subgroup $P = MAN$ whose unipotent radical is a Heisenberg group. We study representations induced from a character of $P$, and using the Lie algebra action on the space of $K$-finite vectors we find the points of reducibility and the complementary series. We identify solutions to the conformally invariant systems of differential operators as subrepresentations.

papers.title: Optimal subtrees of finite metric graphs
papers.abstract: We consider a metric graph analog of a classical extremal problem for Riemann surfaces studied by Teichm\"uller, Jenkins, Strebel, and others. In particular, we prove that on any finite metric graph with a marked point, there is a unique open subtree which maximizes a metric graph analog of the reduced modulus, and we also give an equivalent characterization of this optimal subtree in terms of balanced harmonic measures.

papers.title: Learned Terminal Costs for Short-Horizon Model Predictive Control of Autonomous Trucks in Interactive Highway Traffic
papers.abstract: Autonomous highway driving for heavy-duty trucks is a challenging control problem. The greater mass, dimensions and intricate dynamics increase the requirements for cooperation from surrounding traffic in critical maneuvers, requiring a careful balance between safety constraints and efficient long-horizon decision making. Model Predictive Control (MPC) provides rigorous constraint satisfaction but relies on terminal cost which can limit its effectiveness at short, computationally affordable horizons. Reinforcement Learning (RL) captures long-term driving behavior but offers no constraint guarantees and tends toward overly conservative policies when trained under sparse collision penalties. In this paper, we propose a hybrid MPC and RL framework for highway driving in autonomous trucks, where a finite-horizon MPC, solved via dynamic programming, uses a pre-trained RL model for terminal cost estimation. We evaluate the framework in a simulation environment with reactive surrounding traffic and compare it against pure MPC with zero terminal cost, rollout with terminal cost estimation using a base policy, and pure RL. Results show that the hybrid approach achieves zero collisions with the lowest cost of any configuration.

papers.title: Calibrating Attention-Based Token Pruning for Efficient Multi-Image Synthesis in UMMs
papers.abstract: Unified Multimodal Models (UMMs) enable powerful multi-image synthesis but incur substantial computation from long visual contexts. While token pruning offers a direct route to accelerating inference, existing methods are primarily adapted from understanding tasks, suffering from insufficient reference image exploration, confused conditional guidance, and pooling-induced ambiguity that degrades generation quality. To address these issues, we propose CATP, the first training-free context-compression method tailored to UMM generation, which \textbf{C}alibrates the discrepancies of general \textbf{A}ttention-based \textbf{T}oken \textbf{P}runing for better quality-efficiency trade-off. Concretely, building on independent layer-wise pruning during denoising, we introduce Guidance-Consistent Pruning (GCP) to synchronize pruning decisions across conditioning branches, and a Taylor-Calibrated Attention Metric (TCAM) that derives a theoretically grounded second-order correction for pooling-induced bias. In addition, a Fast Scoring Operator (FSO) fuses the calibration into tiled online Softmax to reduce pruning cost. Extensive experiments across representative UMMs and benchmarks demonstrate that CATP consistently outperforms state-of-the-art token-reduction methods, achieving up to 2.09$\times$ attention-core speedup.

authors.name: Jiaxin Chen
authors.institution: Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Reaction precedents extend retrosynthetic prediction beyond training coverage
papers.abstract: Reaction precedents guide retrosynthesis, but how far they can compensate for gaps in task-specific training coverage remains unclear. Using 2.71 million reactions, we restricted training and retrieval coverage by transformation or time, then expanded only the retrieval corpus with model parameters fixed. For transformations excluded from training, mean Top-1 accuracy increased from 13.0% to 58.0% on a historical test set and from 4.9% to 23.1% on a temporally held-out test set. For temporal coverage gaps, retrieval expansion enabled a model trained on records before 2017 to match or exceed a non-retrieval model trained on records before 2025 on both test sets. Without task-specific fine-tuning, precedents improved all 14 representative general-purpose models on both test sets and USPTO-50K; the strongest with precedents surpassed all eight representative specialized models. These findings show that inference-time reaction precedents can extend retrosynthetic prediction beyond task-specific training coverage without parameter updates.

authors.name: Ruikang Zhang
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Architecture and Technology

authors.name: Yinfan Wang
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: A five-species counterexample to the Hofbauer--Kon--Saito conjecture on qualitative permanence
papers.abstract: Hofbauer, Kon and Saito (J. Math. Biol. 2008) showed that a Lotka-Volterra interaction matrix $A$ with negative diagonal can be qualitatively permanent only if (C1) every cycle of length $\ge 2$ of $A$ is nonpositive and (C2) every negative cycle contains exactly one negative entry. They conjectured that these conditions are also sufficient, and proved this for $n\le 3$. We give a $5\times 5$ integer matrix with seven nonzero off-diagonal entries that satisfies (C1) and (C2) but is not qualitatively permanent. For an explicit integer growth vector the system has an interior equilibrium, and an asymptotically stable heteroclinic cycle on the boundary of the orthant attracts an open set of interior orbits. Adding non-interacting species gives counterexamples for every $n\ge 5$. The interactions form a one-way feedback loop (two one-sided benefits and one one-sided harm) together with a predator of two prey. The verification is elementary except for one heteroclinic connection, which lies in a face that is not Volterra-Lyapunov stable. For it we prove a connection lemma based on invasion graphs.

authors.name: Halanay Andrei-Dan
authors.institution: Université de Pau et des Pays de l'Adour

papers.title: Sharp $L^4$ Strichartz estimate for the Zakharov--Kuznetsov equation on $\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{T}$
papers.abstract: We prove the local $L^4$ Strichartz estimate without derivative loss for the Zakharov--Kuznetsov flow on $\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{T}$. This reaches the sharp spatial regularity endpoint and implies the embedding $X^{0,b}\hookrightarrow L^4$ for every $b>1/2$. The proof reduces the estimate to a semi-algebraic mixed-measure estimate.

papers.title: Sharp global stability for the hard-sphere Boltzmann equation near equilibrium
papers.abstract: We study the hard-sphere Boltzmann equation near a global Maxwellian and have found the bifurcation between the stability and instability in $H_{x}^{s}$ Sobolev space. We prove a strong-weak type instability result in the $s<1$ regularity regime, and establish the global stability under the regularity $s>1$ via the interplay between the dissipation and dispersive effects. In this intricate competition of dispersion, dissipation, large-velocity growth, and the asymmetric nature of the gain and loss terms, we prove that the instability is jointly generated by the dispersive effect and the loss term structure. To reach the sharp regularity for the global stability, we incorporate the dispersive effect into the dissipative energy framework for the analysis near equilibrium. This hence concludes sharp threshold and provides a complete characterization of global well-posedness near equilibrium.

papers.title: Exponential-Nemytskii Neural Operators: Learning Field Evolution Across Step Sizes
papers.abstract: In variable-step operator learning, agreement at observed step sizes does not by itself determine predictions at other temporal resolutions. We propose an operator whose step-size dependence is prescribed by a first-order Duhamel approximation of semilinear dynamics. It combines exact linear propagation with a local nonlinear function of the field and its derivatives, allowing evaluation below the observation interval without supervision densely sampled across step sizes. Under suitable conditions and at fixed spatial resolution, we prove that agreement between models at two step sizes controls their prediction differences throughout a prescribed range. We also give conditions for local identifiability of both components from two step sizes, supporting interpretation of the learned structure. A latent extension applies the same construction to learned fields. We evaluate the base model on two synthetic problems and the extension on two real datasets against several baselines.

authors.name: Jingye Li
authors.institution: Chongqing University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Sequince: a modular sequential Monte Carlo toolkit
papers.abstract: Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) methods approximate sequences of probability distributions using populations of weighted samples and are widely applicable, including in Bayesian inference and particle filtering. We present sequince, a modular Python toolkit for constructing SMC algorithms from reusable and extensible components. The toolkit provides modular steps for weighting, resampling, mutation, transformation, and control operations that are composed to implement different algorithms. It also includes prebuilt samplers for tempered SMC, persistent sampling and nested sampling via SMC. Its core components follow the Python Array API standard, supporting NumPy, JAX, PyTorch, and CuPy, enabling analyses on CPUs or GPUs. Random-number control and checkpointing support reproducible scientific workflows. This paper describes sequince v0.1.0 and its design as reusable infrastructure for methodological research and application of SMC methods.

papers.title: Sharp $L^2$ stability for anisotropic radial Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg inequalities
papers.abstract: We establish quantitative stability for radial Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg inequalities involving the anisotropic radial derivative and the Minkowski functional of a smooth, strictly convex body in $\mathbb R^N$, $N\ge2$. Here, the convex body need not be origin-symmetric. For the $L^2$-Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg inequality, we establish the sharp stability constant $|b+1-a|$ for $a\ne b+1$, and classify all equality cases in the natural weighted completion spaces, by optimizing over the angular coefficients and a common dilation parameter. We also obtain the sharp stability constants $2$ and $4$ for the scale-invariant and scale-noninvariant $L^2$-Heisenberg inequality, respectively. For $2\le p<\infty$, we also establish weighted stability of the anisotropic radial $L^p$-Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg inequalities when $a\neq b+1$ and $(b+1-a)(N-p(b+1))\geq0$, and the anisotropic radial $L^p$-Heisenberg inequalities. As a byproduct, we establish weighted $L^p$-Poincar\'e inequalities for Gamma measures, which serve as the main tool for our stability estimates.

papers.title: Determining norm-Euclidean complex cubic fields
papers.abstract: We prove that Cavallar and Lemmermeyer's list of $58$ norm-Euclidean complex cubic fields is complete. The proof combines a classical discriminant bound with exact certificates of non-Euclideanity. The unit action reduces their verification to finite lattice enumeration with rigorous interval arithmetic. An independent covering computation confirms norm-Euclideanity for the $58$ fields.

papers.title: Primitive flag-transitive generalized quadrangles
papers.abstract:
Let $\mathcal{Q}$ be a finite thick generalized quadrangle of order $(s,t)$ with a flag-transitive automorphism group $G$. A well-known conjecture of Kantor from the early 1990s asserts that up to duality, $\mathcal{Q}$ is either of classical type, or it is one of two sporadic examples of order $(3,5)$ or $(15,17)$. Although this fundamental problem in finite geometry remains open, it has been resolved in some special cases. For example, a theorem of Buekenhout and Van Maldeghem from 1994 proves Kantor's conjecture under the stronger assumption that $G$ acts distance-transitively on the set of points of $\mathcal{Q}$.
  In this paper, we study Kantor's conjecture in the setting where $G$ acts primitively on both the points and lines of $\mathcal{Q}$. Here a theorem of Bamberg et al. implies that $G$ is almost simple with socle $X$ a finite simple group of Lie type, and several special cases where the Lie rank of $X$ is at most $2$ have recently been settled in a sequence of papers. Our main theorem resolves the problem for all almost simple groups of Lie type, thereby completing the proof of Kantor's conjecture for generalized quadrangles with a flag-transitive automorphism group acting primitively on points and lines.

papers.title: A Hierarchical Online-Compression Approach to Proportional Subsets of Bounded Orthonormal Systems
papers.abstract:
Let $(\phi_i)_{i=1}^n$ be an orthonormal system on a probability space with $\|\phi_i\|_\infty\leq L$. We prove that, for every $2\leq k<n$, there is a set $I$ of at least $n-k$ indices such that $$ \|f\|_2\leq CM_k\sqrt{\log(e+M_k)}\|f\|_1 $$ for every $f$ in the span of $(\phi_i)_{i\in I}$, where $M_k=L\sqrt{\frac{n}{k}\log(2k)}$. This replaces the logarithmic exponent $\frac{5}{2}$ in the corresponding theorem of Gu\'edon, Mendelson, Pajor, and Tomczak-Jaegermann by $\frac{1}{2}$. We also obtain a partition into two sets of cardinality $\frac{n}{2}+O(\sqrt n)$ for which both spans satisfy the resulting norm comparison, and for uniformly bounded systems the proportional estimate is $C\sqrt{\log n\log\log n}$ for sufficiently large $n$.
  This is the third paper in a series systematically using gradient descent as a proof mechanism in harmonic analysis, following the $\Lambda(p)$ and Bernoulli restricted isometry papers of Burstein, Iosevich, and Krause, and the descent here is entropic mirror descent. We represent each function in an $L_1$ ball by a probability measure of controlled relative entropy, and this entropy pays for the corrections to the predictions of its coefficients. Processing the thresholds from large to small, we obtain a single weighted bound for all the corrections, which we turn into a finite description of approximate coefficient squares and then into a conditional Rademacher estimate, and symmetrization completes the argument directly on the $L_1$ ball. We also record consequences for concentration and for recovery from coefficient measurements.

papers.title: Early Dark Energy Crowds Out Interacting Dark Energy
papers.abstract: We investigate whether interacting dark energy can provide additional relief to the Hubble tension once early dark energy (EDE) is present. Considering a cosmology containing EDE, an independent late-time dark energy fluid with an equation of state fixed at $w\simeq-1$ interacting with cold dark matter, and a cosmological constant, we find that the data strongly drive the model toward the non-interacting limit. The best fit effectively reduces to the standard EDE cosmology, where a non-zero EDE component provides most of the required increase in $H_0$, leaving little statistical gain for the interaction. Although energy transfer from dark matter to dark energy can raise $H_0$ further, this limited gain is rapidly outweighed by the deterioration of the fit to low-redshift observations. In particular, since the CMB tightly constrains the early-time physical matter density, any additional energy transfer requires a lower present-day matter abundance. Such low values are strongly disfavored by Type Ia supernovae. We show that this limitation becomes particularly severe once EDE has already raised $H_0$ and that the same mechanism extends to a broad class of post-recombination interactions. Allowing a dynamical dark energy equation of state of the Chevallier-Polarski-Linder form does not alter our conclusions.

papers.title: Sheaves on quoric manifolds
papers.abstract: Quoric manifolds are quaternionic analogues of quasitoric manifolds introduced by Hopkinson. Given a quoric manifold over a simple polytope, we study the stratification induced by the faces of the polytope. We then show that the equivariant derived category of constructible sheaves with respect to the face stratification is equivalent to the derived category of constructible DG-modules over a DG-algebra defined on the orbit space. Finally, we prove that the associated DG-algebra is formal.

papers.title: Testing Extended Exponential Infrared Teleparallel Gravity with CMB, DESI, and PantheonPlus
papers.abstract: We place cosmological constraints on an extended exponential infrared (EExpIR) $f(T)$ teleparallel gravity model using current observational datasets. The extension is characterized by an additional parameter, $b$, which governs the late-time cosmological dynamics. Owing to the existence of two solution branches, phase-space analysis is employed to select the cosmological branch and to establish an appropriate prior range for the new parameter. In this framework, the torsion sector acts as an effective dark-energy component, exhibiting a smooth evolution from a quintessence-like phase to a phantom regime, while recovering the standard cosmological behavior at early times. To constrain the model parameters, we combine early-Universe observations from Planck, ACT, and SPT measurements of the CMB with late-time probes from DESI BAO and PantheonPlus Type Ia supernovae. Using the full dataset, including the SH0ES calibration, we obtain $b=0.573^{+0.016}_{-0.060}$ and $H_0=70.67^{+0.31}_{-0.35}~{\rm km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$ at 68\% CL. Model comparison based on Bayesian evidence reveals that the EExpIR $f(T)$ and the $\Lambda$CDM models are statistically indistinguishable when only CMB data are considered, whereas the inclusion of the full cosmological dataset with SH0ES leads to a weak preference in favor of $\Lambda$CDM.

papers.title: Sharp approximation thresholds for power means of common-subspace volumes
papers.abstract: We study how well a single $k$-dimensional subspace can preserve volume from several positive semidefinite matrices at once. Each matrix is compressed to the subspace and scored by the geometric mean of the eigenvalues of that compression; the scores are aggregated by a weighted power mean of order $p \le 1$. For every fixed $k$ and every fixed rational $p$ we determine the optimal approximation factor: it is achieved by a randomized polynomial-time algorithm, and every larger constant is NP-hard. Above a critical power ($p=-k/2$ over the reals and $p=-k$ over the complex numbers) the factor is an explicit product of Gamma functions. At and below the critical power, every positive constant-factor approximation is NP-hard. The factor comes from a concave relaxation over the positive semidefinite matrices of trace one, which agrees with the volume score at every subspace, followed by ordinary Gaussian rounding. For two rank-$k$ matrices the relaxation is exact, giving a closed-form optimum for Martin means of two subspaces.

papers.title: Upcycling Language Models for Multiple Specialized Domains
papers.abstract: Effective multi-domain adaptation of large language models requires prioritizing relevant domain knowledge while minimizing interference from irrelevant domains. Existing approaches commonly use Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) to train a separate adapter for each domain and combine these adapters within one model. However, they either weight adapters equally regardless of the input domain or dynamically weight adapters while still activating all of them including irrelevant ones. Additionally, while efficient, their low-rank structure limits performance. In contrast, upcycling is a model expansion method that adds experts and a router to a dense Transformer layer offering larger capacity than LoRA approaches. In this paper, we propose Domain-Specialized Upcycling (DS-Upcycling) for multi-domain adaptation. We introduce a new domain-aware supervision that allows the router to effectively learn to distinguish domains by selecting the appropriate experts. During fine-tuning on each new domain, we update only the corresponding expert and router while freezing all other parameters. Experiments show that our method achieves the highest average performance across the adapted domains compared to baselines while retaining general performance. With just 256 examples per domain for router supervision, DS-Upcycling achieves 90-98% routing accuracy after adaptation compared with 43-70% for routers trained without our approach.

papers.title: Positivity of the Mirabolic Quantum Groups
papers.abstract: In this paper, we construct the canonical basis for the modified mirabolic quantum $\mathfrak{sl}_n$. We then study the associated $\dot{U}_v(\mathfrak{sl}_n)$-module and $\dot{U}_v(\mathfrak{sl}_n)$-comodule structures and prove the positivity of this basis with respect to these two structures.

papers.title: Structured Pruning of Feedback Delay Networks
papers.abstract: Feedback delay networks (FDNs) are recursive filter structures used to synthesise artificial reverberation. Their feedback matrix governs both energy exchange between delay lines and the computation required at every sample, making its design central to balancing an FDN's acoustic performance and implementation efficiency. In this work, we develop an FDN-specific structured pruning method that connects these acoustic and computational concerns, allowing high-order dense orthogonal designs to be fitted to efficient implementations. The feedback matrix is replaced by stages of fixed permutations and small orthogonal blocks. We characterise connectivity growth with the network depth and derive exact conditional block updates for matrix fitting, followed by refinement against the reference FDN magnitude response. The resulting factors admit direct vectorised evaluation, with arithmetic cost and coefficient storage scaling linearly with network size for fixed block size and depth. On an Apple M2, the selected staged kernels achieve feedback-multiplication speedups over dense BLAS ranging from approximately threefold to over twentyfold across the tested network sizes, while substantially reducing coefficient storage. Objective metrics and listening tests indicate that the proposed staged approximations closely preserve the spectral and temporal character of their dense references. An analysis of processor utilisation and register reuse explains why execution time depends on more than the operation count. Finally, block size and depth provide practical control over response fidelity, storage, and real-time cost, allowing acoustic design to precede the choice of an efficient implementation.

papers.title: Integrated Sensing and Communication via Channel Knowledge Maps Built from Beam Feedback Coefficients
papers.abstract: Channel knowledge maps (CKMs) support wireless localization by linking channel features to user locations. Detailed channel fingerprints, however, can require substantial storage. This paper proposes a CKM-based localization framework that uses beam feedback coefficients collected during communication. These coefficients serve as compact location fingerprints within the beam management process, without requiring full channel feedback or additional sensing measurements. Using a coarse position prior, the base station searches nearby CKM entries and refines the location estimate through local interpolation. We analyze the relationship between spatial fingerprint variation and localization accuracy, and evaluate the effect of feedback quantization. Simulations show favorable storage--accuracy trade-offs relative to dense and sparsified spectral fingerprinting in the tested multipath environments.

papers.title: On the rise of a Taylor bubble-drop assembly in a vertical tube
papers.abstract: In a liquid-filled vertical tube, a Taylor drop typically rises far more slowly than a Taylor bubble owing to the much larger density and dynamic viscosity of the former. In this work, we demonstrate experimentally and numerically that instead of being slowed down by the attached drop, a Taylor bubble-drop assembly rises at the same velocity as an isolated Taylor bubble, leading to a significantly faster rise of the Taylor drop. We discuss the underlying mechanism and use an analytical model to predict the drop radius within the assembly. This phenomenon offers a means for bubble-assisted rapid transport of an immiscible liquid phase in vertical tubes, with potential applicability in gas-lifting systems in confined environments.

authors.name: Quan Yao
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Human Evaluation with Automatic Scores: Separating Sampling and Estimation Gains
papers.abstract: Automatic judges offer inexpensive information about model outputs, but an evaluation team must decide how to turn that information into fewer human annotations. Scores can guide sampling, correct an estimate, or support adaptive acquisition, and these uses may capture overlapping gains. We compare their incremental value on fixed evaluation pools from three preference datasets, and 19 attributed-question-answering systems. Matched comparisons use the same scores, account for pilot labels and budget rules, and separate acquisition from estimation. Score stratification is a strong reference: after ten-bin stratification, the best fixed local linear correction offers only 1.00--5.27% further MSE reduction in the primary configurations. Unequal allocation offers larger gains in some pools, but can increase error when confident scores conceal variable human outcomes. Comparison on AttributedQA, shrinking learned quotas toward score-only quotas lowers pooled MSE for 17 of 19 systems relative to the score-only procedure, but ordinary pooled 95% intervals cover only 88.09--93.54%. The same shrinkage improves on the score-only reference in only one of eight preference configurations. Ranking experiments further show that lower individual MSE need not improve system selection. These findings support a simple starting procedure, proportional sampling within score strata followed by a stratified human mean, and identify what additional evidence is needed to justify correction or adaptation for the intended evaluation output.

authors.name: Chao Xue
authors.institution: First Affiliated Hospital of Chinese PLA General Hospital

papers.title: A Gasch\"utz Lemma for linear algebraic groups with applications to the Riemann-Hilbert correspondence
papers.abstract: The classical Gasch\"utz Lemma states that for a surjective morphism $G\to H$ of finite groups, generators $h_1,\ldots,h_d$ of $H$ can be lifted to generators $g_1,\ldots,g_d$ of $G$, provided that $G$ can be generated by $d$ elements. We prove an analog of this statement for linear algebraic groups. This has applications to the algebraic-geometric theory of linear differential equations: We show that every regular singular differential embedding problem over the rational function field has a regular singular solution. We also establish a purely algebraic variant of the Riemann-Hilbert correspondence on the punctured projective line that works over any countable algebraically closed field of characteristic zero.

papers.title: Learning Calibrated Confidence for Multi-Agent Collaboration
papers.abstract:
Complex information seeking on the Web often requires collecting evidence from multiple documents and reasoning across them, as in multi-hop question answering. Multi-agent systems address such tasks by dividing work among specialized agents, where upstream agents produce intermediate answers and supporting evidence that downstream agents build upon. However, upstream answers vary in correctness, and most systems provide no quantitative signal about it, leaving the downstream agent to judge whether to trust or verify what it receives based solely on the textual evidence.
  In this paper, we propose MASCAL. Each agent learns to produce a correctness probability for its answer by jointly optimizing task performance and confidence calibration in reinforcement learning; the upstream agent passes this probability at handoff, giving the downstream agent a quantitative basis for its decisions, and the final answer also carries a calibrated probability, quantifying the reliability of the system output. To guide the downstream agent in using this signal during training, we introduce confidence-aware weighting, which increases the learning weight at positions responsive to the upstream probability, so that the agent learns more from decisions where it actively uses the signal. Across three collaboration architectures spanning Web retrieval and reasoning tasks, MASCAL improves task accuracy and calibration quality for both agents, and generalizes to deeper collaboration chains and different model scales. Intervention analysis confirms that upstream confidence affects downstream decision behavior, and the learned final confidence supports selective answering and targeted rechecking.

papers.title: Localizing Concepts in Visual Autoregressive Models
papers.abstract: Understanding the internal routing of visual concepts is crucial for the safe and controllable adaptation of generative models. While concept localization has been widely studied in diffusion models, the emerging paradigm of next-scale visual autoregressive models remains largely unexplored. In this paper, we introduce LoCo, the first model-agnostic framework to localize where and when specific concepts emerge within autoregressive models. Driven by the native coarse-to-fine nature of next-scale generation, our method precisely maps conceptual knowledge across three distinct dimensions: Layer, Scale, and Position. To systematically localize and evaluate concept routing without context bias, we propose LoCoBench, a comprehensive dataset spanning 10 diverse categories. Extensive probing on image and video autoregressive models like Infinity, HunyuanImage-3.0, and InfinityStar shows that the localized positions are both interpretable and causally related to concept emergence. Building on these insights, we apply our localization method to three key applications: concept erasure, model personalization, and adversarial concept injection. Experiments demonstrate that our targeted intervention achieves state-of-the-art performance, substantially reducing computational overhead while preserving benign utility. Overall, our findings offer insights into how conceptual knowledge is routed during autoregressive generation, introducing a practical pathway for more interpretable, efficient, and secure adaptation.

papers.title: Locating and Closing Information Gaps in Multi-Agent Systems
papers.abstract: Multi-step Web tasks often require several LLM agents to gather and combine evidence. The communication graph of a fixed workflow restricts which agents can read each other's outputs: evidence retrieved by one agent may never reach the agent that needs it, leaving an information gap and an incomplete or incorrect answer. Adding a connection can deliver the missing evidence, but can also lead the receiver to adopt an incorrect upstream conclusion that displaces a correct answer; the final output alone does not separate the two. We propose Selective Probing and Link Insertion for Closing information gaps in multi-agent Execution (SPLICE), which locates information gaps per query and decides what to adopt after adding an edge. After the original workflow runs, SPLICE uses the query and node outputs to locate a possible gap, adds one directed edge from a source to a receiver to deliver the relevant evidence, and re-executes the receiver and affected downstream nodes, producing a candidate answer. The adoption decision reads both the final answers of the two runs and the process changes the edit caused inside the workflow: how far the receiver moved, where its new content came from, and whether the change reached the final answer. A selector trained on these process features chooses between adopting the candidate answer and retaining the original. On five benchmarks, SPLICE raises the task score on Web tool use by 8.0% and the mean score on four reasoning and planning benchmarks by 5.7% relative to the static skeleton, at 1.25 to 1.44$\times$ the skeleton's cost, and transfers zero-shot to four unseen backbones.

authors.name: Gangyi Zhang
