authors.name: Krishnamurthy Jyothinagaram
authors.institution: National Institute of Technology Andhra Pradesh

papers.title: Order Maintenance in Worst-Case Constant Time, Verified
papers.abstract: Order maintenance asks for a data structure that keeps a sequence of elements under insertions and deletions and tells which of two elements comes first. We give an algorithm, assembled from published components, that performs each operation in worst-case constant time, and verify it in Lean 4. The algorithm is a program for a random-access machine deeply embedded in Lean, whose interpreter counts every instruction. We prove that the program answers every query as a simple reference specification does, that each operation takes at most a fixed number of steps, independent of the number of elements and of the history, and that after $t$ operations no value it has computed has more than $O(\log t)$ bits, so it runs unchanged on a machine with words of that size. A verified translation that preserves step counts exactly connects the high-level proofs to the machine program, so the interpreter is the only cost model to trust. An unverified native implementation shows the algorithm's practical cost.

papers.title: MRUD: Maximally Redundant Unsigned Digit Number Systems for High-Performance Arithmetic Units
papers.abstract: Signed digit redundant number systems such as Maximally Redundant Signed Digit (MRSD) enable carry-free addition but introduce significant overhead in multiplication due to the presence of both positive and negative bits. While Unsigned Digit Redundant (UDR) systems have shown promise in radix-2, their extension to higher radices remains unexplored. This work presents the first generalized Maximally Redundant Unsigned Digit (MRUD) number systems for high-radix arithmetic, extending UDR representations from radix-2 to radix-$2^h$ while preserving carry-free addition. The proposed framework includes digit encoding, digit extension, arithmetic operations (addition, subtraction, and multiplication), sign inversion, forward/reverse conversion algorithms, overflow/underflow detection, and hardware architectures for both signed and unsigned MRUD representations. Unlike MRSD, which is inherently limited to signed arithmetic, MRUD supports both signed and unsigned representations, similar to conventional binary systems. Evaluations across three multiplier modes---RRR (Redundant inputs, Redundant output), BBR (Binary inputs, Redundant output), and BBB (Binary inputs, Binary output)---as well as Multiply-Accumulate (MAC) units, using the FreePDK 45nm library, demonstrate that MRUD achieves up to 30\% lower delay, 26\% smaller area, and 87\% lower power than MRSD. In BBR mode, MRUD achieves up to 43\% delay reduction over the best conventional architecture for 32$\times$32 operands, while in Multiply-Accumulate (MAC) units, performing reverse conversion only once at the end yields up to 64\% higher throughput than DesignWare and over 150\% higher than Wallace. These results demonstrate that MRUD enables high-radix redundant arithmetic with significantly improved multiplier and MAC performance, making it an efficient alternative to conventional signed digit redundant number systems.

papers.title: AVPS-360: A Spatial Audio-Visual Benchmark for Instance Segmentation and Tracking of Sound-Producing Persons
papers.abstract: Audio-visual instance segmentation (AVIS) segments and tracks individual sound-producing objects in videos. Existing benchmarks predominantly use monaural audio, which lacks inter-channel cues for spatially distinguishing concurrent sound sources. We introduce AVPS-360 (Audio-Visual Person Segmentation 360), a spatial audio-visual benchmark bridging AVIS and sound event localisation and detection (SELD). Built upon STARSS23, it pairs first-order Ambisonics audio with synchronised 360{\deg} video across 230 recordings totalling 10.5 hours. Recordings average 164.0 seconds. The dataset captures intermittent sound production in real-world interactions dominated by speech, alongside laughter, clapping, and footsteps. It provides 31,678 manually reviewed instance masks linked to source identities and sound-event labels. We also present a baseline that integrates spatial audio with visual features for frame-level segmentation and identity association across frames. Experiments on AVPS-360 show that existing AVIS methods struggle with detection and identity association in long recordings with intermittent sound production, while our baseline substantially improves performance in both aspects.

authors.name: Yifu Sun
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: The use of post-quantum cryptography in the automotive context
papers.abstract: This study comparatively evaluates post-quantum cryptography (PQC) in automotive communication scenarios, considering the threat posed by quantum algorithms such as Shor's and Grover's algorithms. The simulations use OMNeT++, Veins, INET, and SUMO on two hardware platforms and examine ML-KEM/CRYSTALS-Kyber, ML-DSA/CRYSTALS-Dilithium, and FALCON. ML-KEM and ML-DSA are finalized NIST standards, whereas FALCON is a NIST-selected candidate pending final standardization. The evaluation considers a rural V2V scenario and an urban V2X scenario supported by a roadside unit. Kyber exhibits low {key encapsulation mechanism (KEM)}\color{black} operation latency, Dilithium provides balanced signature performance, and FALCON has high key-generation and signing costs but efficient verification. The results are interpreted as a comparative assessment among the evaluated PQC schemes under the reported simulation conditions; {a conventional ECDSA/ECDH baseline measured in the same simulation setup is also reported for reference.}\color{black} The resulting dataset can support future studies of cryptographic selection in automotive systems.

papers.title: Revision-Bound Evidence Cuts: Authenticated Queries and Contextual Witness Capacity
papers.abstract: Authentic records can support unauthorized narratives when their qualifications, query scope, or counterevidence are silently dropped. We present revision-bound evidence cuts, a framework for authenticating both supporting and opposing inference obligations across changing source versions. Signed complete-update frontiers permit transport of unaffected certificates, alternative-cut recovery, and an exact certified-reuse radius given by a frontier-hypergraph transversal number. Their source obligations induce an integral model of context-bound authorization. To secure database-derived claims, we introduce an authenticated relational query contract that binds original source records, complete selected bags, counting units, parameters, and aggregates independently of execution strategy. A full-source verifier checks 16,824 Chogha Mish records across SQLite scans, indexes, and materialized views; three valid strategies agree and eight contract/view mutations are rejected. A separate 340-row NISP cohort shows that changing the admitted weighting rule can reverse a comparison while preserving every source record. A frozen English text-to-frame compiler produces qualified evidence receipts, with linguistic accuracy evaluated separately from cryptographic integrity. We also separate logical-source from transport commitments so lossless re-encoding need not invalidate unchanged scientific evidence. The SCENE prototype evaluates signed revisions, authenticated queries, scoped disclosures, and adversarial mutations at scales reaching one million source records. These guarantees rely on declared policies and independently pinned trust roots; they authenticate specified computations and obligations, not historical truth, complete counterevidence, or institutional endorsement.

papers.title: From the Gettier Machine to Justified True Output: A Three-Step Account of Rational Trust in Generative AI
papers.abstract: As generative artificial intelligence (AI) settles into everyday practices of inquiry, an old epistemological question returns in a new guise: when does a proposition a user takes from an AI output become something the user knows, and when is it rational to trust it as such? This paper argues that the characteristic failures of AI-mediated inquiry are precisely those that the justified-true-belief (JTB) tradition and its post-Gettier anti-luck refinements were built to diagnose, and it advances three claims. First, AI outputs inherit neither the presumptive warrant of testimony nor the reliabilist warrant of deterministic tools: unaudited trust in a calculator rests on a type-level reliability record, and for general-purpose generative models there is no type-stable process to which such a record could attach -- a practical form of the generality problem. Second, use that stops at obtaining an output turns generative AI into a Gettier machine: the user's fluency-based seeming of justification is disconnected from the truth of what is believed, and, as a clock running ten times too fast illustrates, sheer speed of production multiplies coincidental hits, inflating the appearance of reliability without improving the standing of any single hit. Third, the remedy is a three-step structure of use -- acquisition, understanding, independent verification -- whose first two steps answer to the classical belief and justification conditions and whose third answers to the post-Gettier sensitivity condition. The result is a stakes-indexed criterion of rational trust, justified true output (JTO), with an everyday test: "Had this been false, would I have noticed?" The criterion is defended against objections from over-demandingness, the extended mind, model improvement, and redundancy.

papers.title: Retrieval Sequencing in a Compact Storage System with Side Access
papers.abstract: In a compact storage system with side access, bins are arranged in adjacent vertical stacks. In each retrieval cycle, bins blocking access are lifted to create a temporary tunnel through which a robot extracts one requested bin from the side. The lifted bins are then lowered again, and the energy expenditure of the cycle equals the number of lifted bins. Given a pick list known in advance, we seek a retrieval order that minimizes total energy expenditure. For every number of stacks, we prove that the total energy separates into an instance constant and a pairwise penalty, and that every energy-optimal order is laminar within each stack. For two stacks, we prove that the retrieval sequencing problem is solvable in polynomial time. For three stacks, we give an exact polynomial-time reduction to a merge problem and characterize which merge-problem instances arise from the storage model. We define a recursive class of retrieval orders and construct a polynomial-time dynamic program that minimizes energy expenditure over this class. Finally, we quantify the additional energy savings from batching, which allows several requested bins to be retrieved in one cycle.

papers.title: Chemodynamical Study and Evidence for Hot Compact Companions to Blue Straggler Stars in Berkeley 31
papers.abstract: We present a detailed study of the open cluster Berkeley 31 using Gaia DR3 astrometry, Gaia-ESO Survey DR5.1 spectroscopy, and multi-wavelength photometry. We identify 329 probable cluster members from their proper motions and trigonometric parallaxes and use them to examine the cluster's fundamental parameters, stellar populations, and Galactic orbit. The cluster is located at a distance of $6024 \pm 181$ pc, with a color excess of $E(B-V)=0.148 \pm 0.047$ mag, and has a mean metallicity of [Fe/H] $=-0.36 \pm 0.04$ dex and $\langle [\alpha/{\rm Fe}] \rangle=0.21 \pm 0.04$ dex. Isochrone fitting gives an age of $3.7 \pm 0.2$ Gyr, consistent with the independent chemical-clock estimate of $3.72 \pm 1.42$ Gyr. The systemic radial velocity is $57.89 \pm 0.08$ km s$^{-1}$. We find that about 38% of the MS stars are unresolved binary candidates with $q \gtrsim 0.5$. We identify 62 BSSs and 2 YSS candidates, including 48 BSSs and both YSSs not previously reported in the literature. We constructed multi-wavelength SEDs for these stars, including Swift/UVOT data for 28 BSSs. Two BSSs show clear ultraviolet excesses and are consistent with compact hot companions, one with a hot WD and the other with a pre-ELM WD. The present orbital parameters give a guiding radius of $12.29 \pm 0.29$ kpc and an eccentricity of $0.11 \pm 0.01$. Comparison with the estimated chemical birth radius indicates a moderate outward shift of the guiding center, with the present orbital position also contributing to the radial displacement. These results consistently describe Berkeley 31 as an intermediate-age, metal-poor outer-disk cluster and place its stellar populations in the context of its Galactic dynamical history.

papers.title: Tan's Contact for Trapped Spin-Orbit-Coupled Fermi Gases at Finite Temperature
papers.abstract: Tan's contact, bridging microscopic features of many-body quantum systems to two-body contact interactions, is pivotal in the description of quantum gases. However, past studies of Tan's contact of the spin-orbit coupled Fermi gases have been exclusively discussed at zero temperature. The thermal effects on that, which cannot be neglected in most experimental conditions, has not been explored so far. Here, through a path integral Monte Carlo (PIMC) study, we show that thermal effects fundamentally alter the scaling relation between spin-orbit coupling (SOC) and Tan's contact. The linear scaling of Tan's contact with respect to the strength of SOC found at zero temperature is drastically undermined by the thermal effects. And a new mechanism based on the competition between the mean occupancy and the energy-reweighted occupancy of the opposite spin fermion pairs within the interaction range has been unveiled, which radically changes the above linear scaling to a non-monotonic dependence. Our work should be useful for future experiments to explore the preternatural thermal effects on Tan's contact of the strongly interacting spin-orbit-coupled Fermi gas.

authors.name: Rui Tian
authors.institution: Tianjin Medical University Cancer Institute and Hospital

authors.name: Dongdong Pu
authors.institution: Southwest University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Shuai Li
authors.institution: VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland

papers.title: ExplainCC: Explaining Correlated Clusters by Node Labels
papers.abstract: An increasingly important requirement for clustering algorithms is that decisions and outcomes need to be clearly understandable for human users. We address this requirement for the Correlation Clustering (CC) problem, in case the objects to be clustered are accompanied by labels. In CC one seeks to partition a set of objects into clusters based on pairwise similarity and dissimilarity information. Our proposed model only considers clusters that can be explained by a label tree, which is essentially a decision tree that partitions the objects according to labels. The goal is to find an explainable partition of the data that minimizes the CC objective function. We formalize this problem from a theoretical viewpoint, and prove several hardness of approximation results, also when constraining the size of the tree. Our proposed greedy method finds locally optimal splits, and works recursively in a top-down approach. To efficiently compute the best split, we carefully maintain certain counters. An experimental evaluation demonstrates its effectiveness. The proposed algorithm processes graphs with over million edges in a few minutes, can find the ground truth in synthetic data, and is able to produce interpretable clusters in real world networks.

papers.title: GradSplat: Gradients Inside the Forward Pass for Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting
papers.abstract: Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting predicts a scene from a few images, but our predictor is less accurate than its own Gaussians optimized per scene on those images. This gap lies mostly in the shape of the Gaussians, their scale and rotation, since optimizing the shape alone recovers almost all of it and opacity and color recover less. Gradient steps on the input views correct this shape, and the model holds these views at inference. Log-anisotropy correction changes the axis ratios of each Gaussian in log space at constant volume, and in-forward gradient refinement renders the Gaussians into the input views and applies the gradient of the photometric loss with a learned recurrent update, first to opacity and color and then to the shape. GradSplat is a feed-forward model that refines its own Gaussians by learned gradient steps inside its forward pass, with no target view. On both complete six-view RealEstate10K protocols, it has the best PSNR and SSIM among nine methods and keeps its accuracy from $6$ to $42$ input views. Without fine-tuning, it is the most accurate on DL3DV and has the best PSNR and SSIM on ScanNet++. The code will be released at https://github.com/Jingong-Chen/GradSplat/.

papers.title: DualGuard: Comprehensive and Efficient Memory Safety across Sequential and Speculative Execution
papers.abstract:
Although decades of research have yielded sophisticated mechanisms for enforcing memory safety, speculative execution can subvert these protections through transient memory operations. Conversely, defenses designed specifically for speculative safety, such as Speculative Load Hardening (SLH), cannot enforce memory safety during non-speculative execution. A naive combination of defenses from both domains raises two fundamental challenges: (1) which combination of otherwise fragmented defenses can ensure dual memory safety under speculative and non-speculative executions? (2) whether such combinations introduce redundant protections that incur unnecessary performance overhead?
  We present DualGuard, a unified framework for dual memory protection under non-speculative and speculative executions. DualGuard systematically analyzes memory behaviors, classifying them into four categories, and further identifies the minimal composition requirements for dual memory safety, which allow us to strategically combine existing mitigations and design new ones to avoid redundant or excessive protections. We implement DualGuard through a combination of static analysis and runtime enforcement within the LLVM infrastructure. Our evaluation demonstrates that DualGuard reduces overhead by 3%-72% compared to naive compositions of fragmented defenses. In some cases, it even incurs lower overhead than approaches that guarantee memory safety solely under either non-speculative or speculative execution.

papers.title: Uncertainty-aware Coarse-to-Fine Main Pancreatic Duct Segmentation for Width Measurement in 3D MRCP
papers.abstract: Assessment of the main pancreatic duct (MPD) from volumetric magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography (MRCP) scans is an essential task for ductal dilatation diagnosis and pancreatic cancer analysis. However, manual assessment is affected by reader variability in which automated analysis may assist. Nevertheless, fully automated and uncertainty-aware MPD analysis from volumetric MRCP remains underexplored area of research. In this study, we propose an automatic and uncertainty-aware deep learning-based pipeline for MPD segmentation and maximum-width analysis from MRCP scans. A coarse localisation model first identifies the ductal region-of-interest, followed by a fine model that segments the MPD within the region. The dataset consists of 256 MPD-segmented MRCP scans from 69 patients. A randomly selected holdout test subset of 14 patients with 55 MRCP volumes was used for evaluation. We employed a five-model cross-validation ensemble for improved performance and uncertainty estimation. The best MPD segmentation performance was 0.634 DSC, 0.744 precision, and 0.593 recall. The mean absolute error for maximum MPD width prediction was 0.355~mm and dilated MPD ($\geq 5$~mm) was detected with 75.0\% sensitivity and 74.4\% specificity. These novel results suggest that automated MPD segmentation can be used to aid MRCP-based duct measurements.

papers.title: Human Activity Recognition using Ceiling-Mounted Multi-Radar Sensors
papers.abstract: Continuous activity monitoring in assisted living should work without cameras or wearable devices. Radar meets this requirement, but most radar studies use a single sensor and activities recorded in isolation, and few deliver results in real time. We present an indoor monitoring system in which point clouds from three ceiling-mounted radar sensors are fused using density-based clustering, movement and posture features are derived for activity classification, and results are shown on a real-time dashboard. In a preliminary study with eight participants performing everyday activities as one continuous scenario, a random forest reached 74% frame-level accuracy with a random 80/20 split and 68% with leave-one-participant-out evaluation. Without position features, accuracy fell to 46% and 44%, indicating partial dependence on room layout, while window-level features without position reached 67% and 65%.

papers.title: Sharp Bounds on Torsional Rigidity of Metric Graphs with Signed Delta-Vertex Strengths
papers.abstract: We study torsional rigidity on finite compact connected metric graphs with real \(\delta\)-vertex strengths in the regime of strictly positive torsion. For a fixed total length \(L>0\), let \(I_+\) be the sum of the positive strengths and \(I_-\) the sum of the magnitudes of the negative strengths, with \(I_+>I_-\). We determine the sharp infimum and the exact threshold for a finite universal supremum. The supremum is finite precisely when \(I_-<I_+/(1+LI_+)\). In this regime, an interval with strengths \(I_+\) and \(-I_-\) at opposite endpoints attains the sharp Saint--Venant bound. At and beyond the threshold, torsional rigidity is unbounded even among three-vertex paths with the same data and strictly positive torsion. The sharp infimum is \(L^2/(I_+-I_-)\) throughout the range \(I_+>I_-\ge0\). It is not attained by any finite graph and is approached by graphs with two vertices joined by increasingly many parallel edges of equal length, preserving both strength totals separately. A vertex-matrix formulation and explicit path examples clarify the relation between strength placement, spectral positivity, and solvability.

papers.title: Measuring Deep Learning Performance - An Empirical Study of Performance Distributions Across Architectures and Tasks
papers.abstract: Context: Non-determinism in deep learning algorithm design and implementation leads to performance variation, meaning model performance is not a single value, but rather a distribution. These model performance distributions are underexplored despite their impact on robustness. Objective: We investigate the robustness of deep learning performance to sources of non-determinism, specifically focusing on how performance distributions differ across various architectures and tasks. Method: We conducted 186 experiments on image classification and time series forecasting architectures. Each experiment was run 100 times with different random seeds to generate performance distributions, resulting in 18,600 runs. Robustness was quantified using metrics for spread, symmetry, and tail risk. Results: Performance distributions are frequently non-Gaussian, particularly in time series forecasting. Model size does not systematically affect robustness -- larger image classification models show fewer outliers but not lower spread, while smaller time series models show lower spread but more extreme underperformers. Training duration does not scale linearly; early stopping effectively balances performance and robustness. Mean performance does not predict robustness - time series forecasting shows moderate correlation while image classification shows none. Time series models produce nearly three times more underperforming outliers than image classification models, indicating substantially higher tail risk. Conclusions: Tail risk poses serious concerns for Trustworthy AI in high-stakes applications. Models performing well on average may exhibit long tails and extreme outliers revealed only through distributional analysis. Mean performance alone should not guide model selection; assessment of spread, symmetry, and tail risk is essential for reliable model assessment where consistent performance is critical.

papers.title: Optimal Encodings for Next/Previous Larger/Smaller Value Queries: A Unified Approach
papers.abstract:
Given a 1D array over a total order and a query position in the array, a next larger value query returns the nearest position to the right whose value is larger than the value at the query position. Next smaller value queries and previous larger/smaller value queries are defined analogously. These queries are closely related to the $k$-th range minimum/maximum problem, which asks for the position of the $k$-th leftmost minimum/maximum value when the query range contains multiple minimum/maximum values.
  In this paper, we consider the encoding problem for answering any arbitrary subfamily of these four queries, where the queries must be answered without accessing the input array. We give a unified approach for obtaining space lower bounds for such encodings. We also obtain data structures for the query subfamilies that match the lower bounds up to lower-order additive terms, while supporting the queries in constant time. Our results generalize and improve several previous results on this problem [Gawrychowski and Nicholson, ICALP-2015; Jo and Satti, TCS-2016; Tsur, IPL-2019; Jo and Kim, Algorithmica-2025].
  In addition, these results give tight bounds on the encoding complexity of all subfamilies of these queries for (1) permutations, (2) arrays without consecutive equal elements, and (3) general arrays.

authors.name: Srinivasa Rao Satti
authors.institution: Norwegian University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Soei: Structured Observability of Evidence and Intent for Multi-Agent AI Software Engineering
papers.abstract: AI coding agents now do long, multi-step and multi-session software work with little supervision. When a developer comes back to that work, the useful question is not what the model said but what was actually done, by whom, and whether it is finished. We study this in three parts. First, we verify Agenttrail, an open-source local observability tool for coding agents, against its source at commit e4ba2da: nine documented constants and mechanisms hold at file-and-line level, two event pipelines are never unified, and its Map service has an unauthenticated local mutation surface. Second, we run a prototype of our system on 45 real coding-agent sessions (102,233 records, 20,577 tool executions, 2,336 human-to-agent episodes). With a blind-audited classifier (precision 83.3% and 96.7%) we estimate that 23.4% (95% CI 17.1 to 35.7) of code-editing episodes end with no independent check after the last edit, and that 57.8% of to-dos the agent marked complete after editing had no proof in between. A 10-minute timing heuristic for session hand-offs recovers 6 of the 24 session pairs that content lineage links. 42% of sessions run longer than 24 hours, 48.1% of transcript bytes lie past a 2 MiB replay bound, and 1,326 records in 16 sessions contain credential-like strings. Third, we propose Soei (Structured Observability of Evidence and Intent): an acknowledgement-aware event schema, a hash-chained local ledger, a W3C PROV-aligned graph, calibrated inference for attribution and lineage, and a verification layer that keeps a claim of completion apart from proof. On the same corpus the ledger is 20% of raw size, holds no content or credentials, verifies at about 126k events/s, detects tampering and replays deterministically. We position the work against concurrent 2026 proposals and define autonomy levels with evidence gates and harness metrics baselined on our data.

authors.name: K S Sarun Kumar
authors.institution: Norwegian University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Statistical Detection of Positional Bias in LLM-Based Recommender Systems: Methodologies and Empirical Evidence
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used as recommendation generators in conversational recommender systems (RS) via retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). This flexible design introduces new sources of structural bias. This paper studies positional bias in top-1 and single-turn LLM-based RS: systematic dependence of the recommended item on the order in which candidates are presented in the prompt. We propose two complementary detection methodologies: (i) POB-ICM, based on contingency matrix analysis and Chi-square independence testing, and (ii) POB-UNBP, a sample-efficient approach derived from a uniformity null model under permutation-based evaluation, enabling stochastic decoding with formal statistical guarantees. Using a controlled RAG testbed for product recommendation, built on a real product catalog, a fixed prompt template and 2000 template-generated user queries with 20 permutations each (40,000 instances), both methodologies reject the null hypothesis of positional independence and uniformity in all evaluated state-of-the-art models. We introduce three complementary metrics -- permutation sensitivity, positional bias, and strong positional bias -- to quantify this effect, the latter targeting cases where the position displaces the recommendation towards clearly less relevant items rather than only choosing among comparably relevant ones. A robustness analysis across candidate-set size and decoding temperature shows that the bias is structural and model-dependent, not an artifact of deterministic decoding or candidate-set size. These results establish positional bias as a measurable, reproducible property of prompt-mediated recommendation pipelines in the evaluated setting and motivate routine auditing and governance controls (e.g., order randomization, standardized prompting) for deployed LLM-based RS. Source code is publicly released.

papers.title: Controllability of Nonlocal Partial Differential Equations
papers.abstract: This chapter provides a short survey of recent developments in the controllability of nonlocal partial differential equations. We first review controllability results for evolution equations involving nonlocal spatial operators. Particular attention is devoted to unique continuation properties, observability inequalities, and Carleman estimates in establishing controllability properties. We then discuss controllability issues for partial differential equations with memory terms, highlighting how memory effects influence reachable states, null controllability, and exact controllability. We review and compare various analytical techniques developed to overcome the difficulties arising from the nonlocal structure. We also provide a critical assessment of some of these methods. Throughout the chapter, we emphasize the interplay between controllability and observability, the adaptation of classical control methods to nonlocal settings, and the distinctive phenomena that arise in comparison with local equations. We then discuss geometric inequalities and their role in the controllability of diffusion models. The chapter concludes with a discussion of current challenges and several open problems, aiming to provide directions for future research.

papers.title: A Geometry-Induced Finite Warburg element for Reversible Diffusion Impedance at Microdisk Electrodes
papers.abstract: A compact analytical representation is developed for the diffusion impedance of a disk electrode under reversible conditions, obtained by transforming the chronoamperometric relaxation function into the frequency domain. A Pad\'{e} approximant is constructed for the uniform-concentration boundary condition, preserving the finite low-frequency diffusion resistance of the steady-state disk current and the high-frequency Cottrell regime. It is extended to reactions in which both oxidized and reduced species contribute, with unequal diffusion coefficients and surface concentrations. Its accuracy is quantified against converged numerical solutions, including an exact solution of the coupled problem with finite-rate kinetics. The approximant reproduces the Saito resistance and the $45^{\circ}$ Warburg phase exactly; its modulus is within 0.6\% of the converged solution for $\omega a^2/D\le12$ and 7\% below the Cottrell amplitude at high frequency. The uniform-concentration and uniform-flux boundary conditions both give a diffusion impedance of geometric origin, but differ by up to 11\% in modulus because each couples differently to the spreading diffusion field; a criterion based on the rate constant and the disk radius delineates where each applies. The exact solution shows that this crossover is broad and that the decomposition into a charge-transfer resistance and a diffusion impedance is accurate to about 5\% for $1\le2k^0a/D\le100$. Fitted to a published spectrum of a platinum microdisk, it reproduces the reported diffusion coefficient within 1\%, while the two limiting elements lie 4.8\% below and 4.1\% above it. The element is a practical tool for microdisk impedance analysis.

authors.name: Kazuhiko Seki
authors.institution: National Center of Neurology and Psychiatry

papers.title: Understanding the origin of silver in metal-poor stars based on the non-local thermodynamic equilibrium analysis of Ag I lines
papers.abstract: Silver is a poorly observed neutron-capture element, and understanding its Galactic production history requires accurate abundances for stellar samples covering a broad metallicity range. We refined the method for calculating stellar Ag abundances by considering the non-local thermodynamic equilibrium (NLTE) line formation for Ag I. A comprehensive model atom of silver was built from the atomic data available in the literature, including recent data on inelastic Ag I + H I collisions. We derived abundances using the high-resolution spectra and the synthetic spectrum method with the one-dimensional model atmospheres. From two Ag I lines in the solar spectrum we obtained the NLTE abundances log epsilon = 1.15 and 1.10 for different treatments of collisions with hydrogen atoms. The NLTE abundances of Ag were determined for the first time for 41 stars in the -2.74 <= [Fe/H] <= -0.56 metallicity range. The NLTE abundance corrections for Ag I 3382 A were found to be larger for the giants (up to 0.92~dex) than the dwarfs (up to 0.51~dex). In NLTE, Ag in our sample stars is enhanced relatively to Fe and the [Ag/Fe] Galactic trend is very similar to that for [Eu/Fe]; the [Ag/Eu], [Ag/Ba], and [Ag/Sr] abundance ratios of the r-II stars CS22892-052 and CS31082-001 agree very well with the r-process model of Prantzos et al. (2020); the -1.6 < [Fe/H] <= -0.56 stars have close-to-solar [Ag/Eu] ratios. We conclude that production of silver was dominated by the main r-process throughout the metallicity range we investigated, with the main s-process contribution of not larger than 20% for [Fe/H] > -1.6.

papers.title: Automated identification of quasi-BIC modes in disordered resonator chains using spatial field envelopes and resonance descriptors
papers.abstract: Structural disorder turns bound states in the continuum (BICs) into quasi-BIC resonances and mixes them with spectrally close eigenmodes, so the target mode must be identified anew in every disorder realization. We develop an automated procedure for this task and test it on a chain of 50 ceramic disks, where disorder reorders the standing-wave eigenmodes at the edge of the BIC band: at disorder amplitude $\sigma=0.05$, the highest-quality-factor ($Q$) mode is the target in only 45\% of realizations, and above $\sigma\approx0.06$ the highest-frequency mode is no longer the target. The target is identified from the spatial envelope of its field and its resonance parameters by an ensemble of a convolutional--recurrent neural network and two gradient-boosted decision-tree models. On 299 held-out realizations, the ensemble selects the target in 82.6\% of cases, against 60.9\% and 49.5\% for the highest-frequency and highest-$Q$ rules, and in 69.5\% of cases for $\sigma\ge0.09$, where the best of these rules reaches 57.6\%. The mean $Q$ of the selected modes follows that of the manually labeled modes ($\langle Q\rangle\propto\sigma^{k}$, $k=-0.80\pm0.05$ versus $-0.86\pm0.04$). After adaptation on 50 labeled realizations, the workflow identifies the quasi-BIC of a Ge$_2$Sb$_2$Te$_5$ bar metasurface in 98--100\% of labeled cases, including a lossy phase where $Q$ does not distinguish the mode.

papers.title: A polynomial method over formal power series
papers.abstract: We give new upper bounds on families of integer vectors with prescribed coordinate multiplicities and a forbidden scalar product. Our method uses coefficient functions over formal power series and recovers the Frankl--Wilson bound for binary vectors. For vectors in $\{-1,0,1\}^n$, we obtain an exponential improvement over the ordinary polynomial count in a wide range; in certain regimes, we determine the lower limit of the exponential base. We use the new bounds to make progress on several questions in combinatorial geometry. In particular, we improve the base of the exponent in Borsuk's partition problem: we construct finite subsets of $\mathbb R^N$ requiring at least $(1.37+o(1))^{\sqrt N}$ parts of smaller diameter for all sufficiently large $N$, and obtain a base of $1.3839$ along a subsequence of dimensions.

papers.title: Step Recursion: Rational Strides and Exact Inclusion Orders over the Reals
papers.abstract: We study finite-terminating, address-only step recursion on the nonnegative reals, from zero, unit successor and projections. For reduced positive rational strides $s=a/q$ and $t=b/v$, we prove $\mathcal{C}s\subseteq\mathcal{C}t$ if and only if $q$ divides $v$, for both the bounded and unbounded algebras $\mathcal{C}\in{\mathcal{B},\mathcal{U}}$. The bounded compiler preserves earlier global majorants on every auxiliary input. Mixed rational stride sets are classified by least common denominators and supernatural denominators. Primitive-recursive translated-coordinate grid codes characterize the unbounded algebras and yield $\mathcal{U}{1/q}\cap\mathcal{U}{1/v}=\mathcal{U}{1/\gcd(q,v)}$. For bounded intersections, we prove an exact reduction: all corresponding identities hold if and only if the single identity $\mathcal{B}{1/2}\cap\mathcal{B}_{1/3}=\mathcal{B}_1$ holds, equivalently if the Boolean parts of the integer successor and addition algebras under scalar bounded recursion coincide. A Boolean reconstruction reduces general functions to predicates; a clipped fine-grid simulation with a frozen global resource bound identifies the union of predicate precision classes with the addition level. These reductions do not decide the resulting predicate equality, so literal bounded intersections remain unresolved. We also prove that unbounded-program equality is $\Pi^0_1$-complete and extensional bounded-algebra membership is $\Sigma^0_2$-complete. The model has no free real arithmetic or Zeno limits; semantic majorant validity is distinguished from syntax transformation.

papers.title: Step Recursion: Exact Membership Spectra, Mixed Strides, and Collapse
papers.abstract: For a strictly increasing $G:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ with $G(0)\geq 1$, we study minimal-basis function algebras generated by recursion along generalized inverses of its iterates. Bounded recursion requires an earlier pointwise majorant; unbounded recursion has no such requirement. If the orbit $G^{[t]}(0)$ has no polynomial upper bound, we obtain exact fixed-function membership spectra, reverse-divisibility inclusion, and indexed intersections that need not be single-stride algebras. Every finite divisibility-downset is realized in both regimes, and mixed strides admit fixed functions expressing any finite monotone Boolean condition on their additive stride monoid. For every generator, the realized bounded spectra form a bounded meet-semilattice: a construction sharing a bounding input coordinate realizes finite intersections without an unrestricted selector. Polynomial orbit growth is equivalent to definability of each of ordinary predecessor, unary doubling, and addition in any fixed unbounded stride algebra. In this case the algebra is ordinary primitive recursion relative to its inverse map, giving full collapse for primitive-recursive $G$. Ordinary predecessor belongs to a bounded stride algebra exactly when the orbit is polynomially bounded and $G$ has bounded successive differences; equivalently, ordinary bounded recursion embeds. A locality obstruction explains the additional bounded requirement, and two primitive-recursive generators with quadratic orbits have opposite bounded collapse behavior.

papers.title: On the gauge-invariant orbital angular momentum of vector optical vortices in the paraxial approximation and beyond
papers.abstract: In this paper we present a gauge-invariant formalism for describing the spin and orbital angular momenta of scalar and vector optical vortices. The correction term, arising from consistent incorporation of the transverse vector potential's nonlocality, restores gauge invariance and makes it possible to separate the total angular momentum into spin and orbital components. We propose a method for calculating the orbital and spin angular momenta of multimode vector vortex fields and show that the orbital angular momentum of such beams contains two qualitatively different components. The polarization-independent contribution to the orbital angular momentum is related to the topological charge that determines the order of the phase singularity, while the polarization-dependent one is proportional to the helical topological charge that determines the spatial inhomogeneity of the polarization. We also discuss the quantization procedure for fields with spatially inhomogeneous polarization in terms of modes with a helical topological charge, and examine the limits of applicability of the proposed formalism.

papers.title: Uniqueness and comparison principle for Trudinger's parabolic equation with H\"older continuous boundary values
papers.abstract:
For every $p > 1$, we establish uniqueness and comparison principle for Trudinger's parabolic equation \[
  \partial_t (|u|^{p-2}u) = \text{div}(|\nabla u|^{p-2}\nabla u) \quad \text{in } \Omega \times (0,\text{T}), \] assuming suitable H\"older regularity for the boundary values. Our comparison principle applies to sign-changing weak sub- and supersolutions. As an application, we obtain uniqueness of weak solutions to Cauchy--Dirichlet problems when the lateral boundary data is suitably H\"older continuous in time. In particular, Lipschitz continuous boundary values are covered.

papers.title: Attention, Dynamic Wave and Hybrid Sequence Mixers in Language Models
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) rely on Multi-Head Attention (MHA) for sequence modeling, but scaling to long contexts is constrained by the quadratic cost of attention, motivating sub-quadratic recurrent alternatives. This paper formalizes a Dynamic Wave recurrent layer, based on input-dependent exponential damping and cosine phase modulation, and evaluates three 10.94M-parameter configurations (Pure Transformer, Pure Wave, and Hybrid Wave-Attention) on TinyStories under perplexity, latency, throughput and peak VRAM profiling up to 4096 tokens. The Hybrid configuration reaches the best perplexity, 5.95 on the full held-out split against 6.93 for the Transformer and 7.26 for Pure Wave. The efficiency picture, however, is governed by implementation rather than by architecture. Against an unfused attention baseline, Pure Wave uses 78.7% less peak VRAM at a 4096-token context (1404.3 MB vs. 6601.6 MB); against a fused scaled-dot-product attention kernel the same comparison yields no advantage at all (1404.3 MB vs. 1403.6 MB), and in training mode Pure Wave is 8.3% more expensive than the Transformer. Likewise, hoisting elementwise terms out of the recurrence loop speeds the layer up 2.53-fold with no custom kernel, reducing its latency gap to attention from 2.48-fold to 1.12-fold. A hybrid stack is found to inherit the cost of its more expensive mixer rather than the advantage of its cheaper one, its peak VRAM matching the Pure Transformer to within 0.1%. A closed-form memory model reproduces these measurements and predicts the context length beyond which attention overtakes the vocabulary projection. The findings indicate that reported efficiency gains for recurrent attention replacements must be stated relative to a named attention backend and a named implementation, and that hybridization is best justified on quality grounds.

authors.name: Dmytro Babarytskyi
authors.institution: Kharkiv National University of Radio Electronics

papers.title: Inverse scattering problem for the fifth-order Schr${\rm\bf\ddot{o}}$dinger operator on the whole axis
papers.abstract: A method of solution for the inverse scattering problem for the linear fifth order Schr${\rm\ddot{o}}$dinger operator is found. Two closed systems of linear singular integral equations are obtained. From solutions to these equations, potential on the left and right half-axes is restored unambiguously.

authors.name: Vladimir A. Zolotarev
authors.institution: B. Verkin Institute for Low Temperature Physics and Engineering of the National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine

papers.title: Tangential center problem for planar Hamiltonian differential equations
papers.abstract: Consider a planar Hamiltonian differential equation with a nondegenerate center at the origin. The Tangential Center Problem asks for a characterization of polynomial perturbations for which the center persists at first order. This problem plays a fundamental role in the study of the center-focus problem. We propose an effective algorithmic approach to the Tangential Center Problem for planar polynomial Hamiltonian differential equations. Using this approach, we obtain a complete solution of the quadratic Tangential Center Problem. We further apply it to a non-generic family of cubic Hamiltonian differential equations containing the planar Hamiltonian Lotka--Volterra equation. For a general cubic polynomial perturbation, we derive necessary and sufficient conditions for the vanishing of the corresponding first Poincar\'e--Pontryagin--Melnikov function and characterize all tangential centers.

papers.title: Symmetries and exact solutions of stochastic differential equations: the CIR model
papers.abstract: It is well known that in the celebrated Cox-Ingersoll-Ross process for interest rates there exists a critical relation among the model parameters. In the present work, we explain this critical relation by studying the symmetries of the stochastic differential equation and compute the solution of the model using this symmetry. In this way we also recover results of a recent paper where this property has been studied within a broader context by analyzing the relationships among the symmetries of stochastic differential equations and their corresponding forward Kolmogorov equations.

papers.title: An Introduction to the Obstacle Problem
papers.abstract: We give a self-contained account of the classical obstacle problem, written for graduate students who wish to enter the field of free boundary problems. Starting from a one-dimensional model and an explicit radially symmetric example, we set up the variational problem, show that minimizers exist and are unique, and prove interior $W^{2,p}$-regularity as well as the optimal $C^{1,1}$-regularity. The second half of the notes is devoted to the free boundary: we prove that it is porous, introduce blow-up limits, and use the Alt-Caffarelli-Friedman monotonicity formula to show that every free boundary point is either regular or singular. These notes grew out of a mini-course at the Rio Summer School on PDEs in 2020, and they are meant to be read alongside, not instead of, the monograph by Petrosyan, Shahgholian, and Uraltseva.

papers.intro:
Free boundary problems (FBPs) form one of the most active areas in the analysis of partial differential equations (PDEs). They draw on classical PDE theory, functional analysis, geometric measure theory, and topology, and they arise in applications ranging from physics and biology to finance and engineering.

Free boundary problems (FBPs) form one of the most active areas in the analysis of partial differential equations (PDEs). They draw on classical PDE theory, functional analysis, geometric measure theory, and topology, and they arise in applications ranging from physics and biology to finance and engineering.

Rather than surveying the whole field, these notes treat a single problem in detail: the obstacle problem, arguably the best-known free boundary problem of all. One looks for a function that minimizes the Dirichlet energy among all functions lying above a given obstacle; the free boundary is the interface where the minimizer leaves the obstacle. Our aim is that the reader comes away with ideas and techniques that carry over to other FBPs and related questions.

To see what distinguishes a free boundary problem, think of heat flowing through a wooden table. Write uu for the temperature, Ω\Omega for the table, and ∂Ω\partial\Omega for its boundary. To see what distinguishes a free boundary problem, think of heat flowing through a wooden table. Write uu for the temperature, Ω\Omega for the table, and ∂Ω\partial\Omega for its boundary. Apart from a negligible thermal expansion, the table keeps its shape, so Ω\Omega is a fixed domain and uu is the only unknown.

Suppose instead that the table is made of ice. As it melts, its shape changes over time, and the temperature uu depends on how ∂Ω\partial\Omega moves. At the same time, the motion of ∂Ω\partial\Omega depends on uu, since the parts of the table that receive more heat melt faster.

So for the wooden table only uu has to be found, while for the ice table both uu and ∂Ω\partial\Omega are unknown. This is the essential difference between a PDE in a fixed domain and a free boundary problem. The coupling between uu and ∂Ω\partial\Omega makes the analysis considerably harder, and understanding the geometry and regularity of ∂Ω\partial\Omega is one of the central challenges.

papers.title: Sharp Adams inequality for Critical Biharmonic Equations with Hardy--H\'enon Weights in $\mathbb{R}^4$
papers.abstract: We study a class of weighted fourth-order elliptic problems in \(\mathbb{R}^4\) driven by the biharmonic operator and involving Hardy--H\'enon type potentials. The nonlinear term has critical exponential growth in the sense of an Adams-type inequality. The weights \(|x|^a\) and \(|x|^b\) allow us to incorporate singular, vanishing, and unbounded effects in a unified variational framework. We introduce a suitable weighted function space, establish Sobolev-type embeddings, and prove an Adams-type inequality adapted to this setting. Under appropriate structural assumptions on the nonlinearity, we prove the existence of nontrivial weak solutions. We also obtain regularity properties and derive a Pohozaev identity, which leads to a nonexistence result.

authors.name: J. Carvalho
authors.institution: Centro de Física da Universidade de Coimbra

papers.title: Clean Sheets and Checkpoints: Evidence Complexity for Certifying Sequential Agent Risk
papers.abstract: Dangerous-capability evaluations often test an AI agent from prepared states at ordered milestones. A clean sheet records no successes. What it certifies about a campaign of $B$ attempts depends on what a failed attempt erases. We model the task as a chain of $k$ milestones divided into checkpoint segments and ask how many zero audit responses certify, at level $\alpha$, a completion probability of at most $\epsilon$. For segments chosen before the audit, counting possible completion windows gives a certificate for any specified budget. The bound also covers adaptive deployment processes that follow the chain's transitions, provided their success probabilities after every complete history are capped by the corresponding audit success probabilities. The audit does not test this transport assumption. In rare-risk phase interiors, each segment is either rarely completed within the budget (active) or nearly always completed (free). The minimum expected number of zero responses is asymptotic to $\log(1/\alpha)\,(B^a/(a!\,\epsilon))^{1/K_A}$, where the $a$ active segments contain $K_A$ milestones and are those at least as long as a budget-dependent threshold. The certificate attains this constant. Every asymptotically optimal evaluator must divide its expected response count equally among active milestones in the limit, with a vanishing share elsewhere. Where a single segment passes from active to free, each of its milestones receives a smaller limiting share than an active milestone; a crossover-aware certificate attains the optimal constant. For selected segments with known or unqueried prefix steps, counting failed cycles can sharpen the certificate.

papers.title: Sharp regularity for the anisotropic fractional Laplacian with Morrey data
papers.abstract: We obtain sharp regularity for the anisotropic fractional Laplace equation with a right-hand side belonging to a Morrey space. We derive local $C^{\sigma+\lambda-n}-$regularity of solutions when $\sigma+\lambda-n\neq1$, where $\sigma\in(0,2)$ is the order of the operator and $\lambda\in(n-\sigma,n)$ is the Morrey decay rate of the right-hand side. In the case $\sigma+\lambda-n=1$, we show that solutions are locally in the Zygmund class, and hence are Log-Lipschitz continuous. Explicit examples attest to the sharpness of the conditions.

authors.name: Rafayel Teymurazyan
authors.institution: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Inexact PDHG for Large-Scale Semidefinite Programming
papers.abstract: First-order methods, such as the primal-dual hybrid gradient (PDHG) method, have recently been explored for large-scale semidefinite programming (SDP). However, exact projections can be computationally prohibitive, motivating inexact projections using conditional gradient methods. Although computationally cheap and projection-free, these methods typically converge sublinearly. Recent variants, such as Spectrahedron Frank-Wolfe (Garber, 2026), achieve linear convergence in expectation near the optimal face of the spectrahedron. We develop an inexact PDHG framework with tractable spectrahedral projections using two techniques: (i) adaptive error tolerances that avoid unnecessary inner iterations while guaranteeing convergence, and (ii) a heuristic spectral warm start based on the Lanczos algorithm that accelerates Spectrahedron Frank-Wolfe by initializing near the optimal face. We establish an O(1/t) convergence rate for PDHG in the presence of projection errors and estimate the total number of inner iterations required for convergence. Experiments on large-scale SDP instances demonstrate that combining spectral warm starts with Spectrahedron Frank-Wolfe outperforms Lanczos-based inexact projections.

papers.title: GARDEN: Generalist Autonomous Reward Design Through Evidence Navigation for Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) enables teams of agents, such as robots and autonomous vehicles, to learn coordinated behavior, but what such teams learn is largely determined by their reward function. Because task success alone provides too little guidance for learning, intermediate rewards are usually designed by hand, and this effort must often be repeated whenever the environment or the team changes. Large language models (LLMs) can automate the effort by writing reward functions as code, yet the resulting rewards are typically designed and tested in a single setting. To enable their reuse across settings, GARDEN (Generalist Autonomous Reward Design through Evidence Navigation) is proposed, in which one reward program is developed for a family of related scenarios and transferred, unchanged, to scenarios that were not available during its design. During development, environment code, training records, and agent behavior are investigated by an LLM reward engineer, and draft rewards are tested in trial training runs, while the learning algorithm and the rule for selecting the final reward are held fixed. On unseen scenarios of the Overcooked and SMAX benchmarks, task returns were increased by 58.2% and 52.5% over the default rewards on two kitchen layouts, and the mean win rate in two combat scenarios was raised from 51.0% to 89.9%. Under matched candidate and probe budgets, this exceeded the 84.2% and 79.2% obtained with fixed diagnostic feedback and Eureka-inspired reward reflection. These results show that a single autonomously engineered reward can be reused effectively across related cooperative scenarios.

papers.title: Generation of discrete breathers from linear to nonlinear Anderson disorder in electrical lattices
papers.abstract: We investigate linear and nonlinear localization in a disordered electrical lattice composed of coupled LC resonators. In the linear regime, the normal-mode spectrum and spatial voltage profiles are characterized theoretically and experimentally, revealing strongly localized Anderson modes induced by capacitive disorder. Good agreement is found between numerical predictions and experimental measurements of resonance frequencies, spatial profiles, inverse participation ratios, and localization lengths. Nonlinearity is introduced through varactor diodes, allowing the numerical continuation of a selected Anderson-localized mode into a family of discrete breathers. Floquet analysis indicates that these nonlinear localized solutions remain spectrally stable over the investigated frequency range, while their spatial localization evolves with increasing amplitude. Experimental measurements reveal nonlinear resonance bending, frequency shifts, and hysteresis, in qualitative agreement with the predicted nonlinear behavior. These results provide numerical evidence for the emergence of stable, disorder-pinned discrete breathers from Anderson-localized modes, supported by experimental observations of the associated nonlinear resonant response, and highlight the interplay between disorder and nonlinearity in electrical lattices.

papers.title: You Don't Need Aligned Representations: Knowledge Distillation via Random Prototype Spaces
papers.abstract: A widely held assumption in knowledge distillation is that teacher and student representations must occupy a compatible or explicitly aligned feature space. We propose RPKD (Random Prototype Knowledge Distillation), which discards this assumption by comparing both networks against a shared bank of randomly initialized, frozen prototype vectors. Alignment is therefore carried out in an external reference space rather than in the teacher's native feature coordinates: the teacher side is projected by fixed random maps that carry no trainable parameters, and only the student adapts. Two branches handle the transfer: a logit branch aligning global prototype similarity distributions and a feature branch matching spatially-resolved prototype activation maps. Both operate within the same fixed prototype space, which can be interpreted as a random feature embedding that approximately preserves inter-sample similarity structure, so the prototype bank and the distillation objective stay unchanged across teacher-student pairs while only the input projections are instantiated per architecture. In low-category settings, decoupling the prototype vocabulary from the task label space yields richer supervision than the label space alone, an advantage absent from logit-based methods, whose supervisory signal collapses as class count shrinks. This advantage is especially relevant in real-world scenarios where the label space is typically constrained. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of RPKD, achieving a maximum gain of +7.98% over OFA on CIFAR-100, +12.44% on ImageNet-100, and +1.28% on ImageNet-1K. Source code is available at https://github.com/HamzaEtcibasi/RPKD

papers.title: Guidance-Coupled Nullspace Drifting for One-Step Medical Image Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Generative reconstruction can recover high-quality images from undersampled acquisitions, but state-of-the-art generative priors commonly rely on iterative sampling. Reducing the number of iterations lowers inference cost but also removes opportunities for progressive distributional refinement, making it difficult to retain image realism without sacrificing reconstruction fidelity. Drift modeling offers an alternative by shifting progressive refinement to training, thereby enabling one-step sampling without an iterative inference trajectory. Existing drifting methods, however, do not account for the imaging operator when modeling distributional drift. We propose DriftRecon, a generative method for one-step medical image reconstruction that performs drifting directly in the nullspace of the imaging operator. DriftRecon uses nullspace-restricted noise to construct training samples and a multiscale generator that incorporates measurement conditioning across resolution levels, with its generated component projected onto the operator nullspace. To control the fidelity--realism trade-off at inference, a conditional guidance parameter continuously steers the same generator between measurement-conditioned and unconditional generation. We derive a guidance-dependent similarity-kernel temperature schedule that preserves the guidance-weighted mass receiving strengthened supervision, thereby progressively localizing drift interactions as guidance increases to limit the associated loss of reconstruction fidelity. Experiments in sparse-view CT and accelerated MRI reconstruction show that DriftRecon outperforms established generative reconstruction methods and recent drifting models while producing reconstructions in a single forward pass.

papers.title: BridgeRouter: Gain-Aware Instance Routing over Cross-Modal Bridge Portfolios
papers.abstract: Lightweight representation bridges make pretrained, task-adapted EEG foundation models executable on other biosignal modalities without retraining their backbones. However, selecting a single bridge pathway globally assigns every instance to the same transfer route and ignores complementary errors across routes. We therefore formulate multi-bridge transfer as an instance-level algorithm-selection problem and introduce BridgeRouter, a gain-aware router over a portfolio of frozen cross-modal pathways. A validation-selected Single Best Solver (SBS) serves as a protected default route. During training, task labels are used to compute the reduction in negative log-likelihood provided by each alternative route relative to the SBS, and a lightweight MLP predicts these route-specific gains from a target-modality representation extracted by a frozen encoder. At inference, BridgeRouter observes only the target modality, requires neither EEG, task labels, nor predictions from all candidate routes, and executes exactly one bridge pathway: the route with the largest predicted gain when that gain exceeds a validation-calibrated threshold, and the SBS otherwise. We evaluate seven EEG foundation-model bridge pathways for EMG-based freezing-of-gait detection on FOG and ECG-based sleep classification on ISRUC. Across five seeds, BridgeRouter achieves $81.38\pm1.11\%$ balanced accuracy on FOG, improving over the BIOT SBS by $11.49$ percentage points, and $62.92\pm2.17\%$ on ISRUC, improving over the CBraMod SBS by $3.83$ points. Per-instance bridge oracles reach $99.96\%$ and $78.61\%$, respectively, revealing substantial remaining portfolio headroom. These results show that anchor-relative gain prediction can convert complementary cross-modal bridge behavior into deployable instance-level routing improvements while retaining single-route inference.

papers.title: When Does GenAI Use Support Critical Thinking? A Cross-Cultural Structural Account of Transactive Memory with GenAI
papers.abstract: Whether generative AI (GenAI) use helps or hinders critical thinking remains contested, and existing accounts emphasize exposure to the tool rather than how a person structures their engagement with it. Extending Transactive Memory Systems (TMS) theory to human-AI partnerships, we test a structural account of critical thinking in GenAI-assisted academic work among 891 college students in the United States and T\"urkiye. Self-appraised thinking ability and confidence in the partnership shaped how much practical experience a person built up with GenAI, but neither predicted critical thinking directly. That experience mattered only through two downstream behaviors, dividing and coordinating cognitive labor with the tool, and actively reworking its output rather than accepting it as given. A multigroup comparison found this structure largely invariant, with two theoretically interpretable exceptions. This study offers a structural, TMS-based account of critical thinking in GenAI-assisted work.

papers.title: TensorSpectra: Bridging the Spectral and Tensor Worlds for High-Dimensional PDEs
papers.abstract: High-dimensional partial differential equations (PDEs) remain challenging for spectral methods due to the exponential growth of multidimensional coefficient spaces. We propose TensorSpectra, a low-rank spectral framework that directly parameterizes spectral coefficient tensors in canonical polyadic (CP) form, reducing representation complexity from $\mathcal{O}(N^d)$ to $\mathcal{O}(dNr)$. TensorSpectra combines structure-preserving spectral calculus, de-aliased nonlinear interactions, operator-aware residual weighting, and progressive low-rank corrections to enable efficient PDEs solving in compressed coefficient space. We further establish a theoretical framework connecting spectral truncation, low-rank approximation, and optimization errors. Extensive experiments across five PDE families and 24 benchmark configurations demonstrate State-Of-The-Art accuracy among five representative baselines, with TensorSpectra consistently achieving the lowest relative $L^2$ errors. More broadly, our findings offer a new perspective on high-dimensional PDEs solving, suggesting that exploiting intrinsic low-rank structure in spectral coefficient space provides a viable alternative to conventional physical-space approaches.

authors.name: Bingcheng Hu
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Ivan Oseledets
authors.institution: Skolkovo Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Robustness of Chatbot LLM Judgments of Presidential Actions and Hypothetical Reforms
papers.abstract: Chatbots are increasingly consulted about public affairs, and their judgments of policies are useful only if they are robust. We measure this robustness in the setting of an ordinary user, through consumer chat interfaces. For 30 days, five chatbot configurations (Mistral, Gemini Flash, Claude Sonnet, and Claude Opus at two effort settings) were asked twice a day to score the long-term effect on the United States of 40 actions of the last four presidential administrations and of 15 hypothetical reforms, each with a confidence and a short comment. The judgments are robust: all configurations agree on the sign and the ranking of the administrations' mean scores, and two different configurations asked on the same day give opposite signs to the same action in about 4% of cases. Responses from different days differ more than same-day responses, but the difference grows slowly over the month, except where the service itself changed. We identify three such changes, which shifted the judgments while leaving little or no trace in the interface. Treating the comments as a retrieval task, we find them specific to each item and consistent across runs and chatbots, with lexical and embedding similarities agreeing. We release the dataset of 16,500 judgments.

authors.name: Oleg Vasilyev
authors.institution: Skolkovo Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Simulation of non-stationary anisotropic capillary wave turbulence within the framework of the kinetic equation
papers.abstract: In the present work, numerical simulation of the evolution of capillary turbulence was performed on the basis of the wave kinetic equation taking into account energy dissipation at small scales. For an isotropic initial condition, the simulation results reproduce the Zakharov--Filonenko power-law turbulence spectrum for the wave action, \(n_k \sim k^{-17/4}\). The main result of the work is the calculation of the evolution for a substantially anisotropic initial condition. The numerical data indicate that, during the evolution of an anisotropic wave-action distribution, a factorized spectrum \(n(k,\phi) \sim k^{-17/4}F(\phi)\) is formed in polar coordinates \((k,\phi)\), where \(F(\phi)\) is a function of the angle in Fourier space. In the regime of a steady power-law distribution in \(k\), the calculated collision integral vanishes with high accuracy in the inertial interval of wavenumbers (the region of the power-law spectrum). Thus, the work provides evidence for the realization of a new strongly anisotropic turbulence spectrum, similar to Kolmogorov--Zakharov spectra.

authors.name: E. A. Kochurin
authors.institution: Skolkovo Institute of Science and Technology

authors.name: A. O. Korotkevich
authors.institution: Skolkovo Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Wave Turbulence of Capillary Waves in Finite Systems
papers.abstract: We consider classical problem of turbulence of capillary waves. In a series of numerical simulations it is shown that Zakharov-Filonenko spectrum corresponding to direct cascade of energy has a limited dynamic range of realization in a finite system, which shrinks with decreasing level of nonlinearity. Recent hypothesis that this dynamic range scales with average steepness as $\sim\mu^{8/3}$ is confirmed. As a byproduct the Zakharov-Filonenko spectrum was observed for record dynamic range close to or beyond one decade in a variety of simulation configurations.

authors.name: Alexander O. Korotkevich
authors.institution: Skolkovo Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: ML-COHP: predicting bond descriptors using latent space of a universal interatomic potentials
papers.abstract: The integrated crystal orbital Hamilton population (ICOHP) is the standard measure of bond strength in a DFT calculation, but every structure needs its own DFT single point and LOBSTER projection, which takes days for a cell of a hundred atoms, such as a grain boundary or a catalytic nanoparticle. We predict ICOHP from the frozen descriptors of a MACE foundation model. A symmetric pair head reads the scalar and bond-projected vector channels of the two atoms and corrects a pair baseline built from the element embeddings of the same model. We tested the model on the high-entropy diboride (Hf,Zr,Ti,Nb,Ta)B$_2$, Pt clusters on defective graphene and Pt/Pd nanoparticles with adsorbed O$_2$. The error on bonds stronger than 0.5 eV is 1.6-4.1%, about half that of the Gaussian-process model of Ferreira et al. trained on the same data. Trained only on high-temperature HEB$_2$ snapshots, the model reproduces the LOBSTER ICOHP of relaxed grain boundary cells to 0.06 eV in about a second, against 5-51 hours of LOBSTER. The vector channels halve the error compared to the scalar ones, and the baseline keeps the model usable with two training structures. With geometries from a fine-tuned MACE potential, the model gives the bonding of Pt/Pd particles over a continuous O$_2$ coverage, and DFT on these particles shows that O$_2$ costs a Pt-rich shell several times more metal--metal bonding than a Pd shell.

authors.name: Daniil S. Alekseev
authors.institution: Skolkovo Institute of Science and Technology

authors.institution: Skolkovo Institute of Science and Technology

authors.institution: Skolkovo Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Flow-based neural networks for scalable high resolution imaging of VLBI observations
papers.abstract: Bayesian sampling methods in very-long-baseline interferometry enable reliable imaging of astronomical sources with a record high angular resolution. However, even after the transition from classical MCMC methods to flow-based neural networks, they remain computationally expensive as the number of recovered features grows. We used WaveletFlow neural network architecture to increase the number of pixels in the recovered image distribution, addressing the scaling issues of previous models. We applied the algorithm to both model data and archive RadioAstron project observations of M87 and ALMA telescope observations of HL Tau. While yielding comparable fidelity of the individual images, the algorithm provides more statistical information compared to CLEAN, which may be crucial for future research on compact astronomical objects such as active galactic nuclei.

papers.title: Finite-Step Geometry of Marginal-Preserving Velocity Fields in Generative Flows
papers.abstract: Generative flows can admit different velocity fields that induce the same continuous marginal evolution but behave differently after numerical discretization. We study this finite-step non-equivalence while keeping the marginal path and numerical method fixed. Projected modified equations characterize the component of local integration error that changes the marginal law and give sufficient conditions for higher marginal convergence order. For affine fixed-shape distributions, we characterize exact finite-step reachability and derive spectral obstructions and sharp nearest-reachable Wasserstein errors. For diffusion probability-flow ODEs, we construct skew-score perturbations that preserve the exact marginal path under exact scores and quantify their leakage under score error. Controlled Gaussian and mixture experiments recover the predicted order, reachability, and obstruction phenomena.

authors.name: Ewsey Obzherin
authors.institution: Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology

papers.title: The Minimax Complexity of Federated Optimization under Interpolation: The Role of Oracle Models

authors.name: Darina Dvinskikh
authors.institution: National Research University Higher School of Economics

authors.name: Alexander Gasnikov
authors.institution: Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology

papers.title: Number of ends of conjugacy diagrams
papers.abstract: For each $n\geq 2$, we construct a finitely generated group $W_n$ with a conjugacy class such that the conjugacy diagram of this class has exactly $n$ ends. For this class, we compute the quotient spaces of the space of derivations of the group algebra $\mathbb{C}[W_n]$ modulo quasi-inner and inner derivations, as well as the corresponding component of the first Hochschild cohomology.

authors.name: Alexey V. Naianzin
authors.institution: Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology

authors.name: Andronick A. Arutyunov
authors.institution: V. A. Trapeznikov Institute of Control Sciences

papers.title: PBW theorem for affine super Yangian
papers.abstract: We prove a Poincar\'e--Birkhoff--Witt theorem for the distinguished affine super Yangian $Y=Y_{1/2,1/2}(\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}(m|n))$, where $m,n\geq2$ and $m\neq n$. With respect to the current filtration, there is a canonical isomorphism \[ \operatorname{gr}_F Y\cong U\!\left(\operatorname{uce}\!\left( \mathfrak{sl}(m|n)\otimes\mathbb C[z^{\pm1},u] \right)\right), \] where $\operatorname{uce}$ denotes the universal central extension. For any totally ordered classical basis homogeneous in parity and current degree, ordered supermonomials in arbitrary fixed filtered lifts form a vector-space basis of $Y$, with odd exponents restricted to zero or one. The proof identifies the classical presentation through Steinberg Lie superalgebras and establishes injectivity using evaluation homomorphisms, iterated coproducts in degreewise completions, and coefficientwise tensor separation.

authors.name: Vladimir Stukopin
authors.institution: Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology

papers.title: Meta-Initialization of Implicit Neural Representations to Accelerate Deformable Medical Image Registration
papers.abstract: Implicit neural representation (INR) methods for deformable medical image registration require the network parameters to be optimized for each new image pair, making adaptation speed a practical limitation. This work investigates whether early adaptation can be accelerated using an initialization learned from a collection of previously solved registration tasks. We examine two schemes: Reptile meta-initialization and STRAINER transfer of the shared component of a coordinate network. KAN-IDIR is used as the base INR displacement-field model. Experiments are conducted on OASIS-1, with 364 consecutive pairs used for training and 49 pairs for test-time adaptation. Registration quality is evaluated using mean Dice and HD95, together with the fraction of voxels with a negative Jacobian determinant at iteration 1500. In the configurations studied, both schemes yield higher Dice and lower HD95 at early iterations than random initialization. Reptile numerically outperforms STRAINER under a small iteration budget, although their pretraining budgets are not matched. As the number of iterations increases, the differences between the schemes shrink. STRAINER pretraining takes 39-40 minutes, compared with 44.98 hours for Reptile.

papers.title: Genericity of singularities of solutions to quasilinear systems on compact sets
papers.abstract: We study the genericity of singularities of types $A_2,A_3,D_4^\pm$ in solutions of the equations of gas dynamics and nonlinear geometrical optics. The sets of solutions satisfying the corresponding transversality conditions are proved to be open and dense in spaces of smooth and real-analytic solutions equipped with the Whitney topology on compact sets.

papers.title: An analogue of $\Gamma$-function for irreducible cuspidal representations of the group $\mathrm{GL}(2)$ over a two-dimensional local field
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbf F$ be a non-archimedian local field of odd residue characteristic, ${\mathcal O}={\mathbf F}[\![t]\!]\subset{\mathcal K}={\mathbf F}(\!(t)\!)$. We consider the subgroup $\widehat{\mathrm{GL}}(2,{\mathcal O})={\mathcal K}^\times\cdot{\mathrm{GL}}(2,{\mathcal O})\subset{\mathrm{GL}}(2,{\mathcal K})$, and the normalizer ${\mathrm{GL}}'(2,{\mathcal O})\subset{\mathrm GL}(2,{\mathcal K})$ of an Iwahori subgroup $I\subset{\mathrm{GL}}(2,{\mathcal K})$. We calculate the $\Gamma$-functions for irreducible special representations of $\widehat{\mathrm{GL}}(2,{\mathcal O})$ and ${\mathrm{GL}}'(2,{\mathcal O})$.

authors.name: Michael Finkelberg
authors.institution: National Research University Higher School of Economics

papers.title: Hilbert functions of filtered graphical zonotopal algebras
papers.abstract:
The external zonotopal algebra of a graph is generated by nilpotent vertex elements $X_v$ and determines the graphical matroid after deleting loops. Replacing these generators by $f(X_v)$, for a power series $f(u)$, and filtering by word length gives a family of filtered algebras.
