Evaluating on a widely used benchmark dataset, we find that TFMs predicting full probability distributions in a single forward pass systematically outperform bespoke estimators across both representative and biased training data regimes, matching or exceeding baselines trained on over $40{,}000$ galaxies with just $1{,}000$ training context examples. We also show that the TFM advantage is largest when little to no calibration data are available, and that it persists even when the bespoke baselines are supplemented with up to $10{,}000$ representative calibration spectra. This shows that TFMs offer a sample-efficient framework for upcoming imaging-only astronomical surveys, where observational selection bias can be mitigated simply by including a small representative calibration sample in context.

papers.title: Ghirlanda-Guerra identities and cavity equations for diluted spin glass models
papers.abstract: This note supplies the details of the cavity lower bound used in "The M\'ezard-Parisi formula" [8]. Specifically, we show that small perturbations that do not change the limiting free energy can be chosen so that the asymptotic Gibbs measures arising in the Aizenman-Sims-Starr lower bound satisfy both the Ghirlanda-Guerra identities and the cavity equations. These calculations are standard and require only minor modifications of arguments already available in the literature. We record them here for completeness, avoiding a lengthy repetition of these arguments in [8].

papers.title: The M\'ezard-Parisi formula
papers.abstract: This paper proves the M\'ezard-Parisi formula for the free energy of random $K$-sat and diluted $p$-spin models with even $p$, completing an approach developed in earlier work of the author and collaborators. The upper bound was established by Franz and Leone. Here the matching lower bound is proved for a general class of diluted models under symmetry and integrability assumptions. The main new contribution is a proof of an approximate form of the M\'ezard-Parisi reproducibility hypothesis without assuming that the overlap distribution has finite support.

papers.title: Nonequilibrium statistical thermodynamics of a small quantum system coupled to quantum reservoirs
papers.abstract: A statistical mechanical formulation where nonequilibrium averages of selected quantum observables are given exactly as averages over local density operators is used to describe the dynamics and thermodynamics of a small quantum system coupled to reservoirs. The local density operators are functionals of constraint variables that play the role of thermodynamic forces that satisfy a set of equations of motion. A focus of the work is on the evolution of the average internal energy of the quantum subsystem that may be subject to external autonomous driving that does work on the system, and on entropy production in the system. The nonequilibrium statistical thermodynamics the quantum subsystem coupled to reservoirs, as well as that for the isolated subsystem and reservoirs, are discussed. When the subsystem is coupled to large quantum reservoirs, the effects of the quantum subsystem on the reservoirs can be captured through boundary conditions on the reservoir equations, and these boundary conditions are derived. The formulation is illustrated by considering the heat transfer through a system comprising a quantum system coupled to two heat reservoirs with different temperatures.

papers.title: Escaping Path Mirages in Offline Goal-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Offline goal-conditioned reinforcement learning remains challenging in stochastic long-horizon settings, where compounding value estimation errors hinder reliable goal reaching. While prior methods have sought to address this challenge through various approaches, a key challenge remains path mirage, where agents overcommit to spuriously successful trajectories in offline datasets induced by stochasticity, often leading to failure on difficult tasks. To address this issue, we propose Branch-aware Graph Planning (BGP), which captures stochastic branching structures by identifying high-variability points as graph nodes and designing goal-conditioned edges with segmented learning to avoid unreliable branches and reduce unnecessary stochasticity along paths. As a result, BGP enables reliable goal reaching even in highly stochastic long-horizon environments, and experiments on diverse OGBench tasks show that it substantially outperforms prior state-of-the-art offline goal-conditioned RL methods. Our implementation is available at https://umlic.github.io/papers/BGP/.

authors.name: Gwanwoo Choi
authors.institution: Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: The velocity is deterministic in random walk in 2-valued i.i.d. random environment
papers.abstract: We prove that the limiting velocity for (nearest-neighbour) random walk in i.i.d. random environment is deterministic when the local environment is supported on two points. No ellipticity is assumed. The proof uses a clever adaption (suggested by ChatGPT) of coupling arguments previously developed by the authors. It extends to i.i.d. environments where the local environments are mixtures of two such points.

papers.title: A Conveyor Belt Mechanism for Repositionable Magnetic Coupling Between Continuum Robots
papers.abstract: This work proposes a novel conveyor belt mechanism enabling continuous, active repositioning of functional elements along the body of a tendon-driven continuum robot. Up to three conveyor belt mechanisms are integrated within a 9 mm diameter continuum robot. We demonstrate equivalent or reduced conveyor belt actuation forces compared to robot tendon actuation forces. As a case study, we mount permanent magnets along two conveyor belts, and demonstrate actively reconfigurable inter-robot coupling. Coupling point location and quantity can be adjusted during robot operation to actively tune the effective stiffness of the coupled multi-robot system. We show that effective stiffness follows a predictable inverse-cubic relationship with coupling location, and increases with the number of coupling points. These findings demonstrate that the conveyor belt mechanism enables active functional element repositioning for changing tasks requirements, with magnetic inter-robot coupling as one proof-of-concept.

papers.title: Learning Without Clocks: Partition-Invariant Neural Network
papers.abstract: Event cameras, spiking cochleas and similar sensors emit asynchronous events, yet most learning systems first bin them into frames or packets, so the output depends on how the stream was sliced. Networks whose state is updated exactly at every event and evolves in closed form between events are invariant to this slicing. We ask what more makes the output (i) independent of the processing order of simultaneous events and (ii) continuous in the time stamps, even when two events cross in time, while (iii) staying sensitive to temporal order. For arbitrary nonlinear event models we prove that (i) and (ii) are each equivalent to pairwise commutation of the event updates, and that once updates commute, all order dependence comes from their non-commutation with the inter-event dynamics and vanishes linearly in the time lag. This identifies a class of time-mediated non-commutative (TM) models and yields a resolution-robustness bound for any model. We construct the minimal TM layer, a learnable, provably Lipschitz generalization of the Hassenstein-Reichardt correlator; prove that no single additive layer can uniformly represent ordered pair interactions, whereas a three-dimensional TM state can; show that each TM layer adds two levels of temporal nesting versus one for additive layers; and give a single-layer higher-order construction (TM-k) and a stacking rule preserving all three properties. We instantiate these results as the Clock-Free Event (CFE) layer, linear in the number of events, give a topology-free variant for temporal point processes with closed-form likelihoods, and specify a preregistered clock-robustness protocol with a physical-time threat model for spike-retiming attacks. In preliminary development-set experiments, the TM state beats an otherwise identical additive state by 3.5-9.1 points on DVS128 Gesture and by 24.5 and 30.6 points on SHD and Speech Commands.

papers.title: Non-concordant 2-links in simply-connected 4-manifolds
papers.abstract: We construct an infinite family of smooth 2-component links of 2-spheres $\Sigma_k\subset S^2\times S^2$ whose respective components are smoothly concordant but which are pairwise not topologically concordant in any topological $\mathbb{Z}$-homology cobordism. In particular, the $\Sigma_k$ are pairwise non-concordant in $(S^2\times S^2)\times[0,1]$.

papers.title: Quantitative propagation of chaos on arbitrary finite time intervals for the three-dimensional repulsive Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck equation
papers.abstract: We prove quantitative propagation of chaos in total variation for repulsive Vlasov--Riesz--Fokker--Planck (VRFP) equations on $\mathbb{T}^d$ and $\mathbb{R}^d$ with unregularized interaction potentials with singularity $|x|^{-s}$, $0<s<d/2$. On every finite time interval on which the limiting classical solution satisfies the stated regularity assumptions, the particle marginals with a product initial law converge at an algebraic rate in the particle number, with constants growing at most exponentially in the marginal order. For the three-dimensional repulsive Vlasov--Poisson--Fokker--Planck (VPFP) equation on $\mathbb{R}^3$, a weighted $C^m$ initial probability density, $m\ge3$, with Gaussian velocity decay and polynomial spatial decay of order $M>3$ gives convergence to the global classical solution on every finite time interval. The proof combines conditioning of the initial product law with weighted BBGKY estimates. A decomposition of the potential and a bounded modification of the far-field force yield weighted bounds growing geometrically in the marginal order on the prescribed interval. A centered second-moment estimate permits summation of the error hierarchy, and a synchronous coupling transfers the estimate to the original dynamics.

authors.name: Ning Jiang
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: FIRME: Registry-Anchored Memory Graphs for Evolving, Heterogeneous Investor Knowledge
papers.abstract: Financial AI workflows that reuse investor knowledge need persistent memory that integrates observations across sources and periods without losing identity or provenance. In a knowledge graph, recurring observations may use different surface forms, fragmenting relationship histories and preventing evidence from accumulating. We introduce Fusion and Identity Registry for Memory Evolution (FIRME), a registry-anchored memory graph that reconciles incoming observations to persistent canonical relationships and retains their source, time, and context. Within periods, rule-based fusion links investor-call discussions to portfolio cash-flow signals, directly or through a fixed product-topic ontology. Across periods, canonical identities and persistent aliases direct recurring observations to the same relationship history; deterministic updates summarize reinforcement, inactivity, and reactivation. We evaluate FIRME on proprietary investor-call and cash-flow records and on S&P 500 earnings-call transcripts. Compared with a historical registry that retains canonical identities and semantic fallback but omits alias memory, FIRME increases final-period Correct Match Rate by 7.8-12.1 percentage points across four dataset-backend settings under a fixed-judge and fallback-review protocol. A blinded human audit of 200 incoming observations per setting finds Correct Match Rate gains of 9.0-16.5 points and reattachment-recall gains of 22.5-29.0 points, with higher observed merge precision in all four samples. A separate audit finds valid evidence paths for 293 of 300 outputs from full within-period fusion in the investor-call setting. Extraction-faithfulness and round-trip diagnostics assess source grounding and preservation of extractor-derived graph content.

papers.title: FutureWorld: A Plug-and-Play Causal Next-State Predictor for Interactive Video World Exploration
papers.abstract: Interactive video world models aim to follow user actions while maintaining scene consistency over extended interactions. History-based methods reuse generated latents to preserve scene content, but three limitations of this reuse contribute to error recirculation. 1) The latent generated at each interaction is retained as history, potentially containing blurred details, geometric distortions, or semantic drift. 2) Although retrieved historical content matches the current scene, it can still contain errors that are carried into the next chunk. 3) New outputs then become history for later interactions, potentially reinforcing the same errors through repeated reuse. To limit this cycle, we aim to predict the future scene state from the current generated latent and the next action before generating the next interaction's video chunk. This future-state prior provides guidance for the next chunk, with the aim of reducing the errors carried forward from history. To this end, we propose a plug-and-play Causal Next-Chunk Predictor (C-NCP) with cross-model adaptability and prediction-guided modulation. We integrate C-NCP into four base generators and evaluate the augmented models across three benchmarks for interactive long-video generation and action-conditioned world modeling. Extensive experiments demonstrate reduced error accumulation and improved long-horizon consistency across diverse generation settings. The project page is at https://GuangYuanKK.github.io/futureworld.

authors.name: Shuolin Xu
authors.institution: North China University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Class-aware Latent Attention Replay (CLAR): Class Incremental Hazard Diagnosis for Resilient AI in the Manufacturing Industrial Internet
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems provide critical computation services in the Manufacturing Industrial Internet (MII), and their resilience depends on timely diagnosis of hazards across the data, AI pipeline, and cyber-physical layers. During operation, new hazard types keep emerging with only a few samples each, hazards co-occur, and the diagnosis model runs on memory-constrained computation nodes. Replay-based class-incremental learning (CIL) can learn new hazard classes while revisiting a small memory of past samples, but existing methods assume single-label, balanced streams, store high-dimensional raw samples, and select them independently of the classifier. We propose Class-aware Latent Attention Replay (CLAR), which combines a dual buffer that stores mostly compact latent representations with a few raw samples, an Attention Leverage Score (ALS) that upper-bounds the classifier logit and guides class-balanced reservoir sampling, and an exponential-moving-average teacher that slows latent-space drift. For an idealized buffer model, we prove that the buffer is class-balanced and follows an ALS-weighted class distribution, and that below a critical per-class capacity, ALS-guided replay has a lower replay-gradient error than class-balanced uniform replay. In the case study, On hazard diagnosis data from an MII testbed, CLAR achieves the highest mean average weighted F1 score among the evaluated replay methods with the same buffer size

authors.name: Avranshu Mahanty
authors.institution: University at Buffalo, State University of New York

papers.title: Molecular Electrodynamic Relaxation in Dielectric and Plasmonic Cavities
papers.abstract: Molecular radiative emission is a fundamental relaxation process that governs excited-state lifetimes and significantly influences photophysical dynamics, but direct self-consistent Maxwell--Schr\"odinger simulations of molecular radiation suffer from numerical instabilities in evaluating radiative self-interaction. Herein, this issue is resolved within the self-consistent propagation of classical Maxwell's equations coupled to real-time density-functional electronic dynamics and their tight-binding approximation. By carefully removing the longitudinal components of radiative self-reaction, this framework quantitatively reproduces radiative lifetimes of atomic and molecular emitters in vacuum and further captures cavity-modified emission at weak and strong coupling regimes beyond perturbation theory. For molecules weakly coupled to an optical microcavity, the cavity Purcell effect is shown to reach maximum using a modestly red-detuned cavity due to nuclear thermal motion. Moreover, for a single methylene blue molecule strongly coupled to a realistic nanoparticle-on-mirror plasmonic cavity, the predicted molecular electrodynamical relaxation is accelerated to approximately 11 femtoseconds, directly competing with nonadiabatic nuclear dynamics. This work establishes a route to first-principles design of material radiative properties in a wide range of dielectric environments.

papers.title: UGR: Unified Generative Ranking for Heterogeneous E-commerce Recommendation
papers.abstract: List-wise ranking in e-commerce recommendation must balance user utility and commercial value across organic content, ads, and candidates from other businesses, while modeling candidate interactions and sequential dependencies. Existing generative ranking methods typically learn from logged exposure sequences and operate on truncated candidate sets from a single business. Exposure-sequence learning may not fully exploit post-exposure feedback signals. Meanwhile, generative ranking over heterogeneous, multi-business candidates remains less explored, particularly when recommendation scores and advertising value must be jointly modeled under generalized second-price (GSP) auctions. We propose Unified Generative Ranking (UGR), which performs generative ranking over the full request-level multi-business heterogeneous candidate set, typically comprising around a thousand candidates in production, and directly generates multi-business ranking lists through candidate-aware autoregressive decoding. To go beyond exposure-sequence imitation, UGR introduces complementary feedback supervision through weighted supervised fine-tuning and permutation preference optimization, which respectively leverage observed post-exposure feedback and feedback-derived preferences among permutations. UGR uses a training-time advertising debiasing tower to model historical ad exposure effects and incorporates current ad value during serving while preserving the existing allocation and GSP pricing rules. Multi-value sequence retrieval produces candidate ranking lists, and the existing downstream evaluator selects the final list for exposure. Offline experiments demonstrate consistent gains in ranking quality, while online A/B tests on Taobao's Guess You Like recommendation service yield improvements of 1.76% in Core IPV, 3.29% in Transaction Volume, and 2.10% in GMV over the production baseline.

papers.title: On the $b$-Symbol Weight Distribution of Dual Melas Codes and a Poisson Randomness Postulate
papers.abstract:
We prove a new lower bound on the $b$-symbol weight of codewords in dual Melas codes, which is strictly better than known results. We employ a new strategy that translates a pattern counting problem in linear-feedback shift register sequences to a problem on orbits of binary polynomials under a certain action. We use the same techniques to provide an improved lower bound on the burst-covering radius of Melas codes and a new upper bound on the critical exponent of dual Melas codes.
  We then define a new randomness postulate on (families of) binary sequences, based on the definition of infinite Poisson generic sequences. We conjecture that codewords in the dual Melas code satisfy this postulate, and we show partial progress in establishing this conjecture. We also show how a relaxed version of the problem can be completely resolved, and relate the conjecture to the first part of the paper, giving a justification of why the improved bounds on the $b$-symbol weight were somewhat to be expected.

papers.title: DecompGym: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Designing Decomposition Algorithms
papers.abstract: Benders decomposition and column generation solve large optimization problems by passing cuts, columns, and dual values between a master problem and subproblems, and are hard to implement correctly. Large language models now automate parts of algorithm design, which points toward agents that build decomposition solvers for new problems. As a first step toward such agents, we study how well current coding agents design and implement these two algorithms, and how they fail. We introduce DecompGym, 81 instances from nine problem families (five Benders, four column generation), in which an agent writes a solver for a prescribed method. Each solver must meet three criteria: execution within a 60-second time limit; numerical feasibility together with a method audit, in which an LLM judge reads the solver's code; and an objective within 1% of the stored optimal objective. We evaluate 12 GPT, Claude, and Gemini models running in coding-agent tools. Over up to ten attempts, we compare independent regeneration with reflection, which first diagnoses the failure. On the first attempt, two models solve every instance and seven solve more than 90%. Most Benders failures (48 of 62) are missing or suboptimal solutions. The most common column-generation failure is a method-audit rejection. Output checks alone would accept 93 of the 108 attempts that fail the method audit. The most common rejection, an optimalif, occurs 96 times, 92 of them in one model.Reflection turns 66% of retries into successes, compared with 39% for regeneration, and it repairs method-audit failures, for which the judge names the defecective gaps. Agents for decomposition therefore need checks on how a solver reaches its answer and feedback that locates the error. The benchmark is available at https://github.com/SIKAI-C/DecompGym.

authors.name: Miao Li
authors.institution: Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China

papers.title: Environmental Quenching of Satellite Galaxies out to z~0.4 with GAMA and DEVILS
papers.abstract: While numerous studies have shown that satellite galaxies experience declining star formation rates after infall, direct comparisons across different surveys and redshifts are complicated by varying sample selections, environmental metrics, and techniques used to derive galaxy properties. In this work, we select satellite galaxies from the highly complete Galaxy and Mass Assembly (GAMA) Survey and the Deep Extragalactic VIsible Legacy Survey (DEVILS) to investigate environmental quenching out to z~0.4. These surveys derive galaxy properties and environments in a consistent manner, minimizing systematic biases and enabling a robust comparison across redshift. Using projected phase space as a proxy for infall time, we quantify the evolution of the quenched fraction and trace how satellites evolve relative to the star-forming main sequence (SFMS). We find consistent trends between GAMA and DEVILS, with satellites exhibiting a steady decline in star formation relative to the SFMS at a rate of ~0.14 dex/Gyr following infall. Extending this analysis to include visual morphology, we find similar declining trends for both early- and late-type systems. Overall, we find no significant redshift evolution between GAMA and DEVILS, indicating that group and cluster environments have a comparable impact on the star formation activity of satellite galaxies over the past ~4.5 Gyr.

authors.name: Luke Davies
authors.institution: International Centre for Radio Astronomy Research

authors.name: Sabine Bellstedt
authors.institution: International Centre for Radio Astronomy Research

papers.title: The exact digirth and out-degree bounds for $C(k,k)$-subdivision and out-forest in digraphs
papers.abstract:
For each integer $k\ge2$, let $C(k,k)$ denote the oriented cycle formed by two internally vertex-disjoint directed paths of length $k$ with the same initial and terminal vertices. Picasarri-Arrieta and Rambaud ({\small European J. Combin., 2024}) asked for the smallest integer $g_k$ such that every digraph with minimum out-degree at least two and digirth at least $g_k$ contains a subdivision of $C(k,k)$. We completely resolve this problem by proving that $g_k=k+1$. Our proof relies on a refinement of Thomassen's theorem ({\small Discrete Math., 1985}) on two directed cycles intersecting in exactly one vertex: we prove that every digraph with minimum out-degree at least two contains two directed cycles intersecting in exactly one arc.
  We also establish an embedding theorem for out-forests with prescribed images of their roots, under minimum out-degree and digirth conditions determined by the number of leaves and the heights of vertices in antichains. As an application, for integers $k,\ell\ge2$, we show that every digraph with minimum out-degree at least \(k\) and digirth at least \(k(\ell-1)+1\) contains \(k\) directed paths of length \(\ell\) sharing only their initial vertex, which can be prescribed arbitrarily. This improves the previous digirth bound \((k^\ell-1)/(k-1)+1\) of Picasarri-Arrieta and Rambaud to a sharp bound.

authors.name: Xinmin Hou
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Xinjie Wang
authors.institution: Tianjin University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

papers.title: Threshold Regression with a Nearly Integrated Threshold Variable
papers.abstract: This paper considers threshold regression with an integrated or local-to-unity threshold variable and a threshold fixed in levels. We study the least squares threshold estimator and establish its asymptotic theory under both fixed and diminishing threshold effects. Under a fixed effect, the threshold estimator has a compound Cox argmin limit, whereas under a diminishing effect, its limiting distribution is characterized by a two-sided Brownian argmax with a random scale. We also develop likelihood ratio inference, which is asymptotically pivotal under a diminishing effect and conservative under Gaussian errors for a fixed effect, and show that conventional $t$-ratios for the slope coefficients remain asymptotically standard normal. A sup-Wald test is proposed to detect threshold effects that may be too small for consistent threshold localization. We further extend the framework to allow for integrated slope regressors and for contemporaneous endogeneity of the threshold variable, showing that the leading endogenous contribution cancels over shrinking threshold windows. Monte Carlo simulations examine the finite-sample performance of the proposed methods. An illustration using public debt and economic growth highlights the relevance of allowing for a persistent threshold variable.

papers.title: LogicTree: Object-Oriented Writing for Structured Human-AI Academic Authoring
papers.abstract: Academic writing is non-linear, iterative, and structure-driven, requiring authors to develop fragmented ideas into arguments with local coherence and global consistency. However, current AI-assisted tools primarily exchange linear prompts and free-form text, forcing authors to reconstruct generated logic and repeatedly verify its alignment with their structural intentions. We propose object-oriented writing (OOW), an OOD-inspired representation and interaction paradigm in which persistent writing objects serve as shared, manipulable referents for authors and AI. We instantiate OOW in LogicTree, an Overleaf-integrated prototype that combines a hierarchical object representation with a structure-grounded writing assistance module for author-initiated generation and issue-grounded revision and a structural logical review module for inspecting local coherence and global consistency. A within-subjects study (N=12) provides initial evidence that, in controlled academic writing tasks, LogicTree helps users structure ideas, reduces workload, and improves measured logical quality compared with a conversational baseline.

authors.name: Jiajun Zhu
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology Liaoning

authors.name: Huamin Qu
authors.institution: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Minimizing the spectral radius of unicyclic graphs with fixed order and dissociation number
papers.abstract: A dissociation set of a graph G is a vertex subset S contained in V(G) such that the induced subgraph G[S] has maximum degree at most 1, and the dissociation number of G is the cardinality of a maximum dissociation set denoted by {\Phi}(G). In this paper, we first derive a sharp lower bound on the dissociation number for all unicyclic graphs. Furthermore, we also study the graphs with minimum spectral radius among all unicyclic graphs with given order and dissociation number and explicitly identify all extremal graphs for \(n-4 \le \Phi(G) \le n-1\).

authors.name: Dan Li
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Information-Theoretic Reliability--Safety Bounds and Finite-Alignment Dynamics in AI Knowledge Distillation
papers.abstract: The reliability and safety of artificial intelligence (AI), together with their transfer and evolution through knowledge distillation, have attracted growing attention. We establish an information-theoretic bound on the reliability--safety trade-off and characterize the dynamics of this trade-off under knowledge distillation. We first prove a universal trade-off inequality that is independent of the specific model form. Its boundary is determined solely by a single parameter Kh, which quantifies the hidden layer's ability to distinguish benign from hazardous inputs. We then develop a canonical Boltzmann-machine model of AI response behavior and derive two exact relations between reliability and safety. The trade-off curve is determined by the hazard discrimination capacity K, while the overall answer tendency controls the operating point along the curve. These relations agree well with existing experimental data. In knowledge distillation, we find that teacher responses induce a renormalization of the student model's trade-off parameters. We further use a renormalization-group approach to study multigenerational distillation, deriving exact recursion relations and the associated renormalization-group-like flows for two representative direct intergenerational distillation protocols at arbitrary teacher--student alignment strength. These flows reveal fixed-point structures, long-term dynamics, and critical behavior, yielding testable predictions for the critical transition between capability loss and stable transmission.

authors.name: Miao-Miao Yi
authors.institution: Xuan Wu Hospital of the Capital Medical University

papers.title: Dynamic $(\Delta+1)$ Vertex Coloring with Adaptive Adversaries: Entropy Compression to the Rescue
papers.abstract:
We present a randomized algorithm for maintaining a $(\Delta+1)$ vertex coloring of a fully dynamic graph against an adaptive adversary with $\tilde{O}(\sqrt{n})$ amortized update time. Our algorithm improves upon the recent randomized algorithms of Behnezhad, Rajaraman, and Wasim (SODA 2025) with $\tilde{O}(n^{8/9})$ and Flin and Halld\'orsson (ICALP 2025) with $\tilde{O}(n^{2/3})$ amortized update time. Our result (nearly) matches a fundamental limit of $O(\sqrt{n})$ update time identified by Flin and Halld\'orsson and settles their main open question.
  The previous algorithms' main improvement came from efficient coloring of the dense parts of the graph. Our approach complements these prior work by handling the sparse parts more efficiently, using ideas inspired by the recently developed dynamic entropy compression method. A key new aspect of our work is to tailor this method specifically to dynamic algorithms---as opposed to original local search algorithms---and achieve update times that can be sublinear in the number of involved constraints per update.

papers.title: Anisotropic error estimates for the $L^{2}$-projection onto discontinuous finite element spaces
papers.abstract: Anisotropic error estimates are determined for the $L^2$-orthogonal projection onto discontinuous finite element spaces in two and three dimensions. These estimates are determined in $W^{m,p}$-seminorms, in which $p \in [1,\infty]$ and $0 \le m \le k+1$, where $k \ge 0$ is the polynomial degree. The analysis relies on a geometric condition that is equivalent to the maximum angle condition. As an application, an apriori error analysis is presented for a hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin discretization of the Poisson problem on two and three dimensional anisotropic meshes.

papers.title: Learning Erasing Equal-Length Relational Pattern Languages in the Limit from Positive Data over Binary Alphabets
papers.abstract: Relational pattern languages generalize Angluin's pattern languages by requiring the strings substituted for repeated occurrences of a variable to stand in a given relation, rather than to be identical. We study erasing pattern languages under the equal-length relation, where all occurrences of a variable must be replaced by strings of the same length. Over alphabets with at least three letters, this class is known to be learnable in the limit from positive data. We show that over a binary alphabet it is not, which resolves an open question from earlier work. Our proof reveals that non-learnability already holds for the restricted subclass of languages generated by patterns that have exactly three maximal substrings of variables. We then show that patterns with at most two maximal substrings of variables are learnable in the limit from positive data for every alphabet of size at least two. If the target pattern is known to have at most one maximal substring of variables, this can even be achieved by an iterative learner, which updates its hypothesis using only the current example and its previous hypothesis.

papers.title: Parameterized Approximation of Max k-Weight CSP: A Dichotomy for Boolean Languages
papers.abstract:
We study \textsc{Max $k$-Weight CSP}: maximize the satisfied weight of Boolean constraints with nonnegative rational weights by setting at most $k$ variables to $1$. Each constraint uses at most $d$ distinct variables and a relation from a finite Boolean language $\Gamma$. This includes \textsc{Partial Vertex Cover}, \textsc{Densest $k$-Subgraph}, bounded-frequency \textsc{Maximum Coverage}, and cardinality-constrained \textsc{Max-SAT}.
  We completely classify the fixed finite languages admitting an efficient parameterized approximation scheme (EPAS) with parameter $k+d$. Only nonempty relations excluding the all-zero tuple matter. For such a relation, a coordinate is a \emph{unit witness} if the tuple with a single $1$ in that coordinate is accepted, and a \emph{control} otherwise. A relation is \emph{Direct} if setting any selected control to $0$, with all other coordinates unchanged, preserves satisfaction. It is \emph{Rooted} if every satisfying tuple has a selected unit witness such that keeping it, setting all other unit witnesses to $0$, and setting any subset of selected controls to $0$ preserves satisfaction.
  If all such relations are Direct, or all are Rooted, we give a deterministic $(1-\varepsilon)$-approximation for every rational $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$ in time $2^{O(d+k\log(1+dk/\varepsilon))}\ell_{\mathrm{in}}^{O(1)}$, where $\ell_{\mathrm{in}}$ is the total input length. The algorithms are uniform in $d$ and give an EPAS parameterized by $k+d$ whenever relation membership is polynomial-time decidable. If neither condition holds, no EPAS exists unless $\mathsf{FPT}=\mathsf{W[1]}$, even for unweighted instances where no two constraints involve the same set of variables.

authors.name: Souvik Saha
authors.institution: The University of Kansas Cancer Center

authors.name: Abhishek Sahu
authors.institution: National Institute of Pharmaceutical Education and Research

papers.title: Diagrams for Roots and Quiver Representations in the context of the Gabriel-Kac Theorem
papers.abstract: Using the data of the Dynkin diagrams, we build graphical calculi for representing the positive roots of Kac-Moody algebras and the representations of quivers. Once developed, we use these to analyze the asymptotic size of the root and representation spaces, and discuss how this relates to the Gabriel-Kac theorem, the correspondence between these two structures. We give a refinement of this correspondence in terms of the trichotomy of growth rates for Kac-Moody algebras depending on if they are of finite, affine, or indefinite type, which is done in terms of what we call ``tree like" representations.

papers.title: A Sequential Foundation for Two-Level Nested Logit
papers.abstract: I show that the two-level nested logit demand model arises exactly from a sequential choice process in which group, subgroup, and product taste shocks are revealed stage by stage. The result extends to any number of levels and holds for any nesting parameters below one, without the bounds and ordering that random utility maximization requires. Estimates that applied work discards for violating these bounds are therefore consistent with sequential choice. The standard linear inversion and welfare formula remain valid. Adding a product to a nest can raise another product's share in that nest, even with single-unit demand.

papers.title: Visually Irrelevant Hallucinations in Medical Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Medical vision-language models (VLMs) show strong performance in radiology report generation (RRG) and medical visual question answering (Med-VQA), producing free-form clinical descriptions and answers from medical images. However, they may generate clinically meaningful statements that lack visual evidence or contradict image content. We refer to these errors as visually irrelevant hallucinations and investigate them at the phrase level. We propose CLEAR (Counterfactual Localized Evaluation of Alignment and Response), a model-agnostic post-hoc framework for phrase-level hallucination risk estimation. CLEAR decomposes generated responses into visually assessable clinical phrases. For each phrase, phrase-conditioned grounding identifies a candidate visual region, which is selectively perturbed by a localized counterfactual intervention. CLEAR characterizes the intervention using two complementary auditing cues: response cues, capturing semantic and clinically meaningful changes in the generated response, and alignment cues, measuring changes in image-phrase compatibility. These cues are normalized and jointly modeled to estimate phrase-level hallucination risk. Across four datasets spanning RRG and Med-VQA, CLEAR outperforms state-of-the-art hallucination detection baselines across multiple medical and general-purpose VLMs. On MIMIC-CXR, CLEAR improves AUPRC from 85.10% to 90.23%. Its effectiveness is further validated on a GT-derived controlled VIH benchmark. These results establish visually irrelevant hallucination as an important fine-grained reliability failure mode in medical VLMs and demonstrate the value of model-agnostic visual-support auditing for more trustworthy multimodal clinical generation.

papers.title: StreamStudio: Exploring Video Authoring with Streaming Autoregressive Generation
papers.abstract: We present StreamStudio, a prototype system that explores a new authoring paradigm for streaming video generation. Instead of entering a prompt and waiting for a complete video before making changes, creators can interact with the generation as it unfolds: steering what comes next, returning to earlier moments, and exploring different continuations. In this way, StreamStudio shifts creative control from post-generation revision to continuous interaction with the generative process. Our contribution centers on this authoring paradigm and the interaction mechanisms that make streaming generation directly manipulable. StreamStudio is designed as a plug-and-play interface that can work with compatible generation and editing models, allowing its interaction model to evolve alongside advances in underlying video models. As streaming models become faster and easier to control in the future, such an interface may support more flexible and controllable video creation, including richer edits and multimodal interventions during generation.

authors.institution: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Modeling Broad-Frequency-Band Water-Wave Experiments with Generalizations of the Nonlinear Schrodinger Equation
papers.abstract: Waves generated by storms gradually disperse, forming swells that can travel thousands of kilometers across the ocean's surface. The evolution of deep-water swells, which are unaffected by the seafloor, can be modeled by the nonlinear Schrodinger (NLS) equation and its generalizations. These models typically assume that the wave trains are comprised of a narrow band of frequencies. We present measurements from a new series of laboratory experiments in which the broadbandedness is increased and show that generalizations of the NLS equation can accurately model these measurements.

papers.title: The Welfare Limits of Market Segmentation with Captive Consumers
papers.abstract: In a duopoly with captive and contested consumers, I characterize every pair of consumer and producer surplus that can arise under some market composition and some public segmentation, and construct a market that produces each pair. The set is lens-shaped. At any level of industry profit, consumers do worst when captive and contested consumers are perfectly separated and best in an unsegmented market in which the two firms have equally many captives. A market with unequal captive bases and some contested consumers cannot reach this upper frontier under any segmentation. Between Bertrand competition and monopoly, the frontier itself lies strictly below what consumers would get if everyone paid a single deterministic price yielding the same profit. Firms must randomize, and with downward-sloping demand the resulting price dispersion lowers consumer surplus.

papers.title: Wulff Rigidity for Overdetermined Anisotropic $k$-Hessian Equations
papers.abstract: We establish Wulff rigidity for overdetermined anisotropic $k$-Hessian equations associated with a smooth and strongly convex Finsler gauge. The solutions are subject to homogeneous Dirichlet boundary and a prescribed anisotropic gradient condition on a smooth domain. We prove that the domain must be a Wulff shape. The same rigidity holds under a prescribed positive weighted Neumann-type condition. These results extend the Wulff rigidity for the endpoint cases $k=1$ (Cianchi--Salani, \emph{Math. Ann.}, 2009; Wang--Xia \emph{Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal.}, 2011) and $k=n$ ( Cianchi--Salani, \emph{J. Funct. Anal.}, 2023) to the intermediate cases $2\le k<n$.

authors.name: Yanjun Liu
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: A Gaussian-Process Surrogate for Control Rod Worth with Calibrated Uncertainty: Application to VERA Core Physics Benchmark Problem 4
papers.abstract: Differential and integral control rod worth are usually obtained by differencing eigenvalue calculations at discrete rod positions, which resolves the derivative poorly and gives it no uncertainty. We build a Gaussian-process (GP) surrogate for reactivity as a function of rod position on VERA Core Physics Benchmark Problem 4, a $3\times3$ assembly cluster with a hybrid AIC/B$_4$C rod cluster control assembly, modelled in OpenMC with ENDF/B-VIII.0. A parametric sigmoidal mean carries the dynamic range, a Matern-5/2 GP carries the residual, and the reported Monte Carlo uncertainty of each run enters as known observation noise. Because differentiation is linear, the differential rod worth and its variance follow in closed form from the kernel derivatives. Trained on 43 runs at three particle counts and tested on 11 independent runs, the surrogate meets a fixed 10 pcm accuracy target above the test-run noise, and its intervals are calibrated: the standardized leave-one-out residuals over 129 independent runs have variance 1.07 with 95% interval [0.85, 1.39]. The total worth agrees with the direct OpenMC end-point difference within combined uncertainty, and the differential worth peak is located to within one step. Three mean functions of very different fit quality give the same differential worth to within 0.1 pcm/step, while the width of its band depends on the kernel smoothness by a factor of four. The number of runs required and the remaining approximations are reported, and the extension to rod position and soluble boron is outlined.

papers.title: Predicting Weight Windows for Duct-Streaming Shielding Geometries with a Convolutional Neural Network
papers.abstract: Forward-flux-based weight windows give global variance reduction for duct-streaming shielding problems, but each new geometry needs an iterative Monte Carlo calculation to build them. We report preliminary results on a convolutional neural network (CNN) that learns the map from a two-dimensional duct geometry and source position to the lower window bound of such an iteration, here the MAGIC generator in OpenMC, in milliseconds. A set of 250 random concrete ducts of three curved and rectangular families on the Protvino labyrinth bounding box was run in OpenMC with a Cf-252 point source and MAGIC generation, and a 1.9-million-parameter U-Net was trained on the logarithm of the lower bound. On held-out ducts the error in the cells that carry the flux is 0.14 to 0.51 decades; replicate MAGIC runs show this part of the map to be reproducible to a few hundredths of a decade, so the residual is model error, while below $10^{-6}$ the reference itself is noise. Applied without retraining to the rectangular Protvino labyrinth, the prediction correlates with MAGIC at 0.96. Used as weight windows there, with its deepest cells clamped at deployment, it gives an exit-detector figure of merit 54 times the analog value, 1.7 times that of the MAGIC generation run for the same geometry, and 0.80 of that of reused MAGIC windows whose construction it does not pay for. The run cost of any window set is shown to be set by its deepest cells and predictable from a population proxy.

papers.title: Tiling circular $n$-boards with squares and (1,1)-fences
papers.abstract: We show that the number of ways to tile a circular $n$-board (an annulus divided into $n$ curved unit square cells) with appropriately curved unit squares and curved (1,1)-fences is a Lucas number squared if $n$ is even and an odd-indexed Lucas number otherwise. A curved (1,1)-fence is composed of two curved unit squares separated by a gap in the shape of another curved unit square. This combinatorial interpretation of the Lucas numbers squared and the odd-indexed Lucas numbers allows us to obtain various identities concerning these sequences in a quick and lucid manner.

papers.title: Planar energetics do not determine twin persistence in nanocrystalline aluminium
papers.abstract: Planar energetics are the standard descriptors of twinnability in face-centred cubic metals and the usual validation targets for interatomic potentials. Here we show that they do not determine whether deformation twins persist in nanocrystalline aluminium. Two machine-learned potentials reproducing the same zero-load slip curves and closely spaced layered energy surfaces predict, from a common separated-fault precursor under identical loading, retained twin coverage of 64\% and 14\%. The divergence traces to forces within distorted partial cores acting along the trailing translation that would remove an outer fault. Planar energetics do set the margin: an outer fault more than halves the incremental barrier for middle-plane shear, yet twin completion and fault removal remain separated by only 10--21 mJ m\textsuperscript{-2}. Whether an assembled twin persists is decided instead by the orientation of local traction relative to the full-slip bisector and by the arrival order of partial-slip fronts from the grain-boundary network.

authors.name: Yuan Tian
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology Beijing

papers.title: CARF: Context-Aware Reasoning Supervision for Scientific Evidence Screening
papers.abstract: Systematic reviews synthesize biomedical evidence to inform clinical and public-health decision-making, but require domain experts to manually screen thousands of studies against detailed eligibility criteria. We investigate whether language models can assist with this bottleneck by learning from expert feedback on title and abstract screening decisions and model-generated reasoning. We introduce the Context-Aware Reasoning Framework (CARF), a human-in-the-loop framework that uses expert feedback on model-generated reasoning to adapt language models to context-dependent screening tasks. We evaluate CARF on systematic reviews of verbal autopsy and cause-of-death ascertainment methods used in global public health mortality surveillance. CARF shows competitive screening performance compared to evaluated models while retaining high sensitivity, and is more inclined to retain ambiguous, context-dependent studies for human review. Together, these findings suggest that expert-corrected reasoning is a promising supervision signal for context-dependent scientific screening, while retaining a role for human oversight.

authors.name: Amy Gu
authors.institution: University of Iowa Stead Family Children’s Hospital

authors.name: Li Liu
authors.institution: Capital University of Economics and Business

papers.title: LLMs as Judges and Examinees for Medical Item Difficulty Prediction
papers.abstract: Predicting medical item difficulty from item text alone remains challenging. Prior work has largely relied on linguistic features or text representations derived from general-purpose and domain-specific language models, but predictive performance has remained modest. This study takes a different approach by using difficulty-related signals that emerge when open-weight large language models (LLMs) interact with test items. Using USMLE and PANCE medical licensure examination items, we examined LLMs in two roles. As judges, the models provided absolute difficulty ratings and pairwise difficulty comparisons. As simulated examinees, they generated response-based signals including correctness, keyed-option probability, response entropy, and the probability margin between the top two options. We then combined the strongest judgment and response signals with baseline item features in downstream prediction models. Pairwise difficulty judgment was the most consistent individual LLM signal across both datasets, while simulated-examinee signals and absolute judgments provided complementary information in some feature combinations. The best configurations reached a Spearman correlation of $\rho$ = .447 on USMLE, exceeding the best system in the 2024 BEA shared task ($\rho$ = .25), and $\rho$ = .494 on PANCE. These results were comparable to direct absolute judgments from the proprietary frontier model Claude Opus 5 ($\rho$ = .443 and .488, respectively). Overall, judgment and response signals from open-weight LLMs captured difficulty-related information beyond text representations. Because these models can be deployed locally, the approach offers a practical option for predicting the difficulty of unreleased or high-security test items.

papers.title: Crossing the Chasm: Bridging Visual Augmentations and Designer Intent
papers.abstract: To direct attention and communicate context, visualization designers often employ augmentations such as annotations, animated transitions, and stylistic layouts. While graphical perception principles can helpfully prescribe effective low-level representations of data, they lack guidance for augmentations that service higher-level communication goals. To bridge this gap, we contribute a design space that frames designer intent as viewer-oriented cognitive behaviors, grounding communicative aims in actionable visualization design techniques, including both visual encodings and augmentations. This design space consists of common augmentation tactics (annotation, animation, stylized encodings, etc.) that implement design strategies (spotlighting, sequencing, association, etc.) to achieve higher-level design goals (observe, interpret, introspect), often simultaneously. We demonstrate the analytic and generative value of our design space with examples across varied designer objectives. We discuss how our contributions help align designer intent with reader takeaways, pave the way for readers to learn more effectively, and enable future (semi-)automated systems to support visualization designers in achieving their communication goals.

papers.title: Reciprocity formulas for generalized Dedekind character sums
papers.abstract: In this paper, we apply the Fourier series technique to establish a new formula for the product of the generalized Bernoulli function and the Bernoulli function. As applications, we derive some reciprocity formulas for generalized Dedekind character sums. In particular, we show that the reciprocity formulas of Berndt, Can, and others follow as special cases.

papers.title: What Makes Medical Examination Items Difficult? Using Large Language Models to Explore Patterns Associated With Empirical Item Difficulty
papers.abstract: Research on medical item difficulty has largely focused on prediction rather than on identifying interpretable patterns associated with empirical difficulty. This study used empirical difficulty labels to guide large language models (LLMs) in inducing difficulty rubrics and examined how rubric guidance affected LLM difficulty judgments. Using training items and their empirical difficulty estimates from the United States Medical Licensing Examination (USMLE) and the Physician Assistant National Certifying Examination (PANCE), Claude Opus 5 induced separate rubrics for absolute and pairwise difficulty judgment. None of the induced rubrics treated surface features, such as stem length, option count, or images, as major sources of difficulty. Several patterns emerged across both examinations, including cue convergence, misleading cues, and option competition, although their specific forms differed. Retrieval of knowledge that could not be derived from the stem was particularly prominent in the PANCE rubrics, whereas the USMLE rubrics placed greater emphasis on integrating multiple clinical cues. We compared commercial and open-weight LLMs on held-out items under unguided and rubric-guided conditions. Rubric guidance changed how models used the difficulty scale but did not consistently improve performance. In absolute judgments, guidance encouraged broader use of the scale and generally improved coarse-grained agreement, without consistently improving rank ordering. In pairwise comparisons, its effects varied across models and examinations, and judgments became more sensitive to presentation order. These findings suggest that the value of label-guided rubric induction may lie more in generating interpretable, testable hypotheses from empirical difficulty data than in reliably improving difficulty judgments.

papers.title: A Pretrained Model for Bayesian Filtering in Heterogeneous Dynamical Systems
papers.abstract: Filtering has not yet had its foundation-model moment: state estimation is still dominated either by online Bayesian filtering algorithms that require known dy- namics as inputs, or by learning-based neural filters trained from scratch for a single system or parametric family. The core challenge is structural heterogene- ity: dynamical systems differ in their governing dynamics, physical scales, and noise levels, precluding a shared representation space for a reusable filter. To bridge this gap, we introduce FilterFM, the first pretrained model for Bayesian filtering that estimates latent states across heterogeneous dynamical systems with a single checkpoint. FilterFM employs a hierarchical two-level observation se- quence encoder and a prior-to-posterior state-reconstruction module that together handle varying observation and state dimensions across heterogeneous systems, while modeling state uncertainty via quantile prediction. Trained on a mixture of heterogeneous filtering tasks, FilterFM exhibits superior in-domain performance, delivering significant gains in estimation accuracy, runtime efficiency, and noise robustness compared to existing baselines. Beyond in-domain performance, it marks the first model to successfully enable zero-shot filtering on unseen dynamics, bridging the generalization gap in state estimation. Furthermore, we uncover clear scaling behaviors in foundation-model-based Bayesian filtering, which combined with comprehensive component ablation studies, validate the structural optimality of our design and broaden the generalization scope for this research field.

authors.institution: Wuhan University of Science and Technology
