papers.title: Grounding Long Financial Text with Semantically-Enriched Tables via Multimodal Learning
papers.abstract: We propose a multimodal transformer framework for efficiently modeling long1 financial documents that combine structured tabular data with noisy, unstructured2 textual disclosures. The framework represents financial tables as semantically3 enriched token sequences and integrates them with long-form text through a cross-4 attention mechanism that explicitly captures cross-modal dependencies. In par-5 ticular, we augment each numerical variable with a semantic embedding derived6 from its textual definition, enabling the model to encode both numerical magnitude7 and economic meaning. This design yields a more expressive and parameter-8 efficient representation of tabular data compared to value-only embeddings. Using9 a large-scale dataset of financial statements and MD&A disclosures, we show that10 structured numerical features remain the dominant source of predictive signal;11 however, textual information provides consistent incremental gains when incor-12 porated via cross-attention rather than simple concatenation. Our results further13 demonstrate that noisy textual disclosures are most useful when conditioned on a14 stable, semantically structured tabular representation. In particular, using frozen15 variable-level tabular representations as cross-attention queries enables the model16 to weight MD&A chunks differently for each financial variable and observation.17 These findings suggest that cross-attention provides an efficient mechanism for18 table-conditioned aggregation of long-form narrative evidence.

papers.title: Influences of $N_2$ flow rate on the superconducting properties and dimensionality of epitaxial TiN thin films
papers.abstract: TiN thin films have received great attention in the field of superconducting quantum computing due to their low loss characteristics derived from stable chemical and thermal properties, as well as excellent electrical conductivity. In this study, TiN thin films with a thickness of 35 nm were epitaxially grown on MgO substrates using the DC reactive magnetron sputtering technique. The crystal structure, film thickness, and surface morphology of the thin films were characterized. The films exhibit a very flat surface with a root mean square roughness of only a few tenths of a nanometer. The influences of nitrogen ($N_2$) flow rate on the surface morphology, superconducting transition temperature ($T_c$), residual resistivity ratio (RRR), normal-state resistivity ($\rho_n$), upper critical field, and superconducting dimensionality were investigated systematically. The experimental results show that the TiN film deposited with a $N_2$ flow rate of 1.5 sccm exhibits optimal performance, including the highest $T_c$ (4.93 K), the largest RRR, the lowest $\rho_n$, and the lowest slope of the out-of-film upper critical field near Tc. Moreover, it is found that the background vacuum inside the growth chamber has a significant impact on the superconducting properties of TiN films, and the degradation of vacuum degree can lead to the decrease of $T_c$. The upper critical field reveals a significant anisotropic feature. Importantly, the in-film upper critical field data demonstrates that the optimization of sample quality leads to deviation from two-dimensional superconducting behavior, which provides a new perspective on the influencing factors of superconducting dimensionality beyond the thickness of films. The present results provide useful references for a comprehensive understanding of the relationship between growth parameters and the superconducting properties of thin films.

authors.name: Yihui Sun
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: LLM-PowerTrace: A Dataset of Time-Resolved GPU Power Traces for AI Compute
papers.abstract: AI compute is becoming large and fast-changing electrical loads. Its impacts on data center infrastructure and power grids depend not only on total energy consumption, but also on how their power draw moves over sub-second to minute timescales, including peaks, ramps, and synchronized fluctuations across accelerators. Existing energy benchmarks for large language models (LLMs) report aggregate quantities such as joules per token and rarely release the underlying time-series measurements, leaving these power dynamics poorly characterized and difficult to model. We introduce LLM-PowerTrace, an open dataset of time-resolved, per-GPU power traces for LLM fine-tuning and inference, sampled every 100\,ms on varying NVIDIA platforms paired with complete workload and system metadata. For fine-tuning, LLM-PowerTrace profiles open model families spanning a wide range of model sizes and fine-tuning methods, together with controlled sweeps over batch size, sequence length, precision, parallelism, and checkpointing. For inference, it covers variations in concurrency, GPU frequency, KV-cache and weight quantization, prompt and output lengths, and request-arrival patterns. LLM-PowerTrace profiles a set of open model families across a wide range of model sizes, and controlled sweeps over batch size, sequence length, precision, parallelism, and checkpointing for fine-tuning, and it sweeps concurrency, GPU frequency, KV cache and weight quantization, prompt and output lengths, and request arrival patterns for inference. Built upon power traces, we define power-grid-facing metrics as well as AI-compute power\&energy scaling law for extrapolating beyond the measured settings. Together, LLM-PowerTrace provides a dataset foundation for modeling, forecasting, and managing the fast-changing electrical behavior of AI compute.

papers.title: FFAI: Flow Matching with Feedback Training and Adaptive Initialization for CT Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Although low-dose, sparse-view, and limited-angle CT involve distinct degradation mechanisms, all three pose reconstruction challenges due to limited measurement information and can therefore be addressed within a unified framework. In iterative image restoration with flow matching, prediction errors may cause inference states to deviate from the prescribed training path, while a fixed initialization may be unsuitable for inputs with varying degradation severity. We propose a unified conditional flow matching method that conditions on the initial reconstruction and combines feedback-aware training with degradation-adaptive initialization. During training, a teacher network simulates inference updates to generate shifted states, from which a student network learns to recover high-quality reference images, improving its ability to handle prediction errors. During inference, the starting time is selected based on the noise level or extent of missing projection data, and the noise added to the initial state is adjusted accordingly to adapt the starting point to the input. Experiments on public benchmark datasets show that the proposed method achieves better quantitative results than the compared methods across all three reconstruction tasks, effectively suppressing noise and artifacts while preserving anatomical structures and details.

authors.name: Xing Zhao
authors.institution: Changchun University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Harmonically lifting linear series from curves to K3 surfaces
papers.abstract: We investigate the question of which Brill--Noether special linear series on a curve on a K3 surface lift to the surface. Work of Reid, Donagi--Morrison, Green--Lazarsfeld, Lelli-Chiesa, and others shows that Brill--Noether special linear series admits lifts in many cases, in particular when the linear series computes the Clifford index of the curve. Using the recently defined notion of harmonic filtrations of Lazarsfeld--Mukai bundles, we show the same is true for a linear series computing the Brill--Noether special Clifford index, an analogue of the classical Clifford index considering only Brill--Noether special linear series, and show that the Brill--Noether special Clifford index is constant in linear series on K3 surfaces.

papers.title: A semi-implicit unified gas-kinetic wave-particle method with energy-conserving electromagnetic coupling for multiscale plasmas
papers.abstract: In multiscale plasmas, kinetic regions coexist with collision-dominated, strongly magnetized and quasi-neutral ones. In these regions, the collision time, the cyclotron period and the plasma period, respectively, are far shorter than the flow time scales. Schemes that treat the collisions and the field coupling explicitly must take time steps below these times and below the light-crossing time of a cell. This paper presents a semi-implicit unified gas-kinetic wave-particle (UGKWP) method for the multispecies Vlasov-Maxwell system with Bhatnagar-Gross-Krook collisions. The electric field follows from a reformulated Maxwell equation, a single linear system with a unique solution for any time step. Its current response is built from the implicit-midpoint velocity map, which then pushes the particles and the hydrodynamic wave alike. The field step conserves the discrete total energy exactly and remains stable without resolving the cyclotron period, the plasma period or the light-crossing time, so that the time step follows from the flow and sound speeds. A Gauss's law correction adjusts the electric field and the joint charge of particles and wave while conserving the mass, momentum and energy of every charged species. The method reproduces whistler waves and electron plasma waves from Landau damping to collision-dominated oscillations. It agrees with particle-in-cell, two-fluid and magnetohydrodynamic references in a Brio-Wu problem from weak to strong collisionality and magnetization, the Orszag-Tang vortex and collisionless magnetic reconnection. It needs far less CPU time than either the UGKWP method with an explicit solver for the perfectly hyperbolic Maxwell equations or a deterministic multiscale kinetic scheme. In collisional plasmas, it also needs less CPU time than an implicit particle-in-cell method with the same collision operator, increasingly so as collisions strengthen.

papers.title: DropFENO: A Data-Free, Physics-Based Operator-Learning Framework for Droplet Equilibria on Mixed-Wettability Patterned Surfaces
papers.abstract: We study whether the equilibrium of a drop on a chemically patterned wall, and the capillary forces that the pattern exerts on it, can be learned from the free energy alone, without solution data. We introduce DropFENO (Droplet Free-Energy Neural Operator), in which Fourier (FNO), tensor-factorised Fourier (TFNO) and wavelet (WNO) neural operators are trained in two and three dimensions on the diffuse-interface free energy of the drop, with its volume and centroid constraints imposed as penalties. The predictions are tested with the virtual-work (Hellmann--Feynman) theorem: the force exerted by the pattern on a held drop is a wall integral of the equilibrium field which, for a drop straddling a wettability step, reduces identically to the contact-line law $F=\sigma\Delta\cos\theta\,L$. DropFENO reproduces this law and the energy landscape of a drop crossing a step, and reproduces the pinning of the receding contact line less accurately. The residual error lies in the soft modes of the capillary energy (small displacements of the interface and the contact line). This explains why the energy is predicted accurately while contact-line positions are not, and why on striped walls the operators return Cassie-like states instead of the edge-pinned states whose anisotropic apparent angles the reference minimiser shares with lattice Boltzmann simulations. On held-out patterned walls the median energy of the predictions lies $\NdEmedRandFnoTwo$ of the free-drop energy above the best known minimum (FNO, two dimensions), at about one hundredth of the cost of a per-instance minimisation, and a refinement by a classical solver started from the prediction returns the reference state in almost all cases.

papers.title: SPARSEBLEED: Bypassing Attribute-Inference Defenses via Sparsity Optimizations
papers.abstract: Deep neural networks (DNNs) are widely deployed in safety- and privacy-critical domains such as healthcare and finance, where models are trained on confidential data. This paper presents the first hardware-level attribute-stealing attack that bypasses state-of-the-art privacy defenses, revealing that accelerator optimizations intended for performance can directly undermine data confidentiality. SparseBleed requires no access to gradients, logits, model weights, ground-truth labels, power traces, DVFS manipulation, shared caches, or other channels. Instead, we show that sparsity-driven execution paths encode stable timing signatures that act as a surrogate for model confidence, enabling high-fidelity attribute inference from a single query. SparseBleed generalizes across heterogeneous backends and hardware engines, including Intel AVX2/AVX-512/AMX, NVIDIA Ampere Tensor Cores with 2:4 sparsity, and nine well-known sparse and dense libraries such as Intel oneDNN, oneMKL SparseBLAS, and NVIDIA cuSPARSE. We evaluate SparseBleed to infer sensitive input attributes and true output labels. On Texas-100X, SparseBleed infers sensitive input attributes such as Sex with 66.39% accuracy and recovers the true output label, Surgical Procedure, with 99.8% accuracy. Finally, we evaluate mitigations. Constant-time execution by disabling sparsity optimizations is expensive (e.g., up to $2\times$ higher latency on NVIDIA Sparse Tensor Cores and $\approx 25\%$ higher power in AMX microbenchmarks). By contrast, a padding defense that equalizes responses to the worst-case time masks timing leakage with only 7.24% average performance overhead across nine libraries on Texas-100X/Adult and near-zero extra energy.

papers.title: When Relevant Code Is Wrong: Runtime-Aware Context for AI Coding Agents
papers.abstract: AI coding agents increasingly rely on retrieved code and development history to guide software changes. However, highly relevant artifacts may describe implementations that are inactive or incompatible with the target deployment. Neither semantic similarity nor recency establishes whether retrieved information remains applicable under feature flags, architectural migrations, and deployment-specific configurations. We challenge relevance-oriented retrieval by introducing operational context validity, a task-, deployment-, and time-dependent criterion for determining whether software evidence can legitimately guide implementation decisions. We instantiate this new retrieval principle in CASE, an agent-agnostic framework that connects repository artifacts with runtime configurations and architectural evolution, classifies evidence as valid, invalid, or unknown, and generates context packages distinguishing actionable guidance from historical rationale and unresolved constraints. We investigate its feasibility through a reproducible preliminary evaluation involving six development tasks, 15 artifacts, and three deployments. Conventional retrieval exposes 16 incompatible artifact occurrences as actionable, whereas CASE excludes them while retaining all applicable artifacts under the prototype's reference rules. Recency filtering reduces valid recall to 0.43, while removing feature-flag evidence from CASE reduces it to 0.13. Although these results demonstrate feasibility rather than improvements in coding-agent correctness, they reveal limitations of relevance-based retrieval and motivate a new research direction: enabling coding agents to reason not only about which information is relevant, but also whether it remains operationally valid.

papers.title: Exponential Ergodicity and Invariant Distribution of a Degenerate Reflected SDE with Stable Noise
papers.abstract: We study a two-dimensional degenerate stochastic differential equation with oblique reflection and spectrally positive strictly stable noise of index in $(1,2)$, motivated by join-the-shortest-queue systems with heavy-tailed interarrival times. A polynomial-exponential Lyapunov function and fixed-time minorization establish positive Harris recurrence and exponential ergodicity in weighted total variation. We construct the invariant law from a stable path and prove its absolute continuity. Regulator identities describe stationary dependence and recover the joint Laplace transform from the queue marginal. Idleness inherits the classical stable Ornstein-Uhlenbeck tail; the queue has a sharp exponential tail with a polynomial prefactor whose power is half the stable index and a positive constant represented through regeneration. Conditional on small idleness, idleness divided by the conditioning threshold and the queue converge to independent beta and size-biased limits. Under large-queue conditioning, normalized idleness and queue excess converge to independent Mittag-Leffler and exponential limits.

papers.title: Morphological Features of Murine Pulmonary Arterial Networks for Diagnosing Vascular Disease
papers.abstract: Hypoxia-induced pulmonary hypertension results from prolonged time spent in a low-oxygen environment. The induced pulmonary hypertension leads to vascular remodeling, including vessel dilation and decreased compliance. This study aims to identify changes in vascular morphology in mice with pulmonary hypertension induced by hypoxia. To do so, we examine the pulmonary arterial network morphology using methods from geometry, topological data analysis, and statistical shape analysis. Tools from these fields are applied to arterial networks excised from micro-CT images of thirteen mice at four pressures. Networks from the hypertensive mice were normalized via a radius pruning algorithm, and analysis was conducted on the entire arterial network, as well as on a per-lobe basis. The main objective of this study was to present an adaptable pipeline for extracting features from micro-CT images to study how vascular disease affects arterial network morphology. Using this pipeline, we showed that the hypertensive mice have increased radius ratios and decreased length-to-radius ratios. Persistent homology analysis revealed that hypertension leads to lower branch-to-branch proximity and lower directional complexity in both the posterior and anterior directions. Persistence curves, particularly Betti curves, revealed lobe-specific differences in the left and inferior lobes. The first two shape principal component scores were also able to discriminate between control and hypertension at lower pressures. Importance metrics for each feature are computed using a boosted decision tree, and then an SVM classification model is fit with the most informative predictors for hypertensive classification.

papers.title: Cubic lower bounds for the permanent in odd characteristic, for Pfaffian representations, and for polynomial entries
papers.abstract:
The determinantal complexity of a polynomial is the order of the smallest matrix whose entries are polynomials of degree at most one and whose determinant equals the polynomial. A lower bound for the permanent in this measure is the algebraic form of the question whether the permanent is harder to compute than the determinant. Over the complex numbers, the best known lower bound grows cubically in the size of the permanent. It holds even when the permanent only has to be a limit of such determinants.
  I prove that the cubic lower bound holds over every algebraically closed field of odd characteristic $p$, with a constant that depends on $p$. Hence the cubic bound does not depend on characteristic zero. I also prove the bound for Pfaffians, which are square roots of determinants of skew symmetric matrices. Lower bounds for Pfaffians imply the same bounds for determinants. Further, I prove the bound, divided by $a$, for matrices whose entries are polynomials of degree at most $a$. All three results come from one lower bound for smooth hypersurfaces. I prove it in every characteristic by counting intersection points together with their multiplicities.

papers.title: Averaged Annealed Markov Chains Achieve the Algorithmic Threshold for Tensor PCA, Part II: Langevin Dynamics
papers.abstract: We consider the tensor principal components analysis (tensor PCA) problem on the sphere, in which we are asked to recover an unknown vector in $\mathcal{S}_N=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^N:\lVert x\rVert^2=N\}$ from a noisy observation of its $k$-th tensor power, for a fixed $k\ge3$. Tensor PCA exhibits a well-studied information-computation gap: global algorithms such as spectral methods and sum-of-squares work above an algorithmic threshold, below which we know matching lower bounds (against these and some other restricted models of computation). In contrast, local algorithms such as Markov chains were only known to succeed from a random initialization at a polynomially larger signal-to-noise ratio, and were believed to be inferior to global algorithms for tensor PCA. Continuing the program initiated in Part I [arXiv:2610.16705], we show that spherical Langevin dynamics, when supplemented with annealing and ergodic averaging, achieves polynomial-time strong recovery above the algorithmic threshold from a uniformly random initialization. Together with Part I, our results demonstrate that local Markov chains can succeed all the way down to the algorithmic threshold from an uninformative cold start.

papers.title: How Does Perceived Empathy From AI Chatbots Shape Users' Privacy Attitudes, Behaviors, and Needs?
papers.abstract: Prior research suggests that some dimensions of AI empathy may increase users' disclosure to chatbots, posing growing privacy risks as chatbots become more capable of empathic interaction. Yet this work often conceptualizes AI empathy narrowly, leaving users' own definitions and their broader privacy experiences unexplored. We interviewed 21 AI Chatbot users about what AI empathy meant to them and how it shaped their privacy attitudes, behaviors, and needs. Participants characterized empathy through five components--understanding, resonating, caring, expressing, and helping. Most participants viewed resonating and caring as essential components of human empathy but absent from AI empathy. Yet AI's contextual, in-depth understanding and helpfulness still encouraged highly sensitive disclosure. This highlights that AI empathy can endanger users' privacy without necessarily making AI seem human. Participants also desired varied forms and levels of empathy, each associated with distinct privacy needs. We offer actionable recommendations for designing privacy-enhancing mechanisms for empathic AI interactions.

papers.title: Joint Rigid Alignment and Morphable Reconstruction from Partial 3D Face Scans
papers.abstract: Aligning a partial, real-world 3D face scan to a canonical representation requires solving two coupled problems at once: estimating the rigid pose that brings the scan into a common frame, and completing the facial shape in regions the scan never observed. Existing pipelines typically decouple these steps, running a generic point-cloud registration front end followed by a separate non-rigid fitting or deformation stage. Building on the GeoTransformer superpoint-matching architecture, we propose a single network that predicts both a rigid pose and a shape-complete point cloud in one forward pass: a cross-attention regressor, conditioned on transformer point features and predicted coarse correspondences, maps a partial scan to per-patch coefficients of a 3D morphable face model learned offline from a corpus of 8,000 identities. The resulting morphed template is then used, in the same forward pass, as the target for fine-grained Sinkhorn matching and rigid pose estimation, supervised purely by geometric alignment to ground-truth morphed geometry, so no hand-labeled coefficients are required. Against six classical and learned non-rigid registration baselines on held-out identities, our method leads the strongest ones by 3-4 times on per-vertex error and baselines that collapse the head onto the visible region by more than an order of magnitude, and is simultaneously the most accurate and fastest method on ground-truth-free scans from two independent real-scan datasets, NoW and NPHM. Code will be made publicly available.

papers.title: TabCUQ: Context-Uncertainty Quantification for Tabular Foundation Models
papers.abstract: Tabular foundation models use in-context learning to estimate conditional expected outcomes and average treatment effects for specific groups of individuals. Using these estimates to guide scientific decisions requires reliable uncertainty quantification. The challenge is to account simultaneously for two sources of uncertainty: limited-context bias and context variation arising from the small labeled sample supplied at inference. Predictive spread does not directly quantify both sources of uncertainty, and we observe that the ordinary bootstrap may substantially overestimate context variation, whereas subsampling may underestimate it. We introduce TabCUQ, a perturbation-based framework that injects noise into observed outcomes and applies the foundation model to the perturbed contexts. TabCUQ estimates context variation using wild-bootstrap dispersion and accounts for limited-context bias using the maximum deviation between perturbed and original estimates. For a kernel-regression analogue whose estimation error admits an exact decomposition into these two components, we show that our framework provides asymptotically valid pointwise coverage. In simulations, TabCUQ substantially improves coverage, with average interval widths typically about twice those of an oracle bias-aware benchmark. Across seven real-world tasks, it also improves coverage of reference functions learned from much larger samples.

papers.title: Numerical Investigation of Soft-to-Hard Convergence: Discretization, Admissibility, and Spectral Regularity
papers.abstract: This paper presents a numerical investigation of soft-to-hard terminal constraint convergence for optimal control problems governed by a second-order ordinary differential equation and the one-dimensional heat equation. The study complements the analytical convergence theory through comparisons with exact solutions and independently computed numerical approximations. For the heat equation, a fully discrete Crank--Nicolson finite-difference formulation is validated against exact modal solutions, exhibiting approximately second-order convergence in the terminal-state and midpoint-sampled control errors under simultaneous space-time mesh refinement. Numerical experiments demonstrate the predicted first-order penalty convergence for benchmark problems and investigate the admissibility threshold governing finite-energy exact terminal controllability. Additional modal experiments examine the dependence of terminal-error convergence rates on spectral regularity, illustrating intermediate rates consistent with the theoretical estimates and asymptotic predictions. The results provide computational evidence supporting the soft-to-hard convergence framework and clarify the roles of discretization, target admissibility, and spectral regularity.

papers.title: Galois module structure of Deligne--Lusztig varieties for $\mathrm{GL}_3$
papers.abstract: Let $\overline{\mathbf{Y}}(w)\to\overline{\mathbf{X}}(w)$ be the ramified Galois cover of compactified Deligne--Lusztig varieties. Our objects of study are the Lefschetz numbers for the action of the finite covering group $T^{wF}$ on the coherent cohomology of the structure sheaf of $\overline{\mathbf{Y}}(w)$. The Lefschetz numbers for all elements of $T^{wF}$ determine the virtual $T^{wF}$-representation given by the alternating sum of these cohomology groups. In the two cases of Deligne--Lusztig surfaces of type $A_2$ and ${}^{2}A_2$, we give explicit formulas for the Lefschetz numbers for a generator of the stabilizer of an irreducible component. It follows that the equivariant Euler characteristic of the compactification $\overline{\mathbf{Y}}(w)$ is not virtually free as a virtual module over the covering group.

papers.title: Computationally Constrained First-Order Prediction-Correction Approach for Time-Varying Convex Optimization
papers.abstract: Time-varying optimization methods often predict the locations of time-varying optima, then sample the objective function being minimized, and then compute corrections to those predictions. However, those works typically do not account for settings in which computations are limited. Therefore, in this work we formulate a prediction-correction algorithm that is designed to obey constraints on the total number of iterations it can execute over a given time horizon. We first show that there is a critical threshold for the average number of computations that can be executed between samples of the objective. Then, we show that if the number of allowable computations is above this threshold, then the distance to a time-varying optimum bound decays geometrically. Next, we show that if the number of allowable computations is below that threshold, then the distance to a time-varying optimum still remains bounded. Therefore, it is still possible to track time-varying optima with bounded error even under restrictive limits on the number of computations that can be executed. We also present an algorithm to determine how many prediction and correction steps should be executed for each sample of the objective. Simulation results show that under typical conditions our approach reduces cumulative tracking error by 45.5% compared to a comparable baseline approach.

papers.title: Federated Learning for Semantic Communications over Multiple Access Channels
papers.abstract: This paper presents a federated learning (FL) framework for semantic communication (SemCom) over the multiple access channel (MAC), where multiple distributed transmitters simultaneously convey semantic information to a common receiver using end-to-end learned semantic representations. Semantic feature extraction, compression, wireless transmission, and semantic inference are jointly optimized through FL-based SemCom. Unlike conventional SemCom systems that train users independently, simultaneous semantic transmissions over the MAC enable concurrent training of multiple transmitters within the same transmission interval, thereby reducing training overhead and channel usage. Federated semantic aggregation is incorporated with shared and personalized encoder components, allowing transmitters with limited local training data to benefit from semantic representations learned from transmitters possessing larger datasets while preserving local adaptation. Evaluated using the CIFAR-10 dataset over fading channels, the proposed approach maintains high semantic inference accuracy under shared wireless access and significantly improves performance under severe data imbalance. In the meantime, simultaneous semantic transmissions can significantly reduce training overhead while preserving robust semantic performance across distributed transmitters with heterogeneous local datasets. These results highlight the potential of combining FL and SemCom to support scalable and communication-efficient edge intelligence in future wireless networks.

papers.title: Making Smart Homes Fit for Autistic Children: Family Work and Monitored Independence
papers.abstract: General-purpose smart-home technologies are increasingly present in family life, yet how they support or disrupt autistic children and families with autistic children remains underexamined. We conducted a multi-source qualitative study drawing on five caregiver interviews, Xiaohongshu (also known internationally as RedNote) posts explicitly situated in autism contexts, and contextual posts from Xiaohongshu and Weibo. We find that families create support for autistic children by adapting environmental outputs, prompts, and interaction channels, while sensory intensity, communicative rules, and opaque operating states can turn the same technologies into barriers. Support also depends on continuing family work, including translation, configuration, modification, maintenance, and boundary-setting. Remote monitoring enables conditional independence while generating tensions among safety, privacy, and control. We contribute three concepts, including relational fit, family work as support infrastructure, and monitored independence, for understanding accessible domestic technology. We derive design implications for adjustable interaction, legible and recoverable failure, lower-burden configuration, and negotiable monitoring.

authors.name: Hrishitva Patel
authors.institution: The University of Texas at San Antonio

authors.name: Kyrie Zhou
authors.institution: The University of Texas at San Antonio

papers.title: Multistatic ISAC with Deep Learning-Based Clutter Suppression for 5G and Beyond
papers.abstract: Integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) systems using 5G and beyond signals of opportunity enable joint wireless sensing and communication using shared infrastructure and spectrum resources. While multistatic ISAC can increase sensing coverage with spatially distributed receivers, dense and dynamic clutter can significantly degrade bistatic range and Doppler estimation, leading to errors in target localization and velocity estimation. This paper presents a multistatic ISAC framework with clutter suppression for high-fidelity estimation of target position and velocity. Distributed clutter is modeled with randomly located scatterers with varying Doppler spreads and radar cross sections to capture dense and dynamic clutter effects. A broad range of conventional signal processing baselines are evaluated for clutter suppression, showing limited robustness under strong clutter conditions. To address this limitation, deep learning-based clutter suppression methods are introduced to improve robustness against dense and dynamic clutter by employing residual and attention-enhanced deep neural network architectures that directly enhance target responses from clutter-contaminated observations. These methods substantially outperform conventional approaches in target position and velocity estimation across diverse clutter conditions in multistatic ISAC.

papers.title: Beyond LLM Wrappers: Context Engineering and the Three-Engine Architecture for Reliable Financial AI
papers.abstract:
Financial AI systems must support decision-bearing questions involving payments, collections, cash flow, and compliance while ensuring numerical accuracy, traceability, and auditability. Large language models (LLMs) enable natural language interaction but cannot independently guarantee reproducible calculations or evidence-grounded recommendations. We present a production-grounded architecture integrating three components: a financial knowledge graph for enterprise relationships, temporal context, and provenance; a deterministic optimization engine for financial calculations and decisions; and a multi-agent LLM layer for intent interpretation, task orchestration, explanation, and claim validation. A coordination layer, termed context engineering, selects, ranks, composes, and validates query-specific context across ERP systems, tools, and tenants.
  Based on observations from 15 deployments over approximately 11 months, single-agent pipelines exhibited hallucination rates of about 7-9% (5-10% across query types), including invented invoices and unsupported financial claims. Graph-backed multi-agent validation reduced observed rates to below 1%, although these findings are observational rather than causal. ERP data quality and tenant-specific schemas remained major implementation challenges. Reusable mappings, graph templates, and validation policies coincided with a reduction in deployment time from roughly six to two weeks.
  We argue that financial context engineering extends beyond text-centric retrieval-augmented generation by requiring structured relationships, temporal validity, exact numerical evidence, access controls, and validation against source records and solver outputs. We outline research challenges in evaluation, reproducibility, privacy, context quality, and cross-tenant generalization.

papers.title: TGTV: An Interpretable Framework for UAV Fault Detection and Traceability via Spatiotemporal Graph Learning and Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Fixed-wing unmanned aerial vehicles experience operating-condition transitions, asynchronous sensor sampling, and control-system compensation that can obscure fault signatures. Existing temporal detection methods have limited capacity to represent coupled faults across subsystems, track their evolution, and constrain language-model diagnoses with quantitative evidence. This paper proposes TGTV, an interpretable fault detection and traceability framework that integrates spatiotemporal graph learning with a large language model. A temporal convolutional network and a graph attention network with weighted fused adjacency extract multiscale temporal patterns and spatial dependencies among sensors. A hybrid temporal Transformer and variational autoencoder then evaluates window-level anomalies using prediction errors and reconstruction probabilities. Continuous-time Shapley attribution identifies critical sensors and high-contribution intervals while preserving the temporal continuity of fault evolution. A structured evidence package combines detection results, graph relationships, temporal attribution, sensor attribution, and operating context. An evidence-constrained diagnosis protocol uses this package to generate flight-level conclusions with traceable evidence identifiers. Cross-flight holdout experiments on the public ALFA fixed-wing flight dataset yield a window-level area under the precision-recall curve of 0.976, accuracy of 0.973, recall of 0.902, and F1 score of 0.920. Flight-level fault diagnosis achieves recall of 0.943 and an F1 score of 0.944. These results demonstrate accurate anomaly detection and quantitatively supported fault-tracing cues, providing a basis for interpretable post-flight fault review and analysis.

authors.name: Ji Liu
authors.institution: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

papers.title: Introduction to Separable Simplicial Algebras
papers.abstract: We study separable simplicial algebras and Azumaya simplicial algebras.

authors.name: Eric Zhang
authors.institution: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

papers.title: Tight Stationarity Transfer and Repeatability for Inexact Proximal-Gradient Methods
papers.abstract: Proximal-gradient methods are widely used for composite optimization, but inexact proximal updates introduce a residual in the proximal optimality condition, complicating the analysis of how stationarity changes across a step. We study this question for composite objectives consisting of a smooth convex term and a possibly nonsmooth weakly convex term, focusing on the relationship between the directional-stationarity measures at the input and output points of an inexact proximal-gradient step. We first establish separate input and output bounds, but their combination can yield a conservative estimate because their worst-case residual directions may differ. By exploiting the magnitude and orientation of this shared residual, we establish tight joint bounds and derive an exact one-step stationarity-transfer factor that strictly improves the estimate from separate bounds in the short-step regime. We also identify the precise residual-tolerance threshold for finite uniform stationarity transfer. A further distinction emerges over multiple steps: endpoint worst cases can repeat over arbitrarily many iterations, whereas interior worst cases cannot persist across two consecutive steps, yielding strict two-step submultiplicativity. These results also provide principled tolerance-selection rules, descent estimates, and stationarity-complexity guarantees for inexact proximal-gradient methods.

authors.name: Shenghan Mei
authors.institution: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

papers.title: Evaluating Generalization and Long-Term Stability of Smartwatch-Based Cuffless Blood Pressure Monitoring
papers.abstract: Smartwatch-based cuffless blood pressure (BP) monitoring is a promising low-burden solution for long-term cardiovascular management, but practical deployment remains constrained by model complexity, uncertain cross-dataset generalization, and insufficient evidence on long-term tracking stability. This study presents an efficient Signal-Context Gated Fusion Network (SCGBPNet) for cuffless BP estimation from photoplethysmography (PPG) signals. SCGBPNet integrates signal-level representations through self-attention and further incorporates subject-specific contextual information via a compact gated fusion module. On Aurora-BP, SCGBPNet achieved SBP/DBP mean absolute errors (MAEs) of 7.08/4.90 mmHg, compared with 6.44/4.89 mmHg under within-dataset validation on the private smartwatch dataset, indicating a modest within-dataset discrepancy. Cross-dataset transfer from Aurora-BP to the smartwatch dataset increased the MAEs to 8.98/6.47 mmHg, demonstrating substantial cross-dataset degradation. For long-term stability, the proposed method showed low week-to-week performance variation and a low daily decay rate, indicating good stability over a follow-up period of more than one month. Nevertheless, estimation accuracy deteriorated when BP deviated substantially from an individual's baseline. These findings indicate that favorable aggregate MAE alone should not be interpreted as evidence of deployment-ready performance. More systematic and stratified evaluation across dataset settings, BP ranges, and baseline-deviation levels is needed to assess the practical reliability of smartwatch-based cuffless BP monitoring.

papers.title: AFast Robot Localization Method Based on Monte Carlo Sampling
papers.abstract: Localization is an essential capability of intelligent robots. However, in real-world constrained environments, robots often cannot rely on external localization systems. Therefore, this paper proposes an online particle-filter localization method based on Monte Carlo sampling. The method is applied to the localization of a mobile robot in a maze environment and requires only four range sensors mounted on the front, rear, left, and right sides of the vehicle, without the need for any heading information. Simulation experiments demonstrate that even in a maze where local regions are highly similar, the vehicle can still achieve relatively accurate localization, thereby providing a fast and effective approach for robot localization in complex environments.

authors.name: Hang Li
authors.institution: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

papers.title: Majorana Zero Modes in Fractional Vortices
papers.abstract: Majorana zero modes (MZMs) are promising for topological quantum computation, with vortices in topological superconductors serving as a leading platform. Recent experiments show that integer Abrikosov vortices in iron-based superconductors can split into fractional vortices (FVs) carrying fractional flux quanta. We show that due to topological protection, MZMs hosted by FVs are spatially unfolded over the FV cores, while fermionic bound states remain localized at individual FV cores. This yields zero-bias conductance peaks in both local tunneling and nonlocal crossed Andreev reflection, offering an alternative MZM signature.

authors.name: Haotian Li
authors.institution: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

papers.title: PriorMaskMap: Robust Online Vectorized Map Construction with Biased Priors
papers.abstract: Online vectorized map construction provides autonomous vehicles with essential, real-time semantic and geometric scene understanding. While leveraging prior maps presents an opportunity to improve accuracy, they are often biased due to outdated information or temporary road changes. Existing methods, which typically treat priors as fully reliable or only consider limited noise patterns, suffer severe performance degradation when these priors are imperfect. To address this, we propose PriorMaskMap, a robust framework for prior-guided vectorized map construction. Its first innovation is a Prior-Aware Confidence Estimator (PACE) that evaluates the input rasterized map against current visual observations. It assigns confidence scores to regions classified as reliable, erroneous, or blank, creating a foundational mask that guides two subsequent branches. In one branch, the Dual-Prior Query Generator (DPQG) selectively filters and embeds both rasterized and vectorized priors to initialize informative queries from trustworthy map structures. In the other, the Confidence-Guided Prior Fusion (CGPF) module spatially propagates and refines the mask, using the refined version to govern the fusion of BEV features with the prior map, thereby providing rich contextual representations for the map decoder. Evaluation on the nuScenes dataset shows that PriorMaskMap achieves superior mapping precision over existing approaches and exhibits marked robustness when provided with priors containing apparent errors. Our code is released at https://github.com/healenrens/PriorMaskMap.

papers.title: A Physics-Informed Neural Network for Geodesic Computation and Visualization of Geodesic Spheres on Riemannian Manifolds
papers.abstract:
Visualizing geodesic structures associated with general Riemannian metrics is a challenging problem in computational differential geometry. In this work, we present a computational framework for visualizing geodesics and geodesic spheres on a three-dimensional Riemannian manifold equipped with the metric $g=\text{diag}(1,x^2,1), x>0$. The associated Christoffel symbols and curvature tensors are computed symbolically, and the resulting geodesic equations are solved using both \texttt{SciPy}'s numerical integration method and a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN). The two solutions are compared to assess the accuracy of the neural network approximation. We further develop geodesic spike diagrams and surface visualizations to illustrate the deformation of geodesic spheres relative to their Euclidean counterparts. Intrinsic Riemannian surface area and volume are estimated numerically using the induced metric and the Riemannian volume density, respectively. For the chosen metric and a geodesic ball of radius one, the computed area and volume are approximately
  $0.362\%$ and $0.364\%$ smaller than the corresponding Euclidean values at the base grid resolution. A grid-refinement study is also performed to examine the sensitivity of these estimates to numerical resolution. The proposed framework demonstrates how symbolic differential geometry, numerical integration, and PINNs can be combined to investigate and visualize geometric structures associated with Riemannian metrics.

papers.title: High-dimensional two-sample testing: From optimal transport to optimal derangements
papers.abstract: In recent years, optimal transport has emerged as a useful framework for constructing distribution-free multivariate two-sample tests by transporting observations to a reference distribution under a suitable transportation cost. However, existing optimal transport-based tests can perform poorly in high dimension, low sample size (HDLSS) settings, and their performance depends critically on the choice of the reference distribution and transportation cost. We investigate this phenomenon and show that suitable choices can substantially improve their performance. Motivated by this analysis, we introduce a class of two-sample tests based on optimal derangements that do not require an external reference distribution. The minimum distance pairing test of Rosenbaum arises as a special case when the optimization is restricted to a subclass of derangements, thereby revealing a connection between this method and optimal transport. We propose the optimal derangement (ODER) test and its distribution-free variant, the ODER-SHC test, obtained by restricting the minimization to derangements consisting of a single Hamiltonian cycle. We establish their consistency under both HDLSS and classical large-sample asymptotic regimes. We also develop corresponding procedures based on the $L1$ distance and establish their high-dimensional consistency under conditions involving coordinate-wise energy distances. These $L1$ distance based tests can also discriminate between two high-dimensional distributions with identical first two moments but different marginal distributions. Analyses of benchmark datasets and extensive simulation studies demonstrate the performance of the proposed methods across a variety of alternatives and data settings.

papers.title: Equivariant Morita equivalence for finite cyclic group actions on noncommutative tori
papers.abstract: Li proved that the noncommutative tori $A_\theta$ and $A_{g\theta}$ are strongly Morita equivalent whenever $g\in\mathrm{SO}(n,n|\mathbb{Z})$ and $g\theta$ is defined. We study equivariant extensions of these equivalences for canonical finite cyclic group actions. Let $W\in\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{Z})$ satisfy $W^t\theta W=\theta$, $W^k=I_n$ and $1\notin\operatorname{spec}(W)$, and write $\rho(R)=\operatorname{diag}(R,(R^t)^{-1})$. If $g\rho(W^t)g^{-1}=\rho(P)$ for some $P\in\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{Z})$, we equip Li's $A_{g\theta}$--$A_\theta$ Heisenberg equivalence bimodule with a compatible $\mathbb{Z}_k$-action. Consequently, the crossed products $A_{g\theta}\rtimes_{\alpha_{P^t}}\mathbb{Z}_k$ and $A_\theta\rtimes_{\alpha_W}\mathbb{Z}_k$ are strongly Morita equivalent. For the canonical flip action by $\mathbb{Z}_2$, we prove that Morita equivalence of crossed products implies Morita equivalence of the underlying tori in every dimension, and prove the converse in dimensions two through four. For each fixed dimension $2\leq n\leq 4$, the complete invariants are the central rank and canonical $K_0$-trace range of the underlying torus, with the latter taken up to positive scaling. For the standard cyclic group actions of orders $2$, $3$, $4$ and $6$ on rotation algebras, we prove that the crossed products are Morita equivalent exactly when the action orders agree and the parameters lie in the same fractional-linear $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$-orbit, generalizing the result of B\"onicke et al.\ from irrational to arbitrary real parameters. We also construct infinite families of distinct parameters giving Morita-equivalent crossed products for each fixed $W$ satisfying the stated hypotheses.

papers.title: Local Convergence of Triadic Closures of Sparse Random Graphs
papers.abstract: Triadic closure is a natural mechanism for modeling the clustering phenomenon observed in many real-world networks. Given a possibly random undirected graph $H$, we consider pairs of non-adjacent vertices that have a common neighbor. Conditional on $H$, each such pair is joined by an edge independently and simultaneously, with a probability depending on the degrees of its endpoints and on the number of their common neighbors. The resulting graph is called a triadic closure of $H$. We study the effect of this operation on local convergence. More precisely, we prove that if a sequence of potentially random finite undirected graphs of $\left( H_n \right)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ converges locally in probability to a rooted graph $H^*$, then the corresponding sequence of triadic closures converges locally in probability to the same triadic closure of $H^*$. As a consequence, we obtain a general limit theorem for the clustering coefficients of triadic closures. In particular, we show that the triadic closures can have a strictly positive limiting clustering coefficients even when the limiting clustering coefficients of the parent graph sequence is zero. Finally, we apply our results to several classical sparse random graph models including Erd\H{o}s-R\'{e}nyi, configuration, preferential attachment models and compute the limiting clustering coefficients of their triadic closures.

papers.title: Non-Volatile Memory Devices for Neuromorphic Computing
papers.abstract: This chapter explores the critical role of emerging non-volatile memory (eNVM) devices in advancing neuromorphic computing. Inspired by the human brain's remarkable ability to perform complex tasks like pattern recognition and adaptation, neuromorphic computing offers immense potential for implementing complex neural networks (NNs) in real hardware. Despite ongoing research into the brain's complexities, its fundamental operation relies on neurons (processing units communicating via electrochemical signals) and synapses (junctions between neurons). The modifiable strength of the synapse is key to learning and memory functionality, allowing the brain to adapt and rewire itself. For dense and low-power circuits in neuromorphic computing, these eNVM devices are ideal due to their synaptic-like behavior and non-volatile information storage. Properties such as conductance modulation of these devices emulate synaptic plasticity, which is crucial for learning, and their scalability makes them promising for large-scale neuromorphic architectures. This chapter will delve into the various types of eNVM devices such as resistive RAM (ReRAM), phase-change memory (PCM), spintronics-based memory devices, and their applications in neuromorphic computing, discussing their challenges and opportunities, and highlighting recent advances in their integration within neuromorphic systems.

papers.title: Investigation of perovskite related oxides: structural and magnetic properties
papers.abstract: Perovskites exist in varied structures and show structure dependent magnetic properties which is of great interest in the field of multiferroics, magnetocaloric and spintronic devices. Here we intend to study the various rare-earth(R) and transition metal (TM) ion interactions depending on their structures. Different Curie temperature, spinglass transition and spin reorientation transitions were observed depending on the degree of interactions and structural properties. It is interesting to study the role of orbital interactions, disorder in magnetic transitions leading to change in superexchange and double exchange interaction. On substitution at A-site or B-site results in change in magnetic interactions, as well as creates structural distortions. We also obtained results where the spin interaction of the transition metal and rare-earth interaction, magnetic anisotropy, orientations of orbitals, disorder induced interactions were observed.

papers.title: Bridging Neural Representations and Symbolic Semantics in Audio Classification
papers.abstract: Deep audio classifiers can achieve strong predictive performance, but their hidden representations remain difficult to interpret. Existing audio explainability methods often focus on input-level attribution, such as waveform segments, spectrogram regions, or acoustic features, and provide limited insight into what hidden neurons encode. Interpreting hidden neurons at the concept level can provide a more meaningful view of what an audio model learns internally. This paper investigates whether hidden neurons in audio classifiers can be associated with human-understandable symbolic acoustic concepts. A model-agnostic neurosymbolic framework is presented for analyzing the final hidden layer of audio classifiers, containing 32 neurons, through symbolic concept induction. The framework is evaluated on two audio classification settings: music genre classification using GTZAN dataset and musical instrument classification using IRMAS dataset. Results show that several hidden neurons can be associated with meaningful induced concepts, and most confirmed neuron-concept pairs are statistically supported using the Mann-Whitney U test. These findings suggest that symbolic concept induction is a promising direction for explaining latent audio representations beyond input-level attribution.

papers.title: PhysVLMM: Interaction-Conditioned Physical Belief Maps for Articulated Objects in Robot Scene Maps
papers.abstract: Mobile robots must open doors and drawers, yet their scene maps record what each object is and whether it has moved, not how it will respond to a pull. This paper proposes PhysVLMM, a method that maintains a physical belief for every articulated part of a Vision-Language-Motion Map and answers a planner's queries about it, with two algorithms: a map update and a query. Watching a part move provably cannot identify its dynamics, and a measured pull identifies only the pulled part, up to one direction. PhysVLMM therefore (i) keeps that direction as a posterior instead of a point estimate, (ii) passes the evidence of each pull in closed form to the untouched look-alike parts of the map, and (iii) answers whether an action will succeed at a stated risk, or abstains. On real doors and drawers in 18 homes, it identifies the joint type in 86% of held-out pulls (48% for a learned single-view method) and predicts the response to a pull with 41% lower error than differentiable simulation (CRPS 0.323 vs. 0.544), four orders of magnitude faster (13 ms vs. 230 s per case). The posterior lowers the final-position error from 0.460 to 0.270, sharing lowers the force error of untouched parts from 56% to 42%, and at every stated risk from 0.02 to 0.30 the false-safe answers stay within it. Pooling all measured parts of a home does as well as the look-alike groups, and simpler variants predict where a pulled part stops at least as well.

authors.name: Dibyendu Ghosh
authors.institution: Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science

papers.title: Characterizations of $\varphi$-inner uniform domains and $\varphi$-uniform domains in metric spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study $\varphi$-uniform/-inner uniform domains in metric spaces. In our first main result, we establish quantitative characterizations of three different definitions of $\varphi$-uniformity/-inner uniformity in length spaces. In our second main result, we obtain a geometric sufficient condition of $\varphi$-uniform/-inner uniform domains in doubling length spaces, which extends the corresponding result of Guo-Huang-Wang [arXiv 2025] and Gao-Guo-Huang-Wang [arXiv 2025] for linear case.

authors.name: Miao He
authors.institution: Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region Peoples Hospital

papers.title: Robust LLM-Generated Text Detection through Matched Conditional-Response Probing
papers.abstract: Reliable detection of large language model (LLM)-generated text must remain effective under meaning-preserving text revisions, such as rewriting, polishing, and expansion. In practice, LLM outputs are often rewritten, polished, expanded, translated, or lightly edited before publication, weakening the lexical, syntactic, and local discourse cues used by many existing detectors. We introduce \textbf{M}atched \textbf{C}onditional-\textbf{R}esponse \textbf{P}robing (\textbf{MCRP}), a frozen-LLM probing framework that measures how a candidate text responds when a semantically matched condition is introduced, removed, or replaced. For each candidate, the frozen probe LLM first generates a short semantic condition and then compares token-level losses and prompt--target attention measurements under matched, null, and control conditions. It aggregates bidirectional conditioned alignment, counterfactual sensitivity, and internal attention coupling into a probe representation, on which it trains a lightweight supervised random-forest classifier while keeping the probe LLM frozen. Across standard detection, robustness to meaning-preserving text revisions, multilingual, and multidomain evaluations, MCRP achieves consistently strong performance. Under rewriting, polishing, and expansion, it reaches 93.97\% F1 and 96.24\% ROC-AUC, outperforming the strongest evaluated baseline by 19.50 and 25.77 percentage points, respectively. Component ablations show that the response feature groups make complementary contributions to predictive performance. In the condition-control study, matched conditions consistently outperform random, mismatched, and corrupted alternatives, demonstrating a measurable incremental benefit from semantic matching.

authors.name: Hao Ren
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Heavy Oil

papers.title: Higher order Teodorescu transform in the theory of generalized partial-slice monogenic functions
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the higher order Teodorescu transform in the context of generalized partial-slice monogenic functions. By introducing the generalized poly-partial-slice Cauchy kernel, we derive some integral formulas including higher order Borel-Pompeiu formula and Cauchy integral formula for generalized poly-partial-slice monogenic functions. Furthermore, we define the higher order Teodorescu transform in this context and establish its existence, continuity, and some mapping properties. These results extend classical integral methods in Clifford analysis to the generalized poly-partial-slice setting.

papers.title: A Positivity-Preserving Numerical Method for the Free Cox-Ingersoll-Ross Equation
papers.abstract: We introduce a positivity-preserving drift-implicit square-root Euler method for the free Cox--Ingersoll--Ross (CIR) equation driven by free Brownian motion. The method is obtained by discretizing the square-root equation implicitly in the drift and preserves strict positivity of the numerical solution without any step-size restriction. Under the Feller condition, we establish the uniqueness of the global strictly positive solution and derive an upper bound for its operator norm. A key ingredient for the error analysis is a free stochastic differential representation of the inverse square-root process. Another key ingredient is an a priori grid-point error estimate for sufficiently small step sizes that yields uniform upper and strictly positive lower spectral bounds for the numerical solution on any fixed finite time interval. These results support the strong convergence of order $1$ and improve the classical results. Moreover, both the exact and numerical solutions are exponentially stable with respect to perturbations of the initial value. The numerical stability holds for arbitrary step sizes, and the associated discrete decay rate converges to its continuous counterpart as the step size tends to zero. Numerical experiments confirm the theoretical results.

authors.name: Y. Niu
authors.institution: Key Laboratory of Smart Manufacturing in Energy Chemical Process, Ministry of Education

papers.title: Differentiation and Shift Property Characterisations of the Group Fourier Transform on the Heisenberg Group
papers.abstract: Recently, Krukowski characterised the classical Fourier transform on the real line in terms of its behaviour with respect to differentiation. For locally compact abelian groups, he obtained a characterisation based on the behaviour of the Fourier transform under the shift. Each of these results assumed that the operator (to be characterised) is an integral transform (with a kernel satisfying suitable regularity conditions), paired with a normalisation which he refers to as the Dirac delta property. In this paper, we obtain analogous results for the group Fourier transform on the Heisenberg group. Here, the differentiation property is formulated in terms of the behaviour of the group Fourier transform with respect to the left-invariant vector fields, and the shift property is based on its behaviour under right translation. Both of these characterise the group Fourier transform on the Heisenberg group, once paired with a Dirac delta property. Our results assume that the transform is continuous and linear, and do not require it to be an integral transform a priori.

authors.name: R. Lakshmi Lavanya
authors.institution: Indian Institute of Science Education and Research, Tirupati

papers.title: Langevin Dynamics of Non-reciprocally Coupled Spherical Spin Glasses
papers.abstract: We analyze the limiting dynamics of two copies of a disordered mean-field spherical $p$-spin system coupled non-reciprocally to one another and initialized independently of the disorder. We prove that, on every finite time interval, as the system size tends to infinity, the empirical correlation and integrated response functions converge almost surely and in $L^q$ for $q \geq 1$, uniformly in time, to the unique non-random solution of a system of coupled integro-differential equations. For even $p$-spin models, we establish stationarity and exponential decay of the correlation and response functions in the high-temperature regime. In the special case of the spherical Sherrington--Kirkpatrick model, we derive explicit representations of the limiting correlation and integrated response functions. These representations allow us to characterize the long-time dynamics throughout the full range of temperatures. In particular, we prove the occurrence of aging in the low-temperature regime and fluctuation-dissipation behavior in the high-temperature regime, and provide a separate characterization of the dynamics at the critical temperature.

authors.name: Ratul Biswas
authors.institution: Military Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Quantum-Inspired Pairwise Ranking Aggregation via Active LLM Feedback
papers.abstract: Ranking aggregation from multiple retrievers is a powerful yet under-explored technique in modern retrieval and RAG systems. We introduce LLM-IRA, the first extension of the quantum-inspired interactive ranking aggregation framework to document reranking. By leveraging large language models (LLMs) solely for pairwise judgments on high-disagreement document pairs, our method learns fusion weights in a principled, interactive way. The final ranking is a simple, ultra-fast pointwise linear fusion of scores, no full pairwise matrix or expensive listwise prompting is required. Experiments on the BEIR benchmark and TREC Deep Learning tracks with an open-weight instruction-tuned judge (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct) show that LLM-IRA matches or numerically exceeds strong static fusion baselines on 5 of 6 evaluated benchmarks. We report two weight-update variants: momentum blending and a full accumulated-history refit, which together reach statistical significance (Wilcoxon signed-rank, p<0.05) over the best unsupervised aggregator on 4 of 6 benchmarks (DL19 under momentum; DL20, DBpedia, and NFCorpus under accumulated refit, which is the stronger of the two configurations overall). On the benchmarks we profiled (DL19, DL20), it already clears the best unsupervised baseline within as few as 5 LLM calls per query, well before exhausting its typical ~25--30 call budget. LLM-IRA also achieves cost-effectiveness comparable to state-of-the-art zero-shot LLM rerankers at an order of magnitude fewer LLM calls, and requires no training data or model fine-tuning.

papers.title: PairWatch: Pair-Aware Anomaly Transformer for Detecting Adversarial Rendezvous in Public Satellite Catalogs
papers.abstract: Documented adversarial rendezvous and proximity operations (RPO) appear in the public TLE catalog, yet existing TLE-based maneuver detectors treat each satellite in isolation - mistaking routine station-keeping for adversarial behavior and missing RPO entirely when the target stays passive. We argue that the right unit is the satellite pair and the right inductive bias is the kinematic symmetry between approach and recede. We instantiate both with PairWatch, a pair-aware AnomalyTransformer whose attention prior is augmented with a sign-symmetric geometric similarity over relative-motion features, and release an open benchmark of 359 windows from public Space-Track data spanning 11 documented RPO events, 100 Clohessy-Wiltshire synthetic adversarial windows, and a five-class hard-negative set culminating in the TerraSAR-X / TanDEM-X helix formation. Under the deployment-relevant criterion of a single threshold separating real RPO from operational negatives - a necessary property for catalog-scale screening - PairWatch is the only model that succeeds, with the property holding in 100% of bootstrap resamples versus 0-19.5% for three neural baselines and under 0.1% for four physics-informed detectors. A per-source analysis exposes a shortcut-learning failure mode of single-number AUROC: simpler baselines attain higher overall AUROC by shortcutting a synthetic-vs-formation contrast with no operational meaning; removing this single cell flips the test ranking entirely (LSTM-AD), and these baselines fail the security-relevant task the benchmark was built to measure.

papers.title: DEQ-Stereo: Deep Euilibrium Video Stereo Matching via Adaptive Convergence
papers.abstract: Iterative refinement models have significantly improved stereo matching accuracy, but their rigid, fixed update schedules incur heavy computational costs and a strict trade-off between speed and accuracy. This challenge is magnified in video streams, where traditional online methods resort to reducing feature channels or relying on expensive temporal warping. To address this, we propose \textbf{DEQ-Stereo}, a novel video stereo matching framework based on the Deep Equilibrium (DEQ) paradigm. Instead of unrolling a fixed number of iterations, DEQ-Stereo reformulates the refinement as an implicit fixed-point problem, adaptively terminating once convergence is met. To ensure fast and stable intra-frame convergence, we introduce the \textbf{Convolutional Simplified Gated Unit (ConvSGU)}, which eliminates unnecessary non-linearities by modeling the latent state as a gated, element-wise sum of inputs. Furthermore, to exploit cross-frame temporal coherence, we propose \textbf{Temporal State Transfer (TST)}, a warm-start strategy that propagates the converged hidden state to the next frame without requiring explicit pose or warping priors. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that DEQ-Stereo delivers state-of-the-art performance with a superior accuracy-to-latency trade-off.

papers.title: FARE: Factor-Aware Retrieval with Error-Guided Fusion for Retail Forecasting
papers.abstract: Retail sales forecasting underpins inventory planning, yet promotions and calendar events reshape short-term demand. Although each factor usually has historical occurrences, the complete factor combination of a target week often has few precedents. The challenge is therefore to retrieve informative partial matches and weight them by their reliability, which varies across series. We propose FARE(Factor-Aware Retrieval with Error-Guided Fusion), which ranks historical weeks separately for each known target-week factor and merges the selected weeks into a factor reference under a fixed budget. Guided by shrunk errors from completed development weeks and the current disagreement among candidates, a first gate mixes this factor reference with a shape reference from similar sales histories, and a second gate controls how strongly the mixture corrects a backbone forecast. Both gates remain fixed during testing. On Favorita, M5, Rossmann, and Rohlik, FARE reduces the weighted absolute percentage error (WAPE) of five backbones by 11.46%, 4.06%, 14.63%, and 10.16% on average. With Chronos-2 frozen, FARE also outperforms conventional and existing enhancement methods, including supervised residual correction and retrieval augmentation. Code is available at https://github.com/HousonGu/FARE .

papers.title: Distributional Flexibility under Box-Cox Normality: A Theoretical and Empirical Evaluation of the Power-Normal Distribution
papers.abstract: Methods based on Box-Cox models have recently been developed for inference on clinically interpretable treatment effects in clinical trials. These methods model marginal outcome distributions using the power-normal distribution (PND), but the range of real-world data distributions that it can adequately approximate remains unclear. We evaluated PND approximations using two parameterizations of the four-parameter generalized $F$/generalized beta of the second kind family and 165 laboratory variables from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey. Overall distributional agreement was assessed using the overlap coefficient and Jensen-Shannon divergence, and location and spread on the original scale were evaluated using relative biases in the median and interquartile range. The PND closely approximated a broad range of smooth unimodal positive distributions in both the theoretical and empirical evaluations. Reduced agreement was associated with pronounced lower-bound accumulation, heaping or discretization, and multicomponent or peak-tail features. These features may be recognizable before fitting and provide practical guidance for assessing the suitability of the PND. We also developed the R package powerNormal for distributional calculations, parameter estimation, reparameterization, and random-number generation for the PND.

papers.title: Towards Myocardial Infarction Diagnosis: An Investigation into Machine Learning and Deep Learning Algorithms using ECG Data
papers.abstract: Myocardial Infarction (MI) is a severe and potentially fatal cardiac condition caused by myocardial injury due to ischemia, and timely detection can substantially reduce its mortality. Electrocardiography (ECG) is the primary diagnostic modality for MI, but manual interpretation is susceptible to human error. In this work, we propose Visionary V2, a multi-step, adaptive filtration method for ECG signal normalization, and use it to study machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) approaches to MI detection on the PTB Diagnostic ECG Database using all 15 available leads. On statistical features extracted from the filtered signals, such as the R-R interval, a Bagging ensemble of decision trees reaches 96.6% accuracy, compared with 87.7% when the signals are processed with BioSPPy. We further generate an image dataset from the filtered signals, on which a custom ResNet-50 misclassifies only 1 of 7,000 validation images and a custom CNN reaches an F1 score of about 98.7%. Finally, we apply LIME, Grad-CAM and Integrated Gradients to verify that the image models attend to the ECG waveform rather than the background. These results indicate that careful signal normalization combined with ML and DL models can support fast and accurate automated MI screening.

papers.title: A Defense-Aware Explainable AI Framework for Feature-Level Vulnerability Analysis in Optimal Power Flow
papers.abstract: Optimal power flow (OPF) is a foundational analysis in power system operation, and inaccuracies in OPF decision-making can result in significant operational and security consequences. With the increasing adoption of machine-learning-based OPF surrogate models for real-time and large-scale applications, power system operation has become more susceptible to cyber threats, including data manipulation and false data injection attacks. Explainable artificial intelligence (XAI), particularly Shapley value-based approaches, has been employed to quantify the influence of input features on OPF outputs. Features exhibiting high influence are commonly interpreted as vulnerable. However, this interpretation neglects the role of attack detection mechanisms in the system, which typically monitor input-to-input relationships to detect anomalous behavior. Consequently, highly influential features may be readily detectable and may not represent the most vulnerable attack surfaces. To address this limitation, we propose a defense-aware explainable AI framework that explicitly incorporates attack detectability alongside operational impact. The framework integrates an OPF surrogate model representing input-to-output dependencies with a vanilla autoencoder representing input-to-input dependencies. Shapley-based explainability is applied to both models to construct a feature-level vulnerability metric. Empirical evaluation on IEEE test systems demonstrates that the proposed framework more accurately identifies security-relevant vulnerabilities than conventional OPF-surrogate-model-only explainability approaches.
