Our results explore exciton and valley dynamics as sensitive probes of strongly correlated states in moir\'e systems and highlight possible ways to control excitonic coherence and valleytronic properties in two-dimensional quantum materials.

authors.name: Wataru Idehara
authors.institution: Institute of Advanced Energy, Kyoto University

papers.title: TreemapMix: Dirichlet-Controlled Multi-Image Augmentation for Probability and Ordinal Supervision
papers.abstract: Data augmentation improves visual recognition by exposing models to synthetic training examples that encourage generalization beyond the observed data. Mixed-sample methods extend this idea by combining multiple images. However, many common approaches either mix only pairs of images or rely on fixed small layouts, limiting control over source count, visible area proportions, and induced supervision. We propose TreemapMix, a distribution-controlled multi-image augmentation that samples source weights from a Dirichlet distribution and assigns them to area-proportional regions using a treemap partition. The resulting known region areas support two complementary objectives. TreemapMix with soft cross-entropy (SCE) treats areas as soft class-probability targets, while TreemapMix with a Plackett-Luce (PL) objective converts areas into ordinal supervision. On ImageNet-1K under matched training recipes, TreemapMix-SCE achieves substantially lower calibration error than evaluated mixed-sample baselines, while TreemapMix-PL achieves the strongest Top-1 accuracy. Transfer experiments on object detection and instance segmentation suggest that TreemapMix-pretrained features remain useful beyond classification. These results show that controlled multi-image composition can expose the same region-area information as either probability-matching or rank-matching supervision. Code is available at https://github.com/Ejafa/treemapmix.

authors.name: Yingsheng Geng
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Moments propagation in the Vlasov equation and application to the Navier-Stokes-Vlasov equations
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study how the propagation of particle moments depends on the fluid velocity in the Vlasov equation. We present some new moment estimates involving the velocity in this equation. As an application, we establish Ladyzhenskaya-Prodi-Serrin-type regularity criteria involving only the velocity field for weak solutions of the 3D Navier-Stokes-Vlasov system.

papers.title: When an effort-maximizing team architecture is unstable
papers.abstract: Organizations choose team structures to intensify competition, yet their members may prefer to reorganize. We ask whether an architecture that maximizes aggregate effort can remain stable when contestants may form a replacement team from incumbent rosters. When a coalition draws from identical teams and reproduces their type, its members and the designer rank the reorganization in opposite directions: the coalition gains precisely when total effort falls. A strict effort optimum can therefore supply its own blocking certificate, while a stable optimum can survive only on a plateau where every reachable reorganization of this kind leaves effort unchanged. In a linear benchmark, we characterize stability against every feasible one-team reorganization and global effort maximization over every feasible partition. Except under pair capacity, the two regions do not overlap; with pair capacity, they meet only at one boundary. The ordering persists in a matched quadratic benchmark with strictly convex effort cost, and broader one-step deviation rights cannot restore overlap. Among standardized full-cap designs, the unique stable-effort optimum uses the largest feasible roster and sets incentive concentration at its blocking boundary.

papers.title: Length-Preserving Vessel Trajectory Simplification With Controllable Compression-Precision Bound
papers.abstract: Vessel trajectory data from the Automatic Identification System (AIS) is important for a wide range of maritime analysis and management applications. As AIS datasets continue to grow in scale, trajectory simplification (or compression) algorithms have become indispensable tools for managing their computational demands. Existing approaches, however, largely overlook the preservation of trajectory length, a critical metric of direct relevance to maritime environmental auditing and voyage management. We address this gap by framing trajectory simplification as a pair of dual optimization problems subject to error constraints: Compression-Driven Simplification (CDS), which minimizes data volume for a given length-error tolerance, and Precision-Driven Simplification (PDS), which minimizes length approximation error for a given compression target. Both problems are solved within a unified dynamic programming framework, and we provide mathematical proofs establishing that our formulation yields globally optimal solutions. This guarantees flexible, direct control over both compression ratio and length-approximation fidelity. { We benchmark CDS and PDS on real-world AIS datasets spanning diverse navigation scenarios and representative water area, comparing against state-of-the-art baselines. Experimental results on public benchmark datasets demonstrate that even under a small length error tolerance ($\epsilon=0.1$ nmi), our methods achieve about 91\% data compression rate, approximately 14\% higher than the best-performing baseline, which implies that our methods are capable of maximally preserving the trajectory length while reducing data redundancy significant.

papers.title: Masked Erosion: How Acceptance Gates Lose Redundant Safeguards in Self-Improving Agents
papers.abstract: Self-improving LLM agents edit their own harness, the prompts and rules around a fixed model, and keep an edit only if an acceptance gate scores it higher on a batch of tasks. Such a gate sees what the harness does under the current model, not what it would still prevent if one safeguard failed. When safeguards overlap, deleting one is masked: the others still block the harm, so the gate decides on task success alone and redundancy erodes unseen. We measure harm for every subset of four written safeguards in two agent environments and run 411 improvement loops under ten gate rules, mostly as controlled deletion experiments, plus three runs of the GEPA optimizer. A deletion behind another working safeguard adds almost no observable harm. A paired significance test blocks deletions that pass by chance but not deletions that genuinely raise task success, and a larger evaluation batch lets it delete cheaper safeguards: at the same cost, 20-task batches kept every harness protected while 40-task batches lost all six. Large harm audits prevent exposure but not the loss of depth, which turns into harm when the harness is reused with a weaker model. GEPA kept every safety rule verbatim, yet two of its three final harnesses misused credentials under a weaker model. A statistical model frozen before the runs predicts where each gate's protection breaks as safeguard cost and batch size change, and freezing safety text or auditing one-layer ablations preserves depth.

authors.name: Weicai Long
authors.institution: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)

papers.title: Agent Transfer Protocol: Server-Mediated Agent-to-Agent Communication Architecture for the Agentic Web
papers.abstract: The Agentic Web needs to support continuous collaboration among agents from different organizations. These collaborative relationships may span multiple tasks, network connections and execution instances. Such interactions require stable communication entries, message reception when instances are offline, and source verification after delayed reading. How to organize these responsibilities so that cross domain communication does not depend on specific execution instances being continuously online is a key issue for building long term agent interaction infrastructure. We propose ATP (Agent Transfer Protocol), a cross organization agent communication protocol adopting a domain mediated architecture. In this architecture, administrative domains maintain stable addresses and receiving entries for logical agents. The domain servers of both parties continuously undertake cross domain transmission. The receiving domain verifies and saves messages for execution instances to read later. The sending domain signs the complete message envelope. This allows the receiving instance to independently reverify the domain source and content integrity after the original connection ends, provided the original verification public key is still trusted and obtainable. We implemented an ATP prototype and evaluated it through a controlled cross organization LLM agent workflow, mechanism checks and latency measurements. The workflow completed subsequent business processing after instances went offline or were replaced. The independent verifier successfully verified the domain source and content integrity of saved messages. Latency measurements further quantified the communication and processing overhead introduced by the continuous mediation of domain servers.

authors.name: Haixin Duan
authors.institution: Beijing National Research Center for Information Science and Technology

papers.title: SpaceAct: Benchmarking 3D Spatial and Temporal Reasoning via Closed-Loop Action and Active Perception
papers.abstract: To solve problems in 3D space rather than merely describe images, multimodal large language models (MLLMs) need 3D spatiotemporal reasoning: reconstructing 3D geometry from occluded 2D views, anticipating physical dynamics, and executing precise, closed-loop actions. Prior studies test passive VQA on static images or symbolic planning, requiring no execution or supplying privileged coordinates while ignoring collision, statics, and timing. We introduce SpaceAct, an interactive benchmark evaluating 3D spatiotemporal reasoning via closed-loop physical action and active perception, with SAPA, a Spatiotemporal Active-Probing Agent framework. Built on interlocking bricks and mechanical puzzles, it has 108 verified instances across 36 task families in six categories, without privileged coordinates, and diagnostic modes (+plan, +state, no-camera, blind, L7 levers). In brick-bridging or aperture-threading, models rotate the camera to resolve occlusion, read in-scene rulers, output 6-DoF poses under swept-collision and statics checks, and self-correct via split-screen rollback feedback (dynamic tasks freeze time during deliberation and give five strobe frames). Across 10 frontier MLLMs on the 44 hardest instances, scores span 4.8-79.1 (seven solve at most 27.3% of 6-DoF tasks); for the top three, a reference plan (+plan) closes 44% of the gap while leaving collisions at 5.2 per episode, whereas adding exact 3D state (+state) closes 90% and cuts collisions to 0.5; for four others, +plan lifts the mean score from 10.9 to 35.3 and +state to 81.8; and 46% of failures are collision or observation loops. SpaceAct and SAPA advance evaluation to closed-loop physical interaction, showing that even with a valid plan, MLLMs remain bottlenecked by 3D visual grounding and action refinement, while offering a testbed for active multi-view exploration and explicit 3D grounding.

authors.name: Chenglong Shi
authors.institution: University of Shanghai for Science and Technology

papers.title: PyMsOfa 2.0: A Pure-Python Implementation of the IAU Standards of Fundamental Astronomy Service
papers.abstract: Astrometric calculations require authoritative algorithms so that every result is correct and reproducible. The Standards of Fundamental Astronomy (SOFA) service of the International Astronomical Union (IAU) provides such algorithms, officially released only in Fortran 77 and ANSI C. In an earlier paper we presented the first version of PyMsOfa, a Python package wrapping the SOFA C library. Here we present PyMsOfa 2.0, which re-implements the complete SOFA library in pure Python with NumPy. All 247 official SOFA routines are ported directly to Python, requiring no compilation of any external C library and running identically on Linux, Windows, and macOS. The routines operate on NumPy arrays, so arguments can be processed in batch, which is convenient for survey pipelines and Monte Carlo simulations. The package also provides an extension module with validated models not yet part of the official SOFA release, such as the improved precession--nutation model IAU 2006$_{J_2}$/2000A$_{R26}$. The reimplementation reproduces the official SOFA algorithms: all constants, series, and coefficients are taken unchanged from the SOFA source files, and routine names differ only by the pym prefix. We verify every routine against the official SOFA C release: most reproduce the C results to machine precision, the remainder within the accuracy tolerance stated in the SOFA documentation. The package has been applied to Gaia astrometric reduction and used in astrometric studies of the Closeby Habitable Exoplanet Survey (CHES) mission, and is available through PyPI, GitHub, and Zenodo.

papers.title: Cinematize from Unreal: Agentic Choreography for Controllable World Simulation
papers.abstract: Controllable world simulation requires more than visually plausible frames: scenes must retain persistent state, coordinated actions, and editable temporal structure. Generative world models offer flexible visual synthesis, but their outputs do not always expose the objects and transitions needed for precise revision. Graphics engines provide executable state and direct control, yet translating language into valid operations requires specialized knowledge of assets, geometry, and interdependent APIs. We present CineU (Cinematize from Unreal), an agentic system for language-driven world orchestration and cinematic choreography within Unreal Engine. From a code-based world modeling perspective, an Unreal project serves as a persistent, inspectable world representation, while agent-generated code specifies operations whose effects can be executed and verified. CineU combines hierarchical orchestration, cascaded asset retrieval and geometry-constrained placement, capability-aligned code synthesis, and multi-stage verification with localized repair. Shared scene and timeline context coordinates entities, actions, camera trajectories, and shot boundaries while supporting dependency-aware revisions. Experiments on scene construction, selective editing, multi-shot cinematography, and component ablations show how specialized execution knowledge and engine feedback improve task completion and targeted recovery. CineU illustrates how executable world state can complement learned visual generation to support controllable and revisable simulated worlds.

papers.title: EKR Results for Cuspidal Representations of $\mathrm{GL}_2(q)$
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{S}_\chi$ be a cuspidal representation of $\mathrm{GL}_2(q)$. A subset $S \subseteq \mathrm{GL}_2(q)$ is \emph{$t$-intersecting} if $\dim_{\mathbb{C}}\{v \in \mathcal{S}_\chi: g_1v = g_2v\} \geqslant t$ for any $g_1, g_2 \in S$. In this paper, we determine $\max{|S|}$ where $S$ is $t$-intersecting.

papers.title: Low-regularity global well-posedness for the defocusing cubic wave equation outside a ball with radial initial data
papers.abstract: We study the three-dimensional defocusing cubic nonlinear wave equation with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary condition in the exterior of the unit ball, $\Omega=\R^3\backslash\overline{B(0,1)}$, for radial initial data. For every $\frac12\leq s\leq\frac34$, we establish global well-posedness in $\dot H^s_{D,rad}(\Omega)\times\dot H^{s-1}_{D,rad}(\Omega)$, including the critical endpoint $s=\frac12$, without an additional $L^4$ assumption on the initial displacement. The proof uses the distorted Fourier transform associated with the Dirichlet Laplacian to establish radial Sobolev embeddings, including the quantitative estimate $\|f\|_{L^p(\Omega)}\leq C\sqrt p\,\|f\|_{\dot H_D^{1/2}(\Omega)}$ for $4\leq p<\infty$, with $C$ independent of $p$. We combine a nonlinear Fourier truncation argument with the critical Strichartz estimate to construct a global nonlinear component with high-frequency-truncated initial data. For the remainder, we construct a local energy solution in an affine energy space and derive a logarithmic energy inequality that prevents finite-time energy blow-up. Persistence of the original Sobolev regularity, uniqueness, and local Lipschitz dependence on each finite time interval complete the proof.

papers.title: Nonlinear coercivity and orbital stability of smooth solitary waves for the modified Camassa--Holm equation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish orbital stability of smooth zero-background solitary waves for the modified Camassa--Holm equation in $H^1(\R)\cap W^{1,4}(\R)$ for the full range $\gamma<c<2\gamma$. The main difficulty is that spectral coercivity of the Hessian does not by itself yield nonlinear coercivity in this topology, because normalized perturbations may develop derivative concentration. In order to overcome this obstruction, we apply a penalized Lyapunov functional and introduce a derivative factorization. The key ingredient is a concentration-coercivity principle for the normalized Lyapunov energy, which yields local nonlinear Lyapunov coercivity. Our result extends the $H^1(\mathbb R)\cap W^{1,4}(\mathbb R)$ orbital-stability results of Li and Liu [Ann. PDE, 2021] and Zhang and Zhu [JDE, 2025] to the entire parameter range $\gamma<c<2\gamma$.

authors.name: Ji Li
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: A conditional no-splash criterion for two-fluid Euler--MHD interface
papers.abstract: We study a two-dimensional incompressible two-fluid system: an inviscid, irrotational Euler phase and a viscous, conducting MHD phase, separated by a free interface. We prove a conditional quantitative no-splash criterion for smooth solutions in a specified admissible class. In addition to a bound on the trace of the Euler velocity, an initial bound on the magnetic trace and bounds on the bulk vorticity, this class imposes bounds on the interface Biot--Savart potential and its tangential derivative, fixed exponential vertical localization, and the normal derivative of the bulk vorticity at the interface together with one tangential derivative of it. It also requires a Biot--Savart representation of the Euler velocity up to a bounded-gradient harmonic part and a positive initial chord-arc bound. Under these assumptions the chord-arc functional has a uniform positive lower bound on $[0,T]$, depending only on the interval length, the decay width and the a priori bound, after an enlargement that absorbs the surface tension and the densities. The proof combines a maximum-principle analysis of the interface-vorticity equation, in which the magnetic field enters through the Lorentz term and the pressure jump, with a geometric reduction in the style of Fefferman--Ionescu--Lie.

papers.title: The Polynomially Self-repelling Motion
papers.abstract: [Kosygina et al. 2023] showed that the rescaled polynomially self-repelling walk does not converge to any Brownian motion perturbed at extrema (BMPE). Motivated by this result, we introduce an explicit candidate for the scaling limit, the polynomially self-repelling motion (PSRM), and study its properties. The construction relies on a new family of continuous stochastic flows, called polynomially self-repelling flows, introduced in [Yu 2026]. A key ingredient in relating the limiting process of the rescaled walk to the PSRM is a joint Ray-Knight theorem for rescaled local time processes, extending the classical Ray-Knight theorems of [T\'oth 1996].

papers.title: Discretisation in algebraic $K$-theory of independent ample groupoids and their Steinberg algebras
papers.abstract: An independent ample groupoid $G$ comes equipped with a discrete groupoid $G_d$ and a proper \'etale correspondence $\Omega:G_d\to G$. Discretisation with respect to a homological invariant $\mathcal{H}$ holds when $\mathcal{H}(\Omega)$ is an equivalence. We show for example that discretisation with respect to the $K$-theory spectrum $\mathbb{K} \mathfrak{B}_G$ of the permutative category of bisections always holds, establish excision and continuity for this invariant, and use all this and explicit resolutions by independent groupoids to compute it for several families of ample groupoids. We also prove discretisation with respect to invariants of the Steinberg algebra $\ell[G]$ such as (homotopy) algebraic $K$-theory in several particular cases, and carry out computations.

papers.title: Semantic-Assisted Joint Channel Estimation and Symbol Detection for MU-MIMO Systems
papers.abstract: This paper presents a semantic-assisted joint channel estimation and symbol detection (Sem-JCED) receiver framework for text transmission in multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) systems. Sem-JCED integrates a linear minimum mean-square error (LMMSE) channel estimator, an expectation propagation (EP) symbol detector, and a semantic corrector based on ByT5, a byte-level language model. At each outer iteration, LMMSE estimates the channel from known pilots and data symbol feedback, and EP detects the data symbols. ByT5 then maps the data symbol probabilities to byte probabilities, which provide soft symbol statistics and semantic priors for feedback to LMMSE and EP, respectively, in the next iteration. Simulation results show that Sem-JCED requires about 7~dB lower signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) than conventional JCED to reach a bit error rate (BER) of $1\times10^{-2}$ with four users and four receive antennas, and outperforms maximum-likelihood detection with perfect channel knowledge over the simulated SNR range.

authors.name: Hao Chang
authors.institution: Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs

papers.title: Additive preservers of mutual strong numerical radius orthogonality
papers.abstract: Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space with $\dim H\ge2$. We show that the additive surjections on $\mathcal{B}(H)$ and on its self-adjoint part $\mathcal{B}_s(H)$ that preserve mutual strong numerical-radius orthogonality in one direction are precisely the maps of the form $A\mapsto cUAU^*$, where $U$ is a unitary or antiunitary operator on $H$ and $c$ is a nonzero complex or real scalar, respectively.

authors.name: Yulong Tian
authors.institution: First Hospital of China Medical University

papers.title: The inverse problem for Julia limiting directions in the Eremenko--Lyubich class
papers.abstract: We study the inverse problem for Julia limiting directions in the Eremenko-Lyubich class $\mathcal B$, which is the class of transcendental entire functions with a bounded set of singular values, and its meromorphic generalization $\mathcal B_{mer}$. Every nonempty compact subset of the circle can be the set of Julia limiting directions of an entire $f\in\mathcal B$. For finite unions of nondegenerate closed arcs, the corresponding $f\in\mathcal B$, even with every finite order at or above an explicit bound determined by the arc lengths, can be attained. We also refine the series construction of the latter two authors to obtain $f\in \mathcal B_{mer}$ with any prescribed order and the set of Julia limiting directions.

authors.name: Jun Wang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: REALM: Identifying Minimal Task Assets for LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents often receive access to more files, accounts, and services than a task requires. Prompt injection turns this excess access into an opportunity to redirect execution toward unrelated resources. Applying least privilege therefore requires identifying the assets needed by a task, including assets whose identities emerge only during execution. We present REALM (Required Execution Assets Linked to a Mission), an approach to identifying and maintaining a task's required assets and their permitted uses. The approach represents required assets as Dependency Graph nodes, resolves prerequisite relationships, and admits newly discovered assets through source-scoped selection. It separates discovering an asset from authorizing its use, while preserving the agent's freedom to choose its computation. The REALM Builder maintains the selected grants and projects Asset Files; the Partial API Manager exposes resource-bound Partial APIs to the Agent inside a Task Container. Across 60 clean tasks and 560 injected cases in AgentDyn, it completes 40.0% and 36.4% of tasks and decreases ASR from 16.6% to 0.2% with qwen3.5-flash as the base model.

authors.name: Long Wang
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Cardinality of the K-cones below a non infinitely often $K$-trivial
papers.abstract: Given a real $x\in 2^\omega$, how many reals are there that are simpler (or equally simple) to describe than $x$. With ``simpler to describe" characterized by $K$-complexity of initial segments (hence we call such $y$ with $y\leq_K x$ a solution to $x$), if $x$ is infinitely often $K$-trivial (hence i.o. $K$-trivial), then a simple counting argument shows that the number of solutions to $x$ is countable. If $x$ is non i.o. $K$-trivial, then must it admit uncountably many solutions? Motivated by this question, we show that: (1) There is a non i.o. $K$-trivial $x$ such that most of its solution is i.o. $K$-trivial. i.e., Only countably many solution to $x$ are non i.o. $K$-trivial. In particular, the cardinality of $K$-degree of $x$ is countable. (2) There is a minimal pair of K-degree (meaning their common solutions are all $K$-trivial) so that each of the pair is non i.o. $K$-trivial, generalizing a result of Csima and Montalb\'an (where the pair is not required to be non i.o. $K$-trivial but non $K$-trivial). (3) There is a non i.o. $K$-trivial $x$ whose $\Delta_K$ complexity grows arbitrarily slow (in a weak sense: $\inf_{m\geq n}\Delta_K(x\upharpoonright m)\leq h(n)$ with $h$ a given unbounded and nondecreasing function) such that $x$ admits uncountably many solutions. (4) An ample excess lemma holds for non i.o. $K$-trivial. Namely: $$ \sum_n 2^{-(K(x\upharpoonright n)- \log_2 n)}<\infty. $$ for all non i.o. $K$-trivial $x$. Actually, this even holds for non i.o. $b$-$K$-trivial with $b$ only depends on the universal prefix free machine. The same argument also gives a constant complexity return phenomenon for $K$-trivial where this constant only depends on the universal prefix free machine.

papers.title: Martin-L\"of randomness and rK-reducibility
papers.abstract: Can random real carry arbitrary information. In terms of (Turing) computability, Ku\v{c}era and G\'{a}cs addressed this question in affirmative. i.e., Every real $x\in 2^\omega$ is computable from some Martin-L\"of random real. This result motivated quantitative versions of coding into random reals. i.e., How many bits of the random oracle are needed to compute the first $n$ bits of $x$. Barmpalias and Lewis-Pye obtained a coding that uses $n+O(\log n)$ many bits. Is it possible for the coding to use $n$ bits exactly? This is equivalent to say, if every real is $rK$-reducible to a Martin-L\"of random real. In this paper, we prove that such a coding does not exist. i.e., There exists some real that is not $rK$-reducible to any Martin-L\"of random real.

papers.title: Generalized Discrete Fractal Dimensions of Graph Families
papers.abstract: Quantifying the self-similarity of complex networks via discrete fractal dimensions is a fundamental problem in network science. In this paper, we investigate some general fractal dimensions of graph families based on q-energy and R\'enyi entropy. We first establish several bounds for the energy, and then discuss the monotonicity, measure invariance of the dimensions, as well as some concrete graph families.

authors.name: Cheng Zeng
authors.institution: National Center for Nanoscience and Technology

authors.name: Yumei Xue
authors.institution: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Unstable radial equilibria as sharp concentration thresholds for the J\"ager--Luckhaus model on the unit disk
papers.abstract: We identify unstable radial equilibria as sharp concentration thresholds for the J\"ager--Luckhaus chemotaxis system on the unit disk with no-flux boundary conditions. Concentration is compared through cumulative mass. At fixed total mass, every radial initial profile more concentrated than an unstable equilibrium produces finite-time blow-up, whereas every nonstationary profile less concentrated than that equilibrium generates a global, uniformly bounded solution converging to the least concentrated radial equilibrium. We also classify the radial equilibria and determine their nonlinear stability. Let $\Lambda = j_{1,1}^{2}$, where $j_{1,1}$ is the first positive zero of the Bessel function $J_1$. For $M\ne \Lambda\pi$, the least concentrated equilibrium is the unique locally asymptotically stable equilibrium under mass-preserving radial perturbations. It is spatially homogeneous for $M<\Lambda\pi$ and strictly increasing for $M>\Lambda\pi$. Every other radial equilibrium, including the homogeneous state at $M=\Lambda\pi$, is nonlinearly unstable. These results clarify how total population and initial spatial aggregation jointly determine collapse or bounded redistribution, and how stable peripheral enrichment can occur within the radial model.

papers.title: Omission-Safe Conditional Contracts for Evidence-Closed CI Qualification
papers.abstract: Continuous-integration evidence is conditional: a workflow determines which jobs should run, while an archive records which jobs remain observable. Reconstructing requirements from those observations lets an omission erase its own obligation. We present a qualification method that compiles a pinned workflow into conditional job requirements independently of target presence, retains a fixed capture inventory, and checks source-complete derivation certificates with a separate implementation. For a fixed source, context, scope and binding universe, with sound obligations and applicability judgments that preserve established truth under information extension, withdrawing observation facts cannot create authorization. The implementation handles static matrices, dependency guards and bounded pinned reusable workflows, preserving unknown applicability and separating tolerated outcomes from evidence coverage. Both implementations match the 45 hand-specified authorization controls, reject 180 source-certificate attacks, and exhibit no authorization gain over 704 distinct proper development erasures. An explicitly witnessed 12-job platform run qualifies in both implementations; all 4,095 proper payload-subset erasures block authorization. A frozen collection spans 240 runs in eight workflow families across six projects. All 160 evaluation source certificates independently validate, but unavailable historical execution-source identities leave actual qualification open. Initial gate diagnoses agree on 155/160 runs; a preserved unknown-propagation repair yields 160/160 agreement in a retrospective rerun. The study establishes bounded source extraction and omission resistance, rather than natural-fault prevalence or producer authenticity.

papers.title: On Proximity Gaps for One-Point Algebraic Geometric Codes
papers.abstract:
Proximity gaps and correlated agreement underpin the soundness of interactive oracle proofs. We establish these properties for general one-point algebraic geometry (AG) codes, extending corresponding results for Reed-Solomon codes. For codes of length $n$ over $\mathbb F_q$ with designed distance $n-m$, write $\rho=m/n$ and fix $\rho\in(0,1)$. For polynomial curves of degree at most $\ell$ and any $0<\varepsilon<1$, we prove correlated agreement with multiplicative slack $\varepsilon$ and soundness $O(\ell(\ell+1)/(\varepsilon q))$ whenever $e\le(1-\varepsilon)(n-m)/2$, with no additional genus penalty. This gives asymptotically good AG code families from Garcia--Stichtenoth tower of unbounded length over a fixed field with soundness bounds independent of $n$, beyond the RS restriction $n\le q$. We also establish mutual correlated agreement up to radius $(1-\sqrt{\rho}-\eta)n$, with soundness $O(\ell n/(\eta^3q))$ for $0<\eta<1-\sqrt{\rho}$. Our half designed distance proof combines auxiliary divisors, simultaneous Berlekamp-Welch interpolation, and error-incidence counting to obtain a common polynomial representation without a Polishchuk-Spielman divisibility lemma.
  Finally, two counterexamples on the Garcia-Stichtenoth tower show limitations beyond half the minimum distance, at radii below the Johnson bound and with positive slack. The first requires a positive constant soundness lower bound independent of $q$ and $n$, precluding a uniform $O(1/q)$ guarantee throughout the Johnson regime. The second fixes the field and lets the relative gap above half distance tend to zero while ruling out correlated agreement for every soundness parameter $\sigma<1$, with positive limiting rate and relative error radius.

authors.name: Songsong Li
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology Beijing

authors.name: Chen Yuan
authors.institution: Hunan Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: MemoryFusion: Cross-Temporal Memory Learning for Multimodal Video Fusion
papers.abstract: Multimodal videos contain rich temporal cues that can facilitate faithful fusion. However, existing video fusion methods mainly rely on short-range temporal interactions, leaving valuable long-term information underexplored. Moreover, inconsistent fusion representations can cause flickering artifacts, undermining temporal coherence. To address these coupled challenges, we propose MemoryFusion, a two-stage framework integrating cross-temporal memory learning with progressive temporal refinement. Considering the complementary roles of adjacent and distant frames, the first stage combines a Short-Term Memory Bank for local temporal guidance with a Long-Term Memory Bank that preserves reliable historical information through a fusion-oriented update strategy. To mitigate temporal fluctuations, a Temporal Smoothing Module leverages soft motion cues for coarse background stabilization. Building upon the resulting fusion prior, The second stage further employs a lightweight 3D residual Temporal Refinement Module to correct remaining temporal inconsistencies while enhancing structural details. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MemoryFusion achieves superior fusion quality and temporal consistency over existing frame-based and video-based fusion methods. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/Meiqi-Gong/MemoryFusion.

papers.title: Symmetric Policy Optimization for Zero-Sum Markov Games
papers.abstract: We propose a simple and symmetric method for policy optimization in discounted zero-sum Markov games. The method, termed symmetric policy iteration, operates by evaluating the joint policy and solving the corresponding regularized matrix game at each iteration. By employing a diminishing sequence of regularization strengths, we establish the global linear convergence of the proposed method to the optimal value function and the saddle point. In particular, the method does not require solving any standalone Markov decision process throughout policy optimization, and is symmetric in the sense that it stays invariant regardless of whether we are solving the min-max or the max-min version of the game. To the best of our knowledge, this appears to be the first simple and symmetric policy-based method attaining global convergence for discounted zero-sum Markov games.

authors.name: Yan Li
authors.institution: Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China

papers.title: A Uniform Upper Bound on the Length of MDS Codes from Genus-Two Curves
papers.abstract: We study the maximal length of MDS algebraic geometry codes from genus-two curves over finite fields. Let $C_\mathcal{ L}(D,G)$ be such a code over $\mathbb F_q$, with length $n$ and dimension $k$. Assume that $3\leq k\leq n-3$. We prove that $n<(2q+10\sqrt q+16)/3$. This bound holds for every prime power $q$ and for both parities of $k$. It gives a uniform upper bound of $2q/3+O(\sqrt q)$ for the maximal length. The explicit bound is strictly smaller than $q+1$ when $q\geq125$.

papers.title: Optimal fiber comparisons for random tensors
papers.abstract: We extend Seginer's matrix norm comparison to tensors with optimal dependence on the tensor order. For a real tensor $T$ of order $k\ge2$ with centered, integrable, independent and identically distributed entries, we prove $\mathbb{E} f(T)\le\mathbb{E}\lVert T\rVert_{\mathrm{inj}} \le C\sqrt{k\log k}\,\mathbb{E} f(T)$, where $f(T)$ is the largest Euclidean norm of a one-dimensional fiber and $C$ is universal. The comparison holds for every finite rectangular format, and the entry law may depend on both the dimensions and the tensor order. We show that the factor $\sqrt{k\log k}$ is optimal by considering Rademacher tensors on $[2]^k$.

papers.title: A short survey on the convexity of level sets for divergence-form elliptic equations
papers.abstract:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded, smooth and (uniformly) convex domain, and let $u$ be a positive solution to an elliptic boundary value problem with zero Dirichlet data. A classical problem in the analysis of partial differential equations is to determine whether the convexity of $\Omega$ is inherited by the superlevel (or sublevel) sets of $u$.
  This survey considers divergence-form equations in bounded convex domains. For torsion functions, first eigenfunctions, and semilinear equations with sublinear nonlinearities, concavity of suitable transforms of $u$ gives positive results. Two further methods, i.e. envelope constructions and constant-rank theorems for level-set curvature, often provide alternative routes to convexity and related properties. These results are complemented by counterexamples, showing that in general convexity of the domain and ellipticity of the operator do not guarantee quasiconvexity for every solution. We present these counterexamples through a shared underlying idea, and describe the distinct ways in which different equations implement this idea.

papers.title: Diagnosing the Reference Gap: What Visual Scaffolds Can and Cannot Fix in Multimodal Reasoning
papers.abstract: Multimodal large language models can recognize visual content yet struggle to reason reliably over it across multiple steps. In counting, a model may see all objects but lose track of which ones it has counted. We argue that such failures, commonly attributed to perception, reveal a reference gap: the failure to bind language to the relevant visual entities, regions, or locations. Motivated by the theory of visual routines, we test whether external references such as numbering can narrow this gap. We introduce ReGap-Bench, a paired benchmark of five visual reasoning tasks in which the scene, question, and answer are fixed and only the reference varies. Results show that task-matched references improve accuracy by up to 25\%, while mismatched references provide little benefit or even hurt performance. These findings identify the reference gap as a bottleneck distinct from visual perception and show that constructing task-appropriate visual references can serve as a training-free visual skill for improving multimodal reasoning.

papers.title: Length Bounds for MDS Algebraic Geometry Codes of Arbitrary Positive Genus
papers.abstract: We study the length of maximum distance separable algebraic geometry codes from curves of arbitrary positive genus. For fixed genus, we prove that the asymptotic ratio of the length to the field size is at most $1/2$ when both the dimension and the codimension grow faster than the logarithm of the field size. We also give explicit bounds under logarithmic dimension conditions. The bounds hold in every characteristic and are uniform in the curve and the evaluation set. The proof combines character sums on the Jacobian with an estimate for sums of distinct points.

papers.title: Verifiable LLM-Guided Focal SMT Solving for Quantified Arrays
papers.abstract: Large language models can often identify useful semantic structure in formal artifacts, but their outputs cannot be trusted as proofs or solver decisions. We study whether LLMs can instead guide formal reasoning systems through a narrow, solver-verifiable interface. We instantiate this idea in quantified array SMT solving, where modern instantiation-based techniques can fail when key ground terms and equalities are hidden by auxiliary variables, axiom guards, and nested array terms. We observe that many instances are largely driven by a small set of focal ground terms or constraints, similar to the backdoor sets in SAT solving. Building on this, we present LinguaArray, a framework where an LLM proposes a small Semantic Focus Set (ground terms/constraints), while a conventional SMT solver remains the sole proof engine and certifies all results. LinguaArray uses these LLM-suggested, solver-validated finite sets to significantly enhance solver capability, solving additional satisfiable and unsatisfiable instances that the backend alone fails to solve. It interacts within a finite time and then falls back to the backend solver to mitigate potential regressions. Evaluation on 1015 SMT-LIB instances across five logics under 1200s timeout (including LLM latency) shows that LinguaArray solves up to 69.1% of instances and increases solved-instance counts by 105%--397% over the corresponding backends.

authors.name: Rui Han
authors.institution: The First People's Hospital of Changzhou

papers.title: Ask to Evolve: A Unified Harness for Lifelong Embodied Navigation with Hybrid Action Space and Persistent Memory
papers.abstract: Giving embodied agents the freedom to act autonomously, initiate interactions, and understand their surroundings through experience is a step toward bringing them to life in the physical world. Realizing this vision requires action, interaction, and memory to work together, so that each encounter can inform current decisions and contribute experience for future tasks. We present EvoLife, a unified navigation harness that enables a multimodal embodied agent to choose how to move, when to ask, and what experience to carry forward. Its hybrid action space supports waypoint navigation, local discrete adjustments, pixel-based navigation, and object-directed navigation. Active interaction allows the agent to seek clarification or assistance when it encounters ambiguity or difficulty, while persistent spatial memory binds observations and dialogue to places, retaining useful experience to guide subsequent visits. We evaluate eight benchmarks across four task families: vision-language navigation, object navigation, interactive instance navigation, and continuous multi-task navigation. With an average of only 1.87 active interactions per episode, our method achieves a first-visit success rate (SR) of 100% across four 100-episode sets spanning vision-language navigation and object navigation. Complete-sequence SR reaches 98% on 50 LHPR-VLN sequences and 94% on 50 GOAT-Bench sequences. In the R2R revisit setting, success weighted by path length (SPL) increases from 82.23% to 93.31% with retained experience. Multi-day physical navigation further demonstrates exploration, proactive help-seeking, and revisiting remembered places. Together, these results advance the vision of bringing embodied agents to life through autonomous action, proactive interaction, and the accumulation and reuse of experience.

authors.name: Jinlong Li
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: Achieving Minimax-Optimal First-Order and Best-of-Both-Worlds Regret Simultaneously in Multi-Armed Bandits
papers.abstract: We study first-order and best-of-both-worlds regret guarantees in multi-armed bandits. Pogodin and Lattimore (2019) proposed an algorithm that combines minimax-optimal worst-case regret with a first-order guarantee whose loss-dependent term is $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{K L^\star}\log T)$, where $T$ denotes the horizon, $L^\star$ denotes the smallest expected cumulative loss among fixed arms, and $K$ denotes the number of arms. However, a logarithmic gap remains between this loss-dependent term and the optimal first-order scale. In this paper, we remove this logarithmic factor by proposing an efficient and parameter-free algorithm that achieves the minimax optimal first-order regret guarantee $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{K L^\star})$. Technically, our algorithm is built upon FTRL with a Tsallis entropy regularizer (Zimmert and Seldin,2021), with a learning rate adapted to the learner's cumulative loss and a sampling distribution determined by a scalar fixed point. This construction controls the combined estimation and stability cost in terms of the learner's loss. Moreover, we show that the same algorithm achieves a best-of-both-worlds guarantee, with $\mathcal{O}(\sum_{i\ne i^\star}\frac{\log T}{\Delta_i})$ regret for i.i.d. losses with a unique best arm $i^\star$, where $\Delta_i$ denotes the suboptimality gap of arm $i$.

papers.title: The maximum number of triangles in regular graphs
papers.abstract: We determine the maximum number of triangles in $n$-vertex $k$-regular graphs and characterize all extremal graphs for all admissible orders when $k$ is odd and for an explicit range of orders when $k$ is even. For even $k$, we also give explicit lower and upper bounds for the remaining orders. As a consequence, we obtain a lower bound on the number of independent sets of size three in $k$-regular graphs and characterize all equality cases. Our exact results confirm the conjecture of Petingi and Rodr\'iguez and the triangle case of a conjecture of Cambie, de Joannis de Verclos and Kang for all odd $k$ and the specified orders when $k$ is even. Moreover, for every even $k\ge18$, we construct counterexamples to both conjectures and obtain a recursive characterization of all extremal graphs of order at least $Ck$, where $C$ is an absolute constant.

authors.name: Ya-Hong Chen
authors.institution: Hunan Institute of Science and Technology

authors.name: Shi-Cai Gong
authors.institution: Zhejiang University of Science and Technology

papers.title: CBE: A Complexity-adaptive Boundary-aware Ensemble Method for Imbalanced Data
papers.abstract: In many real-world classification tasks, datasets exhibit class imbalance, which can degrade the generalization performance of conventional learning algorithms. Data complexity has recently been recognized as a more objective indicator of learning difficulty than the imbalance ratio alone, because class overlap and complex decision boundaries often impair classifiers more severely than imbalance itself. Samples near the decision boundary are inherently difficult to classify, which has motivated many researchers to focus on such instances to improve classifier performance. However, most under-sampling approaches fail to differentiate their sampling of boundary samples across datasets of varying complexity. To overcome this limitation, we propose a complexity-adaptive boundary-aware ensemble (CBE) framework that links the sampling weight distribution to data complexity and dynamically adjusts the boundary preference of under-sampling accordingly. We also introduce an overall complexity measure that combines metrics at multiple levels and use it to divide imbalanced datasets into three categories. Extensive experiments on 24 benchmark datasets from UCI and KEEL show that the proposed method outperforms many existing methods in terms of F-measure and G-mean on Easy and Median datasets, without degrading performance on hard cases.

authors.name: Xun Wei
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology Beijing

papers.title: $e$-Positive caterpillars have maximum degree at most three
papers.abstract: Dahlberg, She, and van Willigenburg conjectured that every $e$-positive tree has maximum degree at most three. We prove this conjecture for caterpillars. Our proof introduces a specialization--cone method: we evaluate chromatic symmetric functions under finite-support specializations that are nonnegative on the elementary symmetric functions, express the evaluations through transfer matrices, and certify negativity using finitely generated cones. Two specializations and three cones handle all caterpillars remaining after a connected-partition reduction, with no bound on the number or spacing of their trivalent vertices. The required cone inclusions and strict sign inequalities are certified by exact rational arithmetic. We also exhibit two infinite families of non-spider caterpillars of maximum degree four that admit connected partitions of every type, showing that Wolfgang's criterion alone leaves cases requiring further obstructions. Our result also reduces Li's criterion on $e$-positivity for caterpillars of maximum degree three to an explicit condition on the positions of trivalent vertices.

papers.title: $\mathrm{BMO}$ Domains and Quasicircles Associated with Zygmund Functions
papers.abstract:
We investigate graph domains and graph curves from the viewpoints of $\mathrm{BMOA}$, Zygmund regularity, and asymptotic geometry. First, we prove that every graph domain is a $\mathrm{BMO}$ domain, which provides a proof of a statement of Astala and Zinsmeister. We then use a Weierstrass-type function to construct a Bishop-Jones quasicircle that is asymptotically conformal but not asymptotically smooth. This example yields the strict inclusions \[
  \mathrm{VMOA}(\mathbb H)
  \subsetneq \mathrm{BMOA}(\mathbb H)\cap B_0(\mathbb H),
  \qquad
  \mathrm{SS}(\mathbb R)
  \subsetneq \mathrm{SQS}(\mathbb R)\cap\mathrm{S}(\mathbb R). \] Finally, by a localized lacunary construction, we produce a compactly supported locally absolutely continuous function $f$ with $f'\in\mathrm{BMO}(\mathbb R)\setminus\mathrm{VMO}(\mathbb R)$ whose graph is an asymptotically conformal chord-arc curve that is not asymptotically smooth.

papers.title: Hidden Phase Transition in Single-Polymer Stretching under Elongational Flow
papers.abstract: Using machine learning, we identify a second transition in polymer chain stretching driven by planar elongational flow, beyond the well-known coil-stretch transition. We achieve this by developing a conditional extension of Universal and Identifiable Dissipative Dynamics (UIDD) that jointly learns reduced stochastic dynamics from microscopic trajectories across flow strengths and yields the corresponding stationary nonequilibrium free energy landscapes. As the flow strength increases, the evolving landscape exhibits the expected coil-stretch transition, and then a previously unrecognized dynamical transition. In the latter, the stretched states persist, but the distribution along a folding coordinate becomes bimodal when conditioned on small end-to-end separation. Large-deviation analysis of a simplified analytical chain model reproduces both transitions and shows that they are phase transitions in the long-chain limit. Single-molecule DNA experiments provide qualitative support for the dynamical transition through the predicted reversal of the folding response.

papers.title: Fractal dimensions of paths on three-dimensional random-walk traces
papers.abstract: We study four paths that join the starting site to the final position of a simple random walk of \(N=L^2\) steps on the infinite cubic lattice. The paths are selected on the walk trace---the graph of visited sites and traversed bonds---by different rules: the undirected shortest path \(S_1\), the directed shortest path \(S_2\), the time-respecting shortest path \(S_3\), and the depth \(D_e\) of the final site in a depth-first-search tree. Monte Carlo simulations for \(L\) up to 32768 give mean lengths scaling as \(L^{d_O}\), with \(d_{S_1}=1.48005(9)\), \(d_{S_2}=1.49868(5)\), \(d_{S_3}=1.51205(5)\), and \(d_{D_e}=1.7099(7)\), so that \(d_{S_1}<d_{S_2}<d_{S_3}<d_{\rm LE}<d_{D_e}\), where $d_{\rm LE}=1.62400(5)$ is the known loop-erased-random-walk exponent. Imposing traversal directions increases the shortest-path exponent, and imposing time order increases it further; these constraints therefore change the scaling exponent, not only the amplitude. For every path, the standard deviation scales with the same exponent as the mean, so it is scale-invariant, unlike the visited-site mass; the rescaled length distributions collapse onto a finite-width scaling function. No analytical theory currently predicts these exponents; our results provide precise numerical benchmarks for future studies of path geometry on random-walk traces.

papers.title: Lipschitz regularity of Sobolev maps from $\mathrm{RCD}(K,N)$ spaces to $\mathrm{CAT}(0)$ spaces
papers.abstract: We establish a quantitative criterion for local Lipschitz regularity of Sobolev maps in the sense of Korevaar and Schoen from finite-dimensional \(\RCD(K,N)\) spaces into complete \(\CAT(0)\) spaces, without assuming harmonicity. We quantify the failure of local energy minimality by the harmonic replacement potential, a dyadic sum of the square roots of normalized energy gaps between a map and its harmonic replacements. We prove that this potential, together with an averaged energy term, controls the minimal weak upper gradient pointwise, with constants depending only on the curvature-dimension bounds and the scale. In particular, local boundedness of the replacement potential implies that the map admits a locally Lipschitz representative.

papers.title: AI-driven structural informatics reveals diverse glycosylation machinery across double-stranded DNA viruses
papers.abstract: Glycosylation is widespread in biology and shapes molecular recognition, yet the diversity and biosynthetic organization of viral glycosyltransferases (GTs) remain poorly understood. Here we integrate structural-alphabet-guided searches and structure similarity networks with genomic-neighbourhood and biosynthetic gene cluster embedding analyses to examine viral GT-A proteins. This approach reveals extensive structural diversity overlooked by sequence-based annotation, including previously uncharacterized viral GT lineages. Most strikingly, we identified a jumbo-phage locus encoding five tandem glycosyltransferases alongside hydroxymethyl-pyrimidine biosynthetic and sulfation-associated enzymes, suggesting a previously unrecognized form of viral DNA modification involving a sulfated pentasaccharide. Beyond these examples, predicted saccharide-associated loci span divergent double-stranded DNA viruses, from giant viruses to tailed phages, and occupy multiple regions of the reference biosynthetic landscape. Together, our findings uncover an underappreciated repertoire of virus-encoded glycosylation machinery and suggest that viral glycan biosynthesis encompasses diverse molecular contexts and potential biological functions.

papers.title: Smartphone Indoor Localization Enhanced by Hierarchical Multi-Sensor Context Recognition
papers.abstract: Smartphone indoor localization requires low-cost, robust positioning across scene transitions and phone-use variations. Pedestrian dead reckoning (PDR) enables infrastructure-free deployment but accumulates errors from heading drift, structural transitions, and carrying-mode changes. Existing methods often treat contextual cues as a single event stream or local correction signal, limiting their ability to address distinct localization errors. This paper presents a framework enhanced by hierarchical multi-sensor context recognition. A jointly data- and model-driven recognition model predicts environment, scene, and activity probabilities, which are converted into scene-event and action-context segments. Scene-event segments guide scene-constrained PDR correction through corridor heading constraints, landmark attraction, fixed-lag backtracking, and vertical-transition handling. Action-context segments drive action-aware RoNIN-based position compensation for carrying-mode-dependent drift. Experiments on cross-floor and multi-action trajectories against LiDAR-SLAM references show that the proposed framework outperforms PDR and representative learned inertial odometry baselines, demonstrating that hierarchical semantics provide reliable, localization-specific correction cues.

papers.title: NIF: Normal-Intersection Fields for Geometrically Consistent Oriented Box Refinement
papers.abstract: Accurate oriented detection requires a box to follow object boundaries, yet a standard regression head predicts its center, size, and angle from a pooled region representation. Small errors in these coupled parameters can displace long boundaries even when the object is correctly classified. We propose NIF, a refinement module that replaces an additional box regressor with normal-intersection fields. Given a coarse oriented box, the module observes local features at 20 boundary anchors and predicts signed distances along their outward normals. These observations admit an exact affine representation in five geometric variables. A differentiable, reliability-weighted least-squares fit projects the predicted field onto this representation and analytically recovers a refined rectangle. Tangential pooling preserves the normal position profile, while shared projection limits the added network to 0.132M parameters. On DOTA-v1.0, NIF reaches 78.00%, 79.11%, and 79.02% mAP with Oriented R-CNN, LSKNet-S, and Strip R-CNN, respectively, achieving the highest single-scale SOTA result in Table 1. It reaches 68.19% on DIOR-R, improves matched FAIR1M/DIOR-R baselines by 0.30/0.68%, and raises HRSC mean IoU from 0.867 to 0.888 while reducing field error by 24.5%. Across four different detector frameworks with the detectors frozen, relative AP75 improves by 1.57-4.18% and COCO-style mAP by 0.42-3.74%, without detector retraining. Code is available at https://github.com/zsk466991125-collab/Normal-Intersection-Fields.

authors.name: Shaokai Zheng
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: A Transfer Principle for Elliptic Carleman Estimates: Application to Discrete Calder\'on Stability
papers.abstract: We develop a transfer principle that lifts continuous elliptic Carleman estimates to mesh-uniform estimates for conforming Galerkin discretizations. The main difficulties are twofold: discrete states generally lack the \(H^2\)-regularity required by the continuous estimate, and the Carleman parameter \(s\) must be controlled relative to the mesh size \(h\). We overcome both by introducing a shifted continuous problem whose Galerkin solution is exactly the conforming reconstruction of a prescribed discrete state. Weighted approximation then transfers the inequality back to the original discrete operator without adding stabilization, and yields the range \(s\le ch^{-4/5}\) for radial weights. We verify the framework for piecewise affine finite elements with consistent or lumped mass on fitted, uniformly shape-regular meshes, and for standard Cartesian finite differences through their finite-element realization. As an application, we study the discrete Calder\'on problem for bounded complex Schr\"odinger potentials in dimension \(d\ge3\). Assuming agreement in a fixed connected boundary neighborhood and uniform stability of the discrete Dirichlet problems, we obtain stability from Dirichlet inputs and variational flux observations on independently prescribed, possibly disjoint boundary patches. The resulting estimate in \(H^{-r}\), \(r>d/2\), retains the single logarithmic data term and the \(O(h^{1/2})\) mesh remainder of the full-data estimate.

papers.title: GPU-Resident Speculative Decoding for In-Browser LLM Inference with WebGPU
papers.abstract: WebGPU enables private, offline LLM inference inside web pages, but browser dispatch, inter-process communication, synchronous readback and single-token kernels slow decoding and make conventional speculative decoding inefficient. We present a WebGPU runtime that addresses these browser-specific costs. Deterministic small-batch integer kernels accelerate multi-token verification while preserving exact agreement with greedy decoding in the same quantized runtime. A GPU-resident loop performs drafting, verification, acceptance and KV-cache maintenance without a per-token CPU decision. A draft-free context-mixing drafter reuses page content, conversation history and session memory, while a device-aware controller adapts the speculation width and the submission window to measured costs. Across seven models from 0.5B to 8B parameters, 11 tasks and three client GPUs, our runtime decodes 3.5 to 5.4$\times$ faster than WebLLM on a laptop GPU, 4.8 to 6.2$\times$ faster on an integrated GPU and 4.8 to 8.6$\times$ faster on a workstation GPU. The GPU-resident loop and speculation contribute a further 1.8 to 3.2$\times$ over the optimized kernels on the workstation. Outputs match the quantized greedy decoding of the runtime exactly, and the mean GSM8K accuracy matches that of WebLLM. Optional draft heads raise the peak speedup to 10.2$\times$, while session memory provides additional gains without downloading extra weights.

papers.title: SpeakerTurn: Target-Speaker Semantic Turn Detection in Multi-Speaker Environments
papers.abstract: Semantic completeness alone cannot determine when an assistant should respond in a multi-speaker environment: a completed utterance may belong to an interfering speaker, while the designated user is still speaking, acknowledging, or requesting time. We therefore study semantic turn inference conditioned on speaker identity. We propose SpeakerTurn, a framework that jointly predicts the target transcript and turn state from a speech mixture and an independent target-speaker reference. Built on CocktailASR-1, it links semantic decisions to the corresponding target content through joint supervision, distinguishing complete, incomplete, backchannel, wait, and target-absent states, with a separate interruption task. We also examine whether structured chain-of-thought (CoT) supervision improves decisions by representing speaker presence and semantic cues. On a synthetic multi-speaker test set, SpeakerTurn achieves five-state macro F1 of 0.811 and target-transcription character error rate (CER) of 4.20%, correctly resolving all ten reference-swapped interruption pairs. Joint-format transcription and native-interface recognition nevertheless behave differently, and CoT improves validation transcription without improving turn macro F1. These results show why target attribution, semantic turn discrimination, and recognition retention require separate assessment when adapting speech language models for speaker-conditioned interaction.

authors.name: Nan Li
authors.institution: Tianjin University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

papers.title: Communication-Oblivious Permutation and Sorting
papers.abstract: With the help of secure hardware such as trusted execution environments (TEEs), private data can be uploaded and computed in untrusted cloud clusters, so that an adversary controlling the cloud can only see the data in encrypted form. However, the communication pattern between the processors may still reveal sensitive information about the data, so it is important to develop parallel algorithms in the BSP model whose communication pattern is independent of the input data, a property known as \textit{communication obliviousness}. In this paper, we study such algorithms for three fundamental problems: permutation, sorting, and 0-1 sorting. For the first two problems, we prove a tight (up to lower-order terms) communication complexity of $(2-2/p)n\pm o(n)$. Here, $p$ is the number of processors and $n$ is the input size, assuming $2\le p$ and $p=o(n^{1/3})$. Our lower bound holds regardless of the number of rounds and local memory size, while for balanced permutation and sorting the upper bound is achieved in a constant number of rounds with load at most $n/p+o(n/p)$. For 0-1 sorting, we also derive a tight communication complexity of $C_{\mathrm{cut}}(p) \cdot n \pm o(n)$, where $C_{\mathrm{cut}}(p)$ is the optimal value of a linear program parameterized by $p$. Although there appears to be no closed-form for $C_{\mathrm{cut}}(p)$, we show that it is strictly smaller than $2-2/p$ for all $p\ge 3$, thus separating 0-1 sorting from general sorting in terms of their communication complexity.

authors.name: Ke Yi
authors.institution: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

papers.title: On record behaviours of returns for interval maps
papers.abstract: Given a dynamical system $(X,T)$ and an ergodic invariant measure $\mu$, a $\mu$-typical point $x\in X$ under $T$ visits arbitrarily small neighbourhood of $x$. We will use techniques based on extreme value theory and Laplace functional for point process to show that, for interval maps with suitable mixing and anti-clustering conditions, the limiting distributions of the record times and values of the return process $Y_j(x)=-\log d(T^jx,x)$, after possible normalisation, has Poisson-type laws.

papers.title: Microscopic Mechanism and Control of Reentrant Localization
papers.abstract: Increasing quasiperiodic modulation can restore extended states after localization, raising the question of how the same modulation drives both localization and recovery. We identify a microscopic mechanism in quasiperiodic dimer chains by resolving scattering between Fourier channels. Specifically, scattering into neighboring channels and back shifts the spectral edge relative to a localization boundary determined by a neutral auxiliary resonance. Their successive crossings drive the same spectral packet with fixed integrated-density-of-states (IDS) labels into localization and back into an extended regime. This recovery persists across finite parameter ranges in both gap-opening families, including relative-phase detuning. Furthermore, an exact sublattice mapping enables compensated control of the recovery window and predicts recovery thresholds for individual IDS labels.

authors.name: Gui-Lu Long
authors.institution: Beijing National Research Center for Information Science and Technology

papers.title: Failure of the $H^1\times H^1\longrightarrow L^{1/2,\infty}$ estimate for the lacunary bilinear spherical maximal function and applications
papers.abstract:
In contrast to Christ's theorem that the lacunary spherical maximal operator is bounded from $H^1(\mathbb R^d)$ to $L^{1,\infty}(\mathbb R^d)$ ($d\geq2$), we show that the lacunary bilinear spherical maximal operator $$
  \mathcal B_{\mathrm{lac}}(f,g)(x)
  =\sup_{\ell\in\mathbb Z}
  \Bigl|\int_{\mathbb S^{2d-1}}f(x-2^\ell y)\,g(x-2^\ell z)\,d\sigma(y,z)\Bigr| $$ is not bounded from $H^1(\mathbb R^d)\times H^1(\mathbb R^d)$ to $L^{1/2,\infty}(\mathbb R^d)$ for any $d\geq1$. In particular, it is not bounded from $L^1(\mathbb R^d)\times L^1(\mathbb R^d)$ to $L^{1/2,\infty}(\mathbb R^d)$. More precisely, for every sufficiently large integer $N$, we construct two finite linear combinations of smooth, compactly supported, mean-zero $H^1(\mathbb R^d)$-atoms for which the ratio of the weak $L^{1/2}$ quasinorm to the product of the two Hardy norms is at least $c_d\log(N+1)$. This lower bound holds already for the supremum over a suitable set of $N$ dyadic radii. For $d=1$ this answers the case $p=q=1$ of a question in Borges's survey. For every $k\ge3$ and $d\ge1$, a modification of the construction proves that the lacunary $k$-linear spherical maximal operator does not map $(H^1(\mathbb R^d))^k$ into $L^{1/k,\infty}(\mathbb R^d)$. We also indicate extensions to certain hypersurfaces and to horizontal spherical averages on the Heisenberg group.

authors.name: Ji Li
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: SelfThinker: Self-Evolving Reasoning via Reliability-Verified Intrinsic Visual Thoughts
papers.abstract: Unified multimodal models can both generate and understand images within a single set of weights, offering an opportunity to use image synthesis as training supervision for visual comprehension. However, existing visual chain-of-thought methods rely on human-annotated helper images during training and require slow image generation at test time. We present SelfThinker, the first self-evolving framework that turns a unified model's self-generated visual thoughts into stronger understanding without human image annotations. Given a visual problem, SelfThinker samples candidate helper images from its generation pathway and uses its frozen understanding pathway to score each candidate via conditional pointwise mutual information. High-utility visual thoughts then refine the generator via flow matching and serve as privileged teacher context for on-policy self-distillation. At inference, SelfThinker reasons directly from the original image in text without generating intermediate images. Although trained only on small synthetic visual-search and navigation datasets, SelfThinker transfers broadly to natural-image and spatial benchmarks, raising the seven-benchmark average of ThinkMorph-7B from 52.7 to 64.0 (+11.3 points). Controlled image-perturbation probes further show that SelfThinker surpasses ThinkMorph-7B by up to 40.4 points and its pretrained BAGEL-7B backbone by up to 23.2 points across fine-grained and spatial perception tasks. Our code is available at https://github.com/zhangquanchen/SelfThinker.

papers.title: Learning a Motion Manifold to Constrain Ambiguity in Unsupervised 4D Medical Image Interpolation
papers.abstract: Unsupervised 4D medical image interpolation reconstructs intermediate anatomical states from temporally sparse observations without intermediate supervision. Distinct motion fields may attain comparable endpoint agreement while producing different intermediate anatomy, giving rise to motion ambiguity. This ambiguity is difficult to constrain when many independently adjustable motion variables must be estimated from the observed endpoints. We develop a framework that learns a motion manifold to restrict candidate motion fields while retaining sample-specific variation. Cross-Sample Spectral Basis Learning extracts recurring motion structure from endpoint-derived dense estimates and encodes it in a shared spectral basis. Sample-Conditioned Cayley Basis Reorientation uses predicted motion coordinates to rotate the effective motion directions for each endpoint pair without increasing the number of independent coordinates. Their composition defines a nonlinear family of complete velocity fields across endpoint pairs, accommodating anatomical and motion-state differences within a restricted representation. Integrating each predicted field supports bidirectional reconstruction at arbitrary intermediate times. Theoretical analysis establishes sufficient conditions under which endpoint observations distinguish nearby motions within the learned family. Experiments on ACDC and 4D-Lung demonstrate state-of-the-art performance among the evaluated methods trained without intermediate volumes and competitive results against methods using intermediate supervision.

papers.title: DynaRev: Benchmarking Web Agents under Dynamic Goal Revision
papers.abstract: Web agents are typically evaluated with goals fully specified before execution and fixed thereafter, whereas real users often revise their requirements during interaction. To study such interactions, we introduce DynaRev, a benchmark of 181 tasks to evaluate web agents under dynamic goal revision. DynaRev uses semantic milestones to deliver revisions at task-defined stages, covers additive revisions, unconditional overrides, and runtime-conditioned overrides, and evaluates correctness, responsiveness, and efficiency through trajectory-grounded evaluation. Five-model evaluations show that agents often satisfy only part of the task requirements, with performance varying across task sources, revision types, and models. Further analyses reveal varied milestone timing, mixed effects of dynamic delivery, and contrasting revision-handling outcomes, with gains from instruction rewriting while preserving browser state and losses from browser resets. DynaRev provides a testbed for studying how web agents adapt to evolving user goals. The code and data are available at https://github.com/zsq259/DynaRev.

authors.name: Zesheng Wei
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Von Neumann regular and semisimple rings realized as principal quotients of domains
papers.abstract: In this paper, we show that every commutative von Neumann regular ring is a quotient of a characteristic-zero B\'ezout domain by its principal Jacobson radical. We then characterize the commutative semisimple rings that occur as quotients of Dedekind domains. For a finite product of fields $R=\prod_{i=1}^n k_i$, such a presentation exists exactly when the cardinals $|k_i|^{\aleph_0}$ are all equal. When this condition holds, the source may be taken to be a characteristic-zero semilocal principal ideal domain, and the quotient ideal may again be its Jacobson radical.

papers.title: AcrossDEX 1.0: From Human Motion Pretraining to Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation across Hand Embodiments
papers.abstract: Bimanual dexterous manipulation requires continuous coordination of wrist motion, finger contact, and object motion. Human videos provide rich manipulation experience. Using this experience for robot control requires aligning human poses with robot commands and accounting for embodiment-specific kinematics and contact dynamics. We present AcrossDEX 1.0, a learning system that connects human motion pretraining, simulation-based expert learning, robot demonstration collection, and visual closed-loop execution. Pretraining on HOT3D Aria predicts one second of bimanual motion from five images and thirty annotated hand states over the preceding second. Robot adaptation preserves the visual encoder, temporal backbone, and wrist parameters. Shared wrist representations, separate finger fields, and validity masks support both six-channel Inspire hands and sixteen-joint Allegro hands. The robot policy predicts sixty control targets from frontal images, command history, and task conditions. It executes a prefix and replans from updated observations. We compare direct regression, diffusion, and flow matching on lid opening and return and closed-lid object reorientation. Direct regression achieves success rates of 40.6\% for opening and return, 100.0\% for Inspire reorientation, and 93.3\% for Allegro reorientation. Flow matching achieves 90.0\% on Allegro reorientation. Paired comparisons further show that constraining replanning with the previous plan improves the continuous execution of generative policies. These results demonstrate a common adaptation pipeline for two hand embodiments and highlight the roles of contact coordination and action-chunk continuity.

authors.name: Nan Wu
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: N\'eel vector switching by magnetization-dependent layer-resolved spin-orbit torque
papers.abstract: Layer-resolved spin-orbit torques offer a route to controlling antiferromagnetic order through local spin-charge conversion. First-principles calculations show that the layer-resolved spin Hall conductivity of the antiferromagnetic topological insulator $\mathrm{Mn{Bi}_{2}{Te}_{4}}$ consists of a magnetization-independent spin Hall term plus two spin anomalous Hall terms that are even in the N\'eel vector yet evolve with the local magnetic order, while local inversion asymmetry differentiates surface and inner layers. This response enables reversible, field-free switching of the N\'eel vector in finite-septuple-layer films. Although the magnetization-independent spin Hall term alone can reverse the order, the spin anomalous Hall terms provide magnetization-dependent feedback that redistributes the layer-resolved torques and reshapes the switching trajectory, offering a route to tailoring current-driven switching through layer and interface engineering.

papers.title: Recognizing Dominance through Local Improvement
papers.abstract: Strategy-proofness is the traditional standard for predictable behavior, yet participants often fail to play dominant strategies. Most existing simplicity concepts attribute these failures to the cost of contingent reasoning, which they lower by comparing the worst case of the dominant strategy with the best case of an alternative. I argue that there is another approach, one that makes more use of the structure of the strategy set, which I formalize as a neighbor relation. Comparing neighboring strategies can reduce the need for contingent reasoning, and, even with a single contingency, it can simplify the search through the strategy set. I introduce a new simplicity criterion: a mechanism is local improvement solvable under a neighbor relation if repeatedly moving to an improving neighbor always reaches a dominant strategy. Strategy-proofness is the criterion under the coarsest relation, and many classical mechanisms satisfy it under finer ones. In extensive-form mechanisms without duplicate dominant strategies, the criterion under one-situation neighbors is strict action-proofness, which is distinct from obvious strategy-proofness. Among local improvement solvable mechanisms that implement the same outcomes, the criterion predicts more dominant-strategy play where the local comparison is salient.

authors.name: Linchen Zhang
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Heavy Oil

papers.title: MUSBRIC: LEGO-Compatible Pneumatic Muscle Bricks for Reconfigurable Musculoskeletal Robots
papers.abstract: Musculoskeletal robots combine compliant actuators with articulated skeletons, but exploring alternative configurations often requires repeated fabrication. We present MUSBRIC, a modular hardware platform and accompanying MuJoCo-based simulator for reconfigurable musculoskeletal robots. LEGO-compatible endcaps turn fiber-reinforced extensile pneumatic artificial muscles into reusable, plug-and-play muscle bricks that connect directly to standard LEGO components. Experimentally identified actuator behavior supports corresponding musculoskeletal simulations. An elbow-joint prototype validates load-dependent flexion and extension, showing that pulley-guided routing enables reversible motion and a mechanical stop stabilizes the straight posture. A robotic hand demonstrates compliant grasping and multi-joint construction. Matched hardware and simulation sweeps across 15 leg configurations demonstrate systematic exploration of attachment geometry, while a quadruped assembled from four legs demonstrates walking. Together, these demonstrations span mechanism analysis, configuration exploration, and functional robot construction within a single reconfigurable system. The hardware designs and simulation code will be released as open source soon to facilitate reproduction and further development.

papers.title: Enhanced convergence guarantees of score-based generative models in $\mathcal{W}_2$-distance beyond log-concavity
papers.abstract: Although score-based generative models (SGMs) have achieved remarkable success in real-world sample generation tasks, it is still far from sufficient to understand them from a mathematical perspective.
