In this paper, we aim to provide enhanced convergence guarantees for two existing SGMs in $\mathcal{W}_2$-distance beyond log-concavity. More precisely, we develop a novel framework of {\color{black}discretization} error analysis for Euler-Maruyama (EM) and Poisson midpoint (PM) time discretization schemes for SGMs. Under a non-log-concavity condition, we show that $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(\sqrt{d}/\epsilon)$ iterations suffice to approximate the target distributions in $\epsilon$-accuracy for the classical EM-based SGM, considerably improving upon the existing iteration complexity $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(d/\epsilon^2)$. Notably, the novel framework of error analysis also enables us to establish an $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(\sqrt{d}/\epsilon^{2/3})$ iteration complexity for the PM-based SGM in $\epsilon$-accuracy, significantly outperforming current state-of-the-art Wasserstein convergence guarantees for SDE-based diffusion samplers.

authors.name: Xiaojie Wang
authors.institution: Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China

papers.title: Polarization and Burst Properties of the Repeating FRB~20240209A in a Quiescent Elliptical Host
papers.abstract: We report polarimetric observations of the repeating fast radio burst (FRB) source FRB 20240209A with the Green Bank Telescope at L band and 800 MHz. This source has previously been associated with a quiescent elliptical galaxy with a mass-weighted stellar age of approximately 11 Gyr. We detected three bursts, and the brightest burst resolves into eight components that drift toward lower frequencies. The bursts have mutually consistent rotation measures (RMs), and the small extragalactic RM agrees with the low RM predicted from the small host-galaxy dispersion measure ($\mathrm{DM}_\mathrm{host}$). The linear polarization fraction decreases toward lower frequencies within the brightest burst, consistent with depolarization by an RM scatter of $\sigma_\mathrm{RM}\simeq3.5$ rad m$^{-2}$. This RM scatter is comparable to those of several repeaters in star-forming galaxies. Therefore, FRBs in both star-forming and old, quiescent hosts can reside in relatively complex magneto-ionic environments, which suggests that FRB sources may form through multiple channels.

authors.name: Jin-Tao Xie
authors.institution: Sichuan University of Science and Engineering

papers.title: Cosmological tests of chameleon dark energy with dark sector coupling
papers.abstract: Recent DESI measurements of baryon acoustic oscillations favor a value of $\Omega_{\mathrm m}$ different from that preferred by Planck cosmic microwave background observations. Combined with supernova data, these observations suggest an evolving dark energy equation of state that crosses $w=-1$. As a potential solution to multiple cosmological problems, chameleon dark energy has attracted increasing attention in recent years. In this work, we constrain a chameleon model in which late-time cosmic acceleration is driven by a canonical scalar field nonminimally coupled to dark matter. At early times, the scalar field evolves under the combined influence of its potential and the nonminimal coupling, and its effective mass greatly exceeds the Hubble parameter. The chameleon model with energy transfer from dark energy to dark matter yields a best-fit improvement of $\Delta\chi^2=-7.25$ relative to $\Lambda\mathrm{CDM}$, comparable to that for energy transfer in the opposite direction. Joint sampling over both coupling directions favors a nonzero interaction at $3.3\sigma$. Although no phantom field is introduced, the modified dark matter evolution produces an effective dark energy equation of state that crosses $w=-1$ at $z\simeq0.5$.

authors.name: Jia-Qi Wang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Complete K\"ahler Manifolds with pinched Ricci curvature
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove that a connected complete K\"ahler manifold of complex dimension at least two satisfying $\Ric\geq\varepsilon Rg\geq0$ for a fixed $\varepsilon>0$ is compact or Ricci-flat.

papers.title: NECA: Neighbor Event Curve Augmentation for Multi-Horizon ICU Deterioration Prediction
papers.abstract: Early prediction of ICU organ dysfunction events supports timely clinical monitoring and intervention, but estimating short-term organ-specific risk from early ICU records remains challenging due to irregular measurements, heterogeneous clinical variables, and the need to predict risk across multiple future horizons. Existing supervised models usually treat each patient as an isolated sample and do not explicitly use the observed event timing of similar historical patients. We propose Neighbor Event-Curve Augmentation (NECA), a model-agnostic method that retrieves training-set patients with similar early-window profiles and converts their subsequent organ dysfunction event onset times into cumulative event-curve features over 6h, 12h, 24h, and 42h. These features are concatenated with the original patient representation and used by standard downstream predictors. On PhysioNet 2012 and a 4,000-stay MIMIC-IV subset, NECA improves average PR-AUC and ROC-AUC across four organ dysfunction event tasks and seven supervised learners. The largest gain appears for neurological dysfunction events, where task-level average PR-AUC increases from 0.461 to 0.557 on PhysioNet 2012. Ablations show that clinically meaningful retrieval and horizon-specific neighbor risk drive most of the improvement, while the full cumulative curve adds task-dependent temporal context. These results support similar-patient event timing as a structured temporal risk signal for ICU organ dysfunction event prediction. The source code will be publicly released upon acceptance of this paper.

papers.title: Average pairwise Hamming distance of a subset in a hypercube
papers.abstract: In this note, we prove that for a subset $\mathcal{F}$ of $\{0,1\}^n$ of density $\frac{1}{8}$, its average pairwise Hamming distance is at least $\frac{n-3}{2}$, with equality attained only by $(n-3)$-dimensional subcubes. This answers a question of Lei Yu, and solves an important open case of a more general question posed by Ahlswede and Katona in 1977.

papers.title: Algebraic World Model: From Exploration to Proofs
papers.abstract: AI has made remarkable progress in mathematics, solving challenging problems with machine-checkable proofs in Lean, yet typically relying on predefined mathematical definitions and formal specifications. This raises a natural question: can it reason rigorously about an unknown world? We introduce the Algebraic World Model (AWM), a framework that turns interaction with unfamiliar environments into explicit mathematical models supporting formal reasoning. AWM explores the environment and develops executable Python hypotheses, continually testing and revising them against observations. It then structures these hypotheses into typed objects and shared rules, simplifies their structure through category-theory-guided transformations, and formalizes the resulting model in Lean 4 to prove reachability and impossibility. AWM can formally prove that a goal is unreachable, even beyond explored trajectories. On two impossible game levels, it constructs closed, kernel-checked Lean proofs excluding every legal winning sequence in all six runs, while Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra, equipped with coding tools, produce none in twelve baseline runs. Four of AWM's six initial bounds are correct, compared with one for Opus 5.5 and none for GPT-6 Astra; given only feedback that a cheaper win exists, AWM revises its rules and constructs new proofs, reaching six of six correct bounds. Moreover, AWM produces interpretable mathematical models whose rules can be inspected and tested step by step. Across all 25 public ARC-AGI-3 games, these models enable Lean to replay the winning trajectories of all 183 levels and generalize beyond observed play, predicting unseen transitions and detecting changes in game mechanics. With Claude Opus 5, AWM clears all levels with a score of 99.9, while its certified winning trajectories use only 43% of the human baseline's actions.

papers.title: HairDeck: Animation-Ready Stylized Hair Cards from a Single Image
papers.abstract: The hair of stylized characters in games and avatars is built from hair cards: artist-placed ribbons whose geometry is the visible hair, animated by spring bones. Existing image-based methods produce realistic hair or a single fused mesh, while CHARM, the only generator of stylized hair cards, decodes a hairstyle autoregressively as a long sequence of control points. Observing that a card hairstyle is an unordered set of artist-defined primitives, we propose HairDeck, which generates it as one: each card is a single token, and a set diffusion transformer denoises all cards together. From a single image, HairDeck generates the cards and the spring-bone chains that drive them, yielding an animatable asset that exports to ready-to-use downstream formats. On CHARM's own test set, it lowers Chamfer distance by 44% and card-orientation error by more than half while running 33 times faster, and from single images it outperforms CHARM, image-to-3D pipelines and strand-based methods. Project page: https://hyzcluster.github.io/HairDeck

authors.name: Yuze He
authors.institution: Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs

authors.name: Yong-Jin Liu
authors.institution: Beijing National Research Center for Information Science and Technology

papers.title: Archimedean Asai Zeta Integrals and Cohomological Test Vectors
papers.abstract: We construct explicit test vectors in the minimal $U(n)$-types of cohomological principal series representations of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb C)$, together with Schwartz functions, for which the Flicker zeta integrals equal the corresponding Asai $L$-factors. Both the vectors and the Schwartz functions are independent of $s$, with all normalization constants given explicitly. We construct the vectors through a polynomial realization of Schur modules. Schur orthogonality reduces the Flicker integrals to Mellin transforms of Whittaker functions, and Godement sections yield a recurrence for their Jacquet integrals. The lower-rank vectors depend on the remaining integration variables, preventing a direct reduction to lower-rank Flicker integrals. We overcome this difficulty by combining growth estimates derived from the recurrence with the Asai functional equation. This proves that the holomorphic quotient of the Flicker integral by its Asai $L$-factor is constant. An explicit asymptotic calculation shows that this constant is exactly one.

papers.title: FACTS-MAS: A Multi-Agent Architecture for Adaptive Forecasting from Heterogeneous Evidence
papers.abstract: Real-world forecasting often requires integrating heterogeneous evidence whose predictive value varies across horizons, operating regimes, and domains. We introduce FACTS-MAS, a domain-agnostic multi-agent forecasting framework that decomposes evidence into specialized channels for temporal dynamics, exogenous context, seasonality, structural information, and discrete events. Each agent generates an independently testable forecast through a common interface, while leakage-safe historical validation measures its predictive skill relative to a naive reference. These skill estimates are used to weight and combine agent forecasts, so that uninformative evidence is either removed or downweighted rather than forced to participate. A calibration procedure selects domain-specific constant means based on historical validation folds. We evaluate FACTS-MAS on weekly for-sale housing inventory from Zillow and weekly unemployment insurance claims from FRED, for 15 U.S. metropolitan areas at 4-, 8-, and 13-week forecasting horizons. Our method outperforms both a naive last-value forecast method and the TimesFM foundation model. However, a factor-adjusted exponential smoothing model performs as well as the fused forecast. The evidence therefore supports FACTS-MAS as a systematic protocol for testing, calibrating, and recomposing evidence channels before assembling them into the strongest single model for a specific application domain. Code, data, and results are available at https://github.com/Madumita24/FACTS-MAS.

papers.title: Uniqueness and radial nondegeneracy of nodal states for a mixed-power scalar field equation
papers.abstract:
We consider the scalar field equation $$\begin{cases} -\Delta u+u+\lambda |u|^{q-1}u =\mu |u|^{p-1}u, & x\in\mathbb R^n,\\[2mm] u(x)\to 0, & |x|\to\infty, \end{cases}$$
  where $n\geq3$, $1<q<p<(n+2)/(n-2)$, and $\lambda,\mu>0$. We study uniqueness and radial nondegeneracy of its sign-changing radial bound states. The proof combines a comparison argument for the shooting variation across nodal intervals with uniform compactness estimates for families of bounded nodal number and continuation in a normalized parameter. We show that, for every integer $k\geq1$, fixing the centre and requiring $u(0)>0$ leaves exactly one radial bound state with $k$ nodes. Its radial linearized operator has trivial kernel in the radial space. For each fixed $k$, the corresponding normalized solutions form a global $C^1$ branch.

papers.title: Stable Dynamical Mass Transportation via port-Hamiltonian Structure
papers.abstract: Dynamical optimal mass transportation over nonlinear systems is often hindered by the curse of dimensionality and open-loop implementation. We propose an alternative framework that sacrifices exact optimality in favor of stability, robustness, and scalability. We use a stochastic port-Hamiltonian system as a reference model. Under suitable structural assumptions, we show that its density converges asymptotically to a prescribed steady-state distribution. We then shape a deterministic nonlinear system into a compatible port-Hamiltonian form and add a local density-feedback term so that its closed-loop continuity equation matches the Fokker-Planck-Kolmogorov equation of the reference model. The resulting feedback drives a broad class of initial distributions to the target distribution. Because the density term is local at the particle level, the controller admits decentralized implementation and avoids solving a global finite-horizon transport problem online. Nonlinear examples and simulations illustrate the method. For linear systems with Gaussian targets, we derive necessary and sufficient conditions for stabilizing density feedback and give explicit controller constructions.

authors.name: Dongjun Wu
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

papers.title: A-T-menability and metric amenability for HLS groupoids
papers.abstract: We characterise coarse embeddability of box spaces into Hilbert space in terms of a-T-menability of the associated Higson-Lafforgue-Skandalis (HLS) groupoids. Moreover, we prove that a-T-menability and metric amenability are independent for HLS groupoids: all four possible combinations occur among HLS groupoids associated with approximating sequences of the free group $\mathbb F_2$. The two separating examples are constructed using relative expansion and twisted spectral-gap techniques, respectively.

papers.title: Early Prediction of Cross-Service Implementation Scope: Evidence and Limits from Multiple Microservice Projects
papers.abstract: Microservice architectures aim to localize change, yet feature requests may require implementation across service boundaries. We investigate how well such downstream scope can be anticipated before implementation begins. Using issue--pull-request--commit traceability and implementation evidence corrected through targeted human adjudication, we reconstruct 866 repository-traceable feature requests from 13 open-source microservice projects and map their implementations to validated service boundaries. Cross-service changes occur in 101 requests (11.7%) and exhibit broader implementation footprints, particularly higher code churn, but no clear difference in lead time. Pre-implementation evidence provides limited cross-project predictive signal: the strongest leave-one-system-out model reaches a project-macro Macro-F1 of 0.484, but its advantage over the majority baseline is not significant after Holm correction and is sensitive to small evaluation folds. A local LLM offers no reliable improvement over classical models. Downstream workload is substantially harder to estimate, as learned models do not consistently outperform training-fold median baselines. A simple service-mention heuristic also performs comparably to learned scope triage. These findings show that early feature-request evidence is more useful for lightweight cross-service scope triage than for automated scope determination or precise workload estimation.

papers.title: A counterexample to the pure semisimplicity conjecture
papers.abstract: A ring is right pure semisimple if every right module is a direct sum of finitely generated modules, and the pure semisimplicity conjecture asserts that every such ring is of finite representation type. In this article, a division ring extension $H\subseteq T$ is constructed such that the bimodule ${}_HT_T$ has right dimension sequence $(1,2,2,2,\dots)$ and $T$ is infinite-dimensional as a left $H$-space. The division ring $T$ is the union of the fraction division rings of the nearest-neighbour quantum Laurent algebras with parameter $1/2$, and $H$ is the image of $T$ under a compatible family of conjugations. The extension is controlled by right bases of every length and by two-sided flags of adjacent division subrings, which identify all iterated right duals up to explicit twists. It follows that the triangular ring $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}H&T\\0&T\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ is right pure semisimple but neither left pure semisimple nor of finite representation type, so that the pure semisimplicity conjecture fails.

papers.title: A Proof for Generalized Egalitarianism
papers.abstract: This paper proves a rigidity theorem characterizing the Gini-type Lorenz-area ordering under general decision-theoretic constraints together with weak Lorenz dominance, thereby resolving the characterization problem pursued in this line of research on egalitarianism. This does not, of course, bring the broader inquiry to an end. In a certain sense, it may instead mark a step beyond the infancy of our attempt to connect social choice theory, welfare economics, and formal moral philosophy through a common mathematical language. The main proof strategy was originally obtained by the author's own hand, though 5.6sol and Astra could effortlessly reproduce it without any additional hint.

papers.title: Beyond Region Memory: Local Point Tracking for Vocal Cord Localization in Video Laryngoscopy
papers.abstract: Reliable vocal-cord localization in emergency video laryngoscopy remains visually challenging due to rapid tissue deformation, specular highlights, and instrument occlusions. We propose Local Point Tracking (LPT), a robust framework that combines a single-frame detector, local point propagation, and stateless mask refinement. LPT follows a localize first, snap second pipeline. First, a single-frame semantic detector generates sparse anchors, within which LPT initializes local query points (SAM-supported by default, with a regular grid as fallback). A point-propagation module tracks these points through detector-missed frames and recovers temporal bounding boxes from their geometry. Second, because point-derived boxes can be loose around the visible boundary, a box-snap step refines the selected box to the target boundary. This decomposition keeps temporal state in local point coordinates rather than a stateful mask or whole-region representation, while the spatial refinement module handles single-frame boundary precision without feeding mask errors back into temporal memory. Extensive evaluations on two distinct datasets demonstrate that our proposed LPT method achieves strong overall performance against existing baselines, with the best mAP_50, success AUC, and missing rate on both datasets. Furthermore, ablation studies confirm that point tracking primarily enhances temporal tracking robustness, while box-snap refinement effectively improves boundary tightness.

papers.title: An Analysis of High-Dimensional Land-Water Transitions in the Great Lakes via a Bayesian Discrepancy Model for Multinomial Data
papers.abstract: Global water-level systems have undergone large changes in recent years. Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) land cover data can be used to monitor and understand these changes. However, such data are extremely high-dimensional making them difficult to process while accounting for all sources of uncertainty. Bayesian hierarchical models are commonly implemented using Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods which can be computationally expensive for large datasets. Exact Posterior Regression (EPR) provides an efficient alternative for inference in latent Gaussian hierarchical models under exponential families without requiring MCMC or approximate Bayesian strategies. EPR has not been developed for multinomial data, and we extend this class of models to the multinomial setting. Additionally, we explore signal-to-noise covariance properties of discrepancy models, which we expect to be present in our data. We extend EPR to multinomial likelihoods via a stick-breaking construction to analyze water-level changes. Through simulation studies, we compare the proposed multinomial EPR approach with alternative models implemented using Gibbs sampling and the Integrated Nested Laplace Approximation (INLA). We evaluate each approach based on regression parameter estimation, category probability estimation, and computational efficiency. Overall, EPR and INLA achieve substantial reductions in computation time while EPR shows improved metrics in estimation and prediction.

papers.title: Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics of Semilinear Stochastic Partial Differential Equations
papers.abstract: We develop a rigorous mathematical framework for the nonequilibrium thermodynamics of semilinear stochastic partial differential equations. The invariant Gaussian measure of the associated Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process, which need not be time-reversible, serves as the reference measure. We define thermodynamic quantities in terms of probability densities and derive the entropy balance equation. We obtain explicit expressions for the entropy production rate and prove that its vanishing in the stationary state is equivalent to time reversibility. Sample-path entropy production is identified with the logarithm of the Radon-Nikodym derivative of the forward path measure with respect to the time-reversed path measure and is shown to satisfy fluctuation theorems. For nonstationary systems, sample-path entropy production decomposes into housekeeping heat and free-energy dissipation, each satisfying an integral fluctuation theorem. Both have nonnegative expectations, and the mean free-energy dissipation equals the decrease in relative entropy with respect to the stationary distribution. The theory is applied to semilinear stochastic heat equations with spatially correlated noise, a random polymer model, a nonlinear model with a divergence-free drift, and two coupled stochastic heat equations in contact with heat baths at different temperatures.

authors.name: Hao Ge
authors.institution: University of Shanghai for Science and Technology

papers.title: LightGenBench: A Benchmark for 3D Emission Generation
papers.abstract:
Recent generation methods produce 3D assets with detailed geometry and rich textures. However, these assets are non-emissive: they reflect light but emit none. We study a new task, emission generation: predicting spatially varying RGB emission over a 3D asset's surface from its geometry, non-emissive materials, and a rendered view.
  To support this task, we introduce LightGenBench. Our benchmark makes three contributions. First, we curate a dataset of 37k artist-authored emissive assets in UV, voxel, and multi-view form. Second, we establish baselines across four method families: UV-domain, sparse-voxel, multi-view, and segmentation-based generation. Third, we design an evaluation protocol that measures where an asset emits and how, complemented by user-study comparisons on renderings with varying emission strength.
  Across the four families, the sparse-voxel baseline TRELLIS.2-Emission performs best because generating emission natively in 3D avoids the failure modes of the other representations, such as the fracturing artifacts of UV space and the occluded emitters that multi-view generation cannot see. However, TRELLIS.2-Emission only reaches an IoU of 0.271, leaving the task far from solved. We hope LightGenBench establishes emission generation as a benchmarkable problem for 3D generation.

papers.title: Graded Automorphism of Multiparameter Quantum Matrix Algebra
papers.abstract: We determine the graded automorphism group of the multiparameter quantum matrix algebra $\mathcal O_{\lambda,\mathbf p}(M_n(\Bbbk))$ over an arbitrary field $\Bbbk$ for all $n\ge2$ and $\lambda\ne1$. No other restrictions are assumed on $\mathbf p$ or $\lambda$. Every graded automorphism is a torus automorphism, possibly followed by transposition or by simultaneous reversal of the row and column indices. We give the precise parameter conditions for these two involutions. As an application, we also determine the full automorphism group when the multiplicative group generated by the parameters is torsion-free.

authors.name: Hai Jin
authors.institution: National University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Forward-Backward Map Matching for Airborne Magnetic Anomaly Navigation
papers.abstract: Airborne magnetic anomaly navigation provides a passive, unjammable alternative to Global Navigation Satellite Systems positioning by matching magnetometer measurements against a lithospheric magnetic anomaly map. Existing map-matching algorithms either assume a Gaussian posterior (extended Kalman filter), require Monte Carlo sampling (particle filter), or discard posterior uncertainty in favour of a single optimal path (Viterbi algorithm). Here we formulate map matching as inference on a chain-structured factor graph and solve it segment by segment using the forward-backward algorithm, which yields a discrete posterior over candidate positions and its Shannon entropy $H_t$ at time $t$. Over the \texttt{Renfrew\_395} map, $10^3$ synthetic trials yield a median position error of $32.7$ m, $91\%$ below the median inertial drift of $362$ m. On these trials and $10^3$ flight paths, the median error is $43\%$ below the extended Kalman filter and particle filter. Across these paths, a threshold on segment-level entropy detects $47\%$ of segments with errors above two map cells and $94\%$ of those above three, at a $10\%$ false-alarm rate. The foregoing results indicate that $H_t$ provides a truth-free diagnostic of map-conditioned navigation ambiguity.

papers.title: Secure Wireless Communications with Flexible Reflectors: Joint Position and Rotation Optimization for Physical Layer Security
papers.abstract: By exploiting the spatial selectivity of wireless channels, physical layer security (PLS) protects confidential wireless transmissions. Flexible reflectors (FRs), which are passive metallic plates mounted on movable platforms, offer a low-cost and low-complexity solution for reshaping the propagation environment. However, their potential for secrecy-oriented signal propagation shaping has not been explored. In this paper, we study an FR-aided secure communication over non-line-of-sight links and jointly optimize the positions and rotations of FRs to maximize the secrecy rate under geometric reflection and mutual-blocking constraints. For the single-FR case, we propose a Fibonacci segmentation search (FSS) method, which partitions the feasible region into multiple unimodal intervals and obtains the optimal solution with Fibonacci search over the unimodal intervals. To reduce the computational overhead, we also propose a low-complexity cross-entropy search (CES) method, which employs Gaussian mixture model-based adaptive importance sampling to localize promising search intervals before deterministic refinement. After deriving the blocked placement interval induced by the deployed FRs and integrating it into a sequential deployment scheme, we extend the FSS and CES methods to the multi-FR case. Simulation results show that our proposed FSS method achieves significant secrecy rate performance gains over various benchmark schemes, and our proposed CES method achieves a favorable runtime-performance tradeoff. These results indicate that FRs provide a low-cost and reconfigurable mechanism for PLS.

authors.name: Yiqing Li
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

papers.title: DEG: Diffusion-Enhanced GFlowNet for Solving Vehicle Routing Problems
papers.abstract: Traditional neural solvers for solving vehicle routing problems (VRPs) often suffer from limited solution diversity, motivating the development of Generative Flow Network (GFlowNet)-based models. However, the effectiveness of these models is frequently constrained by insufficient flow expansion in high-reward regions, limiting their ability to distribute probability across promising solution routes. Deeper exploration could yield superior results. Diffusion models, in contrast, provide stronger structural guidance for exploration. These two paradigms are naturally complementary: GFlowNet can supply edge-level signals for diffusion to embed, while diffusion can guide broader exploration. Leveraging this synergy, we propose Diffusion-Enhanced GFlowNet (DEG), a novel framework that integrates GFlowNet with a diffusion model to encourage richer flow expansion toward high-reward regions and derive higher-quality solutions. Specifically, DEG exploits GFlowNet's inherent diversity to generate edge-specific backward signals, applies the stochastic noise schedule of diffusion to perturb these signals, and then denoises them within the GFlowNet paradigm. To further improve scalability, we introduce a specialized decoder capable of dynamically adapting to diverse problem scales. Extensive experimental evaluations on synthetic and real-world datasets, including instances with up to 10,000 nodes, demonstrate that DEG consistently achieves favorable performance compared to baseline methods.

papers.title: Riccati Equations and the Third Problem of Halmos
papers.abstract:
Rencently, Fang, Hou, Jiang, and Zhang reduced Halmos's third problem to invertible operators with conjugate bi-geometric form. An operator has such a form if, with respect to an orthogonal decomposition, it admits a representation
  $$ T = \begin{pmatrix} A & C \\ 0 & B \end{pmatrix}, \quad A^*, B \in B_1(O_\delta),$$
  where $O_\delta=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|<\delta\}$ for some $\delta>0$, and $B_1(O_\delta)$ denotes the rank-one Cowen--Douglas class.
  We restrict our attention to the case $B=A^*$ with strictly positive coupling $C$, and settle Halmos's third problem for this class of operators. More precisely,we prove that every such operator $T$ is invertible and that $T^{-1}$ has a nontrivial closed invariant subspace. This result contributes to the study of Halmos's third problem within the conjugate bi-geometric framework.The proof combines monotone solutions of operator Riccati equations with strong operator convergence to construct invariant subspaces for associated Hamiltonian operator matrices.

papers.title: Textual Response-Aware Guidance for Zero-Shot Adversarial Robustness of Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) exhibit strong zero-shot generalization but remain vulnerable to adversarial attacks. Existing adversarial fine-tuning methods often use pre-trained model guidance to preserve image--text alignment while improving robustness. Our analysis of visual representation drift reveals complementary limitations of two representative forms of guidance. Matching visual features provides broad coverage by constraining all directions equally, but lacks semantic emphasis. Matching prediction distributions prioritizes semantically relevant directions, but remains limited by the candidate texts and prediction probabilities. These limitations can hinder preservation of pre-trained image--text relationships and degrade zero-shot performance. To address these issues, we propose Textual Response-Aware Guidance (TRAG), which constrains visual representation drift using the pre-trained text encoder's responses to local variations in input embeddings. Specifically, TRAG constructs anchor-level constraints from the response directions and magnitudes around semantic anchors, then aggregates them using pre-trained image--anchor relevance, yielding an image-adaptive constraint. Extensive experiments across architectures and tasks demonstrate state-of-the-art clean and robust performance. Further analysis shows that TRAG helps preserve pre-trained image--text relationships.

papers.title: Complementing Text Based Moderation with Multimodal Grounding: Detecting Fraudulent Inducement Behaviors on Short Video Platforms
papers.abstract: Short video platforms have become a primary channel for black and gray industry operations in internet finance, where inducements such as prompts to like, follow, join private chat groups, or click external links frequently steer users toward fraud. Because such videos are short, dynamic, and often convey intent through fleeting visual cues rather than stable text, a moderation system must guarantee detection recall and localize the offending segment so reviewers inspect only the relevant clip. Existing OCR+LLM pipelines transcribe on-screen text frame by frame and classify the transcript, but exploit only textual information. Many inducements are conveyed through visual cues OCR cannot observe, and keyframe-based localization cannot recover precise temporal boundaries. We explore OCR+MLLM, which augments the text pipeline with a Multimodal Large Language Model, and compare three routes: OCR+LLM, OCR+MLLM, and a large zero-shot MLLM, along detection, latency, token consumption, and deployment complexity. OCR preserves the text signal that guarantees recall, while the MLLM jointly performs OCR-grounded discrimination and temporal grounding, localizing both textual and non-textual inducements. We construct a dataset of 2,419 internet finance short videos (66.49 hours) with 3,194 annotated events across four categories, and study reward design for RL-based grounding under class imbalance. We report two findings: auxiliary reward terms are exploited through reward hacking, and stronger localization rewards degrade class-balanced detection. We therefore design a recall-weighted F2 localization reward with class-balanced resampling. Experiments show OCR+MLLM localizes better than the keyframe OCR+LLM baseline (mIoU 26.52 vs. 14.49) and detects non-textual inducements that text-only pipelines miss, while maintaining 67.0 percent macro recall.

authors.name: Xiaoyong Yu
authors.institution: Heilongjiang Center for Tuberculosis Control and Prevention

papers.title: Calculation and rejection diverge in language models tested at known mechanical limits
papers.abstract: When a language model returns engineering quantities with the status "solved", software that trusts it passes them on, even when the requested design is physically impossible. Such failures could reflect poor calculation, how the answer is requested, or a failure to judge feasibility. We set beam loads and disk speeds at known percentages above or below plastic collapse or burst, measured each model's limit calculation separately and tested 12 models in 4,860 calls, including follow-up experiments on new designs. We find that a model can recognize an impossible design when asked only whether it is feasible, yet accept the same design, reporting "solved", when asked for a full answer. Three models accepted beams 10 to 30% beyond collapse despite precise limit calculations in separate questions, and many accepted replies stated the violation. Asked only about feasibility, Opus 5 and Gemini 3.8 Flash rejected every impossible new design they were given, including those accepted in full answers, without false alarms. Rewording when to decline or changing the answer format raised rejection on the original beams, but not consistently on new designs. Software and benchmarks using a model's status should test feasibility judgment and full-answer rejection separately, and report the exact prompt.

authors.name: Shaoliang Yang
authors.institution: Obstetrics and Gynecology Hospital of Fudan University

authors.name: Jun Wang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Machine Learning Based Classification of Type 1 Active Galactic Nuclei
papers.abstract:
Aims. We aim to provide a machine learning based method to distinguish type 1 quasars and type 1 Seyfert galaxies based on photometric data, which could be applied to large all-sky surveys. The method can also be used to obtain relatively complete samples of Seyfert galaxy candidates when broad-line AGNs have been selected.
  Results. The results of PCA show that quasars and Seyfert galaxies are partial distinguishable. The supervised classifier based on random forest (RF) achieves good performances for type 1 quasars with a F1 score of 0.967. The performance for classifying Seyfert galaxies is worse, with a F1 score of 0.791. Increasing the classification threshold can help to derive a sample of Seyfert galaxies with high purity. The classifier are then applied to the cross-matched sample with DESI DR1. When compared with the results of spectroscopic classification, quasars also show high precision and recall. For Seyfert galaxies identified by RF classifier, there are plenty of less luminous sources who are classified as quasars by spectroscopic method. If they are regarded as Seyfert galaxies, our classifier also performs well to predict Seyfert galaxies. Both the median SEDs and the fraction of Seyfert galaxies derived by our classifier are similar with those for the training sample, while the fraction of Seyfert galaxies for spectroscopic classification are lower at all redshift. These results indicate that our classifier can recover the features of Seyfert galaxies, at least those similar to the Seyfert galaxies in the training sample.

authors.name: Jie Li
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Optimal Regret for Communication-Efficient Decentralized Online Learning
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate decentralized online convex optimization with compressed communication, where $n$ learners over a network jointly minimize a sequence of global loss functions based only on their local losses and compressed messages from their neighbors. The best known regret bounds for this problem are $O(\omega^{-1/2}n\rho^{-1}\sqrt{T\ln n})$ and $O(\omega^{-1}n\rho^{-2}\ln n\ln T)$ for convex and strongly convex loss functions, respectively, where $\rho\in(0,1)$ is the spectral gap of the communication matrix and $\omega\in(0,1]$ is the compression quality factor. Compared with the corresponding lower bounds of $\Omega(\omega^{-1/2}n\rho^{-1/4}\sqrt{T})$ and $\Omega(\omega^{-1}n\rho^{-1/2}\ln T)$, these upper bounds exhibit polynomial gaps in their dependence on $\rho^{-1}$. To close these gaps, we first develop Ascent-gossip, which combines an online compression strategy with a Chebyshev recursion and attains a faster consensus rate than existing compressed gossip methods. Furthermore, by adopting Ascent-gossip, we propose an online algorithm that achieves optimal regret bounds of $\widetilde O(\omega^{-1/2}n\rho^{-1/4}\sqrt{T})$ and $\widetilde O(\omega^{-1}n\rho^{-1/2}\ln T)$ for convex and strongly convex loss functions, respectively. Up to logarithmic factors in $n$ and $\rho^{-1}$, these results match the lower bounds in terms of $T$, $n$, $\rho$, and $\omega$.

authors.name: Wei Jiang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Lijun Zhang
authors.institution: Yunnan University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

papers.title: Projective compactifications of hypersurface complements
papers.abstract: Let $U$ be a smooth affine variety of the form $U=\mathrm{P}^n\setminus H$, where $H\subset\mathrm{P}^n$ is a smooth connected hypersurface. We prove that every smooth projective compactification of the complex manifold $U$, by adding a smooth connected divisor, is isomorphic to $\mathrm{P}^n$. The proof uses the rational Reeb index of the normal circle bundle and positive $S^1$-equivariant symplectic homology. This paper is motivated by the work of Chi Li and Zhengyi Zhou, and makes a generalization to their result.

papers.title: On loop-soup clusters in three dimensions and higher
papers.abstract:
We study clusters of the Brownian loop soup on $\mathbb{R}^3$ and of random walk and metric-graph loop soups on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ and $\widetilde{\mathbb{Z}}^d$ within a unified framework. For the continuum model, when the one-arm exponent $\xi(\alpha)$ is positive, we prove that almost surely every cluster has Hausdorff dimension $3-\xi(\alpha)$. A key step is to show that, conditioned on the one-arm event, a crossing cluster has capacity comparable to the crossing scale with uniformly positive probability. This gives one-arm estimates of order $\alpha r^{-\xi(\alpha)}$, uniformly down to zero intensity, and shows that $\xi(\alpha)$ is strictly decreasing and left-continuous. Moreover, $1-\xi(\alpha)\asymp\alpha$ as $\alpha\downarrow0$. As another application of the one-arm estimates, we prove that several critical values coincide, resolving a conjecture of Jego and Lupu in arXiv:2601.04840.
  The proof combines a decoupling technique with a multiscale recursive argument to control the combined effects of large and small loops. These methods also extend to loop soups on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ and $\widetilde{\mathbb{Z}}^d$ for $d=3,4,5$, yielding capacity lower bounds of order $r$, $r^2/\log r$, and $r^2$ for the cluster of the origin, conditioned on the one-arm event, throughout the small-loop decay regime. In particular, these bounds imply strict polynomial comparisons between one-arm probabilities at different intensities in dimension three. We also show that the small-loop decay regime on $\widetilde{\mathbb{Z}}^d$ has upper endpoint $\frac{1}{2}$ by adapting the OSSS sharpness framework to the truncated loop soup.

authors.name: Yifan Gao
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Curvature-Dimension Conditions Along Discrete Refinement Sequences
papers.abstract: We introduce the sequence curvature--dimension condition $SCD(K,N)$ for complete refinement systems of finite metric probability spaces. The condition couples a transport action bound with entropy comparisons along a single probability section through the prescribed refinement layers. Within a bounded comparison range, we prove that midpoint comparisons on three consecutive layers characterize the condition on every fixed finite segment. If, in addition, the refinement sequence converges in the measured sense in its intrinsic bridge realization, then $SCD(K,N)$ is equivalent both to the vanishing of single-layer midpoint defects and to the entropic curvature--dimension condition $CD^{e}(K,N)$ of the limit. In the reverse direction, a $CD^{e}(K,N)$ bound on the limit yields quantitative recovery estimates that identify shrinking transport scales on which finite layers retain its second-order curvature comparison. These estimates are uniform over endpoint measures and include Dirac masses. Examples illustrate the effects of the refinement rule, the layer metrics and the reference measures.

authors.name: Chen Tao
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Unique Positive Extremals and Sharp Stability Constants for Singular Moser-Trudinger Inequalities
papers.abstract:
We combine spectral perturbation with orthogonal transformations in $H_0^1(\Omega)$ to study singular Moser-Trudinger inequalities under the energy constraint $\int_\Omega|\nabla u|^2\,dx\le1$, where $\Omega$ is a smooth bounded planar domain containing the origin. For the weight $|x|^{-2\beta}$, $0\le\beta<1$, the positive maximizer is unique for small $\alpha>0$, and the sharp global stability constant satisfies \[
  C_\alpha=\frac{\alpha}{2}
  \left(\frac1{\mu_1}-\frac1{\mu_2}\right)+O(\alpha^2),
  \qquad \alpha\downarrow0, \] where $\mu_1<\mu_2$ are the first two weighted Dirichlet eigenvalues. We compute the second asymptotic coefficient by a weighted quartic maximization on the second eigenspace, even when the second eigenvalue is multiple. An exact reduction to the sphere orthogonal to the maximizer identifies the attaining functions and yields a limiting global-to-local ratio of $1/2$. On the disk, the energy derivative with respect to the central value characterizes radial constrained degeneracy and yields finitely many exceptional normalized parameters. Combined with known critical uniqueness and nondegeneracy, this gives uniform quadratic stability near criticality, while compactness and analytic reduction yield finite-power stability throughout the admissible range.

authors.name: Yanjun Liu
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Point Corrections and Wall-Crossing Geometry on the Quintic del Pezzo Threefold
papers.abstract:
Let $X=V_5$ be the quintic del Pezzo threefold. Along the negative zero-tilt-slope paths for rational-curve ideal classes, degree five is the first degree admitting a positive point correction. We determine the resulting degree-five outer good moduli space: it is reduced with exactly two irreducible components, a normal ten-dimensional principal branch and a smooth corrected branch $X\times\mathrm{Gr}(2,7)$. Their scheme-theoretic intersection is a normal determinantal ninefold. Along its singular locus, the principal branch has transverse rank-one $2\times 4$ determinantal singularities, while the intersection has the corresponding $2\times 3$ singularities.
  We construct an explicit small resolution of the principal branch as the projectivization of a rank-five extension bundle over the blow-up of the Altavilla--Petkovi\'c--Rota Kuznetsov-component sixfold along its point locus. Uniform wall exclusion and point-correction bounds for degrees two through five establish the first correction threshold; the corrected degree-five factors are precisely the ideals of elliptic linear sections parametrized by $\mathrm{Gr}(2,7)$.

papers.title: Softmax Routing Dynamics in Mixture-of-Experts Models: Collapse and Recovery
papers.abstract: Softmax routing in mixture-of-experts models can concentrate probability on a subset of experts, suppressing access to the others. We study how this concentration forms, why it persists, and how suppressed probabilities recover. For fixed experts, a stationary-loss barrier identifies the face supporting the optimal routed output. In a common-target square-loss model with freely trainable expert outputs, slow adaptation tracks fixed-expert dynamics on finite horizons, while every fixed positive adaptation rate yields an interior routing limit. An exact normal-velocity decomposition separates complementary-expert covariance from relative gradient advantage. Under positive two-sided power bounds along recovery paths, uniform over initial masses, the resulting coefficient's order of vanishing gives logarithmic or power-law recovery times. Integrations of constructed fields reproduce these orders. An exact discrete log-odds identity relates neural updates to threshold crossing. In paired Transformer-MoE training, removing a class-conditional router-gradient contrast delays confirmed recovery and reduces accumulated log-odds on fixed tokens, both with and without capacity constraints.

papers.title: The maximum degree of Nosal graphs
papers.abstract: A graph $G$ with $m$ edges is a Nosal graph if its spectral radius $\lambda(G)$ exceeds $\sqrt m$. At the threshold $\lambda(G)=\sqrt m$, the star $K_{1,m}$ shows that one vertex can be incident with all $m$ edges. In contrast, Li, Liu and Zhang [J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 179 (2026)] proved that every Nosal graph $G$ with sufficiently many edges satisfies $\Delta(G)\le\frac12m+m^{0.99}$, where the constant $\frac12$ is best possible. In this paper, we prove that every Nosal graph $G$ with spectral radius $\lambda$ satisfies $\Delta(G)<m-\frac12(\lambda-1)(\lambda-2)$, and hence $\Delta(G)<\frac12m+\frac32\sqrt m-1$. Both bounds are sharp up to an additive constant less than $\frac12$: for every $r\ge3$, the complete graph $K_r$ with $\frac12(r^2+r-2)$ pendant vertices attached to one vertex is a Nosal graph with $r^2-1$ edges whose maximum degree lies within $\frac12$ of both bounds. Consequently, the largest maximum degree of a Nosal graph with $r^2-1$ edges is exactly $\frac12(r^2+3r-4)$. The first bound cannot be improved by any positive additive constant: its gap on these graphs is less than $\frac{4}{r+5}$ and tends to zero as $r\to \infty$.

papers.title: Sparse domination and an extended $L^p$ range for the trilinear Hilbert transform
papers.abstract: We establish sparse bounds for the trilinear Hilbert transform $$ T(f_1,f_2,f_3)(x):=\textrm{p.v.}\int_{\mathbb R} f_1(x-t)f_2(x-2t)f_3(x-3t)\,\frac{dt}{t}, $$ with averaging exponents arbitrarily close to $2$ from above. As a consequence, we extend OpenAI's $L^3\times L^3\times L^3\to L^1$ bound (entry 086 in the OpenAI Research Catalog) to $L^{p_1}\times L^{p_2}\times L^{p_3}\to L^r$ throughout the range $$ 2<p_1,p_2,p_3<\infty, \qquad \frac1r=\frac1{p_1}+\frac1{p_2}+\frac1{p_3}, \qquad \frac23<r<2, $$ and obtain corresponding weighted estimates for weights in multilinear Muckenhoupt classes. Our proof relies on the normalized local estimate and stopping time argument developed in OpenAI's work.

papers.title: Complete $RO$-Graded Tambara Structure of $H\underline{\mathbb Z}$ for cyclic groups
papers.abstract:
We compute the $RO$-graded Tambara functor of $H\underline{\mathbb{Z}}$ for every finite cyclic group. We introduce a valuation language for homotopy groups: for prime-power cyclic group equivariant, classes are represented by compatible vertex arrays or by edge arrays. In these coordinates we compute products, restrictions, transfers, Weyl actions, and norms. Then we assemble the results into arbitrary finite cyclic group equivariant case.
  Besides the computation, we also develop the Tate compression theory, which is used in the computation. The Tate compression diagram cut an equivariant spectra into several layer, which the homotopy group can be describe directly by each layers. From it we also give a filtration for $\pi_\star(H\underline{\mathbb{Z}})$, compatible with products, restrictions, transfers, Weyl actions, and norms.

authors.name: Dongming Zhang
authors.institution: Tianjin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Holistic Diversity Management in LLM-Guided Evolutionary Search
papers.abstract: LLM-guided evolutionary search iteratively selects existing programs, uses LLMs as mutation operators to generate a new program, and evaluates it to guide subsequent search. To preserve diversity and reduce the risk of premature convergence, it often adopts the island model, in which groups of programs, called islands, evolve separately. However, this structure alone does not guarantee distinct search directions, as islands may start from similar programs or converge toward similar solutions during evolution. This suggests that diversity must be considered throughout the search process, from initializing islands with distinct programs to developing island trajectories and sharing discoveries across islands. To this end, we propose HoliDivEvolve , a holistic approach to establishing and effectively utilizing island diversity throughout evolutionary search. Specifically, we introduce diverse initialization to establish different initial programs, trajectory adaptive island selection to allocate computation based on current score, recent growth, and the remaining search budget, and growth adaptive migration to share alternative ideas across islands. Experiments across diverse benchmarks show that HoliDivEvolve achieves competitive performance on most evaluated tasks. We further conduct controlled analyses to examine how our design choices affect search behavior and final performance.

authors.name: Seockbean Song
authors.institution: Pohang University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Youngsik Yoon
authors.institution: Pohang University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Wei Chen
authors.institution: Shanghai University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

authors.name: Jungseul Ok
authors.institution: Pohang University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Hydrodynamic and Dynamical Phi^4 Limits of Ising-Kac Models with Diffusion-Based Interactions on the Sierpi\'nski Gasket
papers.abstract: We introduce a general form of Ising--Kac interactions through heat-kernel averaging, with the heat-time parameter replacing the role of the interaction range. From the viewpoint of Dirichlet forms theory, this construction provides an intrinsic analogue of the mesoscopic averaging in classical Kac models when translation invariance is unavailable. We then investigate limits of this model on graph approximations of the Sierpi\'nski gasket. For the associated Glauber dynamics, we establish a hierarchy of scaling limits for the magnetization field. First, at fixed interaction heat time and inverse temperature, we derive a nonlocal hydrodynamic equation on the continuum gasket. Second, as the heat time vanishes and the inverse temperature approaches its mean-field critical value, suitably rescaled hydrodynamic solutions converge to the solution of the deterministic Allen--Cahn equation. Finally, under a joint scaling of graph refinement, interaction heat time, and inverse temperature near criticality, we prove convergence of critical magnetization fluctuations to the solution of the dynamical $\Phi^4$ equation. These results provide a concrete realization of the Ising-$\Phi^4$ correspondence in a geometric setting with non-integer spectral dimension.

authors.name: Hongyi Chen
authors.institution: Tianjin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Distributed online learning with growing dimensions for stochastic large regression
papers.abstract: This paper investigates distributed online estimation and prediction for stochastic large regression models with infinitely many unknown parameters. Existing distributed estimation methods are mostly restricted to finite-dimensional parameter spaces, making them inadequate for emerging infinite-dimensional modeling applications. To tackle this problem, this paper proposes a fully distributed online recursive least squares algorithm with dynamically growing model dimension.The algorithm is constructed with an incrementally augmentable recursive structure, where new parameter dimensions can be embedded in the recursion via zero-padded covariance and estimate augmentation without re-initialization.The almost sure convergence of the algorithm is established under a weak cooperative non-persistent excitation condition, without requiring independence or stationarity assumptions on the regressors.This condition integrates spatio-temporal network information and extends existing finite-dimensional results. The paper further derives an almost sure upper bound on the accumulated prediction regret without any excitation conditions. It is proven that the average regret converges to zero almost surely for a broad class of dimension growth sequences, with the optimal finite-dimensional regret bound recovered as a special case. Finally, numerical simulations are conducted to verify the effectiveness of our theoretical findings.

papers.title: Sharp potential and Brenier map $W_2$-stability for log-concave sources
papers.abstract:
We study stability of Brenier potentials and maps under changes of the target measure. Let $\kappa>0$, for a full support $\kappa$-strongly log-concave source $ho$, possibly with a non-smooth potential, the normalized transport potentials satisfy \[ \|u_\mu-u_
u\|_{L^2(ho)}\leqslant\sqrt{2/\kappa}\,W_2(\mu,
u) \] for arbitrary targets with finite second moments. The proof controls normalized Laguerre cell barycentres by their mass derivatives and centers the potential velocity to remove unbounded source cell locations. Bounded variation interpolation then yields the sharp map exponent $1/3$ for targets in a common compact set, \[ \left\Vert T_{\mu}-T_{
u}ight\Vert _{L^{2}(ho)}\leqslant \operatorname{Const} \cdot W_{2}\left( \mu,
uight) ^{1/3}. \] Sharpness of the exponents for both the potential and Brenier map stability are established.

authors.name: Yuanlong Ruan
authors.institution: Tianjin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Petty's equilateral-set conjecture in dimension five
papers.abstract: Petty conjectured that every n-dimensional real normed space contains n+1 equidistant points. The conjecture was proved in dimensions three and four by Petty and Makeev, respectively. We prove the five-dimensional case: every five-dimensional real normed space contains six equidistant points. The proof uses a bordism of equilateral configurations and a homological obstruction.

papers.title: DeFT-RAG: Incrementally Decomposing Multi-Hop Questions into Self-Contained Sub-Questions with Reusable Answers
papers.abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) lets a large language model (LLM) answer questions by retrieving relevant passages from a large corpus. However, RAG struggles with multi-hop questions, which require chaining facts spread across several documents through intermediate entities that the question never mentions. Graph-based RAG methods retrieve once from the entities a question names and so rarely recover the full evidence chain. Iterative RAG methods recover it step by step, but their accuracy is limited by the many tasks they ask the LLM to perform, such as planning the sub-questions, deciding their dependencies, rewriting them as answers arrive, and keeping track of what is known. We propose DeFT-RAG, a RAG framework built on three components. First, DeFT-RAG generates one self-contained sub-question at a time from the original question and the sub-questions answered so far with their answers (QA pairs). Each sub-question names every entity it asks about, which removes the need to plan, track dependencies or rewrite, and lets the LLM focus on a single fine-grained task at a time. Second, DeFT-RAG moves the remaining LLM work outside the LLM: rule-based updates to a QA table that keeps track of what is known, and yes/no decisions made by a fine-tuned lightweight decision model. Third, DeFT-RAG caches the QA pairs and reuses an answer when a later question asks a sub-question with the same meaning. On MuSiQue, 2WikiMultiHopQA and HotpotQA, DeFT-RAG achieves the best accuracy among thirteen baselines with both gpt-4o-mini and Qwen3.6 as the backbone, while giving the LLM fewer input tokens than any other iterative method. With a QA cache shared across 1,000 MuSiQue questions, 23.1% of sub-questions are answered from the cache, which reduces LLM calls by 12.9% without lowering accuracy.

authors.name: Dingyi Kang
authors.institution: The University of Texas at Dallas

papers.title: Width and amplitude inequalities over DG-rings
papers.abstract: We study width over commutative noetherian local differential graded (DG) rings with bounded homology. We establish a derived width formula and prove amplitude inequalities for the derived completion of derived Hom and tensor products. As applications, we obtain Iversen's amplitude inequality and a criterion ensuring that regular sequences on a DG-module are regular on the DG-ring. These applications recover results for DG-modules with finitely generated homology and also hold for derived complete DG-modules. Finally, we characterize Cohen--Macaulay DG-rings by the existence of a bounded derived complete DG-module of finite injective dimension whose amplitude equals that of the DG-ring. This provides a version of Bass' conjecture for derived complete DG-modules.

authors.name: Luigi Ferraro
authors.institution: The University of Texas Rio Grande Valley

papers.title: G-equivariant Alterfold TQFT in any dimension
papers.abstract: For a discrete group $G$, we construct an $(n+1)$-dimensional $G$-equivariant Alterfold topological quantum field theory from a $G$-equivariant $S^n$-algebra satisfying strong semisimplicity, complete finiteness, and Morita invariance. We use state sum on triangulation to define a partition function and prove that it is invariant under local surgery relations and is invariant under gauge transformations relative to the boundary. If the input is given a reflection-positive structure, the theory is unitary. For $n=2$ and input reconstructed from a strict faithful spherical $G$-fusion category, the restriction to ordinary $G$-cobordisms is naturally isomorphic to the Turaev--Virelizier state-sum HQFT \cite{turaev20123}. A Tambara-Yamagami example recovers the Quon language \cite{liu2017quon} as a $\mathbb{Z}_2$-equivariant Alterfold TQFT.

authors.name: Zixuan Feng
authors.institution: Key Laboratory of Automobile Materials, Ministry of Education, Jilin University

papers.title: Optimality and Exact Moment-SDP Formulations for Robust Two-Stage Convex Polynomial Multiobjective Optimization
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study Geoffrion properly efficient solutions of affinely adjustable robust two-stage convex polynomial multiobjective optimization problems with spectrahedral uncertainty. For convex polynomial data, we establish sufficient optimality conditions and necessary conditions under a Slater condition. Under SOS-convexity, we obtain an exact SOS characterization of proper efficiency. Using strictly positive weighted-sum scalarization, we develop a finite-dimensional moment-SDP formulation and establish its optimal-value exactness under the strict feasibility condition. We further establish the recovery results connecting Geoffrion properly efficient solutions with moment-SDP optimal solutions.

authors.name: Yongqi Jiang
authors.institution: Changjiang Institute of Survey, Planning, Design and Research

papers.title: An Adaptive Transferable Neural Network for Partial Differential Equations with Anisotropic or Sharp Solutions
papers.abstract: Transferable neural network (TransNet) has demonstrated great potential for solving partial differential equations (PDEs) with high accuracy and efficiency. However, it struggles significantly when dealing with PDEs featuring anisotropy or sharp solutions. In this work, we propose an adaptive transferable neural network (A-TransNet), a novel machine learning framework that adaptively expands neurons in regions with large solution gradients to effectively capture complex solution behaviors. Instead of relying on training or random sampling, the location parameters of newly added neurons are determined by integrating the active subspaces method and local gradient analysis based on posterior gradient information. This adaptive strategy enables neurons to be allocated where they are most needed, thereby improving the resolution of anisotropic and sharp features without additional computational costs. Moreover, the shape parameters of new neurons are automatically determined from the neuron density induced by their locations, further enhancing the network representation capability. An iterative neuron expansion strategy is developed, together with rigorous analysis of stability, a posteriori error estimation, and convergence of the proposed A-TransNet method. Extensive numerical experiments on challenging PDE problems with anisotropic and sharp solutions demonstrate that A-TransNet achieves superior accuracy, efficiency, and robustness compared with existing methods.

authors.name: Jiacong Qu
authors.institution: Changchun University of Science and Technology

papers.title: After One-Click Video: The Inflow of Service-Type Content, the Failure of the Recommendation Pool Mechanism, and the BoLe System
papers.abstract: In September 2026, a new large language model was released. Soon after, a new way of making explainer videos became very popular: people asked the model to write a program, and the program produced the video. "One-click video" content then appeared in large amounts on many platforms. On the surface, this is a rise in creative power at the level of the individual. We argue that, at a deeper level, it changes the structure of the content industry. This judgment rests on two observations. First, this wave of content is service-type content. People watch it to meet a need, not to enjoy the content itself. The other kind is work-type content. AI makes both kinds faster to produce. But anyone can come in and make service-type content, while work-type content is limited by the number of people who have something to say. So the ratio between the two slowly becomes unbalanced. Second, free platforms choose content through layers of trial viewing, and this uses up user attention. The total amount of attention is fixed. The unbalanced ratio also dilutes good content. A simplified mathematical model shows that, as long as these conditions hold, the recommendation pool mechanism will fail once new content grows past a certain multiple. Based on this, we discuss one possible way out. Machines and entry rules judge whether service-type content passes the bar. Trusted people judge work-type content. We call this the BoLe system. At the end, we briefly imagine how the two kinds of content may develop from here.

papers.title: Thermodynamic Crossovers in Supercritical Matter: One, No One, and One Hundred Thousand
papers.abstract: Beyond a critical point, two thermodynamic phases become continuously connected, without being separated by any thermodynamic singularity. The paradigmatic example is the liquid-gas transition, where several criteria have been proposed to distinguish liquid-like and gas-like regimes within the supercritical region. Recently, a pair of thermodynamic crossover lines, $L^\pm$, was introduced to address a proposed incompatibility of previous definitions with the universal critical behavior of the Ising model. These lines divide the supercritical region into three regimes, meet only at the critical point, and obey the expected critical scaling laws. Here, we demonstrate that these requirements do not uniquely determine the crossover boundaries. Instead, infinitely many pairs of lines satisfy the same conditions, with different choices of thermodynamic paths selecting different crossover boundaries. We further show that the Lee-Yang formalism, despite providing an intrinsic characterization of critical singularities, does not resolve this ambiguity in defining real-axis crossover boundaries. Restricting to regular probing paths that respect the $Z_2$ symmetry of the critical point recovers the Widom and $L^\pm$ prescriptions asymptotically. This restriction, however, is a choice of protocol rather than a property of the system, and even then two inequivalent prescriptions survive. Our results demonstrate that universal critical behavior alone does not select privileged supercritical thermodynamic crossover boundaries. While such lines may identify physically meaningful changes in thermodynamic, structural, or transport properties, their precise locations and the widths of the regions they delimit remain dependent on the operational criteria used to define them.

papers.title: SaiVLA-JEPA: Evaluating Future Latent Prediction in JEPA-Conditioned VLA Control
papers.abstract: Joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs) learn to predict representations rather than pixels, offering a compact way to model how visual scenes evolve. We ask whether this predictive objective improves closed-loop control when a vision-language-action (VLA) policy already uses V-JEPA features. We call our JEPA-conditioned flow policy family SaiVLA-JEPA. It combines a vision-language model with a diffusion transformer action expert and receives features from a frozen V-JEPA encoder. Two lightweight auxiliary heads predict future representations during training and are omitted at inference, leaving the action sampler unchanged. We compare policies without JEPA features, with current JEPA conditioning, and with additional future supervision on 10,030 paired LIBERO-Plus episodes. Current JEPA conditioning reaches about 82.5% success versus 71.6% without JEPA, while future supervision provides no detectable aggregate gain at the evaluated training budget. We separately evaluate SaiVLA-JEPA-TCA, which adapts latent context, and SaiVLA-JEPA-TPA, which adapts selected parameters. The context-retry gain is a system-level result under a larger attempt budget; parameter adaptation shows no consistent advantage over the frozen policy and target controls. These results motivate assessing latent-prediction objectives through paired closed-loop rollouts rather than latent loss alone.

authors.name: Wei Chen
authors.institution: Shanghai University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

authors.name: Xinhai Sun
authors.institution: Jiangsu University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Learning Between the Lines: Interaction Interpolation in a Multi Element Machine Learning Interatomic Potential
papers.abstract: The continuous development of machine learning inter-atomic potentials (MLIAPs)has greatly accelerated materials research in recent years. However, the need to con- struct custom MLIAPs for each unique problem remains a bottleneck which raises the question of the transferability of MLIAPs. While foundation MLIAPs can achieve transferability due to the broad coverage of chemical space represented in their training sets, their size and computational cost limits their routine use. We address this gap by developing a lightweight general-purpose MLIAP for metal alloys spanning twelve elements (Al, Sc, Ti, V, Cu, Zn, Zr, Nb, Mo, Hf, Ta, W). Here, we utilize a step-wise active learning (AL) approach to develop a compact yet diverse dataset and model that generalizes well by interpolating from previously seen interactions. The resulting potentials transfer effectively to unseen, higher body-order alloys systems, requiring only unary and binary training data to capture ternary and quaternary systems. The model also transfers well to new elements via an alchemical extrapolation within the network, requiring only unary data for the new element and its alloys. These findings suggest that MLIAPs trained on targeted, diversity-driven datasets provide transferability at a relatively low computational cost, offering a practical path toward general-purpose, resource-efficient MLIAPs for materials modeling.

papers.title: Intersectional Invariant Learning for Fair Deepfake Detection
papers.abstract: Deepfake detection models achieve high overall accuracy but exhibit large performance disparities across demographic groups, causing some groups to experience substantially higher false-positive rates than others. Existing fairness-aware methods address this by constraining model outputs to equalize group predictions, but do not tackle the underlying feature-level bias. As a result, models may still rely on demographic characteristics, such as skin texture, as indirect cues for detecting manipulated content. To address this problem, we propose Intersectional Invariant Learning (IIL), a framework that improves feature learning rather than only adjusting model outputs. IIL alternates between identifying the most challenging demographic partitions and learning features that remain consistent across those partitions. The framework also includes a false-positive-rate fairness objective and group-balanced sampling across six gender x skin-tone intersectional groups. We evaluate IIL on a large-scale fairness benchmark containing over one million images, 10 baseline detectors, and 21 fairness and utility metrics. Results show that IIL achieves Pareto-optimal performance, simultaneously attaining an AUC above 99%, a false-positive rate under 2.5%, and the lowest intersectional fairness disparity (FMEO) among all compared methods. IIL outperforms prior fairness-aware methods on the large majority of the 21 evaluation metrics, while reducing both false-positive rates and intersectional fairness disparities by several-fold compared with the strongest competing method.

papers.title: FYC: FPR-Disparity Weight Perturbation and Youden Calibration for Fair Deepfake Detection
papers.abstract: Deepfake detectors routinely achieve high aggregate accuracy while exhibiting substantial demographic disparities in their errors: false-positive rates differ by double digits across gender and skin tone. Most existing remedies require either full retraining with a fairness-aware objective or demographic-annotated training data, both impractical when only a pretrained checkpoint is available, while label-free post-hoc calibrators leave the detector's weights unchanged. We introduce FYC (FPR-disparity Weight Perturbation and Youden Calibration), a two-stage post-hoc method that perturbs a detector's weights under an FPR-disparity criterion, then calibrates a separate decision threshold for each demographic group - requiring no architectural changes and no full retraining. Evaluated against every detector benchmarked on AI-Face v2 across six intersectional gender x skin-tone groups, FYC outperforms the field on 18 of 21 reported fairness and utility metrics, including purpose-built fairness architectures, at a fraction of the training cost. We further identify why the choice of fairness criterion is critical: the original Demographic Parity objective used in prior weight-perturbation work is architecture-dependent and unpredictable, improving two of four evaluated architectures, leaving a third largely unchanged, and substantially degrading the fourth (PG-FDD), with no way to anticipate the outcome for a given checkpoint in advance. Conditioning the same objective on real images only - our FPR-disparity criterion - eliminates this unpredictability, improving fairness and accuracy jointly across all four architectures with no exceptions.

papers.title: The equal norm Grassmannian: topology and applications to frame fields
papers.abstract: Given an orientable rank-$d$ vector bundle over a $d$-manifold, the Euler class is the unique obstruction to finding a nowhere-zero section. An equal norm Parseval frame is a certain collection of sections, one of whose properties is that the lengths of each vector at each point are equal. This makes the Euler class an obvious obstruction to finding such a frame. In this work we show that this is the only obstruction so long as the number of sections is at least $2d+2$. We also identify precise obstructions when the number of sections is $2d$ and produce examples showing that for smaller numbers of sections it is sometimes impossible to find Parseval frame fields.

papers.title: Revisiting Guo-Huang-Wang-Wei pointwise estimates for radial solutions to the fourth-order H\'enon equation in the punctured space
papers.abstract:
We study pointwise estimates for positive, $C^4$-solution $u$ to the fourth-order H\'enon equation \[ \Delta^2 u = |x|^\sigma u^p \quad \text{in } \mathbf R^n \setminus \{0\} \] with $n \geq 5$, $p>1$, and $\sigma >-4 $. In an earlier work published in J. Anal. Math. 140 (2020) 371-394, Z. Guo, X. Huang, L. Wang, and J. Wei established the following pointwise estimate \[ -\Delta u \geq \frac 2{n-4} \frac{|\nabla u|^2}u + \sqrt{\frac {n(n-4)}{n^2-4}} u^\frac{n}{n-4} \quad \text{in } \mathbf R^n \setminus \{0\} \] for radial solutions to the critical, fourth-order Lane-Emden equation, namely $\sigma = 0$ and $p=(n+4)/(n-4)$. Inspired by this interesting result, we establish a similar pointwise inequality \[ -\Delta u \geq \frac 2{n-4} \frac{|\nabla u|^2}u + \sqrt{\frac 2{p+1- \frac 8{n(n-4)}}} |x|^{\frac \sigma 2} u^\frac{p+1}2
  \quad \text{in } \mathbf R^n \setminus \{0\} \] for radial solutions to the fourth-order H\'enon equation in $\mathbf R^n \setminus \{0\}$ for any $\sigma \geq 0$ and $p \geq (n+4 + \sigma)/(n-4)$. We also show that the constant $2/(n-4)$ is sharp and that the thresholds $\sigma \geq 0$ and $p \geq (n+4 + \sigma)/(n-4)$ are necessary. As in our previous study on the case of $\mathbf R^n$, our proof is also based on the Bernstein technique via the maximum principle, hence appears to be simpler and more constructive. However, to avoid possible singularity at the origin, we develop a Bernstein technique in one-dimensional space, which is capable of handling equations in punctured spaces.

papers.title: Presentations for sisters of one-cusped Picard modular groups
papers.abstract: We generalize a method devised by Mark and Paupert for finding group presentations of the single-cusped standard Picard modular groups $\text{PU}(2, 1; \mathcal{O}_d)$, where $\mathcal{O}_d$ is the ring of integers of $\mathbb{Q}(i\sqrt{d})$, to a more general class of lattices in $\text{PU}(2, 1)$. As an application, we give presentations for the so-called \textit{sisters} of the standard Picard modular groups for $d=3, 7,$ and $11$. In particular, this shows that the sister of $\text{PU}(2, 1; \mathcal{O}_7)$ is a perfect group.

papers.title: CADENCE: Distributional Next-Transaction Forecasting for Business Cash-Flow Underwriting
papers.abstract: Recurring cash flows are the backbone of cash-flow underwriting: they separate durable revenue from one-off deposits, expose standing obligations, and ultimately determine ability to pay. For small businesses, recurrence is both indispensable and hard to estimate, because much of their income arrives as ambiguous transfers, most payment streams are short, and schedules follow calendar conventions that frequency-domain methods treat as noise. We present CADENCE, Calendar-Aware Distributional Event Network for Cash-Flow Estimation, a compact causal Transformer that treats each transaction as a token and predicts the amount and a full, nonparametric timing distribution of every cash flow's next payment. Inheriting transaction semantics from an external labeler and a frozen text encoder keeps CADENCE compact yet general across the long tail of small-business counterparties, while predicting a calibrated distribution rather than an opaque embedding makes its outputs interpretable enough to feed existing underwriting models and power credit decisions. Ablations confirm the role of each design choice, with counterparty semantics driving recall on short histories, calendar inputs driving timing accuracy, and no-event supervision driving precision. Against the production FFT baseline, CADENCE improves one-day timing accuracy by 93.3% and next-event F1 by 6.7%, while producing calibrated distributions that serve directly as a confidence gate for downstream decisions. In an end-to-end credit evaluation on production applications, replacing FFT recurrence features with CADENCE features raises KS by 4.8%, raises the approval rate at a fixed loss rate by 18.2%, and lowers the loss rate at a fixed approval rate by 13.1%.

papers.title: Nice Partitions of Signed-Graphic Arrangements Are Inductive Factorizations
