papers.abstract: Nice partitions of hyperplane arrangements give tensor factorizations of Orlik-Solomon algebras as graded vector spaces. In general, a hyperplane arrangement admitting a nice partition need not be free. In this paper, we consider signed-graphic arrangements, the subarrangements of type-$B$ Weyl arrangements, over fields of characteristic different from $2$. We prove that every nice partition of a signed-graphic arrangement is an inductive factorization and hence that the arrangement is free, with nonzero exponents given by the part sizes. In particular, Terao's conjecture holds for the intersection lattices of signed-graphic arrangements admitting a nice partition.

papers.title: Transverse rational curves and the homogeneity of contact Fano manifolds
papers.abstract: We prove that every smooth complex projective contact Fano manifold is homogeneous under its connected contact automorphism group. The argument extends and simplifies the incidence method of our earlier proof of the LeBrun--Salamon conjecture. After the classical reductions, balanced transverse rational maps through every point yield tangent sections extending across the nodal boundary. These establish irreducibility and nonlinearity of the general variety of minimal rational tangents associated with contact lines, enabling Hwang's descent theorem to produce global vector fields generating the tangent bundle. Consequences include very ampleness of the contact line bundle, embeddedness of every balanced rational map, K\"ahler--Einstein existence, K-polystability, and the LeBrun--Salamon conjecture.

papers.title: CopyLoop: Fast Looped Transformer Decoding via Context Copying and Shallow Screening
papers.abstract: Looped Transformers increase computational capacity through the repeated application of shared blocks, but their recurrent depth makes conventional full-depth decoding expensive. While existing speculative pipelines accelerate generation by processing consecutive token positions at varying depths, they are typically limited by sequential decoding overheads. We introduce CopyLoop, a training-free decoding algorithm that combines low-cost context-copy proposals with shallow screening and continuous recurrent scheduling. Rather than step-by-step generation, CopyLoop proposes multi-token suffixes from repeated context. It then evaluates them early at a shallow recurrent depth to efficiently filter out incorrect branches, processing newer blocks concurrently while earlier blocks are still progressing toward full-depth verification. We evaluate CopyLoop across six model checkpoints from the Ouro, Raven, and Huginn families, covering code generation and multi-step mathematical reasoning. CopyLoop achieves decoding speedups of 2.98x--10.70x over full-depth autoregressive decoding on Base models and 2.74x--3.52x on Thinking models, consistently outperforming or closely matching all competing baselines across evaluation tasks. Furthermore, ablation studies confirm a strong synergy between shallow screening and continuous scheduling, while our analyses show that CopyLoop requires only lightweight model calibration and yields greater speedups on longer generations with reusable contexts.

authors.name: Stephen Chung
authors.institution: The University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center

papers.title: Cassette-Editor: A Video Editing Agent That Edits the Way You Do
papers.abstract: Language agents increasingly work by calling tools on a persistent artifact, such as a code repository, and the result of each call shapes their next step. Video editing is a demanding case of this pattern: what a frame shows depends on how every clip is trimmed, retimed, cropped, and nested, so knowledge about the footage holds only for particular uses of it, and an invalid edit can leave the timeline structurally broken. Existing video editing agents keep their edits valid with critic agents, reviewers, or restricted output formats. We present Cassette-Editor, a video editing agent with a deliberately simple interface: one tool reads the project and one tool writes to it. Every write passes through the same executor, rules, and commit service as the user's manual edits, and either commits atomically or is rejected with located diagnostics and repair options, while the model keeps the creative choices and decides how to recover. Reads relate stored analysis of the footage to each use of it on the timeline. In a controlled experiment, a real model is shown 277 of its own committed edits after damaging them. It corrected nearly every call with full or minimal feedback, but locating each problem cut the input tokens a correction needed to less than half, and its corrections dropped other values the model had written in one case rather than seven.

papers.title: Telling Is Not Seeing: Textual Personas Rarely Make Vision-Language Models Answer Like the People They Describe
papers.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly prompted with personas, such as "You have low vision", to stand in for people in user studies. We ask whether a persona makes a model see like the person it describes. We compare persona answers with measured people with low vision, color blindness or hearing loss, and with simple rules that use only the facts the persona states. The persona never beats these rules, and it erases the real differences between groups and individuals. Describing blur leaves recognition unchanged in all 14 models we test, while blurring the photo lowers it as it does for people. Inside open models, the description changes neither the image information nor the answer probabilities. Yet the models know the effects they fail to show: they can estimate how blur and illusions affect people. Telling is not seeing: a persona makes a model say what it knows about people, not see what they see.

authors.name: Jiawei Chen
authors.institution: Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: The Yang-Mills flow in vector bundles over higher dimensional Riemannian manifolds
papers.abstract: We develop a parabolic formulation of the Uhlenbeck gauge fixing theorem and use it to prove the maximal existence of the Yang-Mills flow in vector bundles over compact $n$-dimensional Riemannian manifolds for $n \geq 4$. We apply Moser's iteration technique \cite{Mo1} to give a new proof of the bound of the curvature. Using an idea of Hamilton on the Ricci flow \cite{Ha}, we also provide a new proof on uniform estimates of higher order derivatives. Furthermore, we investigate the blow-up of the Yang-Mills flow at the maximal existence time and improve an asymptotical result of Hong-Tian \cite{HT1}.

papers.title: Uniqueness of the weak solutions of the Yang-Mills flow in four dimensions
papers.abstract: We improve a parabolic version of Uhlenbeck's gauge fixing theorem for the Yang-Mills flow. This allows us to prove new existence of weak solutions of the Yang-Mills flow having with better properties than Struwe's weak solution on four manifolds in \cite {St2}. Finally, we apply the new parabolic version of Uhlenbeck's gauge fixing theorem to solve the Struwe problem in \cite {St2} and prove uniqueness of weak solutions to the Yang-Mills flow on compact four-manifolds with initial value $A_0 \in W^{1, 2}(M)$.

papers.title: Contour-Based Fast Fractional Integration in a Jacobi Fractional Polynomial Basis
papers.abstract: We develop a contour-based method for applying Riemann--Liouville fractional integrals in a Jacobi fractional polynomial basis with an endpoint weight. A Gamma-ratio representation reduces the action to contour quadrature and banded ultraspherical solves. For a fixed number of contour nodes, the cost and storage are linear in the polynomial dimension. For fractional equations, we construct selected diagonals of a short rational approximation directly and use their banded factorizations as reusable right preconditioners for Krylov iterations. Numerical experiments show accurate integral actions and substantially reduced solution costs across Abel, multi-order, BBO, deferred-correction, eigenvalue, and boundary-value problems.

papers.title: Splitting Compositions of Monotone Operators
papers.abstract:
Coupled convex optimisation equilibria, bilinear saddle and potential systems, and nonlinear electronic device laws lead naturally to inclusions of the form $0\in Hx+A(Bx)-b$, where $A$ and $B$ are maximal monotone but their composition need not be monotone. We introduce a new class of splitting algorithms that solve such inclusions. Introducing the intermediate graph variable $y\in Bx$ exposes a directed two-row system. A one-parameter family of kernels produces a lower-triangular warped-resolvent iteration evaluated with one application of $H$ and the ordinary resolvents $J_{\alpha A}$ and $J_{\beta B}$. Appropriate specializations of the problem data and algorithmic parameters recover forward--backward, inertial, primal--dual, and Douglas--Rachford constructions, while setting $H=b=0$ generates three novel algorithms for the pure composition $0\in A(Bx)$.
  Convergence of the coupled method is certified by an explicit nonnegative two-block gain matrix. Its Schur condition yields contraction in particular weighted norms, global linear convergence, and residual error estimates. For the general problem class, our convergence condition is shown to be sharp for an explicitly constructed linear family. When the problem is specialized to a pure composition, we prove convergence under the weaker assumption that only one operator is strongly monotone. This weaker regime is illustrated on a nonlinear circuit problem. We further illustrate our methods by solving inference problems for cascaded equilibrium neural networks.

papers.title: Finite-Sample Optimal Conformal Prediction Sets under Covariate Shift
papers.abstract:
We study conformal prediction under covariate shift with a known covariate density ratio, seeking prediction sets with minimum expected length under the target distribution. For every calibration sample size, we prove that the rule combining the inverse conditional-density score with randomized weighted conformal calibration minimizes this expected length among all rules valid over the full weighted-exchangeability class.
  We approximate the oracle using quantile and kernel histograms, including forest-weighted estimators, and select estimators and tuning parameters by resampling to estimate calibrated target length. On a bounded response domain, we bound excess length linearly in $L^1$ density error at fixed calibration size, without requiring a uniform positive lower bound on the true density. We also bound selection-pool and resampling errors. Under explicit growth conditions, the selected procedure approaches the same oracle while the calibration size remains fixed.
  Experiments on 36 known-density configurations and four public regression datasets compare coverage, prediction-set length, and runtime with existing methods.
  In targeted low-coverage and strong-shift comparisons, inverse-density selection yields shorter mean sets in most cases and lower mean runtime than the evaluated weighted baselines, with some differences in achieved coverage.

authors.name: Zhongyang Li
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

papers.title: PALATE: Pretrained Autoregressive LATent Embeddings
papers.abstract: Local-commerce and food-delivery marketplaces run large ads businesses: across hundreds of thousands of stores, merchants pay to be surfaced on browse and search surfaces, and a ranker decides which ads each consumer sees. Ranking well demands strong per-consumer personalization, yet a consumer's raw interaction history is sparse and high-cardinality. Our production ranker had personalized only through hand-engineered signals: aggregate engagement counts, categorical embeddings, and order-agnostic pooled history, with no learned per-consumer sequence representation. We learn one by training a GPT-style generative model of the consumer's engagement sequence to predict their next few engagements, and read its last-token hidden state as the consumer embedding. That single frozen vector becomes one shared personalization input for every ad surface: a daily job refreshes it, and each ranker consumes it as an ordinary dense feature. Offline it is the largest single-feature gain in our ranking-AUC ladder, a relative Eval-AUC gain of +0.59% on a browse-driven feed and +0.57% on a query-driven search surface. Online, it shipped as one component of bundled ranker retrains on both surfaces: Discovery (revenue +0.79%, conversion rate +1.17%) and Search (revenue +0.94%, conversion rate +1.50%). Three design choices adapt the generative objective to a repurchase-heavy marketplace, and are the core of our contribution: an exploration-weighted loss that up-weights businesses new to the consumer over ones already engaged; a two-stage curriculum: a click pretrain that keeps the representation broad and exploratory, then a conversion fine-tune that sharpens purchase intent; and a designed negative set that pairs a fixed popular-business pool and businesses shown but not ordered with random and in-batch negatives.

authors.name: Bin Li
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Pre-modular fusion categories of global dimension $2p$
papers.abstract:
Let $p>5$ be a prime. In this paper, we show that a pre-modular fusion category of
  global dimension $2p$ is either pointed or tensor equivalent to $\text{Rep}(D_{2p})$.

authors.name: Zhiqiang Yu
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

papers.title: CoraLive: Ultra-Low-Power Underwater Vision for Long-term Coral Reef Monitoring
papers.abstract: Effective coral reef protection and restoration demands continuous, long-term underwater monitoring. However, current solutions largely rely on fragmented, manual labor and costly infrastructure, or are severely limited by constrained battery lifespans. In this paper, we present CoraLive, an ultra-low-power underwater camera system for long-term, continuous coral reef monitoring. CoraLive presents a decoupled underwater-shore co-design that minimizes on-board computation and storage, offloading heavy reconstruction and segmentation tasks to offline shore-side processing. To achieve this, CoraLive introduces a dual-rate sensing scheme combining frequent low-resolution frames with sparse high-fidelity samples and a content-adaptive update mechanism that extracts and stores only compact, task-specific data, eliminating the need to save raw video frames. We implement CoraLive on a custom STM32U575-based dual-camera prototype with device-level computation and storage optimization. Compared with raw recording, CoraLive reduces daily storage by $4.51\times$ and average power by $7.78\times$, extending battery lifetime from 20.4 to 159.5~days while retaining high-accuracy segmentation and reconstruction. Further validated in a real-world underwater deployment, we envision CoraLive as a pioneering step for ubiquitous long-term coral reef underwater monitoring.

authors.name: Chenshu Wu
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Strongly Adaptive Online Learning Achieves Uniform Discounted Regret
papers.abstract: Discounted regret measures the performance of an online learner by assigning exponentially decaying weights to past losses, reflecting the greater importance of recent losses in non-stationary online learning. While previous work obtains uniform discounted regret bounds over a continuous range of discount factors using a specialized meta-algorithm, its results are limited to convex functions. In this paper, we demonstrate that strongly adaptive regret bounds can directly imply uniform discounted regret guarantees for convex, strongly convex, and exp-concave loss functions. Our key observation is that discounted regret against a fixed comparator admits an exact decomposition into a convex combination of interval regrets. For convex functions, this reduction yields an $O(\sqrt{\log T/(1-\lambda)})$ discounted regret bound for all discount factors $\lambda\in(0,1)$, matching the previous rate over a broader range of discount factors. For strongly convex and exp-concave functions, we provide regret bounds of $O\left(\log T\left(1+\log\frac{1}{1-\lambda}\right)\right)$.

authors.name: Lijun Zhang
authors.institution: Yunnan University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

papers.title: Dobb: Shard-Local Preconditioning in Block-Diagonal Eigenbases
papers.abstract: Training language models whose parameters and optimizer state exceed a single node's memory requires sharding these tensors across devices. Under tensor parallelism (TP) or fully sharded data parallelism (FSDP), matrix-aware optimizers such as Muon introduce communication to perform global matrix operations across shards. We propose Dobb (Distributed Optimizer with Block-diagonal Eigenbases), a matrix-aware optimizer designed to compute updates locally within parameter shards. Dobb approximates the input-activation second moment with diagonal blocks and tracks a complete basis within each block. It projects momentum into these bases, applies sign normalization to the coefficients, and reconstructs the update. When each block lies within one shard under TP or FSDP, Dobb applies its matrix update locally, requiring no communication beyond data-parallel synchronization of the activation second moments. We benchmark Dobb against Dion, a distributed matrix-aware optimizer designed to retain the benefits of orthonormalized updates while reducing communication. On GPT-2 XL (1.56B parameters), Dobb with 16 blocks reaches a validation loss of 2.476, compared with 2.511 for Dion at rank fraction 1/16. Under FSDP on 32 H100 GPUs, Dobb reduces the amortized optimizer-call time from 124.1 ms for Dion to 9.2 ms.

papers.title: A Zoo of Fermionic Relative R\'enyi Negativities in the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev Models
papers.abstract: Quantum entanglement is a fundamental resource that gives rise to correlations with no classical counterpart in strongly correlated fermionic systems. However, its characterization in mixed quantum states remains challenging. Established entanglement diagnostics, such as logarithmic negativity, are computationally demanding in interacting systems, and their evaluation by exact diagonalization is restricted to small system sizes. Meanwhile, conventional R\'enyi proxies, including twisted and untwisted R\'enyi negativities, can be positive even for separable states. In this work, we introduce a family of \textit{relative R\'enyi negativities} that serve as entanglement witnesses. By relating fermionic partial time reversal to the size superoperator, we establish a path-integral representation for these R\'enyi negativities, enabling their evaluation in thermal states of the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model and its generalizations via a large-$N$ expansion. Applying this method, we investigate entanglement in both the original SYK model and the Maldacena-Qi coupled SYK model. We identify a special class of relative R\'enyi negativities which serve as plausible proxies for logarithmic negativity and uncover first-order entanglement transitions that are invisible to simple observables. These results highlight the utility of relative R\'enyi negativities as probes of mixed-state entanglement in strongly correlated fermionic systems and suggest the existence of a new class of transitions where these negativities serve as free energies.

papers.title: Nevanlinna Theory on Berkovich Curves
papers.abstract: We develop a value distribution theory for finite analytic morphisms between proper connected quasi-smooth Berkovich curves over a complete algebraically closed non-Archimedean field. The central tool is a multi-tail Dirichlet Green function on finite truncations of a generalized skeleton, which makes non-Archimedean potential theory on skeleta compatible with global Nevanlinna asymptotics. Using it, we prove the first main theorem as an exact identity relating the characteristic, counting, and proximity functions. For logarithmic targets we establish a second main theorem in both ramified and level-one truncated forms. The defect relation is also given. The theory provides a Berkovich-analytic framework for non-Archimedean value distribution, bridging classical Nevanlinna theory and its $p$-adic counterpart.

papers.title: Bloch's conjecture for (anti-)symplectic automorphisms of K3 surfaces
papers.abstract:
We prove Bloch's conjecture for (anti-)symplectic automorphisms of smooth projective complex K3 surfaces of Picard number two. Together with the recent result for abelian surfaces and the known K3 cases, this settles the remaining case of Bloch's conjecture for (anti-)symplectic automorphisms of smooth projective complex surfaces with trivial canonical bundle.
  More generally, we prove Bloch's conjecture for (anti-)symplectic derived autoequivalences of projective K3 surfaces whose Picard number is at least three, or is two with anisotropic N\'eron--Severi lattice. The key new result is the congruence property of the subgroup generated by reflective involutions in $O(U\oplus N)$ for anisotropic even lattices $N$ of signature $(1,1)$. Combined with the local generation theorem and Chow-theoretic criterion of Li--Yu--Zhang, this gives the required reflective decompositions and their consequences for zero-cycles.

papers.title: Partially temporal coherent spatiotemporal Laguerre-Gaussian and its propagation dynamics
papers.abstract: Optical spatiotemporal vortices carrying transverse photonic orbital angular momentum have become an intense research topic in the recent study of structured light fields. Despite being mainly studied within the framework of fully coherent optical pulses, the complex topologies of the light field are also investigated with partially coherent light sources, offering an alternative pathway in applications. In this work, we theoretically and experimentally investigate partially temporally coherent spatiotemporal Laguerre-Gaussian (STLG) field with independently controllable radial and azimuthal indices. The spatiotemporal topological information, carried by the structured amplified spontaneous emission source, are well preserved in the presence of inherent instantaneous random temporal phase fluctuations. Under combined spatiotemporal astigmatism and group velocity dispersion, the partially temporally coherent STLG field can be converted into spatiotemporal Hermite-Gaussian (STHG) field. Both structures maintain their spatiotemporal characteristics after propagating through scattering media. Partially temporally coherent structured light fields may offer new insights into photonic topology and complex wave dynamics, with potential applications in high-fidelity optical communications and high-dimensional information processing in highly scattering environments.

authors.name: Youngbin Park
authors.institution: Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology

authors.name: Nianjia Zhang
authors.institution: University of Shanghai for Science and Technology

papers.title: Bregman projections and partition design for accelerating finite Markov chains
papers.abstract: We study Gibbs averaging of finite Markov chains with a prescribed stationary distribution $\pi$. Given a transition matrix $P$ and the Gibbs kernel $G$ induced by a state-space partition, we prove that $GPG$ is an information projection for every admissible Bregman generator $\phi$, with divergences defined using transition probabilities relative to $\pi$. A Pythagorean identity characterizes this projection and recovers the relative entropy and weighted Frobenius cases. A dual characterization identifies $GPG$ as a kernel closest to stationarity among those with the same projection chain as $P$; for relative entropy, it maximizes the entropy rate. The identities also give monotonicity under partition coarsening. For every reversible ergodic baseline $P$, Gibbs averaging cannot increase the squared weighted Frobenius distance to stationarity at any positive integer time, and the inequality is strict unless $P=GPG$. The corresponding mixing time therefore cannot increase. To choose the partition, we identify the divergence of $G$ from stationarity as the exact worst-case divergence of $GPG$ over all $\pi$-stationary baselines $P$. This objective depends only on the block masses. We give an exact algorithm for concave block costs, including those arising from relative entropy and power generators $\phi(u)=u^p$ with $1<p<2$, and a greedy approximation algorithm with a provable guarantee for $p>2$. For power generators $\phi(u)=u^p$ with $p>1$, the objective is proportional to Tsallis entropy of order $2-p$: its minimization favors imbalanced block masses when $1<p<2$ and balanced block masses when $p>2$, while all $k$-block partitions have the same objective value when $p=2$. A numerical experiment compares the resulting projected chains with a local Metropolis sampler on a multi-modal $\pi$.

authors.name: Youjia Wang
authors.institution: Shandong Vocational College of Science and Technology

papers.title: Scalable Bayesian Quadrature via Operator-Adapted Features
papers.abstract: Kernel methods face two recurrent bottlenecks: the cubic cost of inverting an $n\times n$ kernel matrix, as in kernel ridge regression, and the evaluation of kernel integrals, as required in kernel quadrature. Existing low-rank kernel and Gaussian process approximations primarily address the former bottleneck, but do not control the downstream quadrature error when both the kernel matrix and kernel mean are approximated, particularly when the integrand lies outside the kernel reproducing kernel Hilbert space. We address both challenges through an operator-adapted finite-feature approximation. Specifically, we construct a finite-dimensional working kernel from the eigenvalues and eigenfunctions of a second-order differential operator. We establish convergence guarantees for the resulting finite-feature estimators in kernel quadrature, with extension to other related kernel methods. Our results show that, with $m \lesssim n$ basis functions, the truncated estimator attains the corresponding benchmark statistical rates. The theory covers fixed/random designs, noisy/noiseless observations, oversmoothing/undersmoothing regimes, and Mat\'ern/Gaussian-type weights. We provide explicit error bounds that quantify the roles of the spectral cutoff, regularization parameter, lengthscale, sampling geometry, and operator boundary condition. We verify the convergence results in numerical experiments.

papers.title: The cross quadratic bisectional curvature of K\"{a}hler $C$-spaces of classical type
papers.abstract: In this paper, we show that any K\"{a}hler $C$-space of classical type has nonnegative cross quadratic bisectional curvature and positive dual cross quadratic bisectional curvature. As a consequence, such manifolds are Fano. This confirms a substantial part of a conjecture of Ni-Zheng (Conjecture 1.5 in \cite{NZ}).

papers.title: Dense Minors from the Crux
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a graph with average degree $d>0$ and $C_\alpha(G)$ be the minimum order of a subgraph whose average degree is at least $\alpha d$ for any fixed $0<\alpha<1$. Then $G$ has a minor of average degree $\Omega(\sqrt{d\,C_\alpha(G)})$, which is asymptotically tight up to a constant factor. This reveals a unified mechanism underlying previous results on dense minors in locally sparse graphs.

papers.title: Parity-Resolved Many-Body Kinetics of a Topological Qubit under Nonequilibrium Phonon Pulses
papers.abstract: Phonon bursts from ionizing radiation cause correlated errors in superconducting quantum processors. We study prescribed nonequilibrium phonon pulses in a Majorana qubit formed by two $2\,\mu\mathrm{m}$ proximitized nanowires. Combining the lattice Lutchyn--Oreg model, microscopic electron--phonon coupling, and parity-resolved many-body dynamics, we track excitation, relaxation, and logical coherence. Without quasiparticle escape, recombination restores the initial Majorana occupations in about 130 ns, while phonons exchanged during excitation and recovery can retain logical-state information, leaving permanent coherence loss. For mirror-symmetric wires, the fractional coherence loss per wire is 0.75--1.0 times the excitation probability averaged over the two logical states, even at zero Majorana splitting; breaking mirror symmetry can suppress dephasing at small splitting. Factorized Boltzmann kinetics neglects quasiparticle correlations and overestimates residual parity flips. At equal deposited energy density, phonon spectra yield different excitation probabilities and coherence losses. Comparisons with Kitaev chains matched to the wire's gap and Majorana decay length reveal that low electron density suppresses excitation by energetic phonons, whereas hard-wall boundaries in a high-density control increase excitation efficiency by a factor of $5\times10^4$ relative to the wire for pulses centered at 1 meV. Magnetic-field and chemical-potential tuning yield different phonon sensitivities at the same bulk gap through changes in spin and electron--hole structure. Including hybrid states' semiconductor weights reduces near-threshold excitation rates fourfold when the tunnel coupling equals the parent superconducting gap. Our framework connects phonon spectra to leakage, poisoning, and coherence loss to guide Majorana-device design.

papers.title: Higher-order jet and its application to the Novikov conjecture
papers.abstract:
In this paper, we apply higher-order tangent bundles and higher-order derivative maps to study countable subgroups of the deffeomorphism group ${\rm Diff}(M)$ of a closed smooth manifold $M$. Using this framework, we introduce the concept of higher order $\mu$-discreteness for subgroup $\Gamma < {\rm Diff}(M)$.
  As applications, we show that both the strong Novikov conjecture and the coarse Baum--Connes conjecture hold for countable groups with higher order $\mu$-discreteness.

authors.name: Jintao Deng
authors.institution: Shanghai University of Finance and Economics

papers.title: Maximal regular subsemigroups containing the group of units of transformation semigroups that preserve a uniform equivalence relation with two classes
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a nonempty set and $E$ an equivalence relation on $X$. The semigroup $T_E(X)$ consists of all transformations on $X$ that preserve $E$. Although the collection of all regular elements of $T_E(X)$ is not, in general, a subsemigroup, we investigate maximal regular subsemigroups of $T_E(X)$ containing the group of units $G_E(X)$. We construct two such maximal regular subsemigroups, denoted by $\mathcal{M}_1$ and $\mathcal{M}_2$, and show that their maximality holds in full generality for an arbitrary set $X$ and an arbitrary equivalence relation $E$ that is neither the identity relation nor the universal relation on $X$ (whether finite or infinite, uniform or non-uniform). Furthermore, when $X$ is finite and $E$ is a uniform equivalence relation with exactly two classes of cardinality at least $2$, we provide a complete classification by proving that they are the only maximal regular subsemigroups containing $G_E(X)$.

papers.title: Soil Moisture Estimation in Precision Agriculture: A Knowledge Distillation Approach
papers.abstract: Accurate soil moisture estimation is critical for precision agriculture, influencing irrigation, fertilization, and harvesting strategies. Traditional methods primarily rely on meteorological and soil property data, while recent approaches incorporate visual modalities such as aerial and geospatial imagery. However, these high-resolution images are expensive and computationally demanding to analyze. In this work, we propose Soil Moisture Distillation (SMD), a Knowledge Distillation (KD)-based multimodal learning framework that leverages unimodal teachers to enhance multimodal soil moisture estimation. SMD surpasses not only traditional multimodal fusion techniques, including MIS-ME, but also outperforms unimodal models, demonstrating the benefits of guided unimodal knowledge transfer. Additionally, we conduct a comparative analysis of soil patches and crop images, showing that crop images provide superior visual cues, leading to improved prediction accuracy. SMD achieves a 2% improvement in MAPE for soil patches and 1.2% for crops over state-of-the-art baselines, highlighting the effectiveness of leveraging both meteorological and visual data through knowledge distillation for enhanced soil moisture forecasting.

papers.title: Finite-size ignition laws near a vanishing branching deficit on near-regular simple graphs
papers.abstract: We study heterogeneous bootstrap percolation on uniform simple graphs with prescribed degrees of mean $d\to\infty$ and deviations at most $C\sqrt d$. Thresholds are independently one with probability $(1-c/d)/d$ and two otherwise; seeds form an independent uniform set of prescribed size $a$. Let $T_a$ be the terminal number of active vertices and $b$ be one minus the mean number of threshold-one descendants of a reached vertex. Let $K\sim d^2$ be the quadratic response coefficient. If $b>0$ and $nb^3/K\to\infty$, we prove, uniformly over seed counts $a$, $ \mathbb{P}(T_a\ge n/2)=\Phi(\frac{a-n\alpha_{\mathrm{det}}}{w})+o(1)$ with $w=\sqrt{nb/K}$, where $\alpha_{\mathrm{det}}$ is the exact empirical response-barrier center and $\Phi$ is the standard normal distribution function. Put $a_0=(n/K)^{1/3}$. If $d^4/n\to0$, $a/a_0\to x>0$ and $\lambda=ba_0\to\ell\in\mathbb{R}$, then $\mathbb{P}(T_a\ge n/2)\to p(x,\ell)$, the one-sided Brownian parabolic survival probability. A sequential absolute-error law joins these regimes. A graphical counterexample shows that replacing the exact center by its leading term can cause limiting probability error $1/2$. The proof balances adaptive early-exploration transfer against late concentration at a tunable physical horizon, despite exponentially rare simplicity. We also prove quantitative and mesoscopic-seed refinements in explicitly narrower regimes. The only external graph-enumeration input is a stated reduction of McKay--Wormald's estimate; the probabilistic estimates for the cascade argument are proved in the text and appendices.

papers.title: CASE: Concept-Aware Segmentation from Positive and Negative Visual Exemplars
papers.abstract: Few-shot semantic segmentation typically identifies target objects based on positive support examples of a single semantic class. In practice, however, positive cues alone are often underspecified: for instance, "red cars" may be confused with cars of all colors, "vehicles" may include cars that should be excluded, and "material-defined objects" may span multiple categories. Fulfilling precise requests requires positive exemplars to provide inclusion evidence and negative exemplars to act as intent-defining constraints for exclusion and disambiguation. We formulate this setting as Specified Visual Prompt Segmentation (SVPS), where the target concept is specified by both positive and negative visual prompts. In this work, visual exemplars refer to support-image regions specified by bounding-box prompts. To study SVPS, we introduce CASE (Concept-Aware Segmentation from Positive and Negative Visual Exemplars), a benchmark built on COCO and PACO. CASE encompasses six category- and attribute-level task families: exclusion, isolation, union, attribute exclusion, attribute isolation, and attribute union. We evaluate SAM 3 under this setting and find that, despite its powerful positive-only few-shot segmentation capability, frozen SAM 3 does not consistently treat negative visual prompts as exclusion evidence. To address this, we present Concept Prompt Adaptation (CPA), a conservative LoRA-based adaptation baseline that improves positive-negative prompt interpretation on CASE while remaining competitive under positive-only few-shot segmentation. Code is available at https://github.com/WongKinYiu/FSS-CASE.

papers.title: Inflection sets of permutations
papers.abstract: In 2020, Brualdi and Dahl introduced the discrete derivative $\sigma'(i)=\sigma(i+1)-\sigma(i)$ of a permutation $\sigma\in\Sym_n$. In this paper, we focus on the second derivative of a permutation, $\sigma''(i)=\sigma(i+1)+\sigma(i-1)-2\sigma(i)$, and the inflections it determines. We show that for even $n$, the only distinct permutations with the same second derivative are the identity and its reverse, while for odd $n$, the second derivative is not injective even after excluding them. We then study which sets of pairs of integers $(i,j)$ are the inflection set of some permutation and whether a given set is witnessed in $\Sym_n$ for infinitely many $n$. We show that exactly $14$ permutations of $[n]$ have no inflections when $n\ge5$. For a single inflection $\{(k,m)\}$, we determine all $n$ for which it is witnessed in $\Sym_n$: we prove it is always witnessed, and it is witnessed for only finitely many $n$ if and only if $m\ge 2k+1$. In that case, all such $n$ satisfy $2m-2k+1\le n\le 2m-k+2$ (apart from $k=2$, $n=m+1$), and, perhaps surprisingly, this range has gaps once $k\ge 10$, the smallest occurring at $(k,m,n)=(10,21,30)$. Finally, we characterize maximally inflected permutations, whose second derivative alternates in sign, and show that their number $|\mathcal M_n|$ satisfies $2E_n\le|\mathcal M_n|\le(2/3)^{\lfloor n/3\rfloor-1}\,n!$, where $E_n$ is the Euler zigzag number.

papers.title: Explicit matrix hitting points for noncommutative algebraic branching programs
papers.abstract:
We give a deterministic polynomial-resource black-box identity test for noncommutative algebraic branching programs (ABPs), using ordinary matrix evaluations of the output polynomial. Given an alphabet of size $m\ge1$ and an ABP vertex bound $S\ge1$, we construct one fixed tuple of integer matrices of order $R=(m+2)d(d+1)/2$, where $d=(m+2)S$, with entry bit length $O(d\log(d+1))$. Every nonzero polynomial computed by an ABP with at most $S$ vertices has a nonzero evaluation at this tuple. The construction accesses neither the hidden ABP nor its intermediate gates. A rectangular variant improves the order to $O(m^{3/2}S^2)$. Matrix order, description length, and all returned entries are counted; the total resources are polynomial. The result holds in characteristic zero and in characteristic $p>\binom d2$.
  The main ingredient is a fixed polynomial frame spanning the joint cyclic module of every matrix tuple from every prescribed vector. A compensating block makes a tagged encoding nilpotent of index at most three, while preserving the original cyclic module. A differential exterior-vector argument then gives a single triangular recurrence with polynomially many outputs. Its shared left-linear circuit is converted into actual integer query matrices by coefficient duality. Two-sided pairing further gives deterministic nonadaptive reconstruction of an equivalent ABP from polynomially many output-only matrix queries. The same frame gives polynomial-cardinality explicit trace separators for simultaneous-conjugation orbit closures, and a fixed nilpotent substitution for bounded-dimensional recognizable series. The latter also tests rational formulas whose given syntax is defined at the scalar origin. We provide complete proofs, construction costs, and exact implementation checks.

authors.name: Zhipeng Lu
authors.institution: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

papers.title: The Borisov--Nuer conjecture and root decompositions in even unimodular Lorentzian lattices
papers.abstract: We prove that every vector of $\mathrm{II}_{8n+1,1}$, with $n\ge1$, is a sum of two roots if and only if $n=1$ or $2$. This settles the Borisov--Nuer conjecture and implies the existence of Ulrich line bundles for every very ample polarization on a complex unnodal Enriques surface. For vectors of negative norm, we express the number of root decompositions as a Fourier coefficient of a vector-valued theta series, reducing existence to positivity. The main analytic difficulty is to obtain estimates uniform over lattices of unbounded determinant. We address this by combining a reduction based on primitive sublattices of codimension one and least determinant with explicit bounds for theta norms and Fourier coefficients of cusp forms.

papers.title: Composition factors and finite representation type
papers.abstract: We prove that an Artin algebra has finite representation type if its indecomposable finitely generated modules are determined, up to isomorphism, by their composition factors. This gives an affirmative answer to the conjecture on composition factors and finite representation type recorded by Auslander, Reiten and Smalo.

papers.title: Sharp observation time for wave equations with an inverse-square boundary potential
papers.abstract:
We determine the sharp observation-time threshold for the autonomous, pure-potential wave equation with an inverse-square boundary singularity on the unit ball. For every fixed $\kappa<0$, full-boundary observability holds on $(-T,T)$ whenever $T>1$ and fails when $T<1$. This resolves, for this model, the optimal-time question raised by Enciso, Shao, and Vergara [J. Eur. Math. Soc. 23 (2021), 3459--3495] and extends their parameter range $-\frac12<\kappa<0$ to all $\kappa<0$, including the limit-point regime $\kappa\leq-\frac12$.
  Our approach is based on the Ingham--Beurling theory of nonharmonic Fourier series. Spherical harmonic decomposition reduces the problem to one-dimensional singular operators, for which we establish frequency separation, local counting estimates, and lower bounds for the boundary norming constants, uniformly in the angular parameter. A quantitative Ingham--Beurling inequality then yields the sharp-time observability estimate.
  As a by-product, this spectral approach provides an independent proof of boundary observability and an explicit functional characterization of its maximal $L^2$ observation domain. The latter is described by a weighted $\ell^2$ condition on the spectral coefficients and consists precisely of energy solutions whose distributional Neumann trace belongs to $L^2$. It contains the boundary-admissible energy solutions considered in Enciso--Shao--Vergara's original work.

authors.name: Longben Wei
authors.institution: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

papers.title: The Kodaira dimension and minimal models of $\mathcal{A}_6$
papers.abstract: We prove that the moduli space $\mathcal{A}_6$ of principally polarized abelian sixfolds has Kodaira dimension zero, determining the remaining case in the Kodaira classification of the spaces $\mathcal{A}_g$. More precisely, every nonzero scalar Siegel modular form of genus six, weight $k$ and positive boundary order $b$ satisfies $k\geq 7b$, with equality precisely for powers of the weight-fourteen harmonic theta series of Dittmann, Salvati Manni and Scheithauer. The canonical ring is therefore a polynomial ring on one generator of degree two. We also prove numerical dimension zero and construct the unique projective $\mathbb{Q}$-factorial terminal minimal model. Its Picard number is one and its canonical divisor has order two. The perfect cone compactification is a Mori dream space, and the birational automorphism group of $\mathcal{A}_6$ is trivial. The proof combines normal vanishing on the Prym locus, polar intersections on abelian boundary fibers, and an exact theta calculation. A discrepancy estimate recovers the modular open subset from the minimal model.

papers.title: Sizes of cross-intersecting families
papers.abstract:
The size of cross-intersecting families ${\cal F}_1, \dots, {\cal F}_d$ is usually measured by the sum or the product of the sizes $|{\cal F}_i|$. These two natural size functions have different extremal structures, and different techniques have been developed for them.
  We introduce the cross-degree of a size function and show that the potential extremal structures of maximum cross-intersecting families are the same for all size functions of finite cross-degree, including the sum and the product. Our main tool is a strengthened form of the generating family method of Ahlswede--Khachatrian, based on standard generating families and on local modifications of cross-intersecting families, which we call mutations. It treats two completely different types of extremal structures in a unified way and, unlike the original method, needs shifting in only one step.

authors.name: Ziqing Xiang
authors.institution: Southern University of Science and Technology

papers.title: The small Deborah number limit for the fluid-particle flows: incompressible case
papers.abstract: This work is devoted to the study of the hydrodynamic limit for the fluid-particle flows governed by the Vlasov-Fokker-Planck (VFP) equation coupled with the incompressible Navier-Stokes (INS) equation as the Deborah number approaches to zero. The limit is valid globally in time provided that the initial perturbation is small in a neighborhood of a steady state. The proof is based on a formal derivation of the limiting system via the Hilbert approach, followed by a rigorous justification via introducing a novel decomposition involving some macroscopic quantities and a refined energy estimate motivated by macro-micro decomposition. In contrast to the existing results for the same scaled model, the present work provides the first one on the hydrodynamic limits in a strong sense with an explicit convergence rate.

authors.name: Zhendong Fang
authors.institution: First Affiliated Hospital of Wenzhou Medical University

papers.title: Positive Toeplitz Operators Between Gaussian Mixed-Norm Fock Spaces
papers.abstract:
We study positive measure-symbol Toeplitz operators between Gaussian radial--angular mixed-norm Fock spaces throughout the full range of exponents, including infinity. We obtain a complete characterization of boundedness in terms of weighted local masses of the symbol measure, or equivalently in terms of its Gaussian Berezin profile. The criterion separates the transfer of angular integrability from that of radial summability and remains valid in the quasi-Banach and endpoint regimes.
  We further characterize compactness and obtain the corresponding essential-norm estimates through the asymptotic behavior of the same local-mass and Berezin profiles, and determine the mappings involving the large and little outer-endpoint spaces. We also prove an independent characterization of bounded positive Toeplitz sesquilinear forms. The proofs combine atomic recovery, localized Gaussian matrix estimates, and Rademacher extraction.

authors.name: Xiang Fang
authors.institution: Wuhan University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Hybrid CutFEM-IFEM model for embedded and immersed interfaces with triply-cut cells for the 2D Poisson problem
papers.abstract: We present a hybrid CutFEM--IFEM method for 2D Poisson problems with an immersed fluid--fluid interface and an embedded fluid--solid interface on a single unfitted mesh. The proposed method leverages the strengths of both unfitted finite element methods and immersed interface techniques to handle complex interface geometries and strong discontinuities efficiently. A composite equivalent polynomial representation of the Heaviside and Dirac delta functions is used to integrate on triply-cut cells. Moreover, the IFEM basis functions are enriched with the lift functions exactly representing solution and flux jumps. Numerical examples show optimal convergence for linear and quadratic elements, with accuracy comparable to that of a mesh fitted to both interfaces.

papers.title: $L$-Space Knots in $\mathfrak{sl}_{n}$-like Knot Floer Homology
papers.abstract: It has been of particular interest in recent years to relate categorifications of quantum knot invariants like the Jones polynomial to Floer-theoretic invariants like knot Floer homology using spectral sequences. In pursuit of Rasmussen's conjecture, Dowlin constructed a family of invariants with properties like those of Khovanov and Rozansky's $\mathfrak{sl}_n$-homology theories. In this paper, we explore these invariants for $L$-space knots and thin knots. In particular, for $n\geq 2$ the invariants of thin knots can be computed from a change of coefficients from the minus flavor of knot Floer homology, and the same holds for an $L$-space knot exactly when an explicit condition relating $n$ to its Alexander polynomial is satisfied.

papers.intro:
The relationship between Floer-theoretic knot invariants of Ozsváth and Szabó [12] and of Rasmussen [16] and quantum knot invariants of Khovanov [10] and of Khovanov and Rozansky [9, 8] has been an active topic in topology for the past twenty-five years. These invariants categorify many knot invariants. That is, the graded Euler characteristic of the knot Floer homology of a knot returns its Alexander polynomial, and the graded Euler characteristic of the Khovanov homology of a knot returns its Jones polynomial. The first relationship between them came from a spectral sequence from the Khovanov homology of a link to the Heegaard Floer homology of its double branched cover, constructed by Ozsváth and Szabó in [14]. Since then, a slew of spectral sequences of that form have been discovered, yielding a variety of rank inequalities between the associated homologies as well as indicating the possibility of more interesting relationships.

papers.title: From Artifacts to Coordination: Exploring How Shared Canvases Drive Collaboration during Group Ideation
papers.abstract: Recent years have seen a surge in tools that support collaborative ideation through shared canvases. While these canvases offer flexible workspaces, how collaborators leverage them to iteratively develop ideas by externalizing thoughts, organizing artifacts, and coordinating tasks remains underexplored. To address this gap, we conducted an exploratory study with seven triads planning a travel itinerary using an infinite-canvas technology probe. Drawing on participant interviews and video analysis of their canvas interactions, we observed that collaborators contributed in parallel and arranged artifacts freely without a predefined structure. This spatial organization allowed collaborators to coordinate implicitly, made less vocal participants' contributions visible, helped distinguish private exploratory regions from shared working areas, and supported the emergence of distinct roles through repeated patterns of contribution. We discuss design implications for canvas-based ideation tools, including surfacing unnoticed contributions, supporting emergent roles without formalizing assignments, and keeping spatial cues legible for AI integration in collaborative canvases.

papers.title: On stable twist 2-groups of quasi-Hopf algebras
papers.abstract:
For any finite-dimensional quasi-Hopf algebra $A$, we define the notion of a stable twist of $A$. We show that stable twists form a strict 2-group $\2ust(A)$, which is equivalent to $\OAut(\C{A})^{\rev}$. Given a group homomorphism $\rho: G \to \ost(A)$, we determine the obstruction in $H^3(G,Z_G(A))$ to lift $\rho$ to a $G$-action on $\C{A}$. We also establish a bijection between such liftings and cocentral cleft extensions of $\k[G]$ by $A$.
  The main application of $\2ust(A)$ is the computation of $\OAut(\C{A})$, together with an explicit description of the corresponding tensor autoequivalences. We apply this framework to pointed Hopf algebras $A$ that arise as central extensions of Taft algebras by cyclic groups, and we explicitly determine all of their tensor autoequivalences. The equivariantizations of $\C{A}$ by $\ost(A)$ produce a new family of Hopf algebras $\N(n,\xi)$ of dimension $2nm$, where $\xi$ is a scalar of order $m\mid n$ such that neither $\N(n,\xi)$ nor its dual has the Chevalley property.
  In dimension 24, we prove that $\N(6,-1)$ and its dual are precisely the Hopf algebras $H$ for which neither $H$ nor $H^*$ has the Chevalley property. This completes the classification of nonsemisimple Hopf algebras of dimension 24.

papers.title: Skein reduction and stabilization for the odd Khovanov spectra of $T(2,m)\sqcup T(2,n)$
papers.abstract: For split links the even Khovanov spectrum is a smash product of the spectra of the pieces; the odd one is not. For $T(2,m)\sqcup T(2,n)$ we show that the odd spectrum is, in each quantum grading, a wedge of spheres and copies of a suspension of $\mathbb{CP}^{2}$. Using the skein cofiber sequence at the level of spectra, we prove that for fixed $q-m-n$ the number of these copies is determined by finitely many small links and stabilizes for large $m$ and $n$. The $\mathbb{CP}^{2}$ summand of $T(2,3)\sqcup T(2,3)$, due to Sch\"utz and Rajapakse, persists in quantum grading $m+n+8$ for all $m,n\ge3$. We conjecture that the number of copies of $\mathbb{CP}^{2}$ equals the number of copies of $\mathbb{RP}^{2}\wedge\mathbb{RP}^{2}$ in the even spectrum.

papers.title: Local-to-Global Theorems Based on Cones with Applications to Graph Coloring
papers.abstract:
Local-to-Global theorems are a cornerstone of many of recent developments in theoretical computer science from coding theory and PCPs all the way to analyzing mixing time of Markov chains. Building on trickledown theorems on simplicial complexes, several techniques have been established to obtain tighter local-to-global theorems to analyze the spectral gap of the Glauber dynamics, namely matrix trickledown, ${\mathcal C}$-Lorentzian polynomials and more recently Bochner type inequalities.
  In this paper, we adopt non-local local-to-global/Bochner type inequalities on "cones", corresponding to the local neighborhood of a given vertex, to show that the Glauber dynamics mixes in polynomial time to sample proper colorings of maximum degree $\Delta$ graphs as long as $q\geq 1.7408\Delta$.

papers.title: Hypersurface and Foliation Isoparametric Transfer for Generalized $(\alpha,\beta)$-Metrics
papers.abstract: Let $F=\alpha\Phi(q,s)$ be a regular generalized $(\alpha,\beta)$-metric, where $q=\|\beta\|_\alpha^2$ and $s=\beta/\alpha$, endowed with the Busemann--Hausdorff or Holmes--Thompson volume. We derive explicit comparison formulas for the induced hypersurface volume and the associated volume mean curvature and use them to study two transfer problems suggested by the Randers case. The first asks whether the same hypersurface is isoparametric for $\alpha$ and $F$; the second asks whether the same regular foliation is isoparametric for both metrics. Exact local and global criteria are obtained. Their Randers specializations recover the corresponding hypersurface transfer and the condition $df(W)=\varphi(f)$. We also prove an all-normal induced-volume rigidity theorem and construct a complete non-Randers example realizing both transfer mechanisms.

papers.title: Wreath products of distributive quasi relation algebra frames and their application to representability
papers.abstract: We adapt a construction by Comer (1983) for polygroups to define the wreath product of the dual frames of two distributive quasi relation algebras satisfying certain conditions and show that it is itself a frame. Frames play a role analogous to that of atom structures for relation algebras. After introducing the notion of a frame network, we establish a correspondence between frame networks satisfying certain conditions and representability of finite distributive quasi relation algebras. Next we describe a frame network for the wreath product of two finite representable distributive quasi relation algebras that satisfies the aforementioned conditions, as well as additional conditions, and use this to conclude that the complex algebra of the wreath product is a representable distributive quasi relation algebra. Thus, our construction provides a method for obtaining representable DqRAs from certain finite DqRAs that are already known to be representable.

papers.title: Extremely Sparse-View Computed Tomography from 2D Projections via Pose-Aware Diffusion Priors
papers.abstract: Extremely sparse-view computed tomography (xSV-CT) is critical when scanning time, motion, or radiation tolerance limits each scan to only a few projections. In many such scenarios, the same acquisition limits also constrain dataset construction, making pre-reconstructed 3D volumes from dense scans unavailable. This exposes a gap in current sparse-view approaches: Optimization-based methods, which use the sparse measurements directly but lack data-driven priors to suppress artifacts, and learning-based methods, which use strong priors but usually require densely scanned training volumes acquired outside the xSV-CT regime. We study this train-sparse / infer-sparse setting by learning a pose-aware diffusion prior from one 2D projection per training sample, then guiding diffusion sampling with measured-view fidelity, shared-volume reprojection, and projection-physics consistency for tomographic reconstruction. On two public CT datasets across 1-, 4-, and 8-view settings, the proposed method achieves the best novel-view synthesis scores and best or competitive reconstruction quality compared with baselines that use dense-volume supervision.

papers.title: Inverse Scattering of Periodic Surfaces with Multilayer Superlenses: Perturbation Analysis and Resolution Enhancement
papers.abstract: This paper presents a rigorous mathematical analysis of inverse scattering for periodic surfaces through a multilayer superlens. Using the transformed field expansion, we derive a highly explicit reconstruction formula. We theoretically prove that under perfect matching, the reconstruction factor is independent of the number of layers and depends solely on the total material thicknesses, achieving uniform boundedness when the slab thickness dominates. By establishing first-order perturbation formulas and high-frequency asymptotics, we quantify how small material losses induce exponential amplification of high-frequency errors. Crucially, we show that increasing the number of layers substantially reduces this amplification coefficient. Consequently, for fixed total thicknesses, multilayer structures offer significantly improved stability and extended resolution limits for subwavelength reconstruction.

papers.title: Finite-time minimum-work protocols for underdamped traps driven by active forces
papers.abstract: Active systems provide non-equilibrium energy that can, in principle, be harvested using control protocols, making the optimization and reliability of work extraction a fundamental problem in microscopic thermodynamics. Yet how inertia and activity jointly modify the optimal work extraction protocol, the maximum extractable work its fluctuations, and implementability of protocols remains unclear. Here, we design minimum-work protocols, which maximize work extraction whenever extraction is possible, for an underdamped active particle in a translated harmonic trap. Remarkably, both the minimum mean work and its fluctuations are independent of mass, although inertia modifies the protocol. The results are then applied to an underdamped active Ornstein-Uhlenbeck particle (AOUP), designing an explicit work-extraction criterion and revealing extracted work's dependence on rotational noise and initial conditions. We further show that inertia strongly affects the difficulty of implementing the optimal protocol, producing a transition-like change between underdamped and overdamped optimal protocols. These findings uncover work extraction mechanisms at the microscale and guide the design of reliable energy-harvesting microscopic devices and robots.

papers.title: The Support-Distribution Conditions for MSRD Codes Reduce to a Single Inequality
papers.abstract: Byrne, Gluesing-Luerssen, and Ravagnani determined the number of codewords with a prescribed nonzero support in a linear maximum sum-rank distance code whose blocks have a common number of columns. Their formula depends only on the code parameters and the support dimensions. Evaluating it for arbitrary parameters gives a family of necessary nonnegativity conditions for existence. We prove their conjecture that this family is equivalent to the condition at the vector of total dimension $d+1$ obtained by filling the longest blocks first, where $d$ is the distance parameter. The resulting explicit criterion applies over every finite field $\mathbb F_q$, for all row numbers $n_i\leqslant m$ and $1\leqslant d<N$, where $m$ is the common number of columns and $N$ is the total number of rows. It also covers the boundary cases in which this vector fills each of its nonzero blocks completely, not explicitly included in the conjecture's displayed parameter range. The proof uses a generating function and an exchange identity to reduce the problem to vectors obtained by filling the longest blocks first. We then estimate alternating sums of elementary symmetric polynomials, with a separate argument for $q=2$. The dual conditions admit the same reduction. For codes that exist, the joint condition follows from sphere-packing bounds for the code and its dual. An infinite family of parameters satisfies the joint condition but admits no such linear code.

papers.title: Uniform Capacitated Clustering with Few Extra Centers
papers.abstract:
In uniform capacitated $(k,z)$-clustering, we open $k$ centers and assign every client to a center so that no center serves more than $U$ clients, minimizing the sum of the $z$-th powers of the assignment distances; $k$-median and $k$-means are the cases $z=1$ and $z=2$. We study algorithms that may open $k+\lfloor\varepsilon k\rfloor$ centers for a fixed $\varepsilon\in(0,1]$ and must respect the capacities exactly.
  In low dimensions, we give deterministic algorithms that are, except for $k$-median in the plane, the first polynomial-time algorithms with $(1+\varepsilon)k$ centers whose ratio is bounded independently of $\varepsilon$. In Euclidean space of any dimension, with clients of bounded doubling dimension, the ratio is $\mathcal{B}_z-(\mathcal{B}_z-1)\varepsilon+\delta$ for every fixed $\delta>0$, where $\mathcal{B}_z<3^z$ for $z>1$; this is $3-2\varepsilon+\delta$ for $k$-median and $5-4\varepsilon+\delta$ for $k$-means. In doubling metrics, the ratio is $3^z-(3^z-1)\varepsilon+\delta$ when centers may share a location, and a constant otherwise, such as $\min\{7-4\varepsilon,\,3+2\ln(1/\varepsilon)\}+\delta$ for $k$-median. In general metrics, deleting centers greedily gives ratio $3+2\ln(1/\varepsilon)+\delta$ for $k$-median when centers may share a location and $7+2\ln(1/\varepsilon)+\delta$ otherwise, improving the previous $O(\varepsilon^{-2}\log(1/\varepsilon))$.
  Our main tool is a rescue lemma. Splitting a near-optimal uncapacitated solution gives at most $2k-1$ blocks of at most $U$ clients, and giving a block a private center saves its share of the extra cost of following an optimal solution. Since a center of the optimal solution can be closed once all its blocks are rescued, $\lfloor\varepsilon k\rfloor$ extra centers save almost an $\varepsilon$-fraction of this extra cost instead of an $\varepsilon/2$-fraction.

papers.title: New Election, Same Old Story: How Tropes Form a Grammar of Election Rumors
papers.abstract: Recent elections in the United States have seen online rumors become a regular feature of election discourse as voters and election officials work to navigate a sea of digitally spread claims and propaganda. For the uninitiated, these rumors can feel overwhelming and random, sowing doubt about the integrity and legitimacy of recent elections. In this paper, we reviewed and qualitatively coded a large dataset of 590 election rumors collected during the the 2020 and 2022 national elections. We found that there are tropes that recur time and time again in election rumors, highlighting how these rumors are not as random as they may first appear. We make two primary contributions in this work: first, we introduce a hierarchical framework that structures observed tropes in three tiers (Meta-category, Meso-trope, and Micro-trope). Second, combining the framework with our coded data, we identify a visible grammar of election rumors, highlighting how in the majority of cases a rumor contains an Actor, and Object, and an Action, with optional grammatical components of Suggested Remedies and Scene & Setting. The framework and grammar can be used by other researchers to act as the underlying information architecture of analyses examining similar rumors, enabling the rapid identification, analysis, and prediction of election rumors.

papers.title: Vendster: An Evaluation Arena to Investigate How Forecasting Tool Quality Affects LLM Agent Behaviors in Buyer-Vendor Negotiation
papers.abstract: Time-series forecasters are ranked almost entirely by accuracy metrics, but a forecast's decision value, its effect on the downstream decision, need not track accuracy and is rarely measured. This problem compounds as large language model (LLM) agents increasingly consume forecasters as tools, mediating them through stochastic, opaque policies. We present Vendster, an evaluation arena measuring how a forecaster's bias and prediction-interval width change the outcome of a buyer--vendor discount negotiation between two LLM agents. In the reference instance Vendster-M5, sampling base demand patterns from the M5 dataset, we evaluate two frontier-closed LLM families (Claude Opus 4.6 and GPT-5.6 Sol) and two open ones (DeepSeek-V3.2 and Qwen3-235B-A22B). Model-generated forecasts raise sales target attainment by up to +17 percentage points (p<0.001), yet standard forecast evaluation metrics such as relWQL and MASE do not predict negotiation outcomes at a statistically significant level. To isolate the causal structure, we substitute in synthetic forecasts with controlled bias and interval width. Under-prediction bias significantly improves outcomes for agents that react more to the forecasts---dose-response slopes -0.387 and -0.416 (p<0.001). Interval width has no statistically significant effect at zero bias. These findings indicate that the direction of forecast bias and agent forecast-reactivity are more strongly associated with downstream outcomes than forecast accuracy. Vendster is fully customizable and released under CC BY-NC 4.0 at https://github.com/amazon-science/Vendster.

papers.title: Idea Traces: Threading Accretive Content across Scientific Papers
papers.abstract: We introduce idea traces, a novel thread-based representation of accretive content across scientific papers. Rather than capturing fixed themes from papers, idea traces surface similarities and deltas of faceted content that enable inspection of how ideas relate and evolve across the citation network. To extract traces, we contribute an LLM pipeline that deconstructs salient transitions between pairs of papers and collates the output into an idea dependency graph. We leverage idea traces in a visual system that supports idea-driven navigation starting from a seed paper, lifting the "plane" of synthesis from papers to ideas. To evaluate the usefulness and quality of generated ideas, we provide a case study that compares our approach with an LLM Q&A workflow, and interview 10 researchers who used our system and annotated 110 ideas. Experts found that our approach helped extract a useful space of connections that would have been difficult to make otherwise. Drawing on their feedback, we outline several promising directions for future research.

papers.title: Building On Learning-Augmented Online Sorting
papers.abstract: Online sorting is a problem that has gained attention recently, and is a natural translation of sorting into an online setting. The problem at hand is to place elements of an online sequence immediately and irrevocably with the goal of producing an array that is as close to sorted as possible upon inserting all elements. Recent work by Bercea et al. [ESA 2026] introduced the incorporation of learned predictions into the online sorting domain. They show lower bounds for the consistency and robustness of any algorithm, including randomization, then provide a deterministic algorithm that is $O(n/r)$-consistent and $O(r)$-robust, which are tight bounds. However, this algorithm requires prior knowledge of the optimal offline cost of the full input sequence before all elements have been revealed. We resolve this by providing an algorithm with matching bounds that does not require knowledge of the optimal cost, then extend these results to the more general problem of online metric TSP, in line with the prior work.

papers.title: Asymptotic GIT-stability of KSB-stable varieties
papers.abstract: We prove that KSB-stable varieties introduced by Koll\'ar and Shepherd-Barron as a generalization of Deligne-Mumford's stable curves are stable in the sense of geometric invariant theory (GIT). More precisely, we show that KSB-stable varieties are asymptotically GIT-stable with respect to a sequence of linearizations defined by the Hodge bundle.

papers.title: From Geometry to Behavior: How Instruction Exposure Unlocks Latent Rhetorical Directions in LLMs
papers.abstract:
Language models do not merely memorize facts; they absorb rhetorical strategies from pretraining data, including the human tendency to reason by analogy. We ask: is this absorbed capability geometrically accessible before any instruction tuning, and what determines whether it can be activated at inference time?
  We extract an "Analogy Vector" from the residual stream via difference-in-means and show it enables steerable explanation style across seven instruction-tuned models (Gemma-2, Llama-3.1, Qwen-2.5; 2B-32B), improving harmonic mean from 3.22 to 3.94 (+22%) for Gemma-2-9B-IT on 300 held-out test prompts. A small human validation study confirms the LLM judge on Analogy Quality.
  Our central finding, from seven matched base-instruct pairs, is a gradient of behavioral accessibility: the analogy direction exists in every base model, but its behavioral accessibility under linear intervention scales continuously with instruction exposure during training. Gemma-2 base models (strict pretraining/IT separation) show flat steering landscapes: present but behaviorally inert. Qwen-2.5 base models (instruction data woven into pretraining) are already partially accessible before any explicit fine-tuning; base-instruct cosine similarity of the analogy vector reaches 0.94-0.97 for Qwen versus 0.37-0.66 for Gemma, providing geometric corroboration of the behavioral gradient. This challenges the binary "base vs instruct" framing: the relevant variable is how much instruction exposure a model has received across its full training pipeline. We position activation steering as a complementary interpretability tool that reveals how instruction exposure organizes rhetorical knowledge in activation space.

papers.title: Toward Understanding the Value of Anarchy: Empirical Studies on Best Response Dynamics
papers.abstract: We study experimental results of best response dynamics (BRD) in randomly generated weighted action networked multiagent optimization problems where agent utility is the agent's marginal contribution to the system objective. We compare those results to the Price of Anarchy (PoA) established in the literature for marginal contribution and to the expected value of randomly choosing from the available equilibria. PoA is used as a metric to describe the performance of various solutions to multiagent optimization problems, but the utility of this metric may be overrated if such worst-case instances are rare in practice. Our study provides evidence to support this doubt, showing that simple best response mechanics tend to out perform the PoA prediction and a uniform random equilibrium selection, even when agents are unable to observe all other agents' actions. In the process of seeking a more ideal metric, we discover that BRD appears to perform better than average. That is, when multiple equilibria exist, BRD appears to be biased toward the higher-performance ones. This evidence also demonstrates that further investigation into a more robust metric for multiagent optimization solutions is warranted and pushes us to understand whether the bias toward better equilibria hold in more general cases.

papers.title: Nodal magnon spin current at an antiferromagnet/altermagnet junction
papers.abstract:
We investigate the thermally driven magnon spin current across a junction between a $d$-wave altermagnet (AM) and a ferromagnet (FM) or an antiferromagnet (AFM).
  The current consists of a component independent of the interface angle and an angularly dependent component with the $d$-wave form.
  For a sublattice-symmetric interface, the two junctions behave oppositely under reversal of the altermagnetic domain: in the FM/AM junction the angularly dependent component is odd and cancels on averaging over the domains, whereas in the AFM/AM junction the angularly independent component vanishes by symmetry and the angularly dependent component survives the domain average at a fixed N\'eel vector of the AFM.
  Both follow from a selective tunneling: a pair of spins bonded across the interface transmits magnons when the spins are parallel and not when antiparallel, which makes the AFM/AM junction a magnon valve: the configuration in which the bonded spins are antiparallel blocks the current up to the sublattice admixture of the magnons.
  The anisotropic tunneling is detectable as the sign reversal of the current between the interfaces normal to $[310]$ and $[130]$, and the valve reads the N\'eel vector of the altermagnet relative to that of the antiferromagnet through the magnitude of the current at a fixed interface.

papers.title: Linear hereditary quasirandomness
papers.abstract: Conlon, Fox and Sudakov (\emph{Math. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc.} \textbf{164} (2018), 385--399) conjectured that hereditary subgraph counts force quasirandomness with linear dependence on the counting error. We prove this for every graph containing an edge. Let \(H\) have \(r\) vertices and \(m\ge1\) edges, and fix \(p\in(0,1)\). If every subset \(S\) of an \(n\)-vertex graph \(G\) contains \(p^m|S|^r\pm\delta n^r\) labelled injective copies of \(H\), then \(\lvert e_G(A,B)-p|A||B|\rvert\le C_{H,p}\delta n^2\) for all \(A,B\subseteq V(G)\), where \(e_G(A,B)\) counts ordered adjacent pairs. The proof extracts averaged rooted counts and represents each nonlinear term by a linear map in one selected edge factor. Composing two such maps gives an edge substitution with a superlinear cut-norm bound. A separate star expansion gives stronger local estimates for triangle-free graphs. The linear order is best possible even when \(2e(G)/n^2=p+O(n^{-2})\).

papers.title: Stopping Rules and the Poisson Boundary of Random Walks on Countable Groups
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the terminal laws and Poisson boundaries obtained by stopping random walks on countable groups. For a transient walk, we give a direct Green-potential characterization of randomized stopping distributions and show that the terminal law determines the mean stopping time. On free groups, this yields finitely supported randomized stopping distributions at a positive total variation distance from every ordinary stopping distribution. We construct symmetric, fully supported recurrent measures of finite entropy on countable locally finite groups and obtain ordinary strict boundary enlargements when the group is not Choquet-Deny. For generating source and terminal measures of finite entropy, positive asymptotic entropy of the source forces the stopping time to have finite mean. A direct proof of the finite-mean entropy formula and boundary preservation then shows that a finite-entropy stopping chain has at most one strict enlargement. An exact stopped-word entropy identity shows that infinite-mean ordinary stopping with a finite-entropy terminal law has infinite conditional history entropy.

papers.title: KARMA: Training-Free Knowledge-Atomic Harness Evolution for Industrial Advertising Agents
papers.abstract: Industrial advertising agents must continually adapt their decision knowledge to changing product offerings, traffic patterns, and operating policies. We present KARMA (Knowledge-Atomic, Regression-Gated Modular Adaptation), a training-free framework that evolves six typed knowledge modules while keeping model weights and executable harness code frozen. During our evolution, a deterministic Trace Verifier maps observed errors to candidate modules, and a Critic compares successful and failed trajectories to guide a tool-constrained Evolver. The Evolver applies atomic knowledge edits, which a fixed validation gate retains only when their measured gain reaches a threshold; otherwise, the previous knowledge state is restored. We evaluate KARMA with three LLM families on cases sampled from a corpus of approximately half a million real-world operation logs across six e-commerce domains. Across 18 domain--model settings, KARMA raises the average hold-out score from 30.19 to 39.15 (+8.96 points, +29.7%). Ablations show that removing either successful or failed trajectories more than halves the average hold-out gain. Evolved knowledge also transfers across domains without further adaptation, yielding an average hold-out gain of 8.54 points across all source--target pairs. By linking retained patches to their diagnostic evidence and validation outcomes, KARMA supports inspectable, reversible knowledge adaptation for agents in Web marketplaces.

authors.name: Yuanzhen Rong

papers.title: StepControl: Long-Horizon Human Motion Generation from Foot-Contact Schedules
papers.abstract: Controllable human motion generation has largely focused on specifying what action should occur or where the body should move. We study a complementary question: can full-body motion be controlled by specifying only when each foot contacts the ground? We introduce StepControl, an autoregressive diffusion model conditioned on a future binary left/right foot-contact schedule, without requiring target root and body poses, or semantic prompts. StepControl represents contact as explicit temporal events and injects them through dedicated cross-attention with classifier-free guidance. We further introduce a stochastic mixture noise schedule and warmup strategy for stable long-horizon autoregressive generation. Experiments show that StepControl follows prescribed contact timing more accurately than adapting existing spatially guided motion generators to contact constraints. It maintains effective contact control over long continuous rollouts and responds to edited schedules such as cadence changes, stop-and-go pauses, limping gaits, and bilateral jumping. Our results show that minimal foot-contact schedules provide an effective and intuitive temporal interface for controllable motion generation.

papers.title: A note on a problem of Ma and Chen
papers.abstract: Let $S=(s_1,s_2,\cdots)$ be a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers. For any real number $\alpha>0$, let $S_\alpha=(\lfloor\alpha s_1\rfloor,\lfloor\alpha s_2\rfloor,\cdots)$. We prove that if $s_{n+1}\le 2s_n$ for every positive integer $n$, then there exists $0<\alpha<1$ such that $S_\alpha$ is strongly complete. In addition, this gives a negative answer to a problem of Ma and Chen in [Acta Arith. 203 (2022), 307--318]. We also prove that the same result is true if $s_{n+1}\le 2s_n$ for all sufficiently large $n$.
